good-writing-000122.en: Anne: For Sam, Claire, and Jax Lamott, my pride and joy
good-writing-000122.zh: 安妮：献给萨姆、克莱尔和杰克斯·拉莫特，我的骄傲与喜悦

good-writing-000123.en: Easy reading is damn hard writing.
good-writing-000123.zh: 读起来轻松的文字，写起来却难得要命。

good-writing-000126.en: I first wrote professionally for a newspaper in New York’s Hudson Valley.
good-writing-000126.zh: 我最初是在纽约哈德逊谷的一家报纸上从事专业写作工作。

good-writing-000127.en: As a cub reporter at the Kingston Daily Freeman in the late seventies, I cut my teeth on town meetings, county court, the police blotter, and obituaries.
good-writing-000127.zh: 在七十年代末，作为《金斯顿每日弗里曼》报纸的实习记者，我最初的工作是报道镇上的会议、县法院的相关新闻、警方记录以及讣告等新闻。

good-writing-000128.en: I learned to obey the front page’s tight style restraints: omniscient third person, complete sentences, no exclamations or questions, sixth-grade vocabulary, scarce adjectives or adverbs, pretense of objectivity, inverted pyramid, few parentheticals, no slang, no alliteration or rhyming, no long quotes, stricture after stricture straitjacketing my weirder impulses.
good-writing-000128.zh: 我学会遵守头版新闻严格的文体规范：采用全知的第三人称视角，使用完整的句子，不用感叹句或疑问句，词汇难度限于六年级水平，少用形容词和副词，保持看似客观的立场，采用倒金字塔结构，少用插入语，不用俚语、头韵或押韵，不大段引用别人的话。一条又一条的限制，束缚着我那些更古怪的创作冲动。

good-writing-000130.zh: 语言高效、精练，却毫无色彩。

good-writing-000131.en: I had a lot to learn about writing, and in retrospect the overly mannered style of hard news was a godsend to a mind that had spent its youth immersed in literary and experimental fiction, where rules are to be broken and anarchy is always knocking.
good-writing-000131.zh: 我在写作方面还有很多东西需要学习。回顾过去，那些过于拘谨的硬新闻写作风格，其实对这样一个从小就沉浸在文学与实验性小说创作中的人来说，简直是天赐良机——因为在这样的环境中，规则必须被打破，混乱总是不可避免。

good-writing-000132.en: One morning, my editor Sam Daleo looked me in the eye: “Neal, the trick is to write with your verbs.”
good-writing-000132.zh: 一天早晨，我的编辑萨姆·达莱奥看着我的眼睛说：“尼尔，诀窍在于用动词来组织你的文字。”

good-writing-000133.en: He explained the difference between a vivid verb and a weak one.
good-writing-000133.zh: 他解释了“生动动词”和“弱动词”之间的区别。

good-writing-000134.en: Thumb forward in this book of rules, and you’ll see that as Rule 1, with an explanation for how and why it works.
good-writing-000134.zh: 在本书的这套规则中，将看到第一条规则的解释，包括其运作方式及背后的原理。

good-writing-000135.en: In my mind, it’s the Daleo Rule.
good-writing-000135.zh: 在我心里，这就是“达莱奥法则”。

good-writing-000136.en: And for a long time, it protected and encouraged me.
good-writing-000136.zh: 在很长一段时间里，它一直保护并鼓励着我。

good-writing-000137.en: I was happy with my one rule of rhetoric and persuasion, and my career progressed at a steady pace.
good-writing-000137.zh: 我对自己的修辞和说服技巧原则感到满意，我的职业生涯也以稳定的速度发展。

good-writing-000138.en: I became a better and better newsman in terms of fact-gathering and reporting.
good-writing-000138.zh: 在收集信息和进行报道方面，我变得越来越出色了。

good-writing-000139.en: My writing didn’t look so different from what I scanned on the front pages of The New York Times or The Washington Post, at least to me.
good-writing-000139.zh: 我的写作风格与我在《纽约时报》或《华盛顿邮报》的报纸上看到的文章并没有太大区别，至少对我来说是这样。

good-writing-000140.en: And then one day I woke up to the Times’s front-page story on the marriage of Prince Charles and Lady Di.
good-writing-000140.zh: 后来有一天，我醒来后读到了《纽约时报》头版关于查尔斯王子和戴安娜小姐婚礼的报道。

good-writing-000141.en: Here is how New York Times political writer R. W. Apple Jr. revealed the spectacle in his second paragraph: “The 2,500 guests inside Christopher Wren’s Baroque masterpiece, St. Paul’s Cathedral, the hundreds of thousands who watched the wedding party ride in magnificent horse-drawn carriages from Buckingham Palace to the cathedral and back, and the 700 million television viewers around the world witnessed a fairy tale come to life: the handsome Prince Charles in naval uniform marrying the lovely 20-year-old Diana Spencer, daughter of an earl, amid the sort of splendor the modern world has all but forgotten.”
good-writing-000141.zh: 《纽约时报》政治记者小 R. W. 阿普尔在第二段这样描绘这场盛典：“克里斯托弗·雷恩的巴洛克式杰作圣保罗大教堂内的 2,500 位宾客、沿途观看婚礼队伍乘华丽马车往返于白金汉宫和大教堂之间的数十万人，以及全球 7 亿电视观众，一同见证了童话成真：身着海军制服的英俊查尔斯王子，在现代世界几乎已遗忘的盛大排场中，迎娶了美丽的 20 岁戴安娜·斯宾塞。她是一位伯爵的女儿。”

good-writing-000142.en: This syntax didn’t emulate Tom Wolfe or Hunter Thompson in a magazine displaying the New Journalism that was all the rage.
good-writing-000142.zh: 这段句法并不是在模仿汤姆·沃尔夫或亨特·汤普森，也不是杂志上当时风靡一时的“新新闻主义”写法。

good-writing-000143.en: It wasn’t a feature story masquerading as an eventful occurrence.
good-writing-000143.zh: 这并不算是一个以“事件性报道”为幌子的故事。

good-writing-000144.en: Here stood a hard news reporter packing information into one elegant phrase after another, and I trembled in shame.
good-writing-000144.zh: 站在这里的记者正将信息压缩成一句句优雅的话语来报道，而我则因羞愧而浑身发抖。

good-writing-000145.en: Where did the legendary Johnny Apple learn to do that?
good-writing-000145.zh: 传奇记者约翰尼·阿普尔究竟是从哪里学会这一手的？

good-writing-000146.en: He was thinking differently from me about newspaper writing.
good-writing-000146.zh: 他在报纸写作方面的思考方式与我不同。

good-writing-000147.en: For both of us it might be a craft, not an art, but he showed without telling that daily journalism could be graceful and as beckoning as literary fiction.
good-writing-000147.zh: 对我们两人来说，这可能只是一种技巧，而非真正的艺术。但他在不言而喻的情况下表明，日常新闻报道也可以具有艺术性，并且同样具有文学作品的魅力。

good-writing-000148.en: By a couple of years later I had accumulated three or four rules of rhetoric, enough to survive in the medium-sized newspaper where I now worked.
good-writing-000148.zh: 几年之后，我总结出了三四条修辞规则，这些规则足以帮助我在当时工作的中型报纸上立足。

good-writing-000149.en: The Bergen Record in Hackensack, New Jersey, had a circulation of 150,000, but because it catered to some of the richest people in the state, it landed on the doorstep with a thud, fat and thick with advertising and a wide-open news hole overflowing with local and wire reporting.
good-writing-000149.zh: 我当时供职于新泽西州哈肯萨克的《卑尔根纪事报》，发行量为十五万份。可它的服务对象包括州内一些最富有的人，因此报纸被送到门前时总会砰然落地：广告把它撑得厚厚的，宽裕的新闻版面则塞满了本地报道和通讯社稿件。

good-writing-000150.en: The newsroom employed 260 editors, reporters, feature writers, illustrators, opinion writers, cartoonists, photographers, clerks, and librarians, a number more typical of papers three times its size.
good-writing-000150.zh: 报社的新闻部门雇用了260名编辑、记者、专题作家、插画师、评论员、漫画家、摄影师、文员和资料管理员；这样的人员规模，通常只有发行量是它三倍的报纸才会拥有。

good-writing-000151.en: Among the sixty or so writers a few stood out as stylists.
good-writing-000151.zh: 在六十多位作家中，有几位脱颖而出，成为著名的文体家。

good-writing-000152.en: I dissected their stories and occasionally asked for advice.
good-writing-000152.zh: 我分析了他们的故事，并偶尔向他们寻求建议。

good-writing-000153.en: By the time I left five years later, I had corralled another five or six rules.
good-writing-000153.zh: 五年后我离开时，我已经掌握了另外五到六条规则。

good-writing-000155.en: A meager six or eight rules of rhetoric could maintain a career, and ten were enough to be admired by peers.
good-writing-000155.zh: 只要掌握六到八条基本的修辞规则，就能维持一份职业；而要是能掌握十条这样的规则，那自然足以赢得同行的赞赏了。

good-writing-000156.en: That’s the germination of this book.
good-writing-000156.zh: 这就是这本书的诞生过程。

good-writing-000157.en: From my time at the Record through a corporate career in publicity and marketing, and into a third life as a spiritual coach and author, writing has stood fast as my default expertise.
good-writing-000157.zh: 从我在《Record》杂志工作的时期，到在公关与营销领域从事职业工作，再到后来作为精神教练和作家展开新的人生旅程，写作一直是我最擅长的领域。

good-writing-000158.en: I’ve made a living from magazine writing, business writing and editing, speechwriting, copywriting, short story writing, ghostwriting, memoir editing, scriptwriting, presentation writing, and book writing...and all along my hack writing career, I have quietly expanded my kit bag of rules for good writing.
good-writing-000158.zh: 我通过撰写杂志文章、商业文案、演讲稿、广告文案、短篇故事、代笔作品、回忆录编辑、剧本创作、演示文稿写作以及书籍写作等方式来谋生。在漫长的写作生涯中，我不断积累着关于优秀写作的规则和技巧。

good-writing-000159.en: The bag contains thirty-six now, which doesn’t mean I’m three times the writer I was in the eighties.
good-writing-000159.zh: 现在这个包里装着三十六件物品，但这并不意味我的写作能力是八十年代时的三倍。

good-writing-000160.en: I still can’t conceive of arriving at Johnny Apple’s second paragraph all by myself.
good-writing-000160.zh: 我仍然无法想象自己能够独自完成对Johnny Apple的第二部分内容的翻译工作。

good-writing-000161.en: But thirty-six rules are more than enough for me to amuse myself with complex sentence puzzles every time I sit at my keyboard.
good-writing-000161.zh: 不过，三十六条规则已经足够让我在每次坐在键盘前时，通过复杂的句子谜题来消遣时间了。

good-writing-000162.en: These rules don’t restrict me so much as they encourage me to stretch into more and more possibilities, leaps of imagination, and lovely explorations.
good-writing-000162.zh: 这些规则并没有严格限制我，反而鼓励我去探索更多的可能性、发挥更多的想象力，进行更多有趣的探索。

good-writing-000163.en: Thomas Mann defined a writer as someone for whom writing is more difficult than it is for other people.
good-writing-000163.zh: 托马斯·曼将作家定义为那些认为写作难度比其他人更高的人。

good-writing-000164.en: Most books are not composed by people whose primary concern, expertise, and profession is words and rhetoric.
good-writing-000164.zh: 大多数书籍并非由那些以文字和修辞为首要关注点、专业领域的人来编写而成的。

good-writing-000165.en: Most books are written by academics, other experts, or pundits.
good-writing-000165.zh: 大多数书籍都是由学者、其他专家或评论家撰写的。

good-writing-000166.en: Many fiction writers, some of them quite successful, are less concerned with their sentences than with moving the plot along.
good-writing-000166.zh: 许多小说作家，其中一些还相当成功，他们更关心的是如何推动故事的发展，而不是如何优化自己的写作风格。

good-writing-000167.en: For many authors, the main interest is the overall theme they are elaborating or the argument they are proving.
good-writing-000167.zh: 对于许多作者来说，他们最关心的就是自己所要阐述的主题，或是他们想要证明的论点。

good-writing-000168.en: But for some professional writers, the central interest always remains the sentence.
good-writing-000168.zh: 但对于一些专业的作家来说，他们始终将句子的结构作为核心关注点。

good-writing-000169.en: Next comes the consistency or flow of the material.
good-writing-000169.zh: 接下来要讨论的是该材料的稠度或流动性。

good-writing-000170.en: The topic or plot of the book, the content of the speech or lyrics, takes third place—just the material with which to exercise persuasive prowess.
good-writing-000170.zh: 这本书的主题或情节、演讲或歌词的内容，都只是用来锻炼说服力技巧的素材而已，其重要性仅排在第三位。

good-writing-000171.en: Throughout my careers my default comfort with writing, and especially the improvement of sentences, has consistently shown up.
good-writing-000171.zh: 在我的职业生涯中，我一直都具备出色的写作能力，尤其是句子结构的优化方面，这些优点一直都表现得非常明显。

good-writing-000172.zh: 写作仍然是我的职业活动。

good-writing-000173.en: And it is exactly the same to me whether I’m writing a news article, a business letter, a novel, or a self-help book.
good-writing-000173.zh: 对我来说，无论是撰写新闻文章、商务信函、小说还是自助书籍，其写作方式都是完全相同的。

good-writing-000174.en: My job is the sentence, and secondarily the paragraph or flow, and only thirdly the content of what I have learned or am learning.
good-writing-000174.zh: 我的工作重点是句子结构，其次才是段落或文章的整体布局，而第三才是我所学习或正在学习的内容本身。

good-writing-000175.en: Writing is a vehicle for my life to play out.
good-writing-000175.zh: 写作是我展现生命的载体。

good-writing-000176.en: We all have our masteries, a job or avocation that fulfills our social destiny as a groove—often for income and pleasure, but even more so as our field for personal exploration, for finding out about life.
good-writing-000176.zh: 我们每个人都拥有自己的专长或爱好，这些专长或爱好能够帮助我们实现自己的社会使命——通常是为了获取收入和乐趣，但更主要的是，它们能让我们在个人探索中有所发现，了解生活的更多奥秘。

good-writing-000177.en: A garbage collector on a sanitation truck explores freedom and routine and how people live, and with luck has afternoons free.
good-writing-000177.zh: 一辆负责垃圾清理的清洁车，探索着自由与日常生活的本质，以及人们是如何生活的。幸运的话，清洁工们还有空闲的下午时间。

good-writing-000178.en: Writing is like that for me; it mirrors what I’ve explored up to today, and reflects where I’m now standing.
good-writing-000178.zh: 对我来说，写作就是这样；它反映了我至今为止所探索的一切，也体现了我现在所处的位置。

good-writing-000179.en: Oddly, I’m not often conscious of that interplay; when I sit at my desk, shaky or confident, it’s for a job.
good-writing-000179.zh: 奇怪的是，我并没有经常意识到这种相互作用。当我坐在办公桌前时，无论我是紧张还是自信，那都是为了工作而这样做。

good-writing-000180.en: All I anticipate is the difficulty and reward of composing good sentences.
good-writing-000180.zh: 我所期待的，只是创作好句子所带来的挑战与乐趣。

good-writing-000182.en: As any decent writer knows, we don’t write what we want to write.
good-writing-000182.zh: 任何有经验的作家都知道，我们不会写自己想写的内容。

good-writing-000183.en: In my case, that would be a novel with the erudition and voice of William Faulkner.
good-writing-000183.zh: 就我而言，那将是一部以威廉·福克纳的学识与风格为特点的小说。

good-writing-000184.en: No, we grudgingly write what we think we need to write, which means that most of us, including Barbara Kingsolver and Ian McEwan possibly, are stuck with writing about something we haven’t completely gotten over.
good-writing-000184.zh: 不，我们只是勉强写出我们认为需要写的内容而已。这意味着，包括芭芭拉·金斯索尔弗和伊恩·麦克尤恩在内，我们大多数人都得继续写作那些我们尚未完全克服的问题。

good-writing-000185.en: In that sense, all books are, to their authors, memoirs—reorganized diaries of what has been guiding them, or calling them to explore, or keeping them up at night.
good-writing-000185.zh: 从这个意义上说，所有书籍对于它们的作者来说，都相当于一种回忆录——是对那些引导他们探索、或促使他们不断思考的事件的记录。

good-writing-000186.en: After my private clients and I had been examining the mechanics of the inner critic for a few years, I decided to make a book about it, titled Better Days.
good-writing-000186.zh: 在我和我的私人客户们花了几年时间研究“内在批评者”的运作机制之后，我决定撰写一本关于这一主题的书籍，书名为《更美好的日子》。

good-writing-000187.en: I’m a writer; it’s my default job.
good-writing-000187.zh: 我是一名作家，这是我的本职工作。

good-writing-000188.en: My writing rolls along as a vehicle to explore my world.
good-writing-000188.zh: 我的写作是一种用来探索我的世界的工具。

good-writing-000189.en: My study happens to include as one of its subjects the very possibility of elegance in articulation, using the tropes and rules of my upbringing.
good-writing-000189.zh: 我的研究恰好将“发音的优雅性”作为其中一个研究主题，同时运用了我成长过程中所接触到的各种修辞规则和规则。

good-writing-000190.en: In one sense, writing well is the same as articulating well is the same as exploring carefully.
good-writing-000190.zh: 从某种意义上说，写得好等同于表达得清晰，也等同于进行深入的探索。

good-writing-000191.en: But an academic who writes badly is also exploring and articulating well enough.
good-writing-000191.zh: 不过，一个写作能力不佳的学者，其研究内容和表达方式依然相当充分。

good-writing-000192.en: The academic is following her own fascinations in worlds of tiny discriminations and hair-splitting analysis, her own playground far afield from mine.
good-writing-000192.zh: 这位学者沉浸在自己那些琐碎的争论和繁琐的分析之中，她的世界与我所在的世界相去甚远。

good-writing-000193.en: In my world of writing, I hair-split infinitives, not outside discoveries.
good-writing-000193.zh: 在我的写作世界中，我强调动词的完整性，而不是追求表面的发现。

good-writing-000194.en: As long as I’m aware that my being a writer is an arbitrary default, no better or worse than being a garbage collector or academic, I’m capable in my job: to produce good sentences.
good-writing-000194.zh: 只要我知道，我作为一名作家这一身份只是一种任意选择的默认身份，并不比成为垃圾收集员或学者更出色或更糟糕，那么我在工作中就能做好自己的本职工作：创作出优秀的作品。

good-writing-000195.en: So this isn’t a book about becoming a writer, or how to write, or syntax, or rhetoric in the philosophical sense.
good-writing-000195.zh: 因此，这本书并不是一本关于如何成为作家、如何写作、语法或哲学意义上的修辞学的书籍。

good-writing-000196.en: Annie and I aren’t grammarians or the usage police.
good-writing-000196.zh: 安妮和我并不是语法专家，也不懂如何使用语言规则。

good-writing-000197.en: You won’t meet epistrophes or ablative absolutes or master plots.
good-writing-000197.zh: 你不会遇到任何形式的所有格结构、分词结构或固定不变的句子结构。

good-writing-000198.en: This book is curious about what happens after you’ve got a sentence in mind, maybe even after you’ve put the thought to paper, maybe after you’ve finished your entire first draft.
good-writing-000198.zh: 这本书探讨的是，在你心中已经有了某个想法之后，甚至在你把这个想法写下来之后，或者在你完成整个初稿之后，还会发生什么。

good-writing-000199.en: This book is concerned with improving sentences.
good-writing-000199.zh: 这本书致力于改进句子结构。

good-writing-000200.en: The book embraces persuasion in its biggest sense—not to win an argument, but to be elegant, to convince a reader to continue on to the next sentence, and maybe to persuade them that a song fills the air even if the subject is poisonous frogs of Costa Rica.
good-writing-000200.zh: 这本书以最广泛的意义来探讨“说服力”——不是为了赢得争论，而是为了显得优雅，为了吸引读者继续阅读下去。也许，它还能让读者相信，即使主题是关于哥斯达黎加的毒蛙，一首歌依然能够充满空气中的氛围。

good-writing-000201.en: And while we call them rules, these suggestions engage at first as tips.
good-writing-000201.zh: 虽然我们把这些建议称为“规则”，但实际上它们最初只是一些建议而已。

good-writing-000202.en: After trying them out, you might adopt some as useful for your prose.
good-writing-000202.zh: 试用了这些之后，你可能会发现其中一些方法对你的写作非常有用。

good-writing-000203.en: Only then do they become rules, and only temporarily in your mind.
good-writing-000203.zh: 只有到那时，它们才会成为规则，而且这种规则在你脑海中只是暂时的。

good-writing-000204.en: We humans have enough rules already; new ones should be added cautiously and lightly.
good-writing-000204.zh: 我们人类已经有很多规则了；新规则的添加应该谨慎且适度进行。

good-writing-000205.en: Some of the rules in this book won’t work for you or your way of writing; then ignore them.
good-writing-000205.zh: 这本书中的一些规则可能并不适合你的写作风格或习惯；那么，就忽略这些规则吧。

good-writing-000206.en: Troll us if you must, but believe it when we say we don’t mean to be scolds.
good-writing-000206.zh: 如果你们需要，可以随意吐槽我们，但请相信我们并非故意要表现得像恶婆婆一样。

good-writing-000208.en: Almost since meeting my husband, Neal, in 2016, I was aware that he had compiled a list of thirty-six rules of writing, based on his years as a journalist.
good-writing-000208.zh: 自从2016年遇到我的丈夫尼尔以来，我就意识到他根据自己作为记者的经验，总结出了36条写作规则。

good-writing-000209.en: They were at once simple and obvious but also profound.
good-writing-000209.zh: 它们既简单明了，又富有深意。

good-writing-000210.en: They were pretty much all you needed to know when you set out to make sentences, and seemed especially useful if you had gotten something written and were trying to make it better.
good-writing-000210.zh: 在造句时，这些知识基本上就足够了。如果你已经写了一些文字，并希望改进它们，那么这些知识会特别有用。

good-writing-000211.en: I started handing them out to random writing students, and then eventually had my pupils go to his website, where they are still displayed.
good-writing-000211.zh: 我开始将这些作品分发给各个写作课程的学生们，后来学生们还访问了他的网站，那些作品至今仍陈列在他的网站上。

good-writing-000212.en: And I internalized them, so that in the nine years we’ve been together, I’ve called them up like a checklist when I edit my work before handing it over to Neal for his input and response.
good-writing-000212.zh: 我将这些内容内化了，所以在我们共度的九年里，每当我准备将作品提交给尼尔进行评审时，我都会像使用清单一样，逐一检查这些细节。

good-writing-000213.en: Stronger verbs, layered sentences, twist those clichés if you are going to insist on the right to use them—I’d run Neal’s list and make sure I had not committed any of his sins.
good-writing-000213.zh: 使用更强烈的动词，构建层次丰富的句子结构，如果一定要使用那些陈词滥调的话，那就稍微改变一下吧——我会仔细对照尼尔的清单，确保自己没有犯下他的任何错误。

good-writing-000214.en: My teaching has mostly been about the attitude of writing: gaining the confidence to get your stories told, to stop not writing, to tell the truthiest truth, make the plunge into empathy, and, mostly, to develop the habit of keeping your butt in the chair every day.
good-writing-000214.zh: 我的教学主要围绕写作的态度展开：培养写作的信心，不再害怕写作，能够真实表达自己的想法，勇于投入情感表达，最重要的是，养成每天保持专注的习惯。

good-writing-000215.en: Neal tends more toward encouraging people to write better sentences and paragraphs.
good-writing-000215.zh: 尼尔更倾向于鼓励人们写出更优美的句子和段落。

good-writing-000216.en: Hence this book, and my own fixation with the best possible sentences I can write.
good-writing-000216.zh: 因此，这本书的诞生，以及我对写出最完美的句子的执着追求，都是源于此。

good-writing-000217.en: My beloved friend the great food writer M. F. K. Fisher said, “Write one good clean sentence and put a period at the end of it. Then write another one.”
good-writing-000217.zh: 我亲爱的朋友、杰出的美食作家M.F.K.费舍尔说过：“先写出一句简洁明了的句子，然后在句子的末尾加上句号。之后再继续写下一句句子。”

good-writing-000218.en: That is great writing advice, but so much easier said than done.
good-writing-000218.zh: 这确实是很好的写作建议，不过说起来容易做起来却难多了。

good-writing-000219.en: Let me give you an example:

good-writing-000220.en: My mother walked quickly toward me, across the Irish-green lawn, looking at me in a very angry way.
good-writing-000220.zh: 我的母亲快步走向我，穿过那片爱尔兰绿色的草坪，用非常愤怒的眼神看着我。

good-writing-000221.en: Neal would have a field day with that one if I had included it in an essay (and he would also discourage me from using “having a field day” or any other cliché, like “easier said than done” two sentences above).
good-writing-000221.zh: 如果我在这篇论文中引用了那句话，Neal肯定会大发雷霆的。（而且他还会阻止我使用“轻松愉快”或任何其他陈词滥调，比如上面那句“说起来容易做起来难”）。

good-writing-000222.en: He would return this to me with my weak verbs questioned (“walked,” “looking”), the “very” crossed out, and the “Irish-green” challenged.
good-writing-000222.zh: 他会把这份文件还给我，同时修正那些有疑问的动词用法（比如“walked”和“looking”），将那些被划掉的“very”也改回来，并对“Irish-green”这一描述提出了质疑。

good-writing-000223.en: Now the sentence would read “My mother stalked across the lawn toward me.”
good-writing-000223.zh: 现在这句话应该是：“我的母亲沿着草坪朝我走来。”

good-writing-000224.en: Or: “Sometimes you need to spread your wings and take off no matter how shakily from the hard ground on which you stand, and fly; but other times, when things are very weird and scary, you need to find some kind of weighted ballast, to secure you here.”
good-writing-000224.zh: 或者可以说：“有时候，你就需要张开翅膀，从那坚硬的地面上起飞，尽管这个过程可能会很不稳定；但有时候，当情况变得非常奇怪和可怕时，你就需要找到某种可以承受重量的重物，来固定自己在这里。”

good-writing-000225.en: Now, I think that is a perfectly nice sentence, but when I showed it to Neal, it came back “Sometimes you need to lift off and fly, but in times like these you need ropes and ballast.”
good-writing-000225.zh: 现在，我觉得那确实是一个很棒的句子。不过，当我把这个句子展示给尼尔看时，他的回应是：“有时候你需要起飞飞行，但在这样的时刻，你就需要绳索和缓冲装置来帮助你。”

good-writing-000226.en: He took out the excess verbiage, the “very,” the adjectives and adverbs, and voilà, the one clean sentence M. F. K. Fisher asked of us.
good-writing-000226.zh: 他删去了那些多余的词语、那些“非常”这样的词缀，以及那些形容词和副词。就这样，我们得到了M. F. K. Fisher要求我们写的那一句简洁明了的句子。

good-writing-000227.en: One day I got curious what he was up to over in his office, and he explained that he was turning these insights and tips into a book.
good-writing-000227.zh: 有一天，我好奇他会在办公室里做什么，他解释说，他正在将这些发现和建议整理成一本书。

good-writing-000230.en: I had written a book on writing once, and thought maybe two writing books in one family might be a little unseemly.
good-writing-000230.zh: 我曾经写过一本关于写作的书籍，后来觉得，一个家庭中同时拥有两本关于写作的书籍可能会显得有些不适当。

good-writing-000232.en: I loved what he was doing—not simply listing the rules but making sense of them in his often quirky way.
good-writing-000232.zh: 我喜欢他做的事情——他不仅仅是在罗列规则，还以自己独特的方式对这些规则进行了阐释。

good-writing-000233.en: Then in my own hemming and hawing, butting-in fashion, I offered my take on some of what he’d written, tiny little suggestions on points he might want to add or delete, and he shot me a look such as one might make upon seeing a ticket on one’s windshield, flat and annoyed.
good-writing-000233.zh: 然后，以我那种慢条斯理、爱发牢骚的方式，我提出了我对他所写内容的一些看法，对那些他可能需要添加或删除的条款提出了一些小小的建议。而他看着我的眼神，就像看到挡风玻璃上贴着一张罚单时那种烦躁的表情。

good-writing-000234.en: Frantic to save the marriage, I coughed up yet another idea: What if I annotated what he had already written so brilliantly?
good-writing-000234.zh: 为了挽救这段婚姻，我又想出了一个主意：如果我把他之前写得那么精彩的内容加以注释的话，会怎么样呢？

good-writing-000235.en: This suggestion drew a slightly different look on Neal’s face.
good-writing-000235.zh: 这个建议让尼尔斯的脸上露出了略有不同的表情。

good-writing-000237.en: So I have gone ahead and added my two cents.
good-writing-000237.zh: 所以，我决定分享一下我的看法。

good-writing-000238.en: If you knew Neal, you would think me quite brave.
good-writing-000238.zh: 如果你了解尼尔斯，你就会认为我非常勇敢。

good-writing-000239.en: But to be fair, he has done the heavy lifting; I am the water boy.
good-writing-000239.zh: 不过，公平地说，他确实付出了很多努力；而我只是个轻松的助手而已。

good-writing-000240.en: Together we’ve described everything we know about writing better sentences that you might find useful in your work.
good-writing-000240.zh: 我们一起描述了我们所知道的所有关于如何写出更优秀的句子的知识，这些知识可能对你的工作有所帮助。

good-writing-000241.en: I’d like to add briefly that ever since we met, we have collaborated on each other’s material.
good-writing-000241.zh: 我想简要补充一点，从我们相识开始，我们就一直在互相合作，共同完成彼此的作品。

good-writing-000242.en: Collaboration, which we’ll talk about throughout this book, is a pleasure and a great relief, working with a trusted fellow writer to raise your work to its highest potential.
good-writing-000242.zh: 合作，这是我们在本书中反复讨论的主题。与一位值得信赖的同行作家合作，能够将你的作品提升到最佳状态，这是一种享受，也是一种巨大的解脱。

good-writing-000243.en: A colleague can save your bacon and reputation—you don’t want to burn any bridges by sending off work to a boss or agent or editor that is not your best—and the give-and-take can make writing a little more relaxed and playful, like playing doubles instead of singles in tennis.
good-writing-000243.zh: 一位同事可以帮助你避免陷入麻烦或损害自己的声誉——你不会希望因为把作品交给那些不如自己水平的老板、编辑或出版商而毁掉自己的名声。这种相互合作的态度可以让写作过程更加轻松愉快，就像在网球比赛中使用双打方式一样。

good-writing-000244.en: I might ask Neal to tell me everything he knows about spirit, say, or Buffalo Springfield, or Gatsby, or mulch, and I’ll scribble down his answer word for word, and then steal it all, frequently without attribution.
good-writing-000244.zh: 我可能会请尼尔告诉我他关于“精神”、“水牛城快板乐队”、“盖茨比”以及“覆盖层”等主题的所有信息。然后我会逐字记录他的回答，最后将这些内容全部抄袭下来，而完全不注明出处。

good-writing-000245.en: (He knows he is so doomed without me that he must let this pass.)
good-writing-000245.zh: 他知道没有我就注定要失败，所以他必须放弃这件事。

good-writing-000246.en: Or I will hand him a solid second draft to read, and he will return some time later with a marked-up copy, with notes like “The lede is weak. Consider starting with the graf near the bottom of page two.”
good-writing-000246.zh: 或者，我会给他一份完整的第二稿让他阅读。过一段时间后，他会带着一份修改过的稿子回来，其中的注释会这样写道：“引言部分不够精彩。建议从第二页底部的图表开始阅读。”

good-writing-000247.en: Or, similarly, “The ending sucks,” or at least that’s what he’s saying if you read between the lines.
good-writing-000247.zh: 或者，类似地，可以说“结局很糟糕”，或者至少，如果你能领会其中的含义的话，他确实是在这么说。

good-writing-000248.en: He’ll cross out adverbs, make suggestions for stronger verbs, and shift things around.
good-writing-000248.zh: 他会删掉一些副词，提出更合适的动词替换方案，并调整句子的结构。

good-writing-000249.en: And I do exactly the same for him.
good-writing-000249.zh: 我对他也是同样的对待。

good-writing-000250.en: So far, the marriage has survived.
good-writing-000250.zh: 到目前为止，这段婚姻仍然持续着。

good-writing-000251.en: Almost every writer needs a partner who can look at your work with fresh eyes—you are either going to be bored with your work by the second draft and need encouragement and/or advice, or, worse, think it’s just fine and quite ready to send off to your editor that moment.
good-writing-000251.zh: 几乎每个作家都需要一个能够以新眼光看待他们作品的搭档——要么在完成第二稿时就会对作品感到厌倦，需要鼓励或建议；要么，更糟糕的是，认为作品已经足够好，迫不及待地将其交给编辑。

good-writing-000252.en: But you’ll regret not taking a second look.
good-writing-000252.zh: 但如果你不仔细再看看的话，你会后悔的。

good-writing-000253.en: The words may be fine, but a first draft isn’t enough.
good-writing-000253.zh: 这些文字或许不错，但仅有一个初稿还是不够的。

good-writing-000254.en: We’re after really good, and the best each of us can do.
good-writing-000254.zh: 我们在追求真正的卓越，以及每个人所能做到的最好的表现。

good-writing-000255.en: So herewith are Neal’s best rules and advice on how to write better sentences, with my commentary, experience, and encouragement.
good-writing-000255.zh: 以下是尼尔提出的一些最佳写作规则和建议，以及我的评论、经验和鼓励。

good-writing-000256.en: I hope his tips help you as much as they’ve helped me, both to become a better writer and to keep getting a kick out of the process.
good-writing-000256.zh: 希望他的建议能对你有所帮助，就像它们帮助我一样，也能帮助你成为更优秀的作家，并让你在写作过程中持续获得乐趣。

good-writing-000258.en: Replace weak verbs, which are imprecise (“walked,” “stood”), with vivid verbs, which are specific (“trudged,” “malingered”).
good-writing-000258.zh: 把含义不够明确的平淡动词，如 walked（走）、stood（站），换成含义具体、形象鲜明的动词，如 trudged（艰难跋涉）、malingered（装病偷懒）。

good-writing-000260.en: Sometimes this rule is expressed as Write with your verbs.
good-writing-000260.zh: 有时候，这条规则被表述为“用动词来书写”。

good-writing-000261.en: Weak verbs are limp fish, sapped of energy by overuse: “Walk,” “feel,” “think,” “dine,” “talk,” “tell,” “use,” “get”—all colorless.
good-writing-000261.zh: 弱动词就像无力的鱼，因过度使用而失去了活力：“走”、“感觉”、“思考”、“用餐”、“谈话”、“讲述”、“使用”、“得到”——这些动词都缺乏色彩。

good-writing-000262.en: “It felt bad to him” doesn’t do much for the reader, nor does “He walked out of the house.”
good-writing-000262.zh: “他觉得很难过”这样的表述对读者来说并没有什么帮助，同样，“他离开了房子”这样的表述也没有起到什么作用。

good-writing-000263.en: Prosaic words, whether verbs or other parts of speech, leave readers unsteady about what is being conveyed.
good-writing-000263.zh: 那些空洞无物的词语，无论是动词还是其他词性，都会让读者难以理解其真正含义。

good-writing-000264.en: When I question my first bad attempt, more colorful actions—“His stomach churned” and “Rushing out of the house, he tripped on the last step”—magically appear.
good-writing-000264.zh: 当我回想起第一次尝试时出现的那些生动的描述时——比如“他的胃在咕咕作响”，或者“他冲出房子时，在最后一步时绊倒了”——这些描述就自然而然地出现在我的脑海中了。

good-writing-000265.en: Writing with strong, vivid verbs yields new sentence structures.
good-writing-000265.zh: 使用生动、有力的动词可以创造出新的句子结构。

good-writing-000266.en: It’s not just bland to say, “He walked out of the house.”
good-writing-000266.zh: 说“他离开了房子”这种话，实在太乏味了。

good-writing-000267.en: It also doesn’t lead anywhere much.
good-writing-000267.zh: 这也并没有带来什么实质性的进展。

good-writing-000268.en: But once I’ve got him “rushing,” I imagine a consequence, the foot tripping on the last step, which gives me the puzzle of how to manage two verbs in one sentence.
good-writing-000268.zh: 但是一旦我让他“冲了出去”，我就会想到一个后果——他的脚会在最后一步时踩到什么东西，这就让我陷入了一个难题：如何在一个句子中同时使用两个动词呢？

good-writing-000269.en: A more complicated but eminently readable sentence structure emerges.
good-writing-000269.zh: 于是，出现了一种更为复杂但非常易于理解的句子结构。

good-writing-000270.en: As I question my lackluster wordings and try new things out, my sentences mix up; some reel out longer while others sit boldly simple.
good-writing-000270.zh: 当我质疑自己那些平淡无力的文字表达方式，并尝试新的写作方式时，我的句子结构会变得混乱；有些句子变得冗长，而另一些则保持简洁明了的风格。

good-writing-000271.en: The reader won’t be lulled into a soporific monotony of one subject-verb-object sentence after another.
good-writing-000271.zh: 读者不会陷入一种单调乏味的、由主语-谓语-宾语构成的句子模式中。

good-writing-000272.en: The more specific the verb, the less likely you’ll need an adverb.
good-writing-000272.zh: 动词越具体，就越不太可能需要使用副词来修饰它。

good-writing-000273.zh: “Raced”并不需要“快速”地完成。而“Meandered”则不需要“漫无目的地”进行。

good-writing-000274.en: By the way, don’t confuse this rule with the unrelated grammatical distinction between “strong” (irregular) and “weak” (regular) verbs.
good-writing-000274.zh: 顺便提一下，不要将这条规则与“强动词”（不规则动词）和“弱动词”（规则动词）之间的语法区别混淆起来。

good-writing-000275.en: Like any rule, you can take Use strong verbs too far.
good-writing-000275.zh: 像任何规则一样，使用“强动词”这个手法也可能过于夸张了。

good-writing-000276.en: By avoiding the obvious verb “won,” sportswriters imbue the victorious high school team with the courage and skill of Roman gladiators: The opponents typically have been slaughtered, massacred, blasted, blitzed, blown away, clobbered, thrashed, blanked, thumped, walloped, whomped, whipped, flattened, shellacked, crushed, hammered, shafted, or vanquished.
good-writing-000276.zh: 通过避免使用“赢得”这一明显的动词，体育记者将那支获胜的高中球队描绘成具有罗马角斗士般勇猛与技巧的队伍：那些对手通常已经被屠杀、惨败、击败或彻底击败。

good-writing-000280.en: A strong verb in a sentence instantly improves your writing.
good-writing-000280.zh: 在句子中使用有力的动词能够立刻提升你的写作水平。

good-writing-000281.en: If no word springs to mind to vividly describe the action in your sentence, use your online thesaurus.
good-writing-000281.zh: 如果无法想出任何词语来生动描述句子中的动作，可以使用在线词典来辅助思考。

good-writing-000282.en: Don’t use “run” when you can use “sprint,” “race,” or “scurry.”
good-writing-000282.zh: 当可以使用“sprint”、“race”或“scurry”这些词时，不要使用“run”。

good-writing-000283.en: A verb describes what the subject of your sentence is doing: “The dog ate our Thanksgiving turkey.” (This really happened ten years ago.) But Bodhi did not “eat” the turkey.
good-writing-000283.zh: 动词描述了句子的主语正在做什么：“那只狗吃掉了我们的感恩节火鸡。”（实际上这件事发生在十年前。）但是，博迪并没有“吃掉”那只火鸡。

good-writing-000284.en: He devoured, gobbled, wolfed down, and inhaled our Thanksgiving turkey.
good-writing-000284.zh: 他狼吞虎咽地吃下了我们的感恩节火鸡。

good-writing-000286.en: “His grandfather sat on the porch, carving a figure out of a thick twig.”
good-writing-000286.zh: “他的祖父坐在门廊上，用粗树枝雕刻着一个小雕像。”

good-writing-000287.en: OK, close your eyes and look at the screen on the backs of your eyelids.
good-writing-000287.zh: 好的，闭上眼睛，看着位于眼睑背面的屏幕。

good-writing-000288.en: You see the old man—the noun—and what he is doing—the verb: carving something, holding it in one hand, slicing off thin layers of wood into a shape he has in his mind, to be revealed.
good-writing-000288.zh: 你看到那个老人——名词，以及他正在做的事情——动词：雕刻某物，用一只手握住它，将薄薄的木片切割成他心中所想的形状，然后将其呈现出来。

good-writing-000289.en: But what if your sentence read “His grandfather slouched on the porch, whittling”?
good-writing-000289.zh: 但是，如果你的判决结果是“他的祖父坐在门廊上，一边削木头呢？”

good-writing-000290.en: Or “We tried to handle a week without Internet” could be “We hunkered down for a week without Internet.” “Hunker” is a great verb.
good-writing-000290.zh: 或者“我们努力度过了一个没有互联网的一周”可以表达为“我们坚持了一周，没有使用互联网”。这里的“hunker”确实是一个很棒的动词。

good-writing-000291.en: Try to use it more often.

good-writing-000292.en: “The gorilla lowered her body to the ground” could also be “The gorilla hunkered down.”
good-writing-000292.zh: “大猩猩将身体伏在地面上”也可以理解为“大猩猩蜷缩着身体”。

good-writing-000293.en: Here’s another one: “She could not stop thinking about eating an entire chocolate cake.”
good-writing-000293.zh: 还有这样一个例子：“她不停地想着如何吃掉一整块巧克力蛋糕。”

good-writing-000294.zh: 那“她渴望吃巧克力蛋糕”这句话呢？

good-writing-000295.en: “Crave” is a great verb because it is so precise, so psycho-visual.
good-writing-000295.zh: “渴望”是一个非常恰当的动词，因为它非常精准，而且具有强烈的视觉冲击力。

good-writing-000296.en: You know that exact feeling when you’ve been in that state, longing for and obsessed with eating your body weight in cake, and then doing that—gobbling or devouring or wolfing it down.
good-writing-000296.zh: 当你处于这种状态时，你会有一种特别的感觉——渴望并痴迷于吃掉相当于自己体重的蛋糕，然后大口地吃下那些蛋糕。

good-writing-000297.en: Cake is to me as turkey is to Bodhi.
good-writing-000297.zh: 对我来说，蛋糕就像火鸡对博迪而言那样重要。

good-writing-000298.en: Or “She went out to the garden and got a lot of vegetables for the meal she was cooking that night.”
good-writing-000298.zh: 或者“她去了花园里，为当晚的晚餐准备了很多蔬菜。”

good-writing-000299.en: Why not “She gathered vegetables for dinner”?
good-writing-000299.zh: 为什么不用“她为晚餐采摘了蔬菜”这样的表达呢？

good-writing-000300.en: “Gathered” rings with its suggestion of arms embracing lovely things—vegetables, flowers, little kids.
good-writing-000300.zh: “Gathered”系列戒指，象征着双手捧持美好事物——蔬菜、花朵、孩子们。

good-writing-000301.zh: “懒散地坐著”、“啃咬”、“蜷缩着身体”、“渴望”、“聚集”——这些动词表达得非常精准且富有表现力。

good-writing-000302.en: The reader immediately sees and understands the action you are describing—which could also be “The reader gets it.”
good-writing-000302.zh: 读者能够立即理解你所描述的情景——这种理解也可以称为“读者能够明白”。

good-writing-000304.en: The verbs “to be” and “to have” are the weakest of all; by nature static, they slow a narrative.
good-writing-000304.zh: “to be（是）”和“to have（有）”是最无力的两个动词；它们本质上表达静态状态，会拖慢叙述的步伐。

good-writing-000305.en: “To be” and “to have” aren’t just overused; they’re barely verbs.
good-writing-000305.zh: “是”和“有”这些词不仅被过度使用了，它们甚至几乎算不上是真正的动词。

good-writing-000306.en: They suspend the sentence in an inert universe.
good-writing-000306.zh: 他们在一个无生命的宇宙中暂停了刑罚的执行。

good-writing-000308.en: Whatever fills in the blank is fixed in place and time, frozen.
good-writing-000308.zh: 无论填充空白的内容是什么，它都是固定不变的，处于静止状态，无法改变。

good-writing-000309.en: “I am tired.” “I am happy.” “I am a teacher.” “I am a jerk.”
good-writing-000309.zh: “我很累。” “我很开心。” “我是一名老师。” “我是个混蛋。”

good-writing-000310.en: The object of such a sentence characterizes you, or identifies you, or describes you.
good-writing-000310.zh: 这样的句子所描述的对象，就是你本人，或者是指明你是谁，或者是在描述你。

good-writing-000311.en: Most verbs move me along; “to be” keeps me in place.
good-writing-000311.zh: 大多数动词都会推动我前进；“存在”则让我停留在原地。

good-writing-000312.en: Any forward motion that the reader has been chasing slows to a full stop.
good-writing-000312.zh: 读者一直追求的任何前进的势头都突然停止了。

good-writing-000313.en: English reflects the odd behavior of “to be” by declaring that sometimes the nouns on either side of it can both be nominative, which means that they don’t quite separate into subject and object.
good-writing-000313.zh: 英语中“to be”这个词的用法很特殊，它表明有时其前后的名词都可以处于主格形式，这意味着它们并不严格区分主语和宾语的界限。

good-writing-000314.en: It’s called the predicate nominative, which you don’t need to remember.
good-writing-000314.zh: 它被称为谓语主语，不需要记住这个术语。

good-writing-000317.en: The sentence describes an equivalence rather than an action.
good-writing-000317.zh: 该句子描述的是一种等价关系，而非一种具体的动作。

good-writing-000318.en: Other languages reflect the outlying position of “to be” by ignoring it.
good-writing-000318.zh: 其他语言则通过忽略“存在”这一概念来反映“存在”的遥远性。

good-writing-000319.en: In Sanskrit, if two nominative nouns appear without a verb, then “to be” is assumed.
good-writing-000319.zh: 在梵语中，如果有两个宾格名词出现而没有任何动词与之搭配，那么就会假定存在“存在”这一概念。

good-writing-000320.en: You don’t have to bother to write it down to complete a Sanskrit sentence.
good-writing-000320.zh: 完成一个梵文句子时，不必特意将其写下来。

good-writing-000321.en: This emphasizes how the idea of “being” lacks the typical propulsive energy of a verb.
good-writing-000321.zh: 这凸显了“存在”这一概念缺乏动词所具有的那种推动性力量。

good-writing-000322.en: Likewise “to have” does not describe an activity, but an acquisition that took place before the sentence began.
good-writing-000322.zh: 同样，“to have”这个动词并不描述一项活动，而是指发生在句子开始之前的一种状态或获得。

good-writing-000323.en: “I have three dollars.” “I have a sister.” “I have a basket full of trouble.” “I have” means that I already acquired the thing that I am naming.
good-writing-000323.zh: “我有三美元。” “我有一个妹妹。” “我有一篮子麻烦事。” “我拥有”意味着我已经获得了我所要拥有的东西。

good-writing-000324.en: The thing is a possession, which is a little like an identity.
good-writing-000324.zh: 那东西是一种“占有物”，有点像一种身份的象征。

good-writing-000325.en: If I think I own something, then I have stopped it in time as if it is neither in development nor in decay.
good-writing-000325.zh: 如果我认为某样东西属于我，那么我就会及时将其保存起来，就好像它既没有在发育中，也没有在退化一样。

good-writing-000326.en: Both of us—the reader and the object—are immobilized by the sentence.
good-writing-000326.zh: 我们两个人——读者和作品——都被这个句子所束缚，无法动弹。

good-writing-000327.en: Two exceptions to the questioning of “to be” and “to have” are common.
good-writing-000327.zh: 对“是”和“有”的质疑有两个常见的例外情况。

good-writing-000328.en: One, they can be useful helper, or auxiliary, words, especially in constructing passive sentences.
good-writing-000328.zh: 首先，它们可以作为有用的辅助词，尤其是在构建被动句时。

good-writing-000329.en: While “I was running to the store” might be replaced by “I ran to the store,” you probably wouldn’t want to turn “I am running for president” into “I run for president.”
good-writing-000329.zh: 虽然“我正在跑向商店”这句话可以被替换为“我跑向了商店”，但你可能不会希望将“我正在竞选总统”这句话变成“我竞选总统”。

good-writing-000330.en: Two, they can help me sound authoritative.
good-writing-000330.zh: 其次，它们可以帮助我显得更加权威。

good-writing-000331.en: In the next paragraph, I use a declarative sentence with the verb “to be”; “Becoming is an activity; being is static.”
good-writing-000331.zh: 在下一段中，我使用了以“to be”为动词的陈述句；“成为是一种活动；存在则是静态的。”

good-writing-000332.en: If you know a little about Hinduism, then it makes sense that Sanskrit has two verbs for “to be.”
good-writing-000332.zh: 如果你对印度教有一些了解的话，那么 Sanskrit 中有两个动词来表示“是”这个意思，这是合乎逻辑的。

good-writing-000333.en: One, as, is nearly as static as the English “to be.”
good-writing-000333.zh: “One as” 几乎和英语中的“to be”一样，都是表示状态的词汇。

good-writing-000334.en: But the other, bhu, carries a liveliness that often doesn’t make it into English translations.
good-writing-000334.zh: 但另一个词，bhu，则带有一种活力，这种活力往往无法被准确地翻译出来。

good-writing-000335.en: When a form of bhu is used in the Hindu holy work the Bhagavad Gita, for instance, it implies “becoming” as well as “being.”
good-writing-000335.zh: 例如，在印度圣典《薄伽梵歌》中，当使用“bhu”这个形式时，它既意味着“成为”，也意味着“存在”。

good-writing-000336.en: Becoming is an activity; being is static.
good-writing-000336.zh: “成为”是一种活动；而“存在”则是静态的。

good-writing-000337.en: Using bhu, “I am a man” has hidden in it the notion that “I am becoming a man,” and probably “A man is becoming me,” as if identities aren’t resting places but developmental transitions.
good-writing-000337.zh: 在“bhu”这个符号的使用中，“我是一个男人”这一表述隐含了“我正在成为男人”这样的概念；或许还有“男人正在变成我”这样的表述。好像身份并不是某种固定的状态，而是发展的过程而已。

good-writing-000338.en: The language itself unfolds a distinctively non-Western notion of things in constant flux.
good-writing-000338.zh: 这种语言本身体现了一种独特的不西方式的观念，即事物处于不断变化的状态。

good-writing-000339.en: English is not so subtle in its hidden metaphysics.
good-writing-000339.zh: 英语在其隐藏的形而上学层面上的表现并不那么微妙。

good-writing-000340.zh: 我们西方人都是坚定的唯物主义者。

good-writing-000341.en: Things “are,” and what you see is what you get.
good-writing-000341.zh: 事情已经如此了，你所看到的，就是你所得到的。

good-writing-000342.en: You might ask, “What about Hamlet’s soliloquy?”
good-writing-000342.zh: 你可能会问：“那哈姆雷特的独白呢？”

good-writing-000343.en: “To be or not to be, that is the question. Whether ’tis nobler...”
good-writing-000343.zh: “存在还是不存在，这是个问题。是否这更崇高一些……”

good-writing-000344.en: The entire speech runs thirty-three lines.
good-writing-000344.zh: 整篇演讲共有三十三行文字。

good-writing-000345.en: The first fourteen lines include nine occasions of the verb “to be.”
good-writing-000345.zh: 前十四行中，有九处使用了动词“to be”。

good-writing-000346.en: Hamlet punches it out almost exclusively with one- and two-syllable words.
good-writing-000346.zh: 哈姆雷特几乎只使用单音节和双音节的词语来进行攻击。

good-writing-000347.en: Then he makes a course correction.
good-writing-000347.zh: 然后他进行了一次方向调整。

good-writing-000348.en: The final nineteen lines include one occasion of the verb “to be,” and that one an auxiliary verb (“Is sicklied o’er...”).
good-writing-000348.zh: 最后十九行中，有一个地方出现了动词“to be”，而那个动词实际上是一个助动词（“Is sicklied o’er...”）。

good-writing-000349.zh: 出现了更多的三音节单词。

good-writing-000350.en: Hamlet’s language rings with more authority, or ego, in the opening section than in the longer analysis of the situation, and that might remind the reader that a person of Hamlet’s age is caught between the chop of childhood impulse and the gather of reflective adulthood.
good-writing-000350.zh: 哈姆雷特在开篇时的语言显得更加自信或自大，而在对局势的更详细分析中则显得较为冷静。这一点可能会让读者联想到，像哈姆雷特这样年纪的人，正处于童年的冲动与成熟的理性思考之间的过渡阶段。

good-writing-000352.en: Yes, Neal is overeducated and a little woo-woo but he did not get the above distinction off a box of Celestial Seasonings tea: he got a master’s in Eastern studies and had to learn Sanskrit during the first year of Covid.
good-writing-000352.zh: 是的，尼尔虽然受过高等教育，而且有点“玄之又玄”的作风，但他并不是靠一箱《天赐季节》茶叶来获得这些荣誉的——他是在攻读东方研究硕士学位时，在新冠疫情期间才不得不学习梵语的。

good-writing-000353.en: (He did not actually “learn” Sanskrit, per se, so much as study it online with twenty other masochists at his alma mater.)
good-writing-000353.zh: 实际上，他并没有真正“学习”梵语，而是与母校里的另外二十位“自愿学习者”一起在线学习梵语。

good-writing-000354.en: What he is trying to say is that you can do better than “being” and “having.”
good-writing-000354.zh: 他想要表达的是，你可以做得比仅仅“存在”和“拥有”要好得多。

good-writing-000355.en: Question yourself each time you use either.
good-writing-000355.zh: 每次使用这两种工具时，都要自我提问一下。

good-writing-000356.en: See if you can find another verb that adds something to the sentence for us.
good-writing-000356.zh: 试着再找出一个能在句子中增添新意的动词吧。

good-writing-000357.en: “I was tired” might become “I grew tired.”
good-writing-000357.zh: “我累了”可能会变成“我感到疲惫了”。

good-writing-000358.zh: 感到疲惫是积极的表现。

good-writing-000359.en: “I was tired” is flat and, well, tired.
good-writing-000359.zh: “我累了”这种说法很平淡，而且听起来只是简单的“累了”而已。

good-writing-000360.zh: 那句话需要稍作停顿一下。

good-writing-000361.en: “I have some money” might become “I found some coins between the couch cushions,” every child through history’s main income stream.
good-writing-000361.zh: “我有一些钱”这句话，在历史上可能会被理解为“我在沙发垫子之间发现了一些硬币”。每个孩子都曾经历过这种主要的收入来源。

good-writing-000362.en: The new sentence blossoms specific and evocative.
good-writing-000362.zh: 新的句子具有明确而富有表现力的特点。

good-writing-000363.en: Or, in my case, “I took some cash from my husband’s wallet.” (We live in a community property state.)
good-writing-000363.zh: 或者，就我而言，可以说“我从我丈夫的钱包里拿了一些现金。”（我们生活在一个夫妻共同财产制的州。）

good-writing-000364.en: Or “I pocketed some money by using coupons, while people in the express lane glared.”
good-writing-000364.zh: 或者“我通过使用优惠券赚了一些钱，而排队缴费的人则一脸怒容。”

good-writing-000365.en: The great E. L. Doctorow wrote, “Good writing is supposed to evoke sensation in the reader—not the fact that it was raining, but the feeling of being rained upon.”
good-writing-000365.zh: 伟大的作家E·L·多克托罗曾写道：“优秀的写作应该能够引发读者的情感共鸣——不是单纯地描述下雨的事实，而是传达被雨淋湿的那种感觉。”

good-writing-000366.en: And as Neal said, “to be” and “to have” are static, which is OK when that is the condition of the subject.
good-writing-000366.zh: 正如尼尔所说，“存在”和“拥有”都是静态的状态，当主语处于这种状态时，这并无不妥。

good-writing-000367.en: But part of good writing is teasing readers to want more, to keep turning the pages because the story and descriptions are alive, not passive or inert.
good-writing-000367.zh: 但是，优秀的写作方式之一就是吸引读者想要继续阅读下去，因为故事和描述都是充满活力的，而不是平淡无奇的。

good-writing-000368.en: When you are finished with a section, take a break.
good-writing-000368.zh: 当你完成一个部分的工作后，请休息一下。

good-writing-000369.en: Then go through your material again to see how often you’ve settled for what Neal calls “barely verbs.”
good-writing-000369.zh: 然后再次阅读你的材料，看看你有多少次选择了尼尔所说的“勉强算得上是动词”的表达方式。

good-writing-000370.en: Pin each one to the corkboard of your mind and stare it down until an action word pops up that communicates something.
good-writing-000370.zh: 把每一个点都标记在心中的便签板上，然后注视着它们，直到找到一个能够表达某种意义的行动关键词。

good-writing-000372.en: Pay attention to words that end in -ed or -en and are preceded by a form of “to be,” and watch out for -ing endings; try flipping the sentence to get it more active.
good-writing-000372.zh: 留意前面带有某种 be 动词形式、以 -ed 或 -en 结尾的词，也要注意以 -ing 结尾的形式；试着调整句子的说法，让表达更主动、更有动感。

good-writing-000373.en: The rule of thumb is to favor an active voice over a passive voice.
good-writing-000373.zh: 一般来说，应该优先使用主动语态而非被动语态。

good-writing-000374.en: In practice, this is thornier than grammarians would tell you.
good-writing-000374.zh: 实际上，这种情况比语法学家所描述的要复杂得多。

good-writing-000375.en: They stick to a view that -ed and -en verbs (and some others) preceded by an auxiliary verb are the culprits.
good-writing-000375.zh: 他们坚持这样一种观点：即那些以助动词开头的“-ed”和“-en”形式的动词（以及其他一些动词）才是问题的根源。

good-writing-000376.en: As far as they go, this is true and worth examining.
good-writing-000376.zh: 就其本质而言，这一点是真实的，并且值得探讨。

good-writing-000377.en: Watch what happens when a passive sentence is transfigured:
good-writing-000377.zh: 看看当被动语态被改变时会发生什么：

good-writing-000380.en: They were buried by the avalanche.

good-writing-000382.en: We know by ear which sounds stronger, or more appropriate.
good-writing-000382.zh: 我们通过听觉能够判断出哪些声音更强烈或更合适。

good-writing-000383.en: Musicians are said to play by ear or by reading scores.
good-writing-000383.zh: 据说，音乐家们是通过听觉或阅读乐谱来演奏音乐的。

good-writing-000384.en: But they’re always playing by ear.

good-writing-000385.en: The discordant note, whether identified on a score or imagined as an interval in the mind, sounds the same.
good-writing-000385.zh: 那个不和谐的音符，无论是在乐谱上标出，还是在脑海中想象成一个音程，其发音都是相同的。

good-writing-000386.en: Symphony conductors don’t instruct players on the score’s notation; they conjure up scenes in the musicians’ minds—a picnic on the rocks of a windswept beach, a falling-out with a close friend—and ask the players to translate scenic emotions into melodic, harmonic, and rhythmic sounds.
good-writing-000386.zh: 交响乐的指挥家不会直接指导演奏者如何理解乐谱上的音符；他们会想象出一些场景——比如被风轻拂的海滩上的野餐，或是与挚友之间的争执——然后要求演奏者将这些场景中的情感转化为旋律、和声以及节奏上的表现。

good-writing-000389.en: But also use pointers—rules—to find fault and improve.
good-writing-000389.zh: 同时，也使用“指针”——即各种规则——来发现问题并加以改进。

good-writing-000390.en: If the passive voice is inferior, why does it exist?
good-writing-000390.zh: 如果被动语态并不优越，那为什么还要存在呢？

good-writing-000391.en: Sometimes the passive voice is superior, and must be kept.
good-writing-000391.zh: 有时候，使用被动语态更为合适，应该坚持使用这种形式。

good-writing-000392.en: Let’s take our first example above.
good-writing-000392.zh: 让我们以上面提到的第一个例子为例。

good-writing-000393.en: If the context is a detective untying Catherine, he might ask, “Who did this to you?”
good-writing-000393.zh: 如果上下文是一个侦探正在为凯瑟琳解开绳子，那么他可能会问：“是谁这么对你？”

good-writing-000394.en: Catherine might answer, “I was brought here by Jules, but I was handcuffed by Jim.”
good-writing-000394.zh: 凯瑟琳可能会回答：“我是朱尔斯带我来这里的，但吉姆却让我束手无策。”

good-writing-000395.en: The correct usage of the passive voice is to put a special emphasis on the object of the sentence, usually the person or noun found at the end of the sentence.
good-writing-000395.zh: 被动语态的正确用法是将句子的宾语作为重点，通常这个宾语是句子末尾出现的那个人或名词。

good-writing-000396.en: “Jules brought me here, but Jim handcuffed me” slightly deflates the word “handcuffed,” and separates Jim as possibly the more culpable.
good-writing-000396.zh: “朱尔斯带我来到了这里，但吉姆却用手铐铐住了我。”这句话中的“用手铐铐住”这一表述有所减弱，从而将吉姆视为可能更负有责任的一方。

good-writing-000397.en: Generally, “My mother watched over me” is better than “I was watched over by my mother.”
good-writing-000397.zh: 一般来说，“我的母亲守护着我”这种表达比“有母亲在守护着我”更合适。

good-writing-000398.en: But if I were distinguishing parents, and making the case that my father was neglectful, the second version might work.
good-writing-000398.zh: 但如果我需要区分父母双方的情况，并且要证明我的父亲确实疏于照顾孩子，那么第二种说法可能会更合适一些。

good-writing-000399.en: Passive: “I was silenced not by the librarian, but by the person I had a crush on.”
good-writing-000399.zh: 被动状态：“我被沉默的并不是图书管理员，而是那个我暗恋的人的原因。”

good-writing-000400.en: Active: “The librarian didn’t silence me, but the person I had a crush on did.”
good-writing-000400.zh: 活跃状态：“那个图书管理员没有让我闭嘴，但我喜欢的人却让我闭嘴了。”

good-writing-000403.en: Grammarians distinguish the passive voice from verb forms that use participles.
good-writing-000403.zh: 语法学家将被动语态与那些使用分词形式的动词形式区分开来。

good-writing-000404.en: That’s a fancy way of saying that -ing verbs are not considered passive.
good-writing-000404.zh: 用更通俗的话来说，就是“-ing动词”并不属于被动语态。

good-writing-000405.en: But often they might as well be, sounding flabby or inert.
good-writing-000405.zh: 但很多时候，这些作品听起来反而显得空洞无力，毫无活力可言。

good-writing-000406.en: The -ing ending blows up a verb, allowing it to become a noun (swimming is fun), or an adjective (I put on my swimming cap), or part of a direct action (I’m swimming in childhood photographs), or—what we’re talking about here—adding distance to the narrative, often implying a prior action the same way that the passive -ed and -en forms do.
good-writing-000406.zh: 以“-ing”结尾的动词形式可以转换为名词（游泳很有趣）、形容词（我戴上游泳帽），或者作为直接动作的一部分（我在童年照片中游泳）。或者，正如我们在这里所讨论的，这种形式还能为叙事增添距离感，通常意味着某种先前的动作，就像被动形式“-ed”和“-en”一样。

good-writing-000407.en: We previously showed how “He is running for president” can’t necessarily be replaced by “He runs for president.”
good-writing-000407.zh: 我们之前已经证明，“He is running for president”这一表达并不一定能被“He runs for president”所替代。

good-writing-000410.en: “He was running by the bank when the robbers emerged.”
good-writing-000410.zh: “当强盗出现时，他正沿着银行旁边奔跑。”

good-writing-000411.en: Hmm, wonder what those guys are doing there?
good-writing-000411.zh: 嗯，不知道那些人在那里做什么呢？

good-writing-000412.en: “He ran by the bank. Right then, the robbers emerged.”
good-writing-000412.zh: “他沿着河岸奔跑着。就在那时，那些强盗出现了。”

good-writing-000414.zh: 出现在这里实在是个错误的地方。

good-writing-000415.en: The first has a singsong tone.
good-writing-000415.zh: 第一个例子具有一种节奏感强的特点。

good-writing-000416.en: By questioning the -ing verb, which is in all other ways appropriate, I’m led into a more staccato, direct, active phrasing, which adds tension and danger.
good-writing-000416.zh: 通过质疑那些在其他情况下都显得恰当的“-ing”形式，我得以采用一种更加简洁、直接、富有动态感的表达方式，这种表达方式能够增强文本的紧张感和警示性。

good-writing-000418.en: You will note above that Neal says to be careful of verbs ending in -en, but then he forgot to mention any.
good-writing-000418.zh: 你会注意到，尼尔建议要小心那些以“-en”结尾的动词，但他忘记提及其他以“-en”结尾的动词了。

good-writing-000419.en: When I thoughtfully pointed this out to him, he coughed up one: “The soufflé was eaten by the dog” versus “The dog ate the soufflé.”
good-writing-000419.zh: 当我耐心地指出这一点时，他咳嗽了一声，说道：“那个蛋奶酥被狗吃掉了。”而不是说“是狗吃了那个蛋奶酥”。

good-writing-000420.en: I might add the backstory: “The eggs were beaten vigorously for the soufflé” versus “She beat the eggs vigorously for the soufflé.”
good-writing-000420.zh: 我可能需要补充一下背景信息：“这些鸡蛋需要被充分打散，才能用于制作蛋奶酥。”而不是“她自己动手将鸡蛋充分打散，然后用来制作蛋奶酥。”

good-writing-000421.en: These examples hardly matter—who even makes a soufflé anymore?
good-writing-000421.zh: 这些例子根本没什么意义——现在还有谁会做蛋卷蛋糕呢？

good-writing-000422.en: But the point is that when the subject of the sentence receives the action instead of performing it, the sentence is weakened by your choice...Wait, wait.
good-writing-000422.zh: 但问题在于，当句子的主语只是接收动作，而不是亲自执行这个动作时，句子的表达效果就会减弱……等等，等等。

good-writing-000423.en: “The sentence is weakened” is in the passive voice.
good-writing-000423.zh: “判决被减轻”这句话使用的是被动语态。

good-writing-000424.en: “You weaken the sentence” is better, although I do not want you to feel bad about this.
good-writing-000424.zh: “你让这个句子变得太弱了”这样的表达更好，虽然我不想让你因此感到难过。

good-writing-000425.en: Good writing is about taking each sentence and making it as strong and true as you can.
good-writing-000425.zh: 优秀的写作技巧在于，将每一个句子都打磨得既有力又真实。

good-writing-000426.en: Of course, there are many circumstances in which the passive voice works.
good-writing-000426.zh: 当然，有很多情况下可以使用被动语态。

good-writing-000427.en: It is famously useful for those attempting to avoid responsibility for tragic decisions, as in “Mistakes were made.”
good-writing-000427.zh: 对于那些试图逃避承担悲惨决策责任的人来说，这种方法非常有用，就像“错误已经发生了”这句话所表达的那样。

good-writing-000428.en: You might legitimately backload a sentence to build up the drama, to pack a bigger punch.
good-writing-000428.zh: 你完全可以合理地增加一些额外的内容来制造戏剧性效果，让整个情节更加引人注目。

good-writing-000429.en: President Franklin Roosevelt used it at the start of his “Day of Infamy” speech: “Yesterday, December 7, 1941—a date which will live in infamy—the United States of America was suddenly and deliberately attacked by naval and air forces of the Empire of Japan.”
good-writing-000429.zh: 富兰克林·罗斯福总统在《国耻日》演讲的开头用了这种写法：“昨天，1941 年 12 月 7 日——一个将永远蒙受耻辱的日子——美利坚合众国突然遭到日本帝国海军和空军的蓄意袭击。”

good-writing-000430.en: I have always found this to be an interesting and touching decision, placing the emphasis on the 2,400 citizens and personnel who died that day, rather than on the evildoers.
good-writing-000430.zh: 我一直认为这是一个有趣且感人的决定。这个决定强调的是那一天死去的2400名市民和人员的命运，而不是那些作恶者。

good-writing-000431.en: He stirs our hearts before moving on to anger and action.
good-writing-000431.zh: 它在引发我们的愤怒并促使我们采取行动之前，先唤起了我们的情感。

good-writing-000432.en: The late, great Douglas Adams begins his sequel to The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy in a perfectly used passive voice:
good-writing-000432.zh: 已故的伟人道格拉斯·亚当斯在《银河系漫游指南》的续作中，以一种极为精妙的被动语态开始他的创作：

good-writing-000433.en: The story so far: In the beginning the Universe was created.
good-writing-000433.zh: 故事至今的经过如下：在起初，宇宙被创造出来了。

good-writing-000434.en: This made a lot of people very angry and has been widely regarded as a bad move.
good-writing-000434.zh: 这一行为引起了许多人的强烈不满，被广泛认为是一个糟糕的举动。

good-writing-000435.en: That he does not say who created the universe makes this so much more mysterious and quirky.
good-writing-000435.zh: 他没有透露出是谁创造了宇宙，这一点让整个故事显得更加神秘而独特。

good-writing-000436.en: This casual thing happened—the universe was created, like so it goes.
good-writing-000436.zh: 这种偶然的事情发生了——宇宙就是这样被创造出来的，仅此而已。

good-writing-000438.en: Notice that “has been widely regarded” also is passive, which adds a distinctly wry tone.
good-writing-000438.zh: 请注意，“一直被广泛认为”这一表达也是被动语态，这给句子增添了一种独特的幽默感。

good-writing-000439.en: As Neal says above, pay attention whenever you use the passive voice, and see if your sentence might be stronger if you switch to the active.
good-writing-000439.zh: 正如尼尔在上面所说，每当你使用被动语态时，请注意这一点。试着将句子改为主动语态，看看这样是否会让句子更加简洁有力。

good-writing-000440.en: “The sentence was changed to be more muscular” versus “She changed the sentence to be more muscular, and to win dour Neal’s approval.”
good-writing-000440.zh: “判决结果被修改得更为严厉一些”，而不是“她修改了判决结果，只是为了赢得严厉的尼尔的认可”。

good-writing-000442.en: When attributing a quote, “said” is the default verb; the reader’s attention is on who said it, not how it was said.
good-writing-000442.zh: 交代一句话是谁说的时，“said（说）”是默认用词；读者关注的是谁说了这句话，而不是那个人以什么方式说。

good-writing-000444.zh: “笑了起来”、“露出了笑容”、“解释了一下”……这些描述都太过夸张了。

good-writing-000445.en: Don’t look for synonyms, and drop explanatory adverbs from attributions.
good-writing-000445.zh: 不要寻找同义词，也不要在描述中加上那些需要解释的副词。

good-writing-000446.en: This is one time to favor a weak verb.
good-writing-000446.zh: 这是一次支持弱动词的机会。

good-writing-000447.en: “Said” is enough because the quote is what’s important.
good-writing-000447.zh: 只需要“Said”这个词语就足够了，因为引用文字才是最重要的。

good-writing-000448.en: The verb accompanying the attribution—“said” or “chuckled”—is expected but not registered, like prepositions and other word- and idea-connectors.
good-writing-000448.zh: 伴随名词的动词形式——“said”或“chuckled”——是预期存在的，但不被记录下来，就像介词和其他连接词一样。

good-writing-000449.en: “Said” has a mechanical, grammatical function and isn’t intended to project a particular meaning.
good-writing-000449.zh: “Said”在语法上具有机械性功能，并不旨在表达某种特定的含义。

good-writing-000450.en: It’s a weak verb that doesn’t need to be replaced.
good-writing-000450.zh: 这是一个不够恰当的动词，不需要被替换。

good-writing-000451.en: This rule was first taught to me by newspaper editors.
good-writing-000451.zh: 这条规则最初是由报纸的编辑们教给我的。

good-writing-000452.en: If you can still find one, grab any newspaper’s front page and skim through the quotes.
good-writing-000452.zh: 如果你还能找到的话，可以随便翻开一份报纸的头版，快速浏览一下其中的引文。

good-writing-000453.en: You’ll see “said” “said” “said” “said” ad nauseum, and nary an adverb accompanying it.
good-writing-000453.zh: 你会看到“said”这个词被反复出现，而且几乎没有任何副词与之搭配使用。

good-writing-000454.en: Newspaper style prefers an unopinionated, objective tone, devoid of interpretation.
good-writing-000454.zh: 报纸风格的报道倾向于采用中立、客观的叙述方式，不附带任何解读或主观评价。

good-writing-000455.en: By reducing all attributions to “said,” the rule removes subtle bias that invades synonyms such as “claimed” (which inserts the author’s skepticism) or “argued” (which suggests a defensive stance).
good-writing-000455.zh: 通过将所有修饰词都简化为“所述”这一形式，该规则消除了那些会潜入同义词中的微妙偏见，比如“声称”（这种表达方式会带有作者的怀疑态度）或“争论”（这种表达方式则暗示了防御性立场）。

good-writing-000456.en: While other writing may allow interpretation and bias, the rule is still handy as a default.
good-writing-000456.zh: 虽然其他写作方式可能会允许解释和偏见的存在，但这一规则仍然作为默认设置而存在，非常实用。

good-writing-000457.en: Notice that you’re probably adding drama with your attribution; do you want to be so overt all the time?
good-writing-000457.zh: 请注意，您在引用来源时可能会添加一些不必要的元素，是否真的需要一直如此明显地展示这些元素呢？

good-writing-000458.en: Why not let the reader interpret the character’s statement all on their own?
good-writing-000458.zh: 为什么不让读者自己来解读角色的话语呢？

good-writing-000459.en: Maybe you can use “said” most of the time, reserving embellishments for special occasions.
good-writing-000459.zh: 也许你可以大部分时间都使用“said”这个词语，而只在特殊场合才使用那些夸张的表达方式。

good-writing-000461.en: Many verbs to replace “said” sound like the efforts of a person whose first language was not English.
good-writing-000461.zh: 许多动词在翻译时，其发音方式听起来都像那些母语不是英语的人所付出的努力。

good-writing-000462.zh: “笑了出来”是最糟糕的表现了。

good-writing-000463.en: Never, ever use “chuckled” in place of “said.”

good-writing-000464.en: But I challenged Neal on this rule, as there are a number of synonyms I am fine with: “stated,” “announced,” “remarked,” “observed.”
good-writing-000464.zh: 但我对尼尔的这一规则提出了质疑，因为有很多同义词是可以接受的，比如“stated”、“announced”、“remarked”和“observed”。

good-writing-000465.en: He responded by calling me a Philistine.

good-writing-000466.zh: 从那以后，我们就再也没有说过话了。

good-writing-000467.en: But isn’t “responded” the appropriate verb here?
good-writing-000467.zh: 但是，在这里使用“被回应”这个动词不是更合适吗？

good-writing-000468.en: And “whispered” is a great verb, meaning the character is avoiding being overheard, and much better than “said quietly.”
good-writing-000468.zh: 而“低声说道”这个动词非常合适，它意味着角色在避免被他人听到，这个表达方式比“轻声说出”要好得多。

good-writing-000469.en: “Mumbled” contains both “said” and the adverb “indistinctly” in a nice package, but if you use the latter, you have to worry that Neal will go off on one of his tirades about the use of adverbs.
good-writing-000469.zh: “Mumbled”这个词组包含了“said”和副词“indistinctly”，这些词组合在一起使用时效果不错。不过，如果你使用后者这个副词的话，就需要注意尼尔可能会继续滔滔不绝地谈论关于副词使用的各种问题了。

good-writing-000470.en: I would risk it: “Mumbled” tells us in seven letters that the listener may not have caught what the speaker was saying.
good-writing-000470.zh: 我愿意冒险一试：“Mumbled”这七个字母的信息表明，听众可能并没有听清说话者所说的内容。

good-writing-000471.en: The main thing about a long patch of dialogue, which I don’t mind in the right hands, is that you cannot keep saying “he said,” “she said,” or “they said,” because it begins to sound staccato, but by the same token, you can’t substitute a desperate synonym, like “asserted,” “avowed,” or “contended.”
good-writing-000471.zh: 在一段较长的对话中，如果你处理得当的话，这并没有什么问题。不过，你不能使用“他说”、“她说”或“他们说”这样的表达方式，因为这样的表达会显得过于生硬、缺乏连贯性。同样地，你也不能使用“断言”、“宣称”或“争辩”这样的替代词。

good-writing-000472.en: At the reader’s end, we need to know who is speaking at each point in the conversation.
good-writing-000472.zh: 在读者的端，我们需要能够知道在对话的每一部分中，是谁在发言。

good-writing-000473.en: At your end, you need to present dialogue in such a way as to not annoy Neal.
good-writing-000473.zh: 在您的职责范围内，您需要以不会惹恼尼尔的方式来安排对话。

good-writing-000475.en: Let others be erudite; your job is to befriend your reader.
good-writing-000475.zh: 让别人去卖弄博学吧；你的任务是与读者交朋友。

good-writing-000476.en: As muckraker Jessica Mitford famously instructed, murder your darlings.
good-writing-000476.zh: 正如恶毒的记者杰西卡·米特福德所教导的那样，要毁掉那些你钟爱的人。

good-writing-000477.en: (The pedants will point out that she was quoting a now-obscure lecturer and writer from the early twentieth century named Arthur Quiller-Couch.)
good-writing-000477.zh: (那些自以为是的人会指出，她引用的是20世纪初一位现已不为人知的讲师和作家——亚瑟·奎勒-科奇的言论。)

good-writing-000478.en: Your darlings—your carefully crafted cleverness and erudition—run the danger of cracking your book’s seamless world if it’s fiction, and being relegated to the style-over-substance bin in nonfiction.
good-writing-000478.zh: 你们那些令人喜爱的作品——你们精心构建的巧妙构思和渊博学识——如果属于小说领域，就会破坏作品那无缝衔接的世界观；如果属于非小说类作品，则可能会被归入“风格重于内容”的类别中。

good-writing-000480.en: They’ve read too many books, seen too many TV shows, where someone did or said something clever but so out of character that it ruined the experience.
good-writing-000480.zh: 他们读过的书太多了，看过的电视节目也太多了。在这些节目中，总有一些人做出或说出一些很聪明的举动，但这些举动总是与他们的性格不符，结果让整个节目体验都变得糟糕。

good-writing-000481.en: Show-off authors are as repugnant as show-off classmates in grammar school.
good-writing-000481.zh: 那些爱炫耀的作家和小学时那些爱卖弄的同学一样令人厌恶。

good-writing-000482.en: In a third-person novel or a nonfiction work, the hidden narrator/author has to retain a consistent voice and thought pattern.
good-writing-000482.zh: 在第三人称小说或非虚构作品中，隐藏的叙述者/作者必须保持一致的语调和思维模式。

good-writing-000483.en: If your narrator has a propensity to riff philosophically, those meanderings deserve human believability.
good-writing-000483.zh: 如果叙述者有喜欢哲学性论述的倾向，那么这些离题的描写就值得让人相信了。

good-writing-000484.en: A roughneck narrator isn’t likely to spout a perfectly formed description of a caterpillar becoming a butterfly.
good-writing-000484.zh: 一个粗俗的讲述者，不太可能能够精确地描述一只毛毛虫如何变成蝴蝶的过程。

good-writing-000485.en: Save that lovely metaphor for your next book, and a dreamy, clichéd character who can use it.
good-writing-000485.zh: 把那个绝妙的比喻留到你的下一本书里吧。另外，也设计一个梦幻般的、充满陈词滥调的角色，让他能够使用那个比喻吧。

good-writing-000486.en: The French essayist Blaise Pascal was brutal: “Everything that is written merely to please the author is worthless.”
good-writing-000486.zh: 法国散文家布莱兹·帕斯卡尔曾说过这样一句话：“所有为了取悦作者而写出来的作品都是毫无价值的。”

good-writing-000487.en: No gimmicks, said the great short story writer Raymond Carver.
good-writing-000487.zh: 没有噱头，伟大的短篇故事作家雷蒙德·卡弗如是说。

good-writing-000488.en: Don’t shortcut your responsibility to describe a character’s psyche by introducing a dream that coincidentally addresses his driving fear.
good-writing-000488.zh: 不要通过引入一个与角色核心恐惧相一致的梦境来简略地描述这个角色的心理活动。

good-writing-000489.en: Minor characters who are fortune tellers, shrinks, older brothers, or ex-girlfriends often serve the same contrived purpose.
good-writing-000489.zh: 那些担任占卜师、牙医、哥哥或前女友角色的小人物，通常也只具有同样的造作目的而已。

good-writing-000490.en: Don’t have him live in the basement of the Empire State Building unless it’s a novel about living in the basement of the Empire State Building.
good-writing-000490.zh: 不要让他住在帝国大厦的地下室里，除非那是一部关于在帝国大厦地下室中生活的小说的情节。

good-writing-000491.en: Don’t have her swim in the ocean and suddenly hear a dolphin speaking cetacean to her unless you’re writing about Atlantis.
good-writing-000491.zh: 不要让她在海洋中游泳，也不要突然让她听到海豚用海豚语与她交谈，除非你写的是关于亚特兰大的故事。

good-writing-000492.en: Assume seamlessness and then protect it.
good-writing-000492.zh: 保持流畅性，然后加以保护。

good-writing-000493.en: Get rid of anything that stands out or exists only because it shows everyone how good you are with words.
good-writing-000493.zh: 摒弃那些只会显得自己多么擅长用文字表达自己的人或事物。

good-writing-000494.en: A very high percentage of people who read books seem to value being right about things.
good-writing-000494.zh: 大多数阅读书籍的人似乎都重视在事情上保持正确的判断。

good-writing-000495.en: That creates a problem: Do I aim my nonfiction treatise at an erudite audience that is by default skeptical or at the common person who doesn’t need proof?
good-writing-000495.zh: 这就会带来一个问题：我应该将我的非虚构作品定位在那些原本就持怀疑态度的学者群体，还是那些不需要证据就能理解内容的普通读者身上呢？

good-writing-000497.en: Your subject matter will sometimes answer that.
good-writing-000497.zh: 你的主题内容有时能够回答这个问题。

good-writing-000498.en: If it’s a technical manual, then it’s a narrow audience.
good-writing-000498.zh: 如果这是一本技术手册的话，那么它的目标读者就非常有限。

good-writing-000499.en: If it’s a textbook on an arcane subject, likewise.
good-writing-000499.zh: 如果是关于某个深奥主题的教科书的话，也是如此。

good-writing-000500.en: But even for those, it might be a good idea to try to satisfy the erudite using the logic and language of the great middle.
good-writing-000500.zh: 但即便对于这些人来说，尝试用伟大中产阶级的逻辑和语言来满足他们的求知欲，或许也是个不错的主意。

good-writing-000501.en: As a newspaper reporter in the mid-eighties, I developed an expertise in AIDS and women.
good-writing-000501.zh: 在80年代中期，作为一名报纸记者，我逐渐积累了关于艾滋病和女性的专业知识。

good-writing-000502.en: After HIV first rampaged through the gay men’s community, it found its way into female sex workers through bisexual men and addicts sharing needles.
good-writing-000502.zh: 在HIV最初在男同性恋者中传播之后，这种病毒又通过双性恋者和吸毒者共用针头的方式传播到了女性性工作者中。

good-writing-000503.en: The women who were dying from AIDS lived on the margins of society, mostly out of sight, and so weren’t heard from much.
good-writing-000503.zh: 那些因艾滋病而生命垂危的女性，生活在社会的边缘，大多数时候都无人知晓他们的存在，因此他们的消息也很少被报道。

good-writing-000504.en: As I’ve mentioned, I wrote for a suburban paper in a well-heeled, highly educated suburb of New York.
good-writing-000504.zh: 正如我之前提到的，我曾在纽约一个富裕且教育水平较高的郊区的一家报纸上工作。

good-writing-000505.en: My readers were accepting of a sixth-grade vocabulary, mostly, but they also seemed to appreciate it when an article resorted to words like “epidemiology” or “vascular” or, by then, references to “Kaposi’s sarcoma” or “longitudinal metrics.”
good-writing-000505.zh: 我的读者们大多能够理解六年级学生的词汇水平，不过他们似乎也喜欢那些使用诸如“流行病学”或“血管学”等词汇的文章，或者那些提到“卡波西肉瘤”或“纵向测量指标”的文章。

good-writing-000506.en: The subject matter was still fresh when I left the newspaper and freelanced for a supermarket tabloid that catered to women’s issues, and a less-educated audience.
good-writing-000506.zh: 当我离开那家报纸，开始为一家以女性问题为主题的超市小报工作的时候，那些新闻内容仍然历历在目。当时，我服务的对象是一群受教育程度较低的读者。

good-writing-000507.en: I reinterviewed my old AIDS sources and produced a longish piece on HIV’s spread into vulnerable women, keeping it to a sixth-grade vocabulary and simpler sentence structures.
good-writing-000507.zh: 我重新采访了那些曾经为我提供信息的人，并撰写了一篇关于艾滋病如何传播给弱势女性的文章。文章的语言简洁明了，使用的词汇也停留在六年级学生的水平。

good-writing-000509.en: I got everything across that I had before, without any big words or catering to the college-educated, and this time to an audience who first learned about AIDS and women from me.
good-writing-000509.zh: 我仍然能够传达出之前所表达的所有信息，而不需要使用任何华丽的辞藻或迎合那些受过大学教育的人群。而这一次，我面对的是一群刚刚开始了解艾滋病和女性问题的观众。

good-writing-000511.en: The first review of my career was a hit job by Publishers Weekly that arrived in the mail from my agent.
good-writing-000511.zh: 关于我的职业生涯的第一篇评论，是《出版人周刊》杂志发表的一篇好评文章，该文章通过我的代理人寄给了我。

good-writing-000512.en: It was for my novel Hard Laughter, which followed my father’s brain cancer and our family’s response.
good-writing-000512.zh: 这是为我的小说《坚硬的笑声》而写的，这部小说讲述了我父亲患脑癌以及我们全家如何应对这一挑战的故事。

good-writing-000513.en: Some of the book read deep and sad, while some of it was funny in a gallows-humor way.
good-writing-000513.zh: 有些章节读起来令人感到深深的悲伤，而有些章节则带有一种幽默的讽刺意味，读起来还挺有趣的。

good-writing-000514.en: The review said that its meager charms were outweighed by my frequent “show-offy overkill.”
good-writing-000514.zh: 评论中提到，尽管这款产品的魅力并不突出，但其频繁出现的“夸张表演”风格反而盖过了这些优点。

good-writing-000515.en: Luckily, I was still drinking at the time.
good-writing-000515.zh: 幸运的是，当时我还在喝酒。

good-writing-000516.en: Of course this was devastating to my self-esteem, but you know what?
good-writing-000516.zh: 当然，这对我的自尊心打击很大，但你知道吗？

good-writing-000517.en: It guided me through the next nineteen books.
good-writing-000517.zh: 它引导我阅读了接下来的十九本书籍。

good-writing-000518.en: That phrase, “show-offy overkill,” has rung through the chambers of my mind ever since, and on the last draft of everything I write, I go through and cut any flagrant efforts on my part to sound more erudite and charming than I actually am, as well as my more forced efforts to use irony or witticisms to leaven tough emotional moments.
good-writing-000518.zh: “过度炫耀”这个表达从那时起就一直萦绕在我的脑海中。在每次写作时，我都会仔细剔除那些试图让我显得更博学、更迷人的矫揉造作的做法，同时也会避免那些为了表达复杂情感而刻意使用的讽刺或机智手法。

good-writing-000519.en: You have to push back your sleeves and get tough with yourself here.
good-writing-000519.zh: 在这里，你必须坚定立场，对自己保持严格的要求。

good-writing-000520.en: It may hurt you to cut any lines, especially the ones that thrill you, but it will hurt even more when a reviewer beats you up for being a show-off.
good-writing-000520.zh: 剪断这些线条可能会让你感到疼痛，尤其是那些让你感到兴奋的线条。但更糟糕的是，如果某个评论者因为你的炫耀行为而批评你，那只会让情况变得更糟。

good-writing-000521.en: If I notice early on that you are a brain and are trying to prove this to the rest of us, I am probably not going to read much further.
good-writing-000521.zh: 如果我早就能注意到你是一个“脑残者”，并且试图向我们其他人证明这一点，那我可能就不会继续阅读下去了。

good-writing-000522.en: If your book gets published and all sorts of overeducated types are talking about it with excitement, and I end up with a copy, I will leave it around so that guests will think I am brainy.
good-writing-000522.zh: 如果你的书出版了，而那些自认为受过良好教育的人都会兴奋地谈论这本书。如果我也有一本这样的书，我会把它放在某个地方，这样客人就会认为我很聪明。

good-writing-000523.en: I will pick up enough from these conversations, plus a few major reviews, to pretend that I read and enjoyed it.
good-writing-000523.zh: 我会从这些讨论中收集一些信息，再加上一些重要的评论，以此来假装自己确实阅读了这些内容，并且从中获得了乐趣。

good-writing-000524.en: Then I will insist that someone who is visiting take it with them, and they will, because they will want to seem smart, too, and they will leave it out so that their own visitors will comment on it.
good-writing-000524.zh: 我会坚持要求那些来访的客人也带上这些东西，因为他们也想显得自己很聪明，所以他们会把这些东西留下，好让自己的客人可以对此发表评论。

good-writing-000525.en: They will have gotten enough out of what I said about it to hold their own in conversation and will deposit it on one of their visitors, and then we will both be done with it and can get on with our lives, reading books that tell marvelous stories that we find entertaining and can follow.
good-writing-000525.zh: 他们从我关于这个话题的讲述中至少会获得一些信息，足以让他们在对话中保持话题的主导权。然后，我们可以将这些信息分享给他们的访客们，这样我们俩就可以继续我们的生活，阅读那些讲述着我们觉得有趣且值得关注的精彩故事的书了。

good-writing-000526.zh: 法则6：优先采用盎格鲁—撒克逊词汇

good-writing-000527.en: Favor shorter, punchier Anglo-Saxon words over fancy, abstract Latinate words.
good-writing-000527.zh: 比起华丽、抽象的拉丁语源词，优先选择更短、更有力的盎格鲁—撒克逊语源词。

good-writing-000528.en: Part of not showing off is defaulting to common language.
good-writing-000528.zh: 不炫耀的一部分，就是使用常见的语言表达方式。

good-writing-000529.en: Some words seem more physical and are usually preferable to their abstract synonyms.
good-writing-000529.zh: 有些词在感官上更直观，因此通常比它们的抽象同义词更易于理解。

good-writing-000530.en: Pick the Anglo-Saxon word over a Latinate one, when you can: “crash” over “collision,” “hurl” over “propel,” “dockhand” over “stevedore,” “smelly” or “rank” over “malodorous” or “pungent.”
good-writing-000530.zh: 当可能的话，应该选择盎格鲁-撒克逊语中的词汇而非拉丁语词汇：“crash”代替“collision”，“hurl”代替“propel”，“dockhand”代替“stevedore”，“smelly”或“rank”分别代替“malodorous”或“pungent”。

good-writing-000531.en: As readers, we prefer to come across the immediate and concrete over the learned and remote.
good-writing-000531.zh: 作为读者，我们更倾向于接触那些直接而具体的内容，而不是那些抽象或遥远难懂的内容。

good-writing-000532.en: Anglo-Saxon language is conversational, while the Latinate lexicon tends to the academic.
good-writing-000532.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊语风格的语言更适合口语交流，而拉丁语词汇则更倾向于学术性表达。

good-writing-000533.en: Which makes sense, since Latin itself derives much of its usefulness from being dead.
good-writing-000533.zh: 这很合理，因为拉丁语本身之所以能够发挥它的作用，很大程度上是因为它已经“消亡”了。

good-writing-000534.en: Without the corrupting influence of Western cultural changes, Latin has long claimed the title of lingua franca (originally a pidgin French-Italian mishmash developed by the Crusaders).
good-writing-000534.zh: 如果没有西方文化变革的侵蚀，拉丁语早就成为了一种通用语言——最初是由十字军使用的一种法语与意大利语混合而成的混合语。

good-writing-000535.en: It is the precise, incorruptible language of medicine (“gluteus maximus”), botany (“binomial nomenclature”), zoology (“homo sapiens”), science in general (“condensation”), philosophy (“a priori”), writing (“capitalization”)...you get the picture.
good-writing-000535.zh: 这是医学领域中的精确、不可篡改的语言表达方式（如“大臀肌”）;植物学领域中的表达方式（如“ Binomial Nomenclature”系统）;动物学领域中的表达方式（如“Homo Sapiens”）；而科学领域的表达方式则是“Condensation”方式;在哲学领域则表现为“A Priori”原则;在写作领域则体现为“大写字母”的使用方式……你懂我的意思吧。

good-writing-000536.en: It’s helpful in academic research and professional training to have a single-minded, seldom-changing set of words that can cross linguistic boundaries.
good-writing-000536.zh: 在学术研究和专业培训中，拥有一组单一且变化较少的词汇，这些词汇能够跨越语言障碍，是非常有用的。

good-writing-000537.en: If literal meaning were enough and logic ruled over all forms of truth, then Latinate words would delight authors and readers alike.
good-writing-000537.zh: 如果仅仅依靠字面意义来判读事物，而逻辑又能够支配所有形式的真理，那么那些使用拉丁语的词汇就会让作者和读者都感到愉悦。

good-writing-000538.zh: 但我们是三个中心构成的生物。

good-writing-000539.en: We live not only inside our minds, but also within the sensations of our bodies and the emotions of our hearts, which define their own truths.
good-writing-000539.zh: 我们不仅仅存在于自己的思维之中，还存在于身体的感觉以及心灵的情感之中。这些感觉和情感各自承载着属于自己的真实。

good-writing-000540.en: As a long-specialized language, Latin tends to omit the body and heart.
good-writing-000540.zh: 作为一种长期被专门化的语言，拉丁语倾向于省略“身体”和“心脏”这两个词。

good-writing-000541.en: Of course Latin didn’t when spoken by early Romans (“Stick it in your glutei maximi, centurion!”), but in the ensuing centuries the subtleties have been left behind as Latin accepted its role for sharing technical, practical knowledge.
good-writing-000541.zh: 当然，早期的罗马人不会这样说话（“把东西扔到你们的臀部里去吧，百夫长！”）。但在随后的几个世纪里，这种表达方式已经变得不那么讲究了，因为拉丁语已经接受了其作为传递技术知识和实用信息的工具的角色。

good-writing-000542.en: What does it mean to read and write with the body and heart as well as the mind?
good-writing-000542.zh: 用身体、心灵以及思维来阅读和写作，这意味着什么呢？

good-writing-000543.en: Words evoke sensory feelings and emotional memories.
good-writing-000543.zh: 词语能够唤起人们的感官体验和情感记忆。

good-writing-000544.en: If a car crash lived only in my intellect, I might get away with the sentence “Newtonian laws of motion proved true when John’s automobile disassembled.”
good-writing-000544.zh: 如果车祸这种事情只存在于我的想象中，那么我就可以简单地认为“牛顿的运动定律在约翰的汽车被拆解后仍然成立”。

good-writing-000545.en: Instead, I say, “John’s car was totaled,” and a picture of a heap emerges in the mind’s eye, a sinking feeling in the belly, and a sympathetic gloom in the heart.
good-writing-000545.zh: 相反，我会说：“约翰的车被毁了。”这时，脑海中就会浮现出那辆被毁车辆的画面，心中会涌起一种悲伤的感觉，脸上也会露出同情的表情。

good-writing-000546.en: Political speeches often lapse into a kind of imperial jargon that long ago fell into the scrap heap of irony.
good-writing-000546.zh: 政治演讲往往陷入一种帝国主义的术语中，这些术语早已被讽刺的幽默所取代，成为无用的废话。

good-writing-000556.en: The English language is full of brilliant Anglo-Saxon and Anglo-Saxon-ish short words that give sentences a staccato urgency and a personalness.
good-writing-000556.zh: 英语中充满了许多精妙的盎格鲁-撒克逊风格以及具有盎格鲁-撒克逊特色的短词，这些短词让句子具有一种紧迫感与个性特征。

good-writing-000557.en: They show up slangy and often slightly off-color, which excites the body and heart.
good-writing-000557.zh: 他们的表演语言粗俗，而且常常带有一些不雅的意味，但这些特点反而能激发人们的感官和心灵。

good-writing-000558.zh: “汗湿的”与“流汗的”。 “汽车”与“机动车辆”。 “无聊的”与“冗长的”。

good-writing-000559.en: Latin resonates in long drones and la-di-da singsongs, which eventually tire the reader.
good-writing-000559.zh: 拉丁语中的长音效果和拖沓的旋律，最终会让人感到疲惫不堪。

good-writing-000560.en: No matter how detailed the scenery, descriptions needn’t devolve into a technical manual.
good-writing-000560.zh: 无论场景描述多么详细，也不应该将其变成一本技术手册。

good-writing-000563.en: My favorite exception to this rule is the song written by Don George for Duke Ellington in 1948: “You’re Just an Old Antidisestablishmentarianismist.”
good-writing-000563.zh: 我最喜欢的例外情况，就是唐·乔治在1948年为杜克·埃林顿创作的那首歌：“你不过是个反对教会与政党的老顽固分子罢了。”

good-writing-000564.en: The Argentine short story writer Jorge Luis Borges pursued a different take on this rule, in part at least because his writing branches into the philosophical.
good-writing-000564.zh: 阿根廷短篇故事作家豪尔赫·路易斯·博尔赫斯对这一规则有着不同的理解，至少部分原因是他的写作风格倾向于哲学性。

good-writing-000565.en: He said that he preferred writing in English to his native Spanish.
good-writing-000565.zh: 他说，比起用他的母语西班牙语来写作，他更喜欢用英语写作。

good-writing-000567.en: Because unlike Spanish and other languages that are either Germanic or Romance, English retains both heritages, and often presents words that are more physical (Anglo-Saxon, Germanic) paired with near-synonyms that are more abstract (Latinate, Romance).
good-writing-000567.zh: 因为与西班牙语和其他属于日耳曼语或罗曼语族的语言不同，英语同时保留了这两种语言的特色。在英语中，一些源自日耳曼语或罗曼语的词汇与那些源自拉丁语或罗曼语的、更抽象的概念性词汇常常被并置使用。

good-writing-000568.en: One of the pair of words inevitably fits into a particular sentence more securely than the other.
good-writing-000568.zh: 这两个词中，有一个词在特定的句子中比其他词更合适。

good-writing-000569.en: He offers several examples—think about a sentence in which one of the pair rings truer—“regal” versus “kingly,” “fraternal” versus “brotherly,” “obscure” versus “dark,” and “spirit” versus “ghost.”
good-writing-000569.zh: 他举了几个例子——比如，选择其中一个词更能体现其真实含义的句子：“regal”与“kingly”的区别、“fraternal”与“brotherly”的区别、“obscure”与“dark”的区别，以及“spirit”与“ghost”的区别。

good-writing-000570.en: Borges liked the choices in part because he saddled up to abstractions even while the physical action galloped along.
good-writing-000570.zh: 博尔赫斯喜欢这些选择，部分原因是尽管现实中的行动仍在继续，他仍然能够专注于抽象的思考。

good-writing-000572.en: I dropped out of college at nineteen to be a writer and since then I’ve gotten old and funny.
good-writing-000572.zh: 我在19岁时就辍学了，立志成为一名作家。从那时起，我就一直以这种身份生活着——虽然年龄渐长，但依然保持着那份幽默感。

good-writing-000573.en: As a result of those two developments, I had to look up the difference between Anglo-Saxon and Latinate words.
good-writing-000573.zh: 由于这两个技术的发展，我不得不去查阅一下“盎格鲁-撒克逊语”和“拉丁语”中的词汇之间的区别。

good-writing-000574.en: Neal tried to explain above, but let me restate what he said: Anglo-Saxon words are typically short, simple, and specific, whereas Latinate words are longer and more formal.
good-writing-000574.zh: 尼尔之前已经尝试过进行解释，但让我再次重复他所说的内容：盎格鲁-撒克逊语中的词汇通常较短、简洁且具有明确的意义，而拉丁语中的词汇则更为冗长且形式更为正式。

good-writing-000575.zh: “工作”与“职业”，“结束”与“终止”，“光明”与“照明”。

good-writing-000576.en: I once came upon a useful quote from Ward Farnsworth’s book on rhetoric, Farnsworth’s Classical English Style: “For most people most of the time, attractive English isn’t the art of choosing beautiful words. It is the art of arranging humble words beautifully.”
good-writing-000576.zh: 我曾经在Ward Farnsworth的《古典英语风格》一书中发现了一句很有用的话：“对大多数人来说，优秀的英语写作并不在于选择华丽的词汇，而在于如何以优雅的方式运用简单的语言来表达思想。”

good-writing-000577.en: The fanciest words I ever used were in my first novel, Hard Laughter, when I believed all good writers periodically used esoteric, formal words that they’d probably found in a thesaurus, with many syllables and a hint of the BBC.
good-writing-000577.zh: 我使用过的最华丽的语言，都出现在我的第一本小说《Hard Laughter》中。当时，我以为所有优秀的作家都会使用那些晦涩难懂、形式化的词汇——这些词汇很可能是他们从词典中摘取出来的，而且通常都带有许多音节，还带有一些BBC电视台那种特有的风格。

good-writing-000578.en: My dad, who was a writer, read the first draft and convinced me to use humble words instead, twenty-five-cent words instead of silver-dollar words.
good-writing-000578.zh: 我的父亲是一名作家。他阅读了初稿后，说服我使用简洁明了的语言来写作，而不是使用那些冗长、华丽的词汇。
