good-writing-000579.en: But I, like every writer I’ve ever known, am a mixed grill of ego and low self-esteem, and for a long time tried to get away with silver-dollar words so you would think I was more educated than I am.
good-writing-000579.zh: 但我，就像我认识的每一个作家一样，既有着强烈的自我意识，又缺乏自信。很长一段时间里，我试图用那些看似“有教养”的言辞来掩饰自己的不足，这样人们就会认为我比实际更博学。

good-writing-000580.en: I’d use words like “hillock” that I’d found in the thesaurus, for small hill, or “presage.”
good-writing-000580.zh: 我会使用在词库中找到的词汇，比如“小山”或者“预兆”这样的词。

good-writing-000581.en: Do you even know what “presage” means?
good-writing-000581.zh: 你甚至不知道“预兆”这个词是什么意思吗？

good-writing-000582.en: Well, a few of you and my husband do, but a lot of us only sort of know what it means and have to go look it up.
good-writing-000582.zh: 嗯，有几位人和我的丈夫确实了解这一点，但大多数人只是大致知道它的含义，需要去查一下才能明白。

good-writing-000583.en: OK, it means a sign or warning of something probably bad about to happen, but if you are choosing fancy words that I have to look up, the bad thing that is going to happen is that I’ll stop reading your stuff.
good-writing-000583.zh: 好吧，那意味着某种预兆或警告，可能预示着一些糟糕的事情即将发生。不过，如果你选择使用那些我需要去查寻的、听起来很花哨的词汇来描述这些糟糕的事情，那么我就会停止阅读你的内容了。

good-writing-000584.en: Shirley Jackson said that a confused reader is an antagonistic reader.
good-writing-000584.zh: 雪莉·杰克逊说过，思维混乱的读者实际上是一种对抗性的读者。

good-writing-000585.en: Neal is right—use our wonderfully juicy, earthy, familiar Anglo-Saxon words.
good-writing-000585.zh: 尼尔说得对——使用我们那些生动有趣、易于理解的盎格鲁-撒克逊词汇吧。

good-writing-000586.en: And for the love of God, never, ever use “terminate” for “end,” or “perspicacious” for “astute” or “shrewd.”
good-writing-000586.zh: 看在上帝的份上，永远不要使用“terminate”来表示“结束”，也不要使用“perspicacious”来表示“机敏”或“聪明”。

good-writing-000587.en: This is a true story: I read the word “petrichor” on the first page of a book that I was auditioning at a bookstore.
good-writing-000587.zh: 这是一个真实的故事：我在一家书店试镜时，偶然在一本书的第一页看到了“petrichor”这个词。

good-writing-000588.en: Raise your hand if you know what it means.
good-writing-000588.zh: 如果你知道这个手势的含义，请举手。

good-writing-000590.en: It’s a beautiful word for the distinctly earthy smell when it rains on dry soil, which I discovered after I looked it up on my smartphone.
good-writing-000590.zh: 这是一个非常美妙的词，用来形容下雨时落在干燥土壤上的那种独特而浓郁的泥土气息。我在用智能手机搜索这个词时，才发现了它的含义。

good-writing-000591.en: Now, while I love that smell, and loved being reminded of this scent and the first rains in the fall, having to look it up made me feel dumb, which does not make me want to continue reading (that is, buy) the book—possibly yours.
good-writing-000591.zh: 虽然我喜欢那种气味，也喜欢被这种香气以及秋天初降的雨水所吸引的感觉，但不得不去查找相关信息，这让我觉得自己很愚蠢。这并没有让我想要继续阅读这本书——也就是说，想要购买这本书。也许这本书就是你的吧。

good-writing-000593.en: Unless you’re writing a technical manual, keep your language conversational and use modern speech patterns.
good-writing-000593.zh: 除非你在写技术手册，否则应让语言像日常交谈一样自然，并采用现代人的说话方式。

good-writing-000594.en: If it sounds literary, it isn’t.
good-writing-000594.zh: 如果这听起来像是一种文学性的表达，那其实并非如此。

good-writing-000595.en: Our age is casual, and overly formal usages—the King’s English and all that—disturb the reader the same way that stiff English translations of foreign works make some people uneasy.
good-writing-000595.zh: 在我们的时代，人们都喜欢轻松、自然的表达方式。那些过于正式的表达方式——比如“国王的英语”之类的——只会让读者感到不适。就像那些生硬的外文翻译一样，会让一些人感到不悦。

good-writing-000596.en: We like our idioms, our pop culture, and common words that share our everyday hopes and fears.
good-writing-000596.zh: 我们喜欢我们的习语、流行文化，以及那些能够表达我们日常情感与恐惧的常见词汇。

good-writing-000597.en: Formal writing may objectify the focus, but it also adds distance between the writer and the event being described.
good-writing-000597.zh: 正式的写作方式可能会使重点变得抽象化，但同时也会在作者与所描述事件之间制造出一种距离感。

good-writing-000598.en: I don’t welcome an obvious narrator, omniscient or otherwise.
good-writing-000598.zh: 我不喜欢那种显而易见的叙述者，无论是全知型叙述者还是其他类型的叙述者。

good-writing-000599.en: I prefer absorption, as if I’m being guided through a jungle, not a zoo with glass cases and bars.
good-writing-000599.zh: 我更喜欢“吸收”这种方式，仿佛自己是在丛林中前行，而不是在那些有玻璃柜和铁栅栏的动物园里。

good-writing-000600.en: Most fiction writing nowadays has a character-decided point of view.
good-writing-000600.zh: 如今，大多数小说写作都采用由角色来决定的视角进行叙述。

good-writing-000601.en: Whoever’s voice is front and center is the temporary narrator.
good-writing-000601.zh: 无论谁的声音最为突出，他/她便成为这次表演中的临时讲述者。

good-writing-000602.zh: 这种技巧要求内容的真实性。

good-writing-000603.en: The character talking or thinking or narrating has to be consistent with what you’ve learned about their physical description, background, and idiosyncrasies.
good-writing-000603.zh: 那个角色在说话、思考或叙述时，其表现必须与你所了解该角色的身体特征、背景以及个性特点相一致。

good-writing-000604.en: All that individual color can be lost in the abstraction of an externalized narration.
good-writing-000604.zh: 在一种外在的、抽象的叙述方式中，所有这些独特的色彩都可能被抹去。

good-writing-000605.en: Formal writing is so universalized that character has a hard time emerging.
good-writing-000605.zh: 正式写作已经变得如此普遍化，以至于“角色”这个概念都很难被真正体现出来。

good-writing-000606.en: Elizabethan English belongs to Shakespeare, not you or me. I was twenty-four when Laurence Olivier appeared on my TV accepting his honorary Oscar.
good-writing-000606.zh: 伊丽莎白时代的英语属于莎士比亚的时代，而不是你或我的时代。当劳伦斯·奥利维提出现在电视上接受他的荣誉奥斯卡奖时，我只有二十四岁。

good-writing-000607.en: Listen to this jaw-dropping sentence: “In the great wealth, the great firmament of your nation’s generosity, this particular choice may perhaps be found by future generations as a trifle eccentric, but the mere fact of it—the prodigal, pure, human kindness of it—must be seen as a beautiful star in that firmament which shines upon me at this moment, dazzling me a little, but filling me with warmth and the extraordinary elation, the euphoria that happens to so many of us at the first breath of the majestic glow of a new tomorrow.”
good-writing-000607.zh: 请听这个令人惊叹的句子：“在你们国家那无尽的财富与慷慨的胸怀之下，这种特殊的选择或许会被后代视为微不足道的小事。但仅仅因为它本身的存在——那种纯粹而慷慨的善意——就足以被视为那片天空中一颗美丽的星星。此刻，那颗星星照亮了我，让我有些眼花缭乱，但同时也让我充满了温暖与非凡的喜悦。这种喜悦，正是许多人在迎接新世界的曙光时所体验到的。”

good-writing-000608.en: That one sentence took up more than half of his speech.
good-writing-000608.zh: 那一句话占据了他演讲时间的一半以上。

good-writing-000609.en: Maybe you think highly of it, which is absolutely OK.
good-writing-000609.zh: 也许你对此评价很高，这完全没问题。

good-writing-000610.en: To me, it was overblown, formal, and noncolloquial, and left me judging Olivier pompous in his self-deprecation.
good-writing-000610.zh: 对我来说，这种风格显得过于夸张、拘谨，缺乏亲切感。因此，我认为奥利弗在自我贬低时显得非常自大。

good-writing-000611.en: That’s how literary-style writing can damage trust, at least for some of us.
good-writing-000611.zh: 这就是文学风格的写作可能会损害信任的原因，至少对我们中的一些人来说是这样。

good-writing-000612.en: Anyone can accidentally slip into formal, literary writing.
good-writing-000612.zh: 任何人都可能偶然陷入正式、文学性的写作风格中。

good-writing-000613.en: It looks right, seems erudite, has a certain glow, but it’s flat-out wrong.
good-writing-000613.zh: 看起来很正确，似乎很有学识，还带有某种魅力，但实际上完全错误。

good-writing-000614.en: When Annie and I read each other’s pages, the code for “You’re losing me with this flamboyance” is “Maybe a bit much?”
good-writing-000614.zh: 当安妮和我互相阅读对方的笔记时，用来表示“这种夸张的言辞真让我无法忍受”的缩写就是“也许有点过头了吧？”。

good-writing-000615.en: Stiff, formal language has its rare, carefully adopted place in contemporary writing, particularly in light comedy and historical fiction.
good-writing-000615.zh: 在当代文学中，这种严谨、正式的语言风格有其独特的应用场景，尤其是在轻喜剧和历史小说中。

good-writing-000616.en: Herman Wouk’s brilliant first novel, Aurora Dawn, set in the early days of Madison Avenue when soap operas were on radio, adopts the seventeenth-century novelist Henry Fielding’s voice throughout, even beginning each chapter with a summary like this one from chapter 7:
good-writing-000616.zh: 赫尔曼·沃克出色的首部小说《黎明之光》（Aurora Dawn）以麦迪逊大道广告业的早期岁月为背景，当时肥皂剧还在广播里播出。全书模仿 17 世纪小说家亨利·菲尔丁的叙述口吻，甚至每章都以一段概要开头，譬如第 7 章这段：

good-writing-000617.en: In which the reader has the privilege of meeting Talmadge Marquis, reigning satrap in the industrial realm of Soap, and learns more of the truly fascinating history of Aurora Dawn [a soap brand]; but which he may skip if he is only following the love story.
good-writing-000617.zh: 在书中，读者有幸结识了塔尔马吉·马奎斯——这位在肥皂行业中的权威人物。此外，读者还可以进一步了解奥罗拉· Dawn这个肥皂品牌背后的迷人历史；但如果读者只是想欣赏爱情故事的话，也可以跳过这部分内容。

good-writing-000618.en: Political speeches can get away with a little formality, particularly at the top.
good-writing-000618.zh: 政治演讲往往可以稍微简略一些地进行，尤其是在高层场合。

good-writing-000619.en: “Friends, countrymen, we meet in this solemn moment,” and so on.
good-writing-000619.zh: “朋友们、同胞们，我们在这一庄严的时刻相遇，”等等。

good-writing-000620.en: But the temptation to continue with lofty and florid patterns is usually worth resisting.
good-writing-000620.zh: 但是，继续采用那些华而不实、过于复杂的设计风格往往是一种值得抵抗的诱惑。

good-writing-000621.en: Some wag in the audience is snickering, and others are questioning your sincerity, and maybe your bow tie.
good-writing-000621.zh: 观众中的一些人在窃笑，还有些人则在质疑你的诚意，甚至还会质疑你的领带是否合适。

good-writing-000623.en: The last thing I want from a new book in my hand is for it to feel intentionally literary.
good-writing-000623.zh: 我绝不希望自己手中的新书显得过于刻意追求文学性。

good-writing-000624.en: I want to step into a world that the author has carefully crafted, where I can get lost and, thus, found.
good-writing-000624.zh: 我希望能够走进作者精心构建的这个世界，在那里我可以迷失自己，然后重新找到自我。

good-writing-000625.en: If I feel the author is trying to impress me with their literariness, I’m going to put the book back on the shelf.
good-writing-000625.zh: 如果我觉得作者试图用他们的文学风格来打动我，那我就会把这本书放回书架上去。

good-writing-000626.en: The horrible reality of being a writer is that you have to get the reader to keep turning the page.
good-writing-000626.zh: 作为一名作家，最糟糕的现实是必须让读者持续地翻动书本的页面。

good-writing-000627.en: To use the more literary term, you need to suck them in.
good-writing-000627.zh: 用更文学化的术语来说，你需要将它们“吸入”体内。

good-writing-000628.en: You do this by establishing a trustworthy voice that attracts attention.
good-writing-000628.zh: 你可以通过打造一个能够吸引注意力的、可信赖的声音来实现这一点。

good-writing-000629.en: Whether you’ve composed a novel or a biography of Lawrence Welk, the reader has picked up your book planning to accompany you for a few hundred pages, and they may recoil if your voice sounds highfalutin or snobby.
good-writing-000629.zh: 无论你是为劳伦斯·韦尔克创作了一部小说，还是为他撰写了一篇传记，读者购买你的书籍时，通常期望能连续阅读几百页的内容。因此，如果你的写作风格过于夸张或显得势利，那么读者可能会感到不适。

good-writing-000630.en: When I was coming up, a number of writers engaged in literary pyrotechnics—John Updike comes to mind, but he was uniquely gifted and I won’t hear a bad word against him (except that he had tiny, tiny problems envisioning fully realized women characters).
good-writing-000630.zh: 在我成长的过程中，有许多作家致力于文学上的创新——约翰·厄普代克就是其中之一。不过，他有着独特的天赋，因此没人会批评他（只是他在处理女性角色形象时存在一些小问题而已）。

good-writing-000631.en: Tom Robbins was flashy—not elegant like Updike, but so funny that I forgave him everything.
good-writing-000631.zh: 汤姆·罗宾斯很爱炫耀——虽然不如奥普迪克那样优雅，但他的幽默感实在让人忍俊不禁，因此我原谅了他的一切行为。

good-writing-000632.en: Barbara Kingsolver does not sound literary, nor does Mark Twain, but both are entirely committed to the sentence, and such brilliant storytellers that they create an elevated sense of flow, without sounding lofty.
good-writing-000632.zh: 芭芭拉·金斯索尔没有文学家的气质，马克·吐温也是如此。不过，他们俩都极其注重句子的精炼表达，是如此出色的讲故事者，以至于他们能够创造出一种高级的、流畅的叙事效果，而这一切都并不显得夸张或做作。

good-writing-000633.en: If I notice you trying to sound literary, I’m out of here.
good-writing-000633.zh: 如果我注意到你试图用一种“文学化”的语气来说话，我就会立刻离开这里。

good-writing-000634.en: You can have a snobby, affected character who speaks in a formal or courtly way, who comes across as either touching or a fool (or both) and that is obviously OK.
good-writing-000634.zh: 你可以塑造一个自命不凡、装模作样的人物形象，他以一种正式或优雅的方式说话，看起来要么很做作，要么显得愚蠢（或者两者皆有）。显然，这种形象也是可以接受的。

good-writing-000635.en: But using effete words and phrases so you will sound more exalted is a turnoff.
good-writing-000635.zh: 但是，使用那些陈腐的词汇和短语来显得自己更高贵一些，这种做法实在令人反感。

good-writing-000636.en: Just tell me your damn story with the best, truest sentences you can muster.
good-writing-000636.zh: 请用你能用的最简洁、最真实的语言，讲述你的故事吧。

good-writing-000638.en: Your natural voice has its own tempo, pitch, ease, and overall sound.
good-writing-000638.zh: 你自然流露的表达有自己的节奏、音高、舒展感和整体声调。

good-writing-000640.en: My first literary heroes were philosophical and moody, full of self-examination and streams of consciousness.
good-writing-000640.zh: 我的第一批文学英雄都是具有哲学思维且情绪多变的人物，他们充满自我反思的意识流。

good-writing-000641.en: How disappointed I was when my own writing voice turned out to be nothing like that, emerging light and curious mostly, conversational and often good-humored.
good-writing-000641.zh: 当我自己的写作风格与预期完全不符时，我真是感到非常失望。我的文字应该是充满灵性、充满好奇心的，应该是富有对话性的，而且通常都带有幽默感。

good-writing-000642.zh: 不过，我确实得到了补偿。

good-writing-000643.en: Soon after discovering my true voice, with its fatal lack of profundity, I realized that I never had to try so hard anymore.
good-writing-000643.zh: 在发现自己的真实声音之后不久，我意识到自己不再需要如此努力了——因为我的声音根本缺乏深度感。

good-writing-000644.en: My true voice comes out on its own.
good-writing-000644.zh: 我的真实声音会自然流露出来。

good-writing-000645.en: The trick became finding all the ways to disguise it within other people’s personalities.
good-writing-000645.zh: 这个技巧在于找到所有可以在其他人的性格特征中加以掩饰的方法。

good-writing-000646.en: Fortunately, I’m a bit of a chameleon, which might be what gives me a light voice in the first place.
good-writing-000646.zh: 幸运的是，我有点像变色龙，这可能就是让我在最初时能够保持温和声音的原因吧。

good-writing-000647.en: A writing voice is a little more complicated than a singing voice.
good-writing-000647.zh: 书写的声音比歌唱的声音要复杂一些。

good-writing-000648.en: It has its own sense of melody, harmony, and rhythm, but this voice also has coveted interests, a personality, and sentences it wants to get out.
good-writing-000648.zh: 它拥有自己的旋律感、和谐感以及节奏感，但这种声音同样具有独特的魅力、个性特征，以及它想要表达的内容。

good-writing-000649.zh: 通过练习，这种能力就会逐渐形成。

good-writing-000650.en: Your writing voice isn’t created, but discovered.
good-writing-000650.zh: 你的写作风格并非先天决定的，而是通过实践逐渐形成的。

good-writing-000651.en: When you’re in your own voice, neither imitating nor preferring another, you’re allowing yourself to riff, and edit later.
good-writing-000651.zh: 当你以自己独特的声音表达时，既不会模仿他人，也不会偏爱某种声音，这样你就可以自由地创作，之后再对作品进行编辑和整理。

good-writing-000652.en: You might wish that you had a different voice, but any other voice you adopt is immature and relatively ignorant of its place in the world, or even how to behave.
good-writing-000652.zh: 你可能希望自己能拥有不同的声音，但无论你选择什么样的声音，那都显得不够成熟，而且往往对自己在世界上的位置，甚至是如何行事，都缺乏了解。

good-writing-000653.en: Trust your voice—the nexus of all the decisions you make as a writer: topic, point of view, diction, syntax, metaphor, imagery, even formatting—and go with it.
good-writing-000653.zh: 相信你的声音——它是你作为作家所做出的所有决策的核心：主题、视角、语言运用、句法结构、比喻手法、意象选择，甚至是排版方式——都要以你的声音为准则来制定。

good-writing-000654.en: What we call a writer’s voice projects from the writer’s quirkiness.
good-writing-000654.zh: 我们所说的“作家的风格”其实源于作家的独特个性。

good-writing-000655.en: We love how each of our favorite authors thinks differently from others.
good-writing-000655.zh: 我们喜欢我们最喜欢的每一位作家都拥有独特的思考方式。

good-writing-000656.en: Each writer draws on their idiosyncratic set of fears and wishes, and we follow along appreciative of the author’s fresh set of eyes.
good-writing-000656.zh: 每位作家都以其独特的恐惧与愿望为创作灵感，我们则怀着欣赏的心态，跟随这些作家的创作之旅。

good-writing-000657.en: In fiction, the writer’s voice and quirks define the conflicts and revelations that show up in the pages.
good-writing-000657.zh: 在小说中，作者的声音和性格特点决定了故事中出现的各种冲突和秘密。

good-writing-000658.en: Most characters are a constellation of flaws, but only the flaws that a particular writer cares about.
good-writing-000658.zh: 大多数角色都带有各种缺陷，但这些缺陷只是那些特定作者所关注的那些。

good-writing-000659.en: The characters we root for are who we want to become, but only by aligning with the writer’s confidence that their own interests are universal.
good-writing-000659.zh: 我们支持的角色，其实是我们自己想要成为的那种人。但只有当我们与作者保持一致的信念时，即相信自己的利益是普遍适用的，我们才能真正实现这一目标。

good-writing-000660.en: In nonfiction, the writer’s voice is likewise partly determined by their quirky interests and partly by their overall personality.
good-writing-000660.zh: 在非虚构作品中，作者的风格同样部分取决于其独特的兴趣偏好，部分则取决于其整体性格特征。

good-writing-000661.en: Is the nonfiction writer sarcastic, breezy, grave, worried, light, heavy, curious, provocative, distant, expansive, and on and on?
good-writing-000661.zh: 这位非虚构文学作家，他的风格是讽刺的、轻松的、严肃的、忧虑的、轻盈的、沉重的、好奇的、挑衅的、疏远的、宏大的，等等。

good-writing-000662.en: Like music, writing relies on the integration of melody, rhythm, and harmony.
good-writing-000662.zh: 就像音乐一样，写作也需要将旋律、节奏与和谐感有机地结合在一起。

good-writing-000663.en: We’re adept at all three, but usually one is prominent—your default talent.
good-writing-000663.zh: 我们在这三方面都非常擅长，但通常其中某一方面的能力会更为突出——也就是你最擅长的领域。

good-writing-000664.en: Can you find your hidden Beatle?
good-writing-000664.zh: 你能找到你隐藏的披头士乐物吗？

good-writing-000665.zh: 你是保罗吗，一位纯粹的音乐家？

good-writing-000666.zh: 约翰，一个节奏感很强的音乐家？

good-writing-000668.zh: 或者林戈，那个节奏感极强的音乐家呢？

good-writing-000669.en: Melody is the bright or dark stuff, the words that sharpen into wit or aphorisms or telling detail.
good-writing-000669.zh: 旋律是明亮或暗淡的旋律，那些词语能够转化为机智的妙语或简洁的格言，或者成为引人注目的细节。

good-writing-000670.en: Metaphor is melody: It provides instant recognition, meaning, and access to truth.
good-writing-000670.zh: 隐喻就像旋律一样：它能够带来即时的认同感、意义感，并帮助人们理解真相。

good-writing-000672.en: It may have a beat, but the trick is to flow naturally without hitting the snare drum.
good-writing-000672.zh: 它可能会有节奏上的变化，但关键在于节奏要自然流畅，同时不要碰到军鼓的节奏。

good-writing-000673.en: This isn’t the 4/4 or 6/8 rhythm of meter, of iambs or dactyls.
good-writing-000673.zh: 这不是4/4或6/8的节奏，也不是抑扬格或扬抑格的节奏。

good-writing-000674.en: It’s the feel that provides lulls and punch lines and, when appropriate, staccato disruptions.
good-writing-000674.zh: 这种感觉能够带来舒缓与激昂并存的氛围，在适当的时候，还会带来突然的、令人愉悦的打断。

good-writing-000675.en: Harmony is the glue of tonality that is by nature relational and emotional: It might feel friendly in its casual, conversational way, or harsh in its threatening coldness.
good-writing-000675.zh: 和谐是调性的粘合剂，这种粘合力本质上是与人际关系和情感相关的：它可能会以一种随意、交谈式的态度呈现出来，或者以一种充满威胁性的冷漠态度呈现出来。

good-writing-000676.en: Harmony is recognized in the layers that amplify or correct each other, the complications of character or difficult logic that allow us to recognize that this story, this argument, is as garbled, clear, contradictory, and transparent as the jumble of our everyday lives.
good-writing-000676.zh: 和谐体现在各个层面之间的相互强化或修正上。那些复杂的逻辑或矛盾之处，其实只是让我们意识到，这个故事、这个论点，其实就像我们日常生活中的混乱一样，混乱而难以理解。

good-writing-000677.en: As in all things, pay closest attention to your strengths.
good-writing-000677.zh: 在一切事情中，都要特别关注自己的优势。

good-writing-000679.en: Let them spin slightly out of control.
good-writing-000679.zh: 让他们稍微失控一点吧。

good-writing-000680.en: And recognize that your so-called weaknesses aren’t.
good-writing-000680.zh: 要认识到，你所谓的“弱点”其实并不存在。

good-writing-000681.en: If you’re not a natural melodist and your metaphors won’t sing out, don’t break your spirit trying.
good-writing-000681.zh: 如果你不是天生的音乐家，你的比喻也无法被听众感知到，那么就不要尝试去尝试了。不要因为尝试而失去信心。

good-writing-000682.en: An ordinary or imperfect metaphor is worse than no metaphor, always.
good-writing-000682.zh: 普通或不完美的比喻，不如没有比喻好。这一点永远如此。

good-writing-000683.en: No one will notice that metaphors are missing if your drive or your heart are quirky enough, and I promise they are.
good-writing-000683.zh: 如果你的个性和情感足够独特，那么没人会注意到缺少了隐喻这一点。我保证，你的个性和情感确实很独特。

good-writing-000684.en: Amplify what you do naturally, and the reader will be pleased.
good-writing-000684.zh: 自然地展现你的能力，这样读者就会感到满意了。

good-writing-000685.en: The trio of melody, rhythm, and harmony correspond to the three-centered human, a concept that shows up in spiritual works, especially after the Russian mystic G. I. Gurdjieff elaborated on it in the early twentieth century.
good-writing-000685.zh: 旋律、节奏与和声这三要素，对应着以这三方面为中心的人类本质。这一概念在精神哲学著作中有所体现，尤其是在20世纪初，俄罗斯神秘主义者G·I·古尔杰夫对这一概念进行了深入阐述之后。

good-writing-000686.en: Melody is the head center, playful and curious, illuminated and spacious.
good-writing-000686.zh: Melody是一个充满活力的中心，活泼而好奇，空间感也很充足。

good-writing-000687.en: Rhythm is the body center, active and functional, dancing.
good-writing-000687.zh: 节奏是身体的核心，具有活力且富有功能性，能够带来舞蹈般的体验。

good-writing-000688.en: Harmony is the welcoming heart, corralling two or more voices, relational and loving.
good-writing-000688.zh: 和谐是一种接纳的心态，能够融合两个或更多不同的声音，是一种关系性且充满爱意的状态。

good-writing-000689.en: If you think about it, even as lyricists Paul and John kept to their archetypes.
good-writing-000689.zh: 如果你仔细想想，就连保罗和约翰这样的歌词作者，也仍然遵循着他们固有的风格。

good-writing-000690.en: Paul’s lyrics tend to be open and playful (“Silly Love Songs”), and John’s about the challenges of relating in the world (“Help!...I need somebody”).
good-writing-000690.zh: 保罗的歌词往往简洁而富有趣味性，比如《Silly Love Songs》；而约翰的歌词则涉及在现实世界中建立人际关系所带来的挑战，比如《Help!...I need somebody》。

good-writing-000691.en: It often takes years of writing practice before your true voice comes to life.
good-writing-000691.zh: 通常需要多年的写作练习，你的真实声音才能逐渐显现出来。

good-writing-000692.en: Malcolm Gladwell famously says that 10,000 hours of practice in any endeavor yields a sense of flow and mastery that has the feel of switching on cruise control.
good-writing-000692.zh: 马尔科姆·格拉德韦尔曾说过，在任何领域里，只要坚持练习1万个小时，就能达到一种流畅且熟练的状态，这种状态就像打开了巡航控制功能一样。

good-writing-000694.en: After years of dogged reporting and roughly 10,000 hours of writing and rewriting, one day I sat down to write a short story, and it wrote itself for me in forty-five minutes.
good-writing-000694.zh: 经过多年的不懈努力，以及大约1万小时的写作与修改过程之后，有一天我坐下来开始创作一个短篇故事。结果，在45分钟内，这个故事就自动完成了。

good-writing-000695.en: The story was populated with light and feathery thoughts, a natural arc, and an innocence and sincerity that bubbled out.
good-writing-000695.zh: 这个故事充满了轻盈而纤细的思绪，自然的情感发展，以及那种自然流露出的纯真与真诚。

good-writing-000696.zh: 我不要求任何荣誉或奖励。

good-writing-000697.en: My first reaction was “Crap, this doesn’t look like Faulkner at all.”
good-writing-000697.zh: 我的第一反应就是：“靠，这看起来完全不像福克纳的作品啊。”

good-writing-000698.en: But from that day on, writing has been easier.
good-writing-000698.zh: 但从那天起，写作就变得容易多了。

good-writing-000699.en: You can write just as well without having found flow and a sense of voice, but not as easily.
good-writing-000699.zh: 即使没有找到写作的节奏和独特的风格，你仍然可以写作。不过，这样做的话，写作的效率和效果都会大打折扣。

good-writing-000700.en: Learning to write is like learning chess.
good-writing-000700.zh: 学习写作就像学习下棋一样。

good-writing-000701.en: Thinking mechanically, sorting out all the possibilities two or three moves ahead, is how chess goes for a long while.
good-writing-000701.zh: 从机械性的角度来思考，梳理出两到三个步骤之后可能出现的所有可能性，这就是长期以来国际象棋的玩法。

good-writing-000702.en: But if you play enough games, and maybe study openings in a book, you might suddenly find yourself thinking four moves ahead.
good-writing-000702.zh: 但如果你玩足够的游戏，并且可能还会学习棋书中的开局策略，那么你可能会突然发现自己能够预见到未来四步的情况。

good-writing-000703.en: It isn’t that your brain has sped up and found a way to factor more computations in the same time.
good-writing-000703.zh: 并不是说你的大脑运行速度变快了，从而能够同时完成更多的计算任务。

good-writing-000704.en: It’s that you’ve switched from seeing individual moves to registering common patterns.
good-writing-000704.zh: 你从关注单个动作，转变为关注共同的模式了。

good-writing-000705.en: The patterns let you skip over a lot of fruitless possibilities.
good-writing-000705.zh: 这些模式可以让你跳过许多无用的可能性。

good-writing-000706.en: In writing sentences, that means your brain is skipping over a lot of clichés, flabby choices, boring structures, and confusing words, and is happily searching for rare and new strategies down the line.
good-writing-000706.zh: 在编写句子时，这意味着你的大脑会跳过许多陈腐的套路、乏味的选择、枯燥的结构以及令人困惑的词汇，而是积极寻找那些罕见且新颖的写作策略。

good-writing-000708.en: Neal says I’m Paul, a melodist with lots of brightness and surprises, metaphor and humor.
good-writing-000708.zh: 尼尔斯说，我是个充满魅力和惊喜的旋律家，善于运用比喻和幽默感来创作音乐。

good-writing-000709.en: But Paul is my least favorite Beatle, plus Neal and I went to see him last year at the Oakland Coliseum, and we both got Covid.
good-writing-000709.zh: 不过，保罗是我最不喜欢的披头士成员了。另外，去年我和尼尔还去奥克兰体育馆看了他的演出，结果我们都感染了新冠。

good-writing-000710.en: So I’d like to be John.
good-writing-000710.zh: 所以，我希望能成为约翰。

good-writing-000711.en: By the same token, I’d like to write like Barbara Kingsolver or Virginia Woolf.
good-writing-000711.zh: 同样地，我也希望能够以芭芭拉·金斯洛弗或弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫那样的方式写作。

good-writing-000712.en: Neal says Kingsolver is John, a rhythmic harmonist, with a dense, massive score peopled with lots of instruments, colors, and heart.
good-writing-000712.zh: 尼尔斯说，金斯索弗是一位节奏感极强的作曲家，他的作品充满了丰富的乐器演奏、色彩斑斓的旋律，以及充满情感的表达方式。

good-writing-000713.en: Woolf is George, somewhat distant but yearning, disruptive because she is a truth seeker, appalled by what she sees, capable of shouting but not interested in it.
good-writing-000713.zh: 伍尔夫是个充满矛盾、渴望却又有些疏离的人。她是个追求真相的人，对所见的一切感到震惊，虽然能够大声疾呼，但实际上并不关心这些事情。

good-writing-000715.en: If I try to write in Kingsolver’s or Woolf’s style and voice, I not only sound like a fraud, I’ve become a fraud.
good-writing-000715.zh: 如果我试图采用金斯索弗或伍尔夫的写作风格和语调，我不仅会显得很可笑，而且实际上已经变成了一个伪君子。

good-writing-000716.zh: 我的工作状况急剧恶化了。

good-writing-000717.en: When I was thirty and had published three novels, Isabel Allende’s international sensation The House of the Spirits was published in the U.S., and I started trying to emulate that rich, vivid magical realism.
good-writing-000717.zh: 当我三十岁、已经出版了三本小说的时候，伊莎贝尔·阿连德的国际畅销作品《精灵之屋》在美国出版了。从那时起，我开始尝试模仿那种丰富而生动的魔幻现实主义风格。

good-writing-000718.en: (Also, since my father had been dead for six or seven years, quite out of the public eye, I hoped to retool him as a Chilean freedom fighter.)
good-writing-000718.zh: 此外，由于我的父亲已经去世六、七年了，而且他的身份并不为公众所熟知，我希望能够把他培养成一位真正的智利自由战士。

good-writing-000719.zh: 帕尔图马地区的魔幻现实主义，对吧？

good-writing-000720.en: Crazy lights and ancient smells popping out of the toaster, along with the bagel?
good-writing-000720.zh: 疯狂的灯光，以及从烤面包机中散发出来的古老气息，再加上贝果的香气……

good-writing-000721.en: At some point, I accepted that I could write pretty well in one certain way, and I think that Neal was right that I’m a Paul.
good-writing-000721.zh: 在某个时刻，我意识到自己能够以某种特定的方式来写作。我认为尼尔说得对，我确实属于保罗那种风格的人。

good-writing-000722.en: The greater message is that we each need to find the literary abilities where we feel comfortable.
good-writing-000722.zh: 更重要的是，我们每个人都需要找到自己觉得舒适的文学表达方式。

good-writing-000724.en: Of course you can reach for the stars and try to soar as an experimentalist, but to be honest, I probably won’t want to read your work.
good-writing-000724.zh: 当然，你可以尝试以实验主义者的身份去追求更高的成就，但说实话，我可能并不想阅读你的作品。

good-writing-000725.en: So find your own truest voice and style and play it the best you can.
good-writing-000725.zh: 所以，找到你最真实的声音和风格，并尽最大努力去演绎它。

good-writing-000726.en: You’ll know if your rhythm works when you read it out loud, literally using your voice.
good-writing-000726.zh: 当你大声朗读这段文字时，如果你能感觉到自己的节奏是否准确，那就说明你的节奏控制得很好了。

good-writing-000727.en: Maybe sentences aren’t landing, or seem to dangle, or come to an awkward end.
good-writing-000727.zh: 也许这些句子并不通顺，或者显得有些拖沓，或者以一种尴尬的方式结束。

good-writing-000728.en: Even worse, it sounds like you’re just running a lot of words together and there’s no real shape to the sentence.
good-writing-000728.zh: 更糟糕的是，听起来你只是把很多单词堆在一起使用，整个句子并没有什么逻辑性可言。

good-writing-000729.en: The paragraph is losing speed or energy.
good-writing-000729.zh: 这段文字的节奏正在变慢，或者失去原有的活力。

good-writing-000730.en: If needed, you can fool around with the rhythm by putting the stress on other syllables.
good-writing-000730.zh: 如果需要的话，你可以通过改变重音的位置来调整节奏的韵律。

good-writing-000731.zh: 停顿与间歇也是节奏的一部分。

good-writing-000732.en: Harmony is you filling out the picture if it is too thin.
good-writing-000732.zh: 和谐意味着，如果画面过于单薄，你需要补充一些元素来使其更加完整。

good-writing-000733.en: Do you need to mix in some local color?
good-writing-000733.zh: 您需要加入一些当地特色的元素吗？

good-writing-000734.zh: 你能添加一些对位声部吗？

good-writing-000735.en: This might include minor plots or multiple storylines, where one is about psychology, one about plot and detection; the first might be darker, the second lighter.
good-writing-000735.zh: 这可能包括一些次要情节或多个不同的故事线。其中一部分故事涉及心理学，另一部分则涉及情节与侦破过程；前者可能更为黑暗，而后者则较为轻松。

good-writing-000736.en: Create tension between multiple voices in dialogue.
good-writing-000736.zh: 在对话中创造多个角色之间的紧张关系。

good-writing-000737.en: You are creating richness, sweetness, layers.
good-writing-000737.zh: 你正在创造出丰富、甜美、层次丰富的效果。

good-writing-000738.en: An editor will help you figure out which elements of song are missing when the time comes, and that will be easier if you have stayed true to your own sheet of music, to your story and characters and themes.
good-writing-000738.zh: 一位编辑会帮助你找出在演出时缺失的歌曲元素。如果你始终忠于自己的乐谱、故事以及所表达的主题，那么这一切都会变得更加简单。

good-writing-000739.en: In the meantime, never forget what my friend Randi Mayem Singer preaches: “Tell me a story, make me care.”
good-writing-000739.zh: 与此同时，永远不要忘记我的朋友兰迪·梅耶姆·辛格所倡导的理念：“给我讲个故事，让我产生兴趣。”

good-writing-000740.en: And never forget that steady Ringo is there in the background all along like a heartbeat, a pulse: boom-boom, rat-a-tat-tat, oomph, a crack from the snare drum, a sandy whisper of drum brush from the quiet side of things.
good-writing-000740.zh: 永远不要忘记，那个始终在背景中出现的稳定的Ringo，就像心跳、脉搏一般——砰砰作响，节奏明快，还有那来自小鼓的清脆声，以及来自事物平静面侧的、沙沙作响的鼓声。

good-writing-000742.en: Transitional phrases (“then,” “next,” “when,” “meanwhile,” “however”) are not needed unless a gap in time or logic has opened.
good-writing-000742.zh: 除非时间或逻辑上确实出现了需要衔接的空隙，否则不必使用 then（然后）、next（接着）、when（当……时）、meanwhile（与此同时）、however（然而）这些过渡用语。

good-writing-000743.en: Several of these kit-bag rules reinforce the principle to say more with less.
good-writing-000743.zh: 这些包装规则中的几条都体现了“用更少的资源表达更多的信息”这一原则。

good-writing-000744.en: Word economy doesn’t just ease the reader, it often forces out blunders.
good-writing-000744.zh: 文字的简洁性不仅能够减轻读者的阅读负担，还能避免许多错误。

good-writing-000745.en: Noticing extra words can reveal weak verb constructions, provide a gimlet eye to adjectives that might be made redundant by a better noun, and clear a path to forward motion that has been interrupted or slowed by draggy clauses.
good-writing-000745.zh: 注意到多余的词语可以揭示不规范的动词结构，发现那些可能因更好的名词而变得多余的形容词，并为那些因冗长的从句而受阻或变缓的句子提供改进的机会。

good-writing-000746.en: The most common transition, “then,” as in “Victor then placed the knife on the table,” seldom improves on its omission.
good-writing-000746.zh: 最常见的过渡词是“然后”，比如“维克托然后把刀放在了桌子上”。这种用法通常没有更好的替代方式。

good-writing-000747.en: A reader is aware of time passing and assumes that what follows in text also follows in time.
good-writing-000747.zh: 读者能够感知到时间的流逝，并认为文本中所述的内容也会随着时间的发展而持续下去。

good-writing-000748.en: If I don’t need a word, I get rid of it.
good-writing-000748.zh: 如果我不需要某个词，我就不再使用它。

good-writing-000749.en: This ability of the reader to trail along naturally without prompts doesn’t just apply to time.
good-writing-000749.zh: 读者能够不借助提示自然地跟随文本阅读，这种能力并不只适用于时间维度。

good-writing-000750.en: In logic, too, the reader can be trusted.
good-writing-000750.zh: 在逻辑领域里，也可以信任读者。

good-writing-000752.en: When the teacher called on him, he hesitantly stammered out his usual wrong answer.
good-writing-000752.zh: 当老师叫到他的时候，他支支吾吾地吐出了他一贯的错误答案。

good-writing-000753.en: On cue, his classmates broke out laughing.
good-writing-000753.zh: 这时，他的同学们突然笑了起来。

good-writing-000754.en: Fortunately for John, the teacher called them to order.
good-writing-000754.zh: 对约翰来说幸运的是，老师已经让他们重新排队了。

good-writing-000757.en: He stammered out another wrong answer, igniting the class into an eruption of snickers and laughs.
good-writing-000757.zh: 他结结巴巴地又答错了一个问题，这引发了全班同学的哄笑。

good-writing-000758.en: The teacher rapped her ruler for silence.
good-writing-000758.zh: 老师用尺子敲打她，要求她保持安静。

good-writing-000759.en: The reader knows that raising a hand results in being called on.
good-writing-000759.zh: 读者可以知道，举手就意味着会被叫到进行发言。

good-writing-000760.en: “When the teacher called on him” is an unnecessary transition.
good-writing-000760.zh: “当老师点名他时”这个过渡句是不必要的。

good-writing-000762.en: And anyone with a heart recognizes that the teacher’s intervention is “fortunate for John.”
good-writing-000762.zh: 任何有良知的人都会认识到，老师的干预对约翰来说是一件“幸运的事”。

good-writing-000763.en: Watch for paragraphs that start with parenthetical clauses, such as “While Roger blabbed on, John stumbled in.”
good-writing-000763.zh: 注意那些以括号结构开头的段落，比如“当罗杰还在喋喋不休时，约翰却突然倒下了。”

good-writing-000764.en: They feel tentative to the reader, as if the author is backing into the picture.
good-writing-000764.zh: 他们对读者来说显得有些犹豫不决，就好像作者自己也在被描绘的场景中扮演着重要的角色一样。

good-writing-000765.en: While it’s true that too much in media res—starting in the middle—is dizzying, it’s also worth noting that too little is insulting.
good-writing-000765.zh: 虽然在媒体中过度使用“中间部分”的内容确实会让人感到混乱，但同样值得注意的是，如果内容太少的话，也会显得很糟糕。

good-writing-000766.en: Watch for any paragraph that starts with an adverb followed by a comma.
good-writing-000766.zh: 注意那些以副词开头，后面跟着逗号的句子。

good-writing-000767.en: A friend threatened to write what she called a psychedelic Western that would open with the sentence “Suddenly, bullets.”
good-writing-000767.zh: 一个朋友威胁要创作一部她称之为“迷幻西部片”的作品，该作品的开头将是这样的句子：“突然间，子弹飞射而来。”

good-writing-000768.en: A more typical example: “Unexpectedly, the washer overflowed.”
good-writing-000768.zh: 一个更典型的例子是：“出乎意料的是，洗衣机发生了泄漏。”

good-writing-000769.en: An overflowing washer is never expected.
good-writing-000769.zh: 永远不期望会出现溢出的现象。

good-writing-000770.en: Test whether the logic of the story is enough to carry the reader on without the superfluous clause or word.
good-writing-000770.zh: 测试故事的逻辑结构是否足以吸引读者，而不需要过多的修饰词或多余的描述。

good-writing-000771.en: When I was a newspaper reporter, Joe Gemignani, a memorable editor, scanning one of my rushed and skeletal reporting jobs, called out, “Ah yes, the all-powerful ‘Meanwhile.’ ”
good-writing-000771.zh: 当我还是一名报纸记者的时候，有一位非常出色的编辑，名叫乔·杰米尼亚尼。他仔细审阅了我那些匆忙而简略的报道后，说道：“啊，对了，那个无所不能的‘与此同时’栏目。”

good-writing-000772.en: Also think about removing adverbs that act like transitional phrases but simply add an authorial interjection.
good-writing-000772.zh: 另外，还需要考虑去除那些起到过渡作用但实际上只是增加了作者感叹词的词组。

good-writing-000773.en: Most uses of “actually” can be removed, as well as such phrases as “So far as she knew...” or “Showing good manners...”
good-writing-000773.zh: “Actually”这个词的大多数用法都可以被省略，同样地，像“据她所知……”或者“表现得很有礼貌……”这样的表达方式也可以被省略。

good-writing-000775.en: For me, the most important transitions have to do with the passage of time.
good-writing-000775.zh: 对我来说，最重要的转变都与时间的流逝有关。

good-writing-000776.en: In old movies, we watched the hands of a clock spin around and around, or the pages of a daily calendar fly out the window, but you can’t show this on the page.
good-writing-000776.zh: 在老电影中，我们会看到时钟的指针不停地转动，或者日历的页面飞快地翻动，但这些场景是无法在屏幕上呈现出来的。

good-writing-000777.en: You can think of your own cool ways to make time pass.
good-writing-000777.zh: 你可以想出自己的方法来打发时间。

good-writing-000778.en: If it hasn’t been long, you could say, “She had made a decision by the time the light turned green” or “the bread had fully risen,” or “When he had finished the last of the haggis, he struggled to his feet.”
good-writing-000778.zh: 如果时间不长的话，你可以这样描述：“当绿灯亮起时，她已经做出了决定”；“面包已经完全发酵了”；“当他吃完最后一口哈吉斯后，他才勉强站了起来。”

good-writing-000779.en: If real time has passed, the leaves outside the window have turned red, or fallen off, or just begun to bud.
good-writing-000779.zh: 如果时间已经过去，窗外的叶子已经变红，或者已经掉落，或者刚刚开始发芽。

good-writing-000780.en: The dog’s muzzle had gone gray, or the narrator’s beard.
good-writing-000780.zh: 那只狗的口罩已经变得灰白，或者可以说，是叙述者胡须的颜色也变成了灰色。

good-writing-000781.en: The baby left for college, or she found herself midway through her master’s program, or (in my case) “She married the love of her life three days after receiving her first Social Security check.”
good-writing-000781.zh: 那个孩子进入了大学学习，或者她在硕士课程进行到一半时便离开了，或者（就我的情况而言）“她在收到第一份社会保障金后的第三天就嫁给了她的真爱。”

good-writing-000782.en: “Easter came early that year” lets the reader know that it is now March.
good-writing-000782.zh: “那年复活节来得早”这一表述让读者立刻意识到现在已经是三月了。

good-writing-000783.en: “Labor Day couldn’t come soon enough for the harried mother, who frequently questioned whether she should have raised orchids, or teacup poodles, instead of children.”
good-writing-000783.zh: 对那些疲惫不堪的母亲来说，劳动节这个日子来得真是时候——她们常常在思考：当初是否应该培育兰花或者茶杯犬，而不是孩子呢？

good-writing-000785.en: Neal says that most uses of “actually” can be removed, but I say all uses of “actually.”
good-writing-000785.zh: 尼尔斯说，大多数情况下都可以去掉“actually”这个词，但我认为所有情况下都应该保留“actually”这个词。

good-writing-000786.en: Thirty years ago, a friend pointed out the extreme overuse of “actually” in both the spoken and written word and ever since, I hear and see it everywhere.
good-writing-000786.zh: 三十年前，一位朋友指出，无论是在口语还是书面语中，都出现了“actually”这种词的过度使用现象。从那以后，我就不断听到和看到这种用法。

good-writing-000787.en: It is a tic of the writer or speaker.
good-writing-000787.zh: 这是作者或说话者特有的习惯行为。

good-writing-000788.en: Once you start listening for it, you will hear it everywhere.
good-writing-000788.zh: 一旦你开始倾听它，你就会在任何地方听到它。

good-writing-000793.en: Use the “find” function on your word processor to root out “actually,” but for what it’s worth, I don’t mind “meanwhile.”
good-writing-000793.zh: 请使用文字处理软件中的“查找”功能来去除“actually”这个词。不过，值得一提的是，我并不介意保留“meanwhile”这个词。

good-writing-000794.en: It is most often used as an adverb, meaning at the same time or during the time in between this or that event—“I am going to Norway this fall. Meanwhile, I am bingeing on Scandinavian noir.”
good-writing-000794.zh: 它通常用作副词，表示在某一事件发生的同一时间或期间——“我今年秋天要去挪威。与此同时，我正在大量阅读斯堪的纳维亚地区的黑色小说。”

good-writing-000795.en: In its guise as “meantime,” “meanwhile” can also be a noun—it’s two, two, two mints in one: “In the meantime, elections have become billion-dollar processes.”
good-writing-000795.zh: 在“meanwhile”这个词的用法中，它也可以作为名词使用——即“与此同时”，意味着“在这两个时间点上，选举过程已经变成了价值数十亿美元的大工程”。

good-writing-000796.en: It has been used as both since the 1300s, and Neal comes along and announces that we shouldn’t use it?
good-writing-000796.zh: 自13世纪以来，这种工具就一直被使用着。而现在，尼尔出现了，却宣称我们不应该再使用这种工具了？

good-writing-000797.en: You decide: Seven hundred years–plus of recorded use, or cranky, wiseacre Neal?
good-writing-000797.zh: 你来决定吧：使用记录已达七百年之久，还是选择那个脾气暴躁、爱挑剔的尼尔呢？

good-writing-000799.en: If two sentences are tightly linked and one progresses from the other, consider separating them with a semicolon.
good-writing-000799.zh: 如果两个句子的意思紧密相连，后一句又承接前一句向前推进，可以考虑用分号把它们连接起来。

good-writing-000800.en: A semicolon links two complete sentences; it reinforces and seems to prove their connection.
good-writing-000800.zh: 分号用于连接两个完整的句子；它起到了强化这种连接关系的作用，似乎还证明了这两个句子之间的关联。

good-writing-000801.en: This oft-neglected tool glides in effortlessly.
good-writing-000801.zh: 这个经常被忽视的工具，使用起来非常方便。

good-writing-000802.en: It’s a beautiful way to reflect without adding a transitional phrase.
good-writing-000802.zh: 这是一种简洁的表达方式，无需使用过渡性短语就能达到反射的效果。

good-writing-000803.en: (The semicolon’s other use as a super-comma is more on the grammatical side of things; we won’t go into it here.)
good-writing-000803.zh: （分号另一种用途是作为超级逗号使用，但这属于语法方面的细节问题；我们在这里不详细讨论这一点。）

good-writing-000804.en: As a rhetorical device the semicolon is unlike any other: It creates a sliding pause, as if the sentences on either side would be less without their partner.
good-writing-000804.zh: 作为一种修辞手法，分号具有独特的特性：它制造了一种“悬置停顿”，仿佛如果没有分号作为连接，两边的句子就会显得不够完整。

good-writing-000805.en: See what happens when I replace a period with a semicolon:
good-writing-000805.zh: 看看当我将一个句号替换为分号时会发生什么：

good-writing-000806.en: My eyes are green, my hair red.
good-writing-000806.zh: 我的眼睛是绿色的，头发是红色的。

good-writing-000807.en: For Halloween I usually dress as a six-foot-four leprechaun.
good-writing-000807.zh: 在万圣节期间，我通常会装扮成一个身高六英尺四英寸的小精灵。

good-writing-000808.en: My eyes are green, my hair red; for Halloween I usually dress as a six-foot-four leprechaun.
good-writing-000808.zh: 我的眼睛是绿色的，头发是红色的；在万圣节期间，我通常会装扮成一个身高六英尺四英寸的小妖精。

good-writing-000809.en: The semicolon acts as a knowing gesture, tucking the second thought into the first.
good-writing-000809.zh: 分号起到了连接两种思考方式的作用，将第二种思考方式融入第一种思考方式中。

good-writing-000810.en: If you’re anti-semicolon, that’s all right, too.
good-writing-000810.zh: 如果你不喜欢使用分号的话，那也没关系。

good-writing-000811.en: Many writers refuse to use it in either Rule 10’s way or as a super-comma.
good-writing-000811.zh: 许多作家拒绝使用规则10中的这种用法，也拒绝将其视为一种特殊的逗号用法。

good-writing-000812.en: A tweener of questionable birth, the semicolon makes them uncomfortable.
good-writing-000812.zh: 这个年纪稍小的孩子出身可疑，那个分号符号让他们感到不安。

good-writing-000815.en: There are self-righteous people who secretly think that the semicolon is a hybrid invention that is neither this nor that, unnecessary and lazy.
good-writing-000815.zh: 有一些自以为是的人，暗自认为半号是某种“混合发明”，既不属于这个类别，也不属于那个类别；这种发明毫无必要，而且显得很敷衍。

good-writing-000816.zh: 他们可以思考这个问题。

good-writing-000817.en: I use semicolons whenever it makes sense to connect two related sentences—cousin sentences.
good-writing-000817.zh: 在需要连接两个相关的句子时，我会使用分号来分隔它们。

good-writing-000818.en: Of course you could put a period between them, but that might be a more abrupt disconnection and thus block the flow of language and meaning that you were going for.
good-writing-000818.zh: 当然，你可以在这两个词之间加上一个句号，但那样做可能会让语言与意义的连贯性被打破，从而无法保持原本想要传达的流畅性。

good-writing-000819.en: The late, great John Gardner wrote that the fiction writer is creating a dream in the reader’s mind, and the dream must be vivid and continuous.
good-writing-000819.zh: 已故的伟人约翰·加德纳写道，小说家在读者脑海中创造了一个梦境，而这个梦境必须生动且持续不断。

good-writing-000820.zh: 写作是一种创造，而非单纯的教义陈述。

good-writing-000821.en: You do have to stay within grammar, but even grammar is a little more flexible than you might think.
good-writing-000821.zh: 你确实必须遵循语法规则，但即使是语法规则，其灵活性也比你想象的要强一些。

good-writing-000822.en: I tell my students they can play around with any part of speech if they can get away with it—that is, if the reader (me) does not stop and think about how the sentence should be corrected.
good-writing-000822.zh: 我告诉我的学生们，如果他们能够妥善处理任何语法问题，那么他们就可以自由地使用任何语法结构——也就是说，只要读者（我）不会停下来思考如何修正这个句子。

good-writing-000823.en: I don’t write for the anti-semicolon Church Lady crowd; I write from my heart and mind.
good-writing-000823.zh: 我不为那些反对分号写作风格的人而写作；我是以自己的心灵和思维来创作作品的。

good-writing-000824.en: (See how the semicolon was fine there?)
good-writing-000824.zh: （看看那个分号在那里是怎么处理的？）

good-writing-000825.en: I’ve had the same editor for fifteen years who is very East Coast and strict grammatically, and often calls me on my hippie-dippie ways, like using “grok” or “vibe,” but he never tries to get me to change semicolons to periods if they are in the natural order of things, the collagen between two complete cousinly thoughts, whose shoulders just naturally touch at the kids’ table.
good-writing-000825.zh: 十五年来，我一直使用同一个编辑。他非常注重语法规范，而且总是批评我那些“嬉皮士”式的写作风格，比如使用“grok”或“vibe”这样的表达方式。但他从未试图要求我把分号改为句号，因为这两种标点符号的使用方式在语法上都是自然合理的。两个完整的想法之间，就像两个肩膀自然相贴的表兄弟一样，这种关系在写作中是非常自然且恰当的。

good-writing-000826.en: Rule 11: Drop “Very” and Other Crutch Words

good-writing-000827.en: The word “very” seldom improves a sentence.
good-writing-000827.zh: “very（非常）”这个词很少能让一个句子变得更好。

good-writing-000828.zh: “非常”这个词会减弱它所修饰的词语的强烈程度。

good-writing-000830.zh: 通常这样就已经足够了。

good-writing-000831.en: But if, when you delete it, the remaining word is insufficient, find the appropriate substitute.
good-writing-000831.zh: 但是，如果你在删除某个词后，剩下的词数量不足，那么就需要找到一个合适的替代词。

good-writing-000832.en: The scriptwriter Tom Schulman has Robin Williams’s character in Dead Poets Society describe this rule succinctly: “Avoid using the word ‘very’ because it’s lazy. A man is not very tired, he is exhausted. Don’t use ‘very sad,’ use ‘morose.’ Language was invented for one reason, boys—to woo women—and in that endeavor, laziness will not do.”
good-writing-000832.zh: 编剧汤姆·舒尔曼在《死去的诗人》中，用罗宾·威廉姆斯的笔触简洁地描述了这一规则：“避免使用‘非常’这个词，因为那样显得很懒。一个人不是‘非常疲惫’，而是已经筋疲力尽。不要使用‘非常悲伤’这样的表达，应该用‘忧郁’来形容。语言的存在就是为了一个目的——吸引女性，而在这一过程中，懒惰是行不通的。”

good-writing-000833.en: Schulman got an Oscar for lines like that.
good-writing-000833.zh: 舒尔曼因这样的台词而获得了奥斯卡奖。

good-writing-000835.zh: 非常大——庞然大物般、高耸入云、像猪一样笨拙

good-writing-000837.zh: 非常饥饿——饥渴难耐，渴望食物到极点

good-writing-000838.zh: 非常古老——古老的、陈旧的、过时了

good-writing-000839.en: The early twentieth-century editor William Allen White reportedly told a group of reporters, “If you feel the urge of ‘very’ coming on, just write the word ‘damn,’ in the place of ‘very.’ The editor will strike out the word ‘damn,’ and you will have a good sentence.”
good-writing-000839.zh: 20世纪初的编辑威廉·艾伦·怀特曾对一群记者说：“如果你觉得需要用‘damn’这个词来替代‘very’，那么就在‘very’的位置上写上‘damn’这个字即可。这样，你就能得到一句不错的文章了。”

good-writing-000840.en: Other crutch words that are better scrapped: “really,” “some,” “basically,” “rather,” “important.”
good-writing-000840.zh: 其他应该被淘汰的套用词有：“真的”、“一些”、“基本上”、“相当”、“重要”。

good-writing-000841.en: That last one, “important,” loses its last remnant of power when you notice it is short for “important to me.”
good-writing-000841.zh: 最后一个词“important”在听到它实际上是“对我而言很重要”这个意思时，就已经失去了它原本的权威性。

good-writing-000842.en: If the reader can always disagree with the thing’s importance, then it can’t be important the way the word is meant to convey.
good-writing-000842.zh: 如果读者总是能够质疑某件事的重要性，那么这件事就不可能是像文字所表达的那样重要的。

good-writing-000843.en: By the way, “thing” is another of those everyday words to omit and replace with a vivid substitute.
good-writing-000843.zh: 顺便说一下，“thing”也是那些可以省略并替换为更生动表达方式的日常词汇之一。

good-writing-000844.en: While written language often shines at its most conversational, these oddly disempowering words have a way of troubling the reader.
good-writing-000844.zh: 虽然书面语言在表达口语化内容时往往表现得非常自然，但这些奇怪的、反而让人感到无力的词语，却会困扰读者。

good-writing-000845.en: We readers are of two minds: We want the comfort of everyday speech and its patterns, and we want signs that the author is concisely attuned to the written idiom.
good-writing-000845.zh: 我们读者有两种不同的想法：一方面，我们希望能够使用日常语言中的表达方式，并了解这些表达方式的规律；另一方面，我们也希望这些标识能够表明作者已经熟练掌握了书面语言的运用方式。

good-writing-000846.en: In my own everyday speech I use “actually,” “very,” “some,” “thing,” and “basically” regularly, usually emphatically.
good-writing-000846.zh: 在平时的对话中，我经常会使用“实际上”、“非常”、“一些”、“东西”以及“基本上”这些词，而且通常都是带着强调的语气来使用的。

good-writing-000847.en: My voice italicizes these weak words to make them stick.
good-writing-000847.zh: 我用斜体来强调这些薄弱的词语，以便让它们更引人注意。

good-writing-000849.en: Neal is a stickler about the use of “very,” and in the early days of our marriage, when he edited my writing and redlined all the “verys,” I used to wonder what kind of rigid, puritanical killjoy I had married.
good-writing-000849.zh: 尼尔斯对“非常”这个词的用法非常严格。在我们婚姻的初期，当他编辑我的文章、并标出所有需要修改的“非常”部分时，我常常在想，自己究竟嫁了一个多么刻板、保守且令人讨厌的人啊。

good-writing-000850.en: But then I did a word search in the essay I was working on and discovered I had used “very” seven times.
good-writing-000850.zh: 不过后来，我在正在撰写的论文中进行了词搜索，发现“very”这个词被我使用了七次。

good-writing-000851.en: Because he does have certain skills and charms, I decided not to pursue a legal separation, but instead to use “very” as sparingly as possible.
good-writing-000851.zh: 因为他确实具备一些技能和魅力，所以我决定不采取法律手段来分离，而是尽可能谨慎地使用“非常”这个词。

good-writing-000852.en: Once you start to notice how often you are letting it in, you’ll feel a mild chagrin, as if you are still in junior high and repeating “totally” every few sentences.
good-writing-000852.zh: 一旦你开始注意到自己如此频繁地重复“完全”这个词语，你就会感到一阵轻微的懊恼，就像还在初中阶段，每说几句话就不得不重复“完全”这个词一样。

good-writing-000853.en: Maybe start experimenting with using “totes” a lot, as in, “It was totes a surprise” or “He was totes against using the word ‘very.’ ”
good-writing-000853.zh: 或许可以试着更多地使用“totes”这种表达方式，比如“这真是个惊喜啊”，或者“他完全反对使用‘非常’这个词。”

good-writing-000854.en: Here are three sentences from the first paragraph of the introduction to Bird by Bird: “Our house was very quiet after dinner—unless, that is, some of my father’s writer friends were over. My father was a writer, as were most of the men with whom he hung out. They were not the quietest people on earth, but they were mostly very masculine and kind.”
good-writing-000854.zh: 在《Bird by Bird》的引言部分，第一段中有三句话：“晚餐过后，我们的房子非常安静——除非，也就是因为我的父亲的一些作家朋友来拜访了。我的父亲也是作家，和他一起出去的大多数男人也都是作家。他们并不是世界上最安静的人，但他们大多都很男性化且友善。”

good-writing-000855.zh: 这些“虚词”没有任何实际意义。

good-writing-000856.zh: 编辑部在哪里？他怎么没出现在名单上？

good-writing-000857.en: Then, four paragraphs down, “I was very shy and strange-looking, loved reading above everything else, weighed about forty pounds at the time, and was so tense that I walked around with my shoulders up to my ears, like Richard Nixon. I saw a home movie once of a birthday party I went to in the first grade, with all these cute little boys and girls playing together like puppies, and all of a sudden I scuttled across the screen like Prufrock’s crab. I was very clearly the one who was going to grow up to be a serial killer, or keep dozens and dozens of cats. Instead, I got funny.”
good-writing-000857.zh: 然后，在第四段中这样写道：“我当时非常害羞，看起来也很奇怪。我最喜欢读书，当时的体重大约四十磅左右。因为太紧张了，以至于走路时肩膀都抬到了耳朵的位置，就像理查德·尼克松一样。有一次，我在小学时参加一个生日派对时，看到一段家庭录像。那些可爱的男孩和女孩们在一起玩耍，就像小狗狗一样。突然间，我就像普鲁弗洛克的螃蟹一样冲过了屏幕。很明显，我将来会成为一个连环杀手，或者养几十只猫。但实际上，我变得很有趣。”

good-writing-000859.en: Four uses of “very” in the first five paragraphs, none of which adds a thing.
good-writing-000859.zh: 在前五段中，“very”出现了四次，但其中没有任何一次能增加任何意义或效果。

good-writing-000860.en: Do a word search when you finish your first draft and take out almost all the “verys,” unless you are describing an unusually hungry caterpillar.
good-writing-000860.zh: 在完成初稿后，进行词汇搜索，删除几乎所有不必要的词语，除非你描述的是非常饥饿的毛毛虫。

good-writing-000861.zh: 法则12：扔掉［那些］多余的小词

good-writing-000862.en: Remove the clutter of short words (pronouns, prepositions, connectors).
good-writing-000862.zh: 清除那些堆积起来的小词，如代词、介词和连接词。

good-writing-000863.en: If you see a bunch of little words in a sentence, you can probably get rid of some [of them].
good-writing-000863.zh: 如果你在句子中看到一些小词，那么很可能可以去掉其中的一些词。

good-writing-000864.en: I don’t have anything against auxiliary verbs and prepositions.
good-writing-000864.zh: 我对辅助动词和介词并没有任何意见。

good-writing-000865.zh: 在它们缺失的情况下，这些物品就显得至关重要了。

good-writing-000866.en: But I know from experience that many in a row are a tip-off to excess verbiage.
good-writing-000866.zh: 但根据我的经验，连续使用过多的动词结构往往是一种过度用词的迹象。

good-writing-000867.en: In that last sentence, does “in a row” help with meaning enough to warrant slowing down the sentence?
good-writing-000867.zh: 在最后一句话中，“in a row”这个表达是否足以增强句子的意义，从而值得放慢语速来强调它呢？

good-writing-000868.zh: 这是个关于品味的问题。

good-writing-000869.en: Also, if the preposition “of” is repeated in a clause, you can probably rewrite it.
good-writing-000869.zh: 另外，如果介词“of”在一个句子中重复出现，那么可以重新编写这个句子。

good-writing-000870.en: “The attitude of the lord of the manor repulsed her” becomes “The lord of the manor’s attitude repulsed her.”
good-writing-000870.zh: “庄园主的态度让她感到厌恶”这句话，正确的翻译应该是“庄园主的态度让她的情绪受到打击”。

good-writing-000871.en: Also, I’m never happy seeing “in order to” as a synonym for the quite effective “to.”
good-writing-000871.zh: 此外，每当看到“为了”这个表达时，我总会觉得它其实可以替代更简洁的“为了”。

good-writing-000872.en: (Once again, the first fourteen lines of Hamlet’s soliloquy are the exception.)
good-writing-000872.zh: （再次强调，哈姆雷特独白的前十四行是个例外。）

good-writing-000873.en: Having scissors in hand, eyeing where to snip, you can spotlight redundancies.
good-writing-000873.zh: 手持剪刀，仔细考虑该从哪里剪断，这样就能清楚地看到哪些地方需要改进或简化。

good-writing-000874.en: “A new dawn” becomes “dawn.” “Tax haven of the rich” becomes “tax haven.” “Bedridden in a hospital” becomes “hospitalized.”
good-writing-000874.zh: “新的黎明”变成了“黎明”。“富人的避税天堂”变成了“避税天堂”。“住院”变成了“被医院收治”。

good-writing-000875.en: Folksy clichés often have redundancies and extra words: “tried and true,” “to and fro,” “through thick and thin,” “above and beyond,” “ready, willing, and able.”
good-writing-000875.zh: 这些常见的陈词滥调往往包含冗余的词汇和多余的描述方式：比如“经过验证的可靠方法”、“时起时落”、“历经千辛万苦”、“超越预期”、“随时准备、心甘情愿”等等。

good-writing-000876.en: Conversational English often adds unnecessary prepositions: “Meet up with” seldom needs “up” or “with.”
good-writing-000876.zh: 在口语英语中，常常会添加不必要的介词。例如，“Meet up with”这个短语中，其实并不需要加上“up”或“with”这些词。

good-writing-000877.en: I don’t need the “of” to throw things out the window.
good-writing-000877.zh: 我不需要用“of”来把东西扔出去。

good-writing-000878.en: “As a matter of fact” becomes “In fact,” or, more commonly, gets cut right out.
good-writing-000878.zh: “As a matter of fact”这句话实际上应该被改为“事实上”，或者更常见的是，直接省略掉这句话。

good-writing-000882.en: I used to buy little pieces of furniture for holding books, paper, gewgaws, whenever the most recent piece of furniture I’d bought for this purpose was crammed with stuff.
good-writing-000882.zh: 我过去常常购买一些小型的储物家具，用来放置书籍、纸张以及各种小物件。不过，每次我购买新的此类家具时，都会发现它们已经被塞得满满的，无法再容纳更多的物品了。

good-writing-000883.en: So I might have three cute cabinets and bookcases in one room.
good-writing-000883.zh: 所以，我可能会在一个房间里放置三个漂亮的橱柜和书架。

good-writing-000884.en: And I loved each of them.
good-writing-000884.zh: 我真的很喜欢他们每一个人都。

good-writing-000885.en: One day I had an epiphany: Not only were my small pieces of furniture crammed with stuff, but my rooms were crammed with small pieces of furniture.
good-writing-000885.zh: 有一天，我突然意识到：不仅我的小家具里塞满了各种杂物，而且我的房间里也堆满了各种小家具。

good-writing-000886.en: They were low to the ground and it felt like having a few of the Seven Dwarfs in each room.
good-writing-000886.zh: 他们低垂在地面上，感觉就像每个房间里都住着几个小矮人一样。

good-writing-000887.en: Uncramming—in all realms of life—makes everything better, clearer, lighter, whether it is the breakfast nook or a long sentence.
good-writing-000887.zh: 在生活的各个方面，简化一切都能让事物变得更加美好、清晰易懂，无论是在准备早餐时，还是在处理冗长的句子时。

good-writing-000888.en: Look at this passage from a poem by Gary Snyder that I used as an example of perfect writing in Bird by Bird:
good-writing-000888.zh: 请看这段来自Gary Snyder的诗篇。我以它作为《鸟与鸟》一书中对完美写作的范例。

good-writing-000889.en: Ripples on the surface of the water—

good-writing-000890.zh: 有银色鲑鱼从下方穿过——各不相同

good-writing-000891.en: from the ripples caused by breezes

good-writing-000892.en: None of us can or should even try to write like Gary Snyder.
good-writing-000892.zh: 我们没有人能够或应该尝试模仿Gary Snyder的写作风格。

good-writing-000893.en: But these nineteen words are breathtaking.
good-writing-000893.zh: 但這十九个字真是令人惊叹不已。

good-writing-000894.en: (Read more poetry! I have urged my writing students to study poetry for forty years now.)
good-writing-000894.zh: 再读一些诗歌吧！我已经要求我的写作学生学习诗歌四十年了。

good-writing-000895.en: Now consider the sentences I wrote to introduce Snyder’s poem as I reassured the class that clarity and details would emerge in their writing the same way Polaroids develop: “One of these images might show up dimly in the lower-right quadrant of the imaginary Polaroid you took; you didn’t even know at first that it was part of the landscape, and here it turns out to evoke something so deep in you that you can’t put your finger on it.”
good-writing-000895.zh: 现在，让我们来欣赏一下我用来介绍斯奈德诗歌的这段文字。在向同学们强调“清晰度和细节性”在写作中同样具有重要性时，我这样写道：“这些文字中的某一部分，可能会在你所拍摄的‘想象中的宝丽来照片’的右下角区域显得模糊不清；起初，你甚至不会意识到那部分内容其实是风景的一部分。而如今，这些文字却能够唤起你内心深处某种难以言表的情感。”

good-writing-000896.en: Right off the bat, there are three “its,” positioned like ashtrays on my tiny cabinets.
good-writing-000896.zh: 立刻就能看到三个“its”装置，它们像烟灰缸一样摆放在我的小柜子上。

good-writing-000897.en: And I could have written “you didn’t notice that it was part of the landscape,” losing “at first.” “Notice” implies all of a sudden—that is, at first.
good-writing-000897.zh: 我本可以写“你没有注意到那其实是风景的一部分”，从而省略“起初”这一环节。这里的“注意到”意味着突然间——也就是说，最初的时候并没有注意到。

good-writing-000898.en: What about “and here it turns out”?
good-writing-000898.zh: 那么“结果如此”这句话呢？

good-writing-000899.en: Better to have written “While it evokes something...”
good-writing-000899.zh: 最好写的是“虽然这唤起了某种情感……”

good-writing-000900.en: And if I had given this passage to Neal to edit, he would have challenged me on the cliché “you can’t put your finger on it.” (See Rule 19.)
good-writing-000900.zh: 如果让我把这段文字交给尼尔斯来编辑的话，他肯定会因为我使用了那种陈腐的表达方式而批评我：“你无法真正理解它。”（参见规则19。）

good-writing-000901.en: The sentences you write are in flux.
good-writing-000901.zh: 你写的句子处于不断变化的状态。

good-writing-000902.en: You go over them, trimming, revising, and auditioning words, until you arrive at the sentence you were after all along.
good-writing-000902.zh: 你会对这些文字进行反复修改、润色和试听，直到找到你真正想要的句子为止。

good-writing-000903.zh: 法则13：给“this”添上明确的内容

good-writing-000904.en: Pronouns are hard for readers to follow, especially “this” and “it.”
good-writing-000904.zh: 读者常常难以追踪代词究竟指什么，尤其是 this 和 it。

good-writing-000906.en: Place a noun after it that names it.
good-writing-000906.zh: 在它后面加上一个能够命名该名词的名词。

good-writing-000907.en: Not “This was hard” but “This conversation was hard.”
good-writing-000907.zh: 不是“这很困难”，而是“这次对话很艰难”。

good-writing-000908.en: Not “This was complicated” but “This process was complicated.”
good-writing-000908.zh: 不是“这很复杂”，而是“这个过程很复杂”。

good-writing-000909.en: When you focus on the unadorned “this,” the pronoun often disappears altogether, replaced by the noun itself.
good-writing-000909.zh: 当你专注于那个朴实无华的“这个”时，代词通常会完全消失，被名词本身所替代。

good-writing-000910.en: “This wasn’t the end of it” becomes “Trouble was lurking.”
good-writing-000910.zh: “这并非结束”变成了“麻烦还在后面等着。”

good-writing-000911.en: You might want to expand this rule to other pronouns, too.
good-writing-000911.zh: 你或许希望将这一规则扩展到其他代词上。

good-writing-000912.en: Yes, we all agree that a pronoun refers to the last preceding noun of the same number and gender.
good-writing-000912.zh: 是的，我们都同意，代词应该指代同一数和同一性别中最后一个被提及的名词。

good-writing-000913.en: But do you want to make your reader work that out every time?
good-writing-000913.zh: 但是，您真的希望每次读者都需要自己计算出来吗？

good-writing-000914.en: Naming the noun too often can annoy the reader, but so can littering your text with pronouns to keep track of.
good-writing-000914.zh: 过度使用名词可能会让读者感到困扰，而频繁使用代词来指代各种事物同样会让人感到混乱。

good-writing-000915.en: As a freshman in college encountering Aristotle, I was challenged by sentences like this: “Of a pair of contraries such that they have no intermediate, one or the other must needs be present in the subject in which they naturally subsist, or of which they are predicated; for it is those, as we proved, in the case of which this necessity obtains, that have no intermediate.”
good-writing-000915.zh: 作为大学一年级的学生，当我接触到亚里士多德的思想时，我遇到了这样一些句子：“对于一对矛盾的事物来说，由于它们之间没有中间状态，因此要么其中一个必然存在于它们所存在的主体中，要么就不存在这样的主体。正如我们所证明的那样，只有那些满足这种必然性的事物，才不存在中间状态。”

good-writing-000916.en: I couldn’t believe how much Aristotle depended on pronouns.
good-writing-000916.zh: 我简直不敢相信，亚里士多德如此依赖代词的使用。

good-writing-000917.en: Only later did I learn that as a heavily declined language, Ancient Greek’s pronouns carried information that didn’t depend on “the nearest proximity” rule, but on what grammatical case the original noun displayed.
good-writing-000917.zh: 直到后来我才了解到，作为一门高度屈折的语言，古希腊语的代词所携带的信息并不取决于“最近距离”原则，而是取决于原始名词所处的语法格。

good-writing-000918.en: A case tells you whether the noun represents a location, or a subject, or an object, or a direct object, or a possession, or even a direction.
good-writing-000918.zh: 一个例子可以告诉你，名词表示的是地点、主语、宾语、直接宾语、所有物，还是其他含义。

good-writing-000919.en: It might make more sense to be pronoun-heavy in Ancient Greek or Latin or Sanskrit.
good-writing-000919.zh: 在古希腊语、拉丁语或梵语中，使用较多的代词可能会更合适。

good-writing-000920.en: We have a few declensions in English (which give us the difference between “I,” “me,” and “mine”), but Aristotle had twice as many.
good-writing-000920.zh: 在英语中，我们有几种词性变化（这些词性变化区分了“I”、“me”和“mine”这三个词的不同含义），但亚里士多德使用的词性变化数量却是我们的两倍。

good-writing-000921.en: The poor translator of my Aristotle texts was stuck with English grammar, which isn’t as happy to economize with pronouns.
good-writing-000921.zh: 我那些翻译亚里士多德著作的翻译者遇到了英语语法的难题，因为在英语中，使用代词来节省字数并不是一种理想的做法。

good-writing-000922.zh: 我最近才了解到这一点。

good-writing-000924.en: My writing professor friend Alexandra Youmans brought it—this rule—to my attention in 2023.
good-writing-000924.zh: 我的写作教授朋友亚历山德拉·尤曼斯在2023年提醒了我这条规则的重要性。

good-writing-000925.en: Now that I know it—this rule, that is—I find it, the rule, screaming out to me daily.
good-writing-000925.zh: 现在，当我了解这项规则之后——这个规则，每天都会让我意识到它的存在。

good-writing-000926.en: I see it, this rule, everywhere.
good-writing-000926.zh: 我到处都能看到这条规则。

good-writing-000927.en: But also, it’s unusual, this rule, in that it, the rule, is subject to overuse.
good-writing-000927.zh: 不过，这个规则也有其特殊性，那就是它容易被滥用。

good-writing-000928.en: None of these rules is set in stone.
good-writing-000928.zh: 这些规定都没有是固定不变的。

good-writing-000929.zh: 语法有明确的黑白分明的规则。

good-writing-000930.en: Persuasive writing needs to be grammatical, of course, but syntax is ambivalent toward meaning, persuasion, elegance, or anything that might be called content.
good-writing-000930.zh: 有说服力的写作当然需要遵循语法规则，但句法结构对于意义、说服力、优雅性，或是任何可以被称为“内容”的因素来说，其实并不重要。

good-writing-000931.en: Once we’re in the content world of semantics, choices open up to the wild.
good-writing-000931.zh: 一旦我们进入语义的内容领域，选择就会变得无穷无尽。

good-writing-000932.en: For any one writer, some rules will be more relevant than others.
good-writing-000932.zh: 对于任何一个作家来说，有些规则比其他规则更为重要。

good-writing-000933.en: Some may need to be dismissed altogether.
good-writing-000933.zh: 有些可能需要完全被淘汰掉。

good-writing-000934.zh: 其他工具可以谨慎使用。

good-writing-000936.en: I’m not sure what I can add to this, except to attack Neal for dredging up Aristotle.
good-writing-000936.zh: 我不确定还能补充什么，除了提醒尼尔不要继续讨论亚里士多德的问题之外。

good-writing-000938.en: When he quotes something like this at an otherwise pleasant gathering, I look away, with a dead, flat, reptilian expression, no matter that his audiences seem to enjoy the discussion.
good-writing-000938.zh: 在这样一个原本愉快的聚会中，当他引用这样的内容时，我会把目光移开，脸上露出一种冷漠、无表情的表情。尽管他的听众似乎很喜欢这次讨论，但我却毫不在意。

good-writing-000939.en: I recommend that you ignore the quote and his ensuing remarks.
good-writing-000939.zh: 我建议你们忽略那段引文以及他随后的言论。

good-writing-000940.en: However, he is right about “this” and “it.”
good-writing-000940.zh: 不过，他在“这个”和“那个”这两个词的使用上是正确的。

good-writing-000941.en: They can be hard to follow.
good-writing-000941.zh: 它们可能很难理解或跟随。

good-writing-000942.en: Thirty-five years ago, my editor thought it made sense to make me a list of my most annoying habits as a writer.
good-writing-000942.zh: 三十五年前，我的编辑认为，将我作为作家时那些最令人讨厌的习惯列出一份，是个不错的主意。

good-writing-000943.en: I am not making this up.
good-writing-000943.zh: 我不是在编造这些事情。

good-writing-000944.en: I remember two, and live by them.
good-writing-000944.zh: 我只记得两个原则，并以此来生活。

good-writing-000945.en: The first was the overuse of “this” and “it,” often at the beginning of a sentence.
good-writing-000945.zh: 第一个问题是过度使用“this”和“it”这个语法结构，这种情况经常出现在句子的开头。

good-writing-000946.en: Either is a lazy way for any of us regular writers to begin, although Jane Austen begins Pride and Prejudice with “it.” (“It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.”) As does George Orwell in 1984.
good-writing-000946.zh: 无论是哪种方式，对我们这些普通作家来说都是一种轻松的开始方式。不过，简·奥斯汀在《傲慢与偏见》中是以“it”来开始句子的。（“一个拥有财富的男子，必然会渴望找到一个妻子。”）乔治·奥威尔在《1984》中也采用了同样的手法。

good-writing-000947.en: (“It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen.”)
good-writing-000947.zh: “那是四月的某个寒冷而明亮的日子，时钟的指针指向了十三点。”

good-writing-000948.en: Notice, though, that in both cases the subject the pronoun refers to follows right after it; the author has introduced a speck of suspense.
good-writing-000948.zh: 不过，需要注意的是，在这两个例子中，主语代词都紧跟在句子之后；作者故意制造了一种悬念感。

good-writing-000949.en: Notice also the perfectly fine use of the verb “to be.”
good-writing-000949.zh: 另外要注意的是，文中对动词“to be”的使用非常恰当。

good-writing-000950.en: Opening with a fixed notion of existence is a tip-off that the world is about to wobble.
good-writing-000950.zh: 以某种固定的存在概念作为开端，这预示着世界即将发生动荡。

good-writing-000951.en: Promise me you won’t write the naked “this” or the isolated “it” anymore, unless you are as good a writer as Austen or Orwell or as brave a writer as Snoopy.
good-writing-000951.zh: 请答应我，你不要再使用那种完全裸露的“this”或者孤立无援的“it”了，除非你的写作能力能像奥斯汀或奥威尔那样出色，或者你的勇气能像斯诺比那样强大。

good-writing-000952.en: His novels always began, “It was a dark and stormy night,” but he was a dog, a beagle.
good-writing-000952.zh: 他的小说总是以“那是一个黑暗而多风的夜晚”开头，但他其实是一只狗，一只比格犬。

good-writing-000953.en: (I mean no offense to you beagles.)
good-writing-000953.zh: （我没有任何冒犯的意思，那些比格犬们。）

good-writing-000954.en: Even “The night was dark and stormy” is an improvement.
good-writing-000954.zh: 即使是“夜色昏暗，风雨交加”这样的描述，也算是一种进步吧。

good-writing-000957.en: “This was what she so objected to” might be “All that punning was what she so objected to” or “Her habit of scrubbing the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher was what finished the marriage.”
good-writing-000957.zh: “这正是她所反对的”——这句话实际上可以理解为“那些令人厌烦的举动正是她所反对的”；或者“她那种在将餐具放入洗碗机之前先清洗餐具的习惯，正是导致婚姻破裂的原因。”

good-writing-000958.zh: 每次都要问自己：“这个”是什么？

good-writing-000959.zh: 那么，这个“它”指的是什么呢？

good-writing-000960.en: The three-legged dog, or the sandwich he snatched off an old man?
good-writing-000960.zh: 那只三条腿的狗，还是那个从老人手中抢来的三明治？

good-writing-000961.en: The watering can or the water it held?
good-writing-000961.zh: 那个浇水罐，还是它曾经盛装水的那个罐子呢？

good-writing-000962.en: For the record, the second rule I remember was that I used “just” way too often: “She just had to wonder why the man wore a snorkel mask at the library” or “There was just a little more cumin in the soup than absolutely necessary” or “He was just positive that a little more cumin wouldn’t hurt.”
good-writing-000962.zh: 需要明确的是，我记得的第二条规则是：我太频繁地使用“just”这个词了。“她只是好奇为什么那个男人在图书馆会戴着潜水面具”、“汤里的大蒜量比必要的时候稍微多了一些”、“他只是觉得再多一点大蒜也没关系而已。”

good-writing-000963.en: Of course, you can write any way you want, if you can get away with it—that is, keep us reading.
good-writing-000963.zh: 当然，你可以以任何你喜欢的方式来写作，只要这样做不会让人觉得奇怪——也就是说，要保持我们继续阅读的兴趣。

good-writing-000964.en: All the people I love have, sadly, gotten much older and no longer share an enthusiasm for experimental writing.
good-writing-000964.zh: 所有我爱的那些人，遗憾的是，都已经年纪很大了，他们不再对实验性写作抱有热情了。

good-writing-000965.en: We once loved James Joyce and Gertrude Stein and Céline, who were celebrated for their avant-garde writing because they were brilliant, groundbreaking, and fearless.
good-writing-000965.zh: 我们曾经热爱过詹姆斯·乔伊斯、格特鲁德·斯坦和塞利纳。他们以他们的先锋派写作而闻名，因为这些作品既卓越又具有开创性，且毫无畏惧之心。

good-writing-000967.en: We do not want to have to figure out what you are trying to say.
good-writing-000967.zh: 我们不想不得不去理解你试图表达的内容。

good-writing-000968.en: I’m in it for the story.
good-writing-000968.zh: 我是为了这个故事而参与其中的。

good-writing-000969.en: Help me see your story as you tell it.
good-writing-000969.zh: 请帮助我以您讲述的方式来理解您的故事。

good-writing-000970.en: I wouldn’t get to page 3 of Thomas Pynchon now.
good-writing-000970.zh: 现在我可不会读到托马斯·潘尼奇的第三章了。

good-writing-000971.zh: 挑战每一个“这个”和“那个”。

good-writing-000972.en: You’ll leave a lot of them in, but do better when you can.
good-writing-000972.zh: 你会留下很多这样的东西，但当你能够做到更好时，就会取得更好的效果。

good-writing-000973.en: Neal asked, “Do you want to make your reader work that out every time?”
good-writing-000973.zh: 尼尔问道：“你真的希望每次读者都要自己计算出来吗？”

good-writing-000975.en: You want them to keep reading, savoring your images, voice, and clarity, grateful for a fluid ride.
good-writing-000975.zh: 希望他们能够持续阅读你的作品，享受你的文字、声音以及文字的清晰度，并对这种流畅的阅读体验感到满意。

good-writing-000977.en: Spend less time defending what you’ve written, and more time revealing the truth.
good-writing-000977.zh: 少花些时间为自己写下的东西辩护，多花些时间揭示真实。

good-writing-000979.en: Writers are paid to articulate hidden, complex, and sophisticated concepts through clever storytelling.
good-writing-000979.zh: 作家的职责是通过巧妙的叙事方式，来表达那些隐藏在复杂、微妙的概念。

good-writing-000980.en: The temptation is to prove the concept at hand, which is like showing your work in arithmetic.
good-writing-000980.zh: 这种诱惑在于证明所提出的概念，这就像是在算术中展示你的计算结果一样。

good-writing-000981.zh: 这是一种根深蒂固的习惯。

good-writing-000982.en: In college we trained in educational texts that featured proofs, examples, and an expectation of a logical thread that displayed all components as it progressed from cause to effect.
good-writing-000982.zh: 在大学期间，我们学习的是以证明、例子以及逻辑顺序为特点的教学文本。这些文本将各个组成部分以从原因到结果的顺序呈现出来。

good-writing-000984.en: In fiction, authors create believable characters whose decisions create actions that drive the plot along.
good-writing-000984.zh: 在小说中，作者需要塑造出令人信服的角色，这些角色的决策会引发相应的行动，从而推动故事的发展。

good-writing-000985.en: In nonfiction, writers describe events and arguments that pursue meaning and catharsis.
good-writing-000985.zh: 在非小说类作品中，作家们描述各种事件和争论，以寻求意义与心灵的慰藉。

good-writing-000986.en: The author has to know how the character made that decision or how the facts add up to a particular conclusion, including lots of backstory and logic, but the reader—or listener if, say, it’s a political speech—doesn’t always need all the background.
good-writing-000986.zh: 作者必须清楚，这个角色是如何做出那个决定的，或者各种事实是如何导致某个特定结论的。这其中包含了大量的背景信息和逻辑推理过程。但是，读者——或者如果这是一场政治演讲的话，听众——并不总需要了解所有这些背景信息。

good-writing-000987.en: Unlike in school, showing your work is not necessarily a virtue.
good-writing-000987.zh: 与在学校时不同，展示你的作业并不一定是一种优点。

good-writing-000988.en: Most of the boring stuff that needs to be removed is excess logical detail.
good-writing-000988.zh: 需要删除的那些繁琐内容，大多都是多余的逻辑细节。

good-writing-000989.en: Yes, people go to the bathroom, but that’s seldom a place for action relevant to the story, unless porcelain is the setting for an adulterous tryst during a party.
good-writing-000989.zh: 是的，人们会去卫生间，但那很少成为与故事相关的行动发生的场所，除非是在派对上发生不道德的约会时，环境才会变成类似卫生间这样的场景。

good-writing-000990.en: Yes, that minor character wears fifties-style birdwing eyeglass frames because she’s stuck in a conservative nostalgia for the past, but you can let the frames appear on her face without explanation.
good-writing-000990.zh: 是的，那个小角色戴着五零年代风格的鸟翼形眼镜框，因为她对过去怀有保守的怀旧情绪。不过，你可以让这些眼镜框出现在她的脸上，而不需要额外的解释。

good-writing-000991.en: And if the reader misses the point, well, it’s a minor character.
good-writing-000991.zh: 如果读者没有理解这个要点，那也没关系，毕竟他只是个次要角色而已。

good-writing-000992.en: Yes, Brown v. Board of Education was decided as much on modern sociological principles as on legal precedent, but unless you’re writing for a legal audience, that argument is probably less relevant than you think and you can leave it out.
good-writing-000992.zh: 是的，《布朗诉教育委员会案》的判决既基于现代社会学原理，也基于法律先例。不过，如果你不是为法律专业人士撰写文章的话，那么这种论点可能并不像你想象的那样重要，因此可以省略它。

good-writing-000993.en: Sometimes explaining is necessary and right.
good-writing-000993.zh: 有时候，进行解释是必要的，也是正确的做法。

good-writing-000994.en: At the end of a crime novel, a side character might ask the detective how they knew something, and that leads to a reminder of a clue the reader likely missed.
good-writing-000994.zh: 在犯罪小说的结尾部分，某个次要角色可能会向侦探询问他们是如何得知某些信息的，而这一提问会让人想起读者可能忽略的线索。

good-writing-000995.en: But a little explaining goes a long way.
good-writing-000995.zh: 不过，简单解释一下就能解决问题了。

good-writing-000996.en: Too much explaining is called “telegraphing,” and it’s not only boring, but insulting, too.
good-writing-000996.zh: 过多的解释被称为“冗长无味”，而且这种行为不仅令人厌烦，还会显得无礼。

good-writing-000997.en: We don’t want to be told things we can figure out on our own; reading a novel is solving a puzzle, anticipating consequences, trying to stay ahead of a fast-moving plot.
good-writing-000997.zh: 我们不希望别人告诉我们那些我们可以自己解决的问题；阅读小说就像解谜一样，需要预测各种后果，努力跟上快速发展的故事情节。

good-writing-000998.en: We tease our brains with novels.
good-writing-000998.zh: 我们用小说来娱乐自己的大脑。

good-writing-000999.en: If too much is explained, we find ourselves in a paint-by-numbers art class—accurate but lifeless.
good-writing-000999.zh: 如果解释得太多，我们就会像参加一种死记硬背的艺术课程一样——虽然结果很准确，但缺乏生机与活力。

good-writing-001000.en: As an inveterate explainer, I’m prone to overdoing it.
good-writing-001000.zh: 作为一个喜欢解释的人，我很容易就会说得太过火了。

good-writing-001001.en: Sometimes long after I’ve published something, I’ll notice a flaw in logic, often what’s called an enthymeme—jumping past a necessary condition to a conclusion.
good-writing-001001.zh: 有时候，在我已经发表完某个内容之后，我才会发现其中存在逻辑上的缺陷，通常这种缺陷被称为“隐含逻辑错误”——即从一个必要的前提直接推导出一个结论。

good-writing-001002.en: The root equation of logic is the syllogism, which has three steps: “All men are mortal. Socrates is a man. Therefore, Socrates is mortal.”
good-writing-001002.zh: 逻辑的基本公式是三段论：第一步“所有人都是有限的”；第二步“苏格拉底是一个人”；第三步“因此，苏格拉底是有限的”。

good-writing-001003.en: If I write “All men are mortal. Socrates is therefore mortal,” I’ve left out the middle term.
good-writing-001003.zh: 如果我写下“所有人类都是有限的，因此苏格拉底也是有限的”，那么我就省略了中间的部分。

good-writing-001004.en: It’s a form of jumping to conclusions, and a strict taboo in academic writing.
good-writing-001004.zh: 这是一种草率下结论的行为，在学术写作中是完全被禁止的。

good-writing-001005.en: No reader has ever pointed out a flaw in logic to me.
good-writing-001005.zh: 没有读者曾经指出过我逻辑上的任何错误。

good-writing-001006.en: Either they don’t care, or they don’t notice.
good-writing-001006.zh: 要么他们根本不在乎，要么他们根本没注意到。

good-writing-001007.en: Which frees me to include only the parts of an argument or scene that might leave an impression.
good-writing-001007.zh: 这让我可以只包含那些可能留下印象的论点或场景部分。

good-writing-001008.en: Let the reader assume you know what you’re talking about.
good-writing-001008.zh: 让读者假设你已经了解你所谈论的内容。

good-writing-001009.en: You’re not a professor or logician when writing for the casual reader.
good-writing-001009.zh: 当你为普通读者写作时，你并不属于教授或逻辑学家这一群体。

good-writing-001010.en: Hinting, foreshadowing, and misdirecting are all paths to the truth.
good-writing-001010.zh: 暗示、预示以及误导性的表达，都是通往真相的道路。

good-writing-001011.en: Often, explaining isn’t just unnecessary; it spoils the punch line.
good-writing-001011.zh: 通常，解释不仅毫无必要，反而还会破坏原文的精彩之处。

good-writing-001012.en: As puzzle solvers, we want only enough information to feel proud of getting to the answer ourselves.
good-writing-001012.zh: 作为解谜者，我们只需要获得足够的信息，能够自豪地自己找到答案。

good-writing-001013.en: Too much information and we think, “Well, any jerk could have figured that out.”
good-writing-001013.zh: 信息太多，以至于我们甚至认为：“唉，任何笨蛋都能猜出来啊。”

good-writing-001014.zh: 提示机制确保了游戏的公平性。

good-writing-001015.en: Foreshadowing sets the frame for the mind.
good-writing-001015.zh: 伏笔设置是为思维创造背景的要素。

good-writing-001016.en: Misdirection allows for appropriate curveballs and later revelations; we want things to not quite be what they seem, especially at the beginning of a puzzle.
good-writing-001016.zh: 这种误导手法能够制造出适当的意外转折和后续揭示；我们希望事物看起来并不像它们实际的样子，尤其是在谜题开始阶段。

good-writing-001017.zh: 不然的话，还有什么乐趣可言呢？

good-writing-001018.en: A meaning is what comes at the end of everything we conceive or do.
good-writing-001018.zh: 意义，就是存在于我们所构想或所进行的每一件事的终结处的一种东西。

good-writing-001019.en: Part of doing and conceiving things is concluding them.
good-writing-001019.zh: 创造和构思事物的过程，其中很重要的一步就是将其完成。

good-writing-001020.en: We substitute the word “meaning” for the word “conclusion,” but that’s mostly what a meaning is: a sentence played back to oneself at the end of an experience.
good-writing-001020.zh: 我们将“意义”这个词替换成了“结论”，但实际上，意义本质上就是这样的：在经历结束后，对某个句子进行回顾时所呈现出的感受。

good-writing-001021.en: In that way, a meaning is the last square entered in a crossword puzzle.
good-writing-001021.zh: 换句话说，意思就是纵横字谜中最后被填入的方块。

good-writing-001022.en: Once entered, the puzzle registers as complete.
good-writing-001022.zh: 一旦输入完毕，这个谜题就被视为完成。

good-writing-001023.en: I never have to look at it again.
good-writing-001023.zh: 我以后再也不需要看到它了。

good-writing-001025.en: Of all the most important rules, this is the most important one of all.
good-writing-001025.zh: 在所有最重要的规则中，这一条是最为重要的。

good-writing-001026.en: I think Neal has done a good job addressing the issue, although I think the stuff about enthymeme, and Socrates, is a little boring; also, show-offy.
good-writing-001026.zh: 我认为尼尔在解决这个问题方面做得很好，不过关于enteimema以及苏格拉底的那些内容，我觉得有点乏味，而且显得有些做作。

good-writing-001027.en: You have to give him credit, though, for how succinctly he describes the problem and the solution.
good-writing-001027.zh: 不过，他描述问题及解决方案的方式非常简洁明了，这一点确实值得肯定。

good-writing-001028.en: Take out about a third of the descriptions, editorializing, and details.
good-writing-001028.zh: 去掉大约三分之一的描述、评论以及细节内容。

good-writing-001029.en: I assume that Neal’s original meditation on this rule was somewhat longer, however, and he already did take out (most of) the boring stuff.
good-writing-001029.zh: 我认为，尼尔最初对这条规则的探讨其实更为深入一些，而且他确实已经删除了那些繁琐的内容。

good-writing-001030.en: FYI, as I am writing nonfiction these days, I also go through the final draft and take out all the lies that I can bear to part with.
good-writing-001030.zh: 供您参考，这几天我在撰写非虚构作品时，也会仔细审阅最终稿，并剔除所有我无法忍受的谎言。

good-writing-001031.en: I probably leave in close to a quarter of the lies, the ones that I might call exaggerations, or composites.
good-writing-001031.zh: 我可能会省略掉大约四分之一的谎言，那些可以被称作夸张或虚构的内容。

good-writing-001032.en: I definitely take out the things I shoehorned in that I wish had happened but didn’t, or that put me in a more sympathetic/desperate light so the reader will feel sorry for me or anxious on my behalf, and like me more.
good-writing-001032.zh: 我肯定会把那些我勉强加入的内容删掉——那些本来应该出现但并未出现的情节，或者那些让我看起来更可怜/更绝望的情节。这样，读者就会对我产生同情，或者为我感到焦虑，从而更愿意喜欢我。

good-writing-001033.en: There is nothing more stunning than the truth presented as carefully and unvarnished as one can get away with; and nothing more boring than a lot of details and descriptions that make you feel like you’re listening to an eight-year-old narrate a movie plot.
good-writing-001033.zh: 没有什么比那些被精心呈现、不加修饰的真相更令人惊叹的了；也没有什么比那些充满细节和描述的内容更无趣的——这些描述会让你觉得自己像是在听一个八岁的孩子讲述电影情节一样。

good-writing-001035.en: Don’t repeat a distinctive word unless you must.
good-writing-001035.zh: 除非确有必要，否则不要重复使用一个特别显眼的词。

good-writing-001036.en: Don’t repeat the same word in a paragraph.
good-writing-001036.zh: 在一段文字中不要重复使用同一个词。

good-writing-001037.en: Don’t repeat the same unusual usage in a chapter.
good-writing-001037.zh: 在某一章节中，不要重复使用相同的特殊用法。

good-writing-001038.en: Don’t repeat the same aphorism in a book.
good-writing-001038.zh: 不要在一本书中重复相同的格言。

good-writing-001039.zh: 经过验证的例外情况非常常见。

good-writing-001040.en: (Prepositions, pronouns, connectors—those sorts of skeleton tools of speech—don’t count.)
good-writing-001040.zh: （介词、代词、连接词——这些所谓的“语言的基本要素”并不算数。）

good-writing-001041.zh: 我们人类追求新奇的事物。

good-writing-001042.en: We constantly pull things close to examine them.
good-writing-001042.zh: 我们总是把东西拉近一些以便进行观察。

good-writing-001045.en: They’re oddly the same thing, curiosity and joy.
good-writing-001045.zh: 它们其实本质上是相同的东西——那就是好奇心与喜悦。

good-writing-001046.en: We want to catch what’s new and different, and get tickled by the knowledge or the upcoming puzzle and how the new object fits in.
good-writing-001046.zh: 我们渴望捕捉到那些新鲜且独特的事物，享受那些即将揭晓的谜题所带来的乐趣，以及新出现的对象如何与这些谜题相契合。

good-writing-001047.en: If I encounter a distinctive word, I don’t want to see it again for a while.
good-writing-001047.zh: 如果我遇到一个不常见的词，我希望在一段时间内都不再看到它。

good-writing-001048.en: I already got a kick out of it, and as with my taste buds, I need time between bites before it can again jolt me with a thrill.
good-writing-001048.zh: 我已经从中获得了乐趣，就像我的味觉一样，需要时间让食物再次给我带来刺激感。

good-writing-001050.en: Above, I get away with repeating the words “curiosity” and “joy” because I’ve offered them in a novel switch, making them synonyms.
good-writing-001050.zh: 在上面，我通过重复“好奇心”和“喜悦”这两个词来避免重复，因为我把这两个词用了一个新颖的关联词来连接，使它们成为同义词。

good-writing-001051.en: An exception to not repeating a distinctive word is called “bridging.”
good-writing-001051.zh: 如果某个独特的单词没有被重复出现，这种情况就被称为“桥接”。

good-writing-001052.en: Sometimes using a word or phrase repeatedly helps speed the reader from one sentence to the next, in a rhythmic trance.
good-writing-001052.zh: 有时候，反复使用某个词或短语可以帮助读者以有节奏的方式快速地过渡到下一个句子。

good-writing-001053.en: Here’s a single stanza from Edgar Allan Poe that bridges through repeating a name:
good-writing-001053.zh: 以下是埃德加·艾伦·坡作品中的一节诗，其中通过重复一个名字来营造一种循环往复的效果：

good-writing-001054.en: For the moon never beams, without bringing me dreams
good-writing-001054.zh: 月亮从不照耀，也无法带给我梦想

good-writing-001055.zh: 关于美丽的安娜贝尔·李；

good-writing-001056.en: And the stars never rise, but I feel the bright eyes
good-writing-001056.zh: 而星星永远不会升起，但我能感受到那明亮的目光

good-writing-001057.zh: 关于美丽的安娜贝尔·李；

good-writing-001058.en: There’s a reason Martin Luther King’s March on Washington Address became known as the “I Have a Dream” speech.
good-writing-001058.zh: 马丁·路德·金在华盛顿的演讲被命名为“我有一个梦想”是有原因的。

good-writing-001059.en: For ten years starting in 1966, televangelist Kathryn Kuhlman began her weekly show with the words “I believe in miracles. Why do I believe in miracles? Because I believe in God.” “I believe” and “miracles” rose as sturdy bulwarks to contain her message—and her flock.
