good-writing-001059.zh: 从1966年开始，电视传教士凯瑟琳·库尔曼每周都会播出她的节目，节目开头总是这样说道：“我相信奇迹的存在。我为什么相信奇迹呢？因为我相信上帝的存在。” “我相信”和“奇迹”这两个词，成为了她传播信息的核心概念——也是她所带领的追随者们的信仰基础。

good-writing-001061.en: You cannot use an exotic word twice in the same book, because we will feel we have caught you trying to slip something past us, and we will turn on you.
good-writing-001061.zh: 在同一本书中，你不能使用同一个生僻词汇两次。因为如果我们发现你试图使用这个生僻词汇来隐藏某些信息，我们就会立刻抓住你，并追究你的责任。

good-writing-001062.en: Also, never use “bloom” even though it is a beautiful word, because everyone has taken to overusing it to sound poetic.
good-writing-001062.zh: 另外，永远不要使用“bloom”这个词，尽管它听起来很优美，但实际上大家都过度使用了这个词，以至于它变得过于雕琢化，失去了原本的简洁之美。

good-writing-001063.en: Once you start to look for “bloom,” it will disrupt every work of fiction you read, and ruin otherwise pleasant literary experiences.
good-writing-001063.zh: 一旦你开始寻找“美感”这种东西，它就会破坏你读到的每一部小说，并毁掉原本愉快的文学体验。

good-writing-001064.en: Only in emergency situations is it OK to use “granular,” “existential,” “myriad,” “bespoke,” “lament,” and, of course, “cherish.”
good-writing-001064.zh: 只有在紧急情况下，才可以使用“颗粒化的”、“存在的”、“无数的”、“量身定制的”、“哀叹”这些词汇，当然，还有“珍视”这个词。

good-writing-001066.en: I also don’t recommend any word that you pause to carefully define in your mind before setting down, such as “liminal.”
good-writing-001066.zh: 我也不建议使用那些需要仔细定义、并在书写前先明确其含义的词汇，比如“liminal”这个词。

good-writing-001067.en: This is yet another reason you need someone to look over your work before you send it off to an editor or agent in the hope of publication: Your own eye will have glanced off exotic words that you have repeated, in its desire to keep moving through the material.
good-writing-001067.zh: 这又是另一个需要有人先仔细审阅你的作品的原因——这样在将作品提交给编辑或出版商之前，可以及时发现那些你重复使用的生僻词汇。毕竟，编辑在审阅作品时，难免会不自觉地浏览这些重复出现的词汇。

good-writing-001068.en: People have found descriptions and even one-liners repeated in my early drafts, but more frequently phrases that I just love, love, love.
good-writing-001068.zh: 人们发现，在我的早期草稿中，有一些描述甚至俏皮话被反复使用；不过，更常见的是那些我特别喜欢的表达方式。

good-writing-001069.en: This is not a moral failing, but the reality of having to keep track of various ideas and characters over many pages.
good-writing-001069.zh: 这不是一种道德上的缺陷，而只是需要在许多页面上记录各种想法和角色的现实需求而已。

good-writing-001070.en: If a friend catches repeated or pretentious words in your manuscript before you send it off, it is customary to offer them your first grandchild or a fancy dinner, their choice.
good-writing-001070.zh: 如果朋友在您提交手稿之前发现您手稿中有重复出现或过于夸张的词汇，那么按照惯例，您应该赠送他们您的第一个孙辈或一顿高档晚餐——这由他们自己选择。

good-writing-001071.en: Rule 16: Know Your Words Inside and Out

good-writing-001072.en: Examining the etymology of words makes them more concrete and useful.
good-writing-001072.zh: 探究词语的词源，可以让它们的含义更具体，也更便于运用。

good-writing-001073.en: The complete etymology of a word is tucked into its current meaning.
good-writing-001073.zh: 一个词的完整词源已经融入了它的现代含义之中。

good-writing-001074.zh: 了解你使用的重点词汇的起源。

good-writing-001075.en: Most words trace back to orientation (up/down, front/back) or resources (full/empty).
good-writing-001075.zh: 大多数词汇都可以追溯到方向（上下、前后）或资源（满/空）这两个概念。

good-writing-001076.en: So does most of life; our basic functions are to go places for things to fill up our stomach or bag or time, and our most sophisticated ideas also have direction and fulfillment.
good-writing-001076.zh: 大多数生命活动都是如此；我们的基本功能是为各种需求去移动物体、填饱我们的肚子或填充我们的时间，而我们最复杂的想法也同样具有明确的方向和目的。

good-writing-001077.en: Sometimes just noticing the connections to a word’s antecedents can open up new passages to write.
good-writing-001077.zh: 有时候，仅仅注意到某个词与其前后词之间的关联，就能为写作打开新的可能性。

good-writing-001078.en: Say I’m discussing truth, which originally meant “tree.”
good-writing-001078.zh: 我说的是“真理”，而“真理”这个词最初指的是“树”。

good-writing-001079.en: By picturing a tree, I might note solidity, permanence, aliveness, stillness, slowness, cycles, and rootedness as possible attributes of the truth I’m describing.
good-writing-001079.zh: 通过想象一棵树，我可以将“实体性、持久性、生命感、宁静、缓慢、循环性以及根植性”等特性，视为我所描述的“真理”的潜在属性。

good-writing-001080.en: When a word sticks out as distinctive or strange or somehow important to the text, you might investigate its etymology.
good-writing-001080.zh: 当一个词在文本中显得特别、独特或具有某种重要性时，你可以研究一下这个词的词源。

good-writing-001081.en: Writing is about connections and leaps of imagination, and those too are tucked into etymologies.
good-writing-001081.zh: 写作涉及各种联系和丰富的想象力，而这些元素也都被融入到词源学中。

good-writing-001082.en: Three words—synonyms usually—fascinate me more than any other: “satisfaction,” “equanimity,” and “contentment.”
good-writing-001082.zh: 有三个词——通常是同义词——让我特别着迷： “满足感”、“平静心”以及“知足”。

good-writing-001083.en: While most of our decisions are made from at least faint dissatisfaction, we hope to land in satisfaction.
good-writing-001083.zh: 虽然我们大多数决策都是出于某种程度的不满而做出的，但我们希望最终能够获得满足感。

good-writing-001084.en: Buddhists describe equanimity as a desirable state of grace, maybe the ultimate result of all that meditation.
good-writing-001084.zh: 佛教徒将平等心描述为一种令人向往的境界，或许这是所有冥想努力的最终成果吧。

good-writing-001085.en: Contented cows produce the best milk, we’re told.
good-writing-001085.zh: 我们听说，满足的奶牛会产出最优质的牛奶。

good-writing-001086.en: Now where do these words come from and why do I care?
good-writing-001086.zh: 这些词是从哪里来的呢？为什么我会关心它们呢？

good-writing-001087.en: “Satisfaction” etymologically leads us to satiation, which is a property of digestion, and the opposite of hunger.
good-writing-001087.zh: “Satisfaction”一词在词源上源自“satiation”，而“satiation”则指的是消化的过程，与“饥饿”相反。

good-writing-001088.en: What would it mean if satisfaction left me with the feeling of a hamburger in my belly?
good-writing-001088.zh: 如果满足感让我只感觉到肚子里有汉堡的感觉，那这算什么意思呢？

good-writing-001089.en: That sounds crass at first, but don’t we have sexual hunger, too?
good-writing-001089.zh: 乍看之下，这听起来可能有些粗俗，但难道我们不是也有这种性的渴望吗？

good-writing-001090.en: Or an appetite for work or play?
good-writing-001090.zh: 或者是对工作或娱乐的渴望呢？

good-writing-001091.en: Something in our past recognized a kinship between food and sex, work, and play.
good-writing-001091.zh: 我们过去的经历中，似乎已经认识到食物、性爱、工作以及娱乐之间存在着某种联系。

good-writing-001092.en: Knowing that might lead the characters in your novel into new understandings.
good-writing-001092.zh: 了解这一点可能会让小说中的角色们获得新的领悟。

good-writing-001093.en: “Equanimity” etymologically takes us to an ancient word for “calmness” pressed against a word for “mind” that refers further back to a synonym for “breath.”
good-writing-001093.zh: “Equanimity”一词的词源可以追溯到一个古老的词汇，意为“平静”；而“equanimity”又与另一个表示“心智”的词汇相关联，这两个词汇又都与“呼吸”这一概念有联系。

good-writing-001094.en: So I might notice a calm breath after exercise, or during meditation, or the calm mind that allows me to stop being offended by other people’s foibles.
good-writing-001094.zh: 因此，我可能会在锻炼后或冥想时感受到一种平静的呼吸；或者，我也能体会到那种能够让我不再被他人的小毛病所冒犯的平静心态。

good-writing-001095.en: “Contentment” is the weirdest of the three.
good-writing-001095.zh: “满足感”是三者中最奇怪的一种。

good-writing-001096.en: It hearkens back to a Proto-Indo-European word for “extension,” as if this kind of grace is tied to a feeling of expansiveness or limitlessness or simply space.
good-writing-001096.zh: 它似乎源自一个原始印欧语中的词汇，意为“延伸”；这种优雅感似乎与一种扩张感、无限感，或者仅仅是空间感有关。

good-writing-001097.en: If I’m content, does the world empty of things and smooth out into a plain?
good-writing-001097.zh: 如果我感到满足，那么世界会变得空无所有，变得平坦无垠吗？

good-writing-001098.en: If your character is described as “content” as he is driving, do his eyes scan out to the horizon?
good-writing-001098.zh: 如果描述中表明你的角色在驾驶时显得“满足”，那么他的眼睛是否会注视着地平线呢？

good-writing-001099.en: So three words that mean about the same thing emerge from distinct human interests that offer the possibility of liberation: breath, relief from hunger, and expansiveness.
good-writing-001099.zh: 因此，有三个词表达了类似的意义，它们源自人们不同的需求，这些需求为解脱提供了可能性：呼吸、摆脱饥饿、以及心灵的广阔。

good-writing-001100.en: Why are these three words so interesting to me?
good-writing-001100.zh: 为什么这三个词会让我如此感兴趣呢？

good-writing-001101.en: For one thing, they’re about all we have to describe the endpoint of all our yearning in one word.
good-writing-001101.zh: 首先，它们可以用一个词来描述我们所有渴望的终点。

good-writing-001102.en: You’d think we’d have dozens of words that mean exactly what these three represent—one pinnacle of human experience—but we don’t.
good-writing-001102.zh: 你可能会认为，我们有许多词汇能够准确表达这三种人类体验的精髓——但它们其实并不存在。

good-writing-001103.en: By the way, knowing that the word “truth” is derived from an ancient word for “tree” might give you the statement “as true as a tree,” which oddly enough isn’t a cliché.
good-writing-001103.zh: 顺便提一下，了解到“真理”这个词源自一个表示“树”的古老词汇，这可能会让你想到“像树一样真实”这样的表达。有趣的是，这其实并不是什么陈词滥调。

good-writing-001104.en: Feel free to steal it and take credit for coining a new metaphor.
good-writing-001104.zh: 请随意使用它，并声称这是你创造了新的比喻手法。

good-writing-001106.en: Some of you—a few of you—will not end up getting published, but that is not the point of the writing life.
good-writing-001106.zh: 你们当中有些人——仅仅少数几个人——的文章可能最终不会被发表，但那并非写作生活的意义所在。

good-writing-001107.en: If you’re a writer, the point is to write, at least a little every day, and to commit to full immersion in the writing life.
good-writing-001107.zh: 如果你是一名作家，那么关键就是每天至少写一点东西，并且全身心投入写作的生涯中。

good-writing-001108.en: This means reading about craft, sitting at the feet of masters from every era, studying how they create brilliance, and becoming better and better writers.
good-writing-001108.zh: 这意味着要阅读有关写作技巧的书籍，向各个时代的写作大师们学习他们如何创造出卓越的作品，从而成为更优秀的作家。

good-writing-001109.en: Learning where words spring from enhances your fascination for what we are all up to here, which is creating meaning.
good-writing-001109.zh: 了解词语的起源能够增强我们对于创造意义的兴趣。我们所做的这一切，本质上都是为了创造意义。

good-writing-001112.en: Let’s look up the roots of the word “writing.”
good-writing-001112.zh: 让我们来探究一下“writing”这个词的起源吧。

good-writing-001113.en: It goes back through the Middle English word writen, from Old English wrītan, from Proto-Germanic wrītaną (“to carve, write”), and finally from the Proto-Indo-European *wrey- (“to rip, tear”).
good-writing-001113.zh: 这个词的起源可以追溯到中古英语中的“writen”一词，而“writen”又源自古英语中的“wrītan”，该词又源自原始日耳曼语中的“wrītaną”，意为“雕刻、书写”。最终，这个词的起源又可以追溯到原始印欧语中的“*wrey-”，意为“撕裂、切割”。

good-writing-001116.en: Into bark, which is what papyrus is made from, and on which people began telling their stories 4,500 years ago.
good-writing-001116.zh: 使用的是莎草纸这种材料，而人们从4,500年前开始就使用这种材料来记录他们的故事。

good-writing-001117.en: To tear down, like Murasaki Shikibu in the eleventh century, Charles Darwin and Shakespeare and Harriet Beecher Stowe, Karl Marx, Walt Whitman, and Emily Dickinson.
good-writing-001117.zh: 要摧毁它们，就像十一世纪时的紫式部那样，摧毁查尔斯·达尔文、莎士比亚、哈丽特·比彻·斯托，卡尔·马克思、沃尔特·惠特曼，以及艾米丽·迪金森。

good-writing-001119.en: To carve into, to tear down, to create.
good-writing-001119.zh: 进行切割、破坏，然后创造。

good-writing-001120.en: The verb “to create” is from the Proto-Indo-European root *ḱerh, whose original meaning seems to have been “to grow.”
good-writing-001120.zh: 动词“创造”源自原始印欧语根*ḱerh，其最初的含义似乎是“生长”。

good-writing-001122.en: To plant, to seed, to tend to, to produce, to bring forth.
good-writing-001122.zh: 去种植，去播种，去照料，去培育，去产出。

good-writing-001123.en: This is the very work of the writer, to create a garden into which the reader may enter, with a path from where we begin, through the main characters—the commoners (daisies, poppies), the elite people (purple Eleanor Roosevelt irises, yellow roses of Texas), and the weeds, those damn weeds.
good-writing-001123.zh: 这正是作家的使命所在：创造出一个可供读者进入的“花园”。我们从一个起点开始，穿过各种人物——普通人（如雏菊、罂粟花）、精英人物（如紫色的埃莉奥诺拉·罗斯福鸢尾花、德克萨斯州的黄色玫瑰）——以及那些讨厌的杂草。

good-writing-001124.en: And the soil, the rocks and earth you have chosen to root your stories in, with words.
good-writing-001124.zh: 以及那些你选择作为故事根基的土壤、岩石和大地，用文字来承载这些元素。

good-writing-001125.en: My brilliant friend the writer Abigail Thomas was feeling guilt-stricken for putting together a happy life after her husband had to move permanently to a nearby nursing home: “So I got my American Heritage Dictionary of Indo-European Roots, looked up ‘guilt,’ which had historically always been ‘guilt’; ugh—nothing useful there. Then I looked up ‘acceptance,’ and found it had derived from a word meaning ‘a thread used in weaving.’ My life changed on that dime.”
good-writing-001125.zh: 我的好友、作家阿比盖尔·托马斯因为丈夫不得不永久搬去附近的养老院而感到非常内疚，她试图为自己创造一种幸福的生活。于是她查阅了《美国传统印欧语根词典》，查找“guilt”这个词的释义。历史上的“guilt”一直被解释为“一种用于编织的线”。结果，她发现“acceptance”这个词的起源与“一种用于编织的线”这个意思有关。从那一刻起，她的生活发生了改变。

good-writing-001127.en: The better word is both precise and unnoticed.
good-writing-001127.zh: 更好的用词既准确，又不会刻意引人注意。

good-writing-001128.en: A thesaurus is your book of magic spells.
good-writing-001128.zh: 同义词词典，就是你的魔法咒语书。

good-writing-001129.en: If a word reads false to me, it will to the reader.
good-writing-001129.zh: 如果一个词在我读起来显得不自然，那么在读者读的时候也会显得如此。

good-writing-001130.en: In some ways you want to underestimate your reader’s intelligence.
good-writing-001130.zh: 在某些方面，你希望低估读者的智力水平。

good-writing-001131.zh: 不要使用晦涩难懂的词汇。

good-writing-001133.en: Dumb down while conveying the same information.
good-writing-001133.zh: 在传达相同信息的情况下，使用更简洁的表达方式。

good-writing-001134.en: But in other ways, you can’t overestimate your reader’s smarts.
good-writing-001134.zh: 但在其他方面，你无法高估读者的智慧。

good-writing-001135.en: They will pick out anything that looks phony, out of place, or not quite right.
good-writing-001135.zh: 他们会挑出任何看起来虚假、不自然或不符合标准的东西。

good-writing-001136.en: Part of keeping the scenery seamless is getting the words just ducky.
good-writing-001136.zh: 保持画面流畅性的关键之一，就是让文字的显示恰到好处，不会显得过于拥挤。

good-writing-001138.en: Yes, it’s full of fancy words, but it’s mostly made up of common words that you don’t regularly use.
good-writing-001138.zh: 是的，里面确实充满了一些复杂的词汇，但大部分内容都是由那些你并不常用的普通词汇构成的。

good-writing-001139.en: And one of them is closest to what you mean.
good-writing-001139.zh: 其中有一个表达与你想要表达的意思最为接近。

good-writing-001140.en: As a cub reporter at the Daily Freeman forty-five years ago, I would often lean across to my fellow scribe Craig Gilbert’s desk and call out, “I need a word for [so-and-so].”
good-writing-001140.zh: 四十五年前，我还是《每日自由报》的一名新记者。经常我会走到同事克雷格·吉尔伯特的办公桌旁，对他说：“我需要跟[某人]说几句话。”

good-writing-001141.en: If I said, “The owner of a clothes store,” Craig would respond instantly, “Haberdasher.”
good-writing-001141.zh: 如果我说：“一家服装店的老板”，克雷格会立刻回答：“Haberdasher。”

good-writing-001143.en: But I also knew that “haberdasher” would look ridiculous in a daily newspaper unless used to describe Harry Truman.
good-writing-001143.zh: 不过我也知道，“haberdasher”这个词在日报上使用时会显得很荒谬，除非是用来描述哈里·杜鲁门这样的历史人物。

good-writing-001144.en: “No, that won’t work. What else you got?”
good-writing-001144.zh: “不，那样行不通。你还有别的办法吗？”

good-writing-001145.en: And Craig would rattle away, “Storekeeper, proprietor, merchant...” until he hit the right one and I cut him off with, “Retailer. That’s it!”
good-writing-001145.zh: 克雷格会滔滔不绝地念叨着“店主、业主、商人……”直到他找到正确的那个为止。然后我打断他，说：“零售商。就这样吧！”

good-writing-001146.en: When I no longer worked in the same newsroom as Craig, I bought the fattest thesaurus I could find.
good-writing-001146.zh: 当我不再与克雷格在同一新闻编辑部工作时，我买下了我能找到的最厚的词库。

good-writing-001148.en: I also now have an Annie around.
good-writing-001148.zh: 我现在也有一个叫安妮的人陪伴着我了。

good-writing-001149.en: More than half of our time collaborating—reading, remarking, editing, discussing—is spent on synonyms.
good-writing-001149.zh: 我们一半以上的时间都用于合作——阅读、评论、编辑、讨论等事务上。这些工作都涉及到同义词的使用。

good-writing-001150.en: She calls out from the other room, “What’s the word for the plastic thingamabob at the end of a shoelace?”
good-writing-001150.zh: 她从另一个房间喊道：“鞋带末的那个塑料小玩意儿，它的学名是什么？”

good-writing-001153.en: This commandment to find the perfect word trips over Rule 15, which suggests that you shouldn’t use the same word twice in a paragraph.
good-writing-001153.zh: 这条“寻找完美词语”的指令违反了规则15的规定，该规则要求在一个段落中不应使用相同的词语两次。

good-writing-001154.en: You lose all your points for not repeating a word when the second reference is a stretch.
good-writing-001154.zh: 如果你在第二次引用时重复了同一个词，那么你的所有积分都会清零。

good-writing-001155.en: “The thirty-six rules were a formula for success. Other writing algorithms had failed him.”
good-writing-001155.zh: 这三十六条规则是通往成功的秘笈。其他写作方法都未能帮助他取得成功。

good-writing-001156.en: Sometimes it’s hard work to find the right word.
good-writing-001156.zh: 有时候，找到合适的词语真的需要付出努力。

good-writing-001157.en: It might force a change in sentence structure.
good-writing-001157.zh: 这可能会迫使句子结构发生改变。

good-writing-001158.en: My friend Yeshim Ternar used to write her short stories in longhand, and in tiny handwriting stacked possible synonyms on top of prominent words.
good-writing-001158.zh: 我的朋友耶希姆·特纳尔过去常常用长体字来写作她的短篇故事，她的笔迹非常细小，会在重要的词语上方标出所有可能的同义词。

good-writing-001159.en: She knew to torture the critical words.
good-writing-001159.zh: 她知道如何巧妙地使用那些具有批判性的词语。

good-writing-001160.en: She seemed to spend as much time reviewing individual words as she did writing the sentences in the first place.
good-writing-001160.zh: 她似乎在复习单个单词上花费的时间，与最初撰写句子时花费的时间一样多。

good-writing-001161.en: When I was newspapering, I often got into my biggest trouble with sources or subjects over an unfortunate word choice.
good-writing-001161.zh: 在从事新闻工作的时候，我经常因为一些不恰当的词汇选择而遇到麻烦。这些不恰当的词汇选择往往会导致与消息来源或主题相关的重大问题。

good-writing-001162.en: Early in my career, I reported the discovery of the body of a missing hiker.
good-writing-001162.zh: 在我的职业生涯初期，我报道了失踪徒步者的遗体被发现的情况。

good-writing-001163.en: Imagine how his parents felt when they saw my story refer to his remains as his “carcass.”
good-writing-001163.zh: 想象一下，当他的父母看到我的报道中把他的遗体称为“尸体”时，他们会有怎样的感受。

good-writing-001164.en: I found out when they complained to the publisher.
good-writing-001164.zh: 我是在他们向出版商投诉时才知道这件事的。

good-writing-001165.en: A month later in a story about an amateur astronomer, I mentioned the portly gentleman’s “distended stomach,” and to my everlasting shame received a nasty letter in which he described a harrowing disease that swelled his abdomen, and he banned me for life from his backyard planetarium.
good-writing-001165.zh: 一个月后，在一篇关于业余天文学家的报道中，我提到了那位身材肥胖的先生所患的“腹部膨胀”疾病。令我感到无比羞愧的是，我收到了他的严厉批评信，他在信中描述了自己所患的痛苦疾病，并让我永远不得进入他的后院天文馆。

good-writing-001167.en: Sometimes when I am hurrying to get to the next paragraph, or trying to impress the reader with my erudition, I’ll use a word that is pretentious or overwrought, and I’ll leave it there either as a placeholder or in the hopes that when I return to it in the edit, it will turn out to be fine.
good-writing-001167.zh: 有时候，当我急于推进文章到下一个段落时，或者试图用我的学识来吸引读者时，我会使用一些显得浮夸或过分的词语。我会把这些词语留在这里，或者作为过渡性措辞，希望在编辑时，这些词语不会影响到文章的整体效果。

good-writing-001168.en: But when I get to it during the reread, I’ll feel a minor sense of dread and embarrassment—“Oh my God, I don’t even know what ‘thaumaturgy’ means!” (It’s the ability of a magician to work real magic, instead of sleight of hand. Don’t ever use it in a sentence. We’ll snicker to ourselves that you are trying too hard.)
good-writing-001168.zh: 但在重新阅读的时候，我会感到一些轻微的恐惧和尴尬——“天啊，我甚至不知道‘魔法术’到底是什么意思！”（所谓“魔法术”，指的是魔术师能够施展真正的魔法，而不是那些花哨的把戏。绝对不要在任何句子中使用这个术语。我们可能会嘲笑你试图过度使用这个术语的举动。）

good-writing-001169.en: A thesaurus is great, not because you can find fancy silver-dollar words that will make people think you are the literary Stephen Hawking, but rather because you can find the perfect buffalo-head nickel word, down-to-earth and trustworthy and all you need.
good-writing-001169.zh: 一个词库非常实用，不是因为你可以找到那些听起来很文艺的词汇，让人以为自己像是文学界的斯蒂芬·霍金，而是因为你可以找到那些简单、直接且易于理解的词汇，这些词汇正好满足你的需求。

good-writing-001170.en: That comfort, as in real life, is a wonderful thing.
good-writing-001170.zh: 这种舒适感，就像在现实生活中一样，是一种美妙的东西。

good-writing-001171.en: Every writer has had the experience of having gone over an important sentence four or five times, obsessed with finding the right word.
good-writing-001171.zh: 每个作家都经历过这样的情景：反复修改同一个句子好几次，一心只想找到最合适的词语来表达自己的想法。

good-writing-001172.en: You like the image or the idea, but you keep changing your mind.
good-writing-001172.zh: 你喜欢这个形象或这个概念，但你不断改变自己的想法。

good-writing-001173.en: You can’t decide: Is a wispy palm frond feathery or feathered, plumed or plumose (which means having filaments of branches that sustain a feathery appearance)?
good-writing-001173.zh: 你无法判断：那种纤细的棕榈叶叶缘是呈羽毛状，还是更偏向于羽毛般的形态？或者，它是否更像是带有细丝的叶缘，从而呈现出羽毛般的视觉效果？

good-writing-001174.en: “Plumose” is almost exactly right, but you cannot use it because it is obscure and esoteric and phony.
good-writing-001174.zh: “Plumose”这个词汇几乎完全准确，但我们不能使用它，因为这个词的含义模糊、深奥且带有虚假的色彩。

good-writing-001177.en: You send your work off to an editor, agent, or someone at a quarterly who has asked to see it, and you bolt awake at dawn filled with dread and self-loathing.
good-writing-001177.zh: 你把作品寄给编辑、代理人，或者那些要求查看作品的第三方。而到了黎明时分，你醒来时心中充满了恐惧和自我厌恶。

good-writing-001178.en: They are going to laugh at how pretentious you sound, and in fact read it out loud to nearby editors.
good-writing-001178.zh: 他们会嘲笑你听起来多么做作，实际上他们还会把你的话大声读给周围的编辑们听。

good-writing-001180.en: Personally, I would use “feathery” to describe the leaflets of a frond.
good-writing-001180.zh: 我个人会用“羽毛般的”来形容叶子的质地。

good-writing-001181.en: But the right word for me might not be the right word for you.
good-writing-001181.zh: 但对我来说正确的词，可能对你来说并不正确。

good-writing-001182.en: For instance, there is a zero chance I would ever use the word “ducky,” as Neal does above: “Part of keeping the scenery seamless is getting the words just ducky.”
good-writing-001182.zh: 例如，我绝对不会使用“ducky”这个词，就像尼尔上面所写的那样：“要使对话的流畅性达到最佳，就必须选择恰到好处、符合语境的词汇。”

good-writing-001183.en: I mentioned this to him, with perhaps a little contempt, and suggested he take it out.
good-writing-001183.zh: 我向他提到了这一点，可能还带有一点轻蔑的语气，并建议他把它处理掉。

good-writing-001184.en: He said he was leaving it in, and our editor could decide.
good-writing-001184.zh: 他说他会把它留在那里，由我们的编辑来决定如何处理。

good-writing-001185.en: So if you have come upon “ducky,” you’ll know whose side our editor is on.
good-writing-001185.zh: 所以，如果你遇到了“Ducky”，那么你就知道我们的编辑支持谁的观点了。

good-writing-001186.en: I would have said “getting the words right” or “choosing the right words.”
good-writing-001186.zh: 我可能会说“用正确的词语表达”或者“选择恰当的词语”。

good-writing-001187.en: No one expects this marriage to last.
good-writing-001187.zh: 没人期望这段婚姻能够持续下去。

good-writing-001189.en: Metaphors mirror humdrum experiences through elegant comparison.
good-writing-001189.zh: 比喻通过精妙的比较，映照平凡的生活体验。

good-writing-001190.en: In the hands of an expert, they both illuminate and offer depth of field.
good-writing-001190.zh: 在高手笔下，比喻既能使事物豁然清晰，又能赋予它们层次和纵深。

good-writing-001191.en: In his discussion of writing, titled Poetics, Aristotle states, “The greatest thing by far is to be a master of metaphor.... It is a sign of genius, since a good metaphor implies an intuitive perception of the similarity in dissimilars.”
good-writing-001191.zh: 在《诗学》这一著作中，亚里士多德在讨论写作时指出：“最了不起的事情就是能够成为比喻的大师……这是一种天才的标志，因为一个好的比喻意味着对差异中的相似之处的直观感知。”

good-writing-001192.en: Aristotle’s is the common view, that metaphor is an authorial contrivance, an adornment that adds loftiness and cleverness to phrases that might otherwise sound crude or ordinary.
good-writing-001192.zh: 亚里士多德的观点是，隐喻是一种作者为了增强语句的优美和巧妙而创造出来的修辞手法，它能让原本可能显得粗糙或普通的话语变得更加生动有趣。

good-writing-001193.en: In the right hands—think Bob Dylan or Emily Dickinson—metaphor cuts to the quick of meaning and leaves the reader a little breathless.
good-writing-001193.zh: 在恰当的人手中——比如鲍勃·迪伦或艾米莉亚·狄金森——隐喻能够深刻地揭示意义的本质，让读者不禁屏息。

good-writing-001194.en: But our basic vocabulary, our ordinary and familiar everyday words, are also metaphorical.
good-writing-001194.zh: 但是，我们的基本词汇，那些日常中常用且熟悉的词语，其实也都具有隐喻性。

good-writing-001195.en: (I’m using the broad sense of metaphor, which includes simile and analogy.)
good-writing-001195.zh: 我使用的是广义的隐喻概念，其中包含了明喻和类比两种形式。

good-writing-001196.en: Look at the subhead for this rule.
good-writing-001196.zh: 看看这条规则的标题吧。

good-writing-001197.en: The verb “mirror” is a metaphor; no one’s literally holding up a shiny hand mirror to my page, hoping to catch sight of a metaphor.
good-writing-001197.zh: 动词“mirror”是一个比喻用法；实际上并没有人真的拿着一面闪亮的手镜来照我的页面，试图发现其中的比喻意味。

good-writing-001198.en: The hum in “humdrum” is from a beehive, which also shares the drone that humdrum implies.
good-writing-001198.zh: 歌曲《humdrum》中的那种嗡嗡声，其实源自蜂巢的鸣叫声，这种鸣叫声与《humdrum》中的旋律有着相似之处。

good-writing-001199.en: “Elegant” sounds awfully abstract, until its etymology is noticed: to pluck or root out.
good-writing-001199.zh: “Elegant”这个词听起来非常抽象，直到我们注意到它的词源：它意味着“采摘”或“根除”。

good-writing-001200.en: “In the hands of” isn’t literal; an expert writer isn’t showing me her palms full of goodies.
good-writing-001200.zh: “在……的手中”并不是字面意思；这位专家作家并没有向我展示她那些装满好处的手。

good-writing-001201.zh: 她没有递给我任何东西。

good-writing-001202.en: An “expert” is from the word for “first in line.”
good-writing-001202.zh: “专家”这个词来源于“排在最前面的人”的意思。

good-writing-001203.en: You may be tempted to insert metaphors in the most likely places—a description of an emotional reaction or a bit of local color.
good-writing-001203.zh: 你可能会倾向于在最合适的位置使用比喻手法——比如描述一种情感反应或增添一些地域特色。

good-writing-001204.en: Go ahead and do that, making sure the metaphor captures the thought well and succinctly, pinning down a subtle characteristic of the person or experience at hand.
good-writing-001204.zh: 请继续这样做吧，确保这个比喻能够很好地表达你的想法，并且简洁明了地概括出所描述的人物或经历中的某个微妙特征。

good-writing-001205.zh: 但是，这些隐喻可以适用于任何场合。

good-writing-001206.en: A parable is a metaphor, as are allegories and analogies.
good-writing-001206.zh: 寓言是一种比喻手法，这与象征和类比一样，都属于比喻的范畴。

good-writing-001207.en: Fairy tales are metaphors, as is any moral tale.
good-writing-001207.zh: 童话故事其实都是隐喻，任何道德故事也是如此。

good-writing-001208.en: Your moral thoughts operate metaphorically, taking a skeletal system of good versus bad, right versus wrong, first learned by rote as a child, then imposing it on a new situation, searching for what is similar.
good-writing-001208.zh: 你的道德观念是以一种比喻的方式运作的，它将“善”与“恶”、“对”与“错”这两个概念抽象化地呈现出来。这些概念最初是在童年时期被机械性地习得的，之后便被应用到新的情境中，试图找出其中的相似之处。

good-writing-001209.zh: 我们将其称为模式识别。

good-writing-001210.en: We might also call it metaphorical thinking.
good-writing-001210.zh: 我们也可以将其称为隐喻性思维。

good-writing-001211.en: Once you recognize that everything’s a metaphor, your notions of how to convey information may change.
good-writing-001211.zh: 一旦你认识到一切都是一种隐喻，那么你传递信息的观念就会发生变化。

good-writing-001212.en: Maybe you don’t need a three-word metaphor; maybe what’s called for is a diversion into a little story, a homespun parable, a story-within-a-story, a character’s jogged memory, or an apparent non sequitur that eventually reveals a similar truth.
good-writing-001212.zh: 也许你不需要一个冗长的比喻句；或许，更好的方式是将故事化，用一种简单而朴实的故事形式来讲述，或者是一个故事中的故事，或是某个角色的回忆，又或者是一个看似不合逻辑的叙述，但最终却能揭示出类似的真理。

good-writing-001213.en: Annie thinks in delightful metaphors that fill her books.
good-writing-001213.zh: 安妮用充满诗意的比喻来思考，这些比喻也体现在她的书中。

good-writing-001214.en: Here’s a typical nonfiction passage where she displays that genius that Aristotle talks about: “As I drove along, I kept sniffing the air like a Doberman pinscher, until even the inside of my nose started to smell bad: it smelled like two tiny windowless hallways.”
good-writing-001214.zh: 这是一段典型的非小说类文章，她在这里展现了亚里士多德所提到的那种天赋：“当我开车行驶时，我像杜宾犬一样不停地嗅着空气，甚至鼻子的内部也开始有异味了——那气味就像两个没有窗户的狭窄走廊一样难闻。”

good-writing-001216.en: I bend to the literal; metaphors don’t spring up naturally.
good-writing-001216.zh: 我倾向于采用字面意思来理解；隐喻并不是自然而然就能想到的。

good-writing-001217.en: But I try to make up for it with strong verbs (“bend to,” “spring up”) that hide their own metaphors.
good-writing-001217.zh: 不过，我会通过使用一些强动词来弥补这一点，比如“弯曲”、“跳起”这样的动词，它们能够隐藏其内在的隐喻性。

good-writing-001219.zh: 我喜欢那些优美的比喻。

good-writing-001220.en: Life really is a stage, a highway, a river, and in the right hands these basic images can do what metaphors are paid to do: explain the unknown in terms of the known.
good-writing-001220.zh: 生活确实是一个阶段、一条道路、一条河流……在恰当的人手中，这些简单的意象能够发挥比喻所拥有的功能：用已知的事物来解释未知的事物。

good-writing-001221.en: A bad metaphor is, for example, the bumpy road, although you can use those words if you are describing an actual bumpy road beneath your feet or tires.
good-writing-001221.zh: 例如，“崎岖的道路”就是一个不好的比喻，不过如果你在描述现实中的崎岖道路或轮胎所经历的坎坷时，也可以使用这样的词语。

good-writing-001222.en: A great road metaphor can be found in songs by Bruce Springsteen and the Beatles, such as the ride along “Thunder Road,” or the long and winding one.
good-writing-001222.zh: 在布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀和披头士乐队的歌曲中，可以找到一个非常有效的道路隐喻，比如《Thunder Road》中的“漫长的道路”或者“蜿蜒曲折的道路”。

good-writing-001223.en: Metaphor megastar Emily Dickinson wrote, “Dying is a wild Night and a new Road.”
good-writing-001223.zh: 隐喻大师艾米莉·迪金森曾写道：“死亡是一条狂野的道路，也是一条新的道路。”

good-writing-001224.zh: 如此黑暗的美与舒适啊！

good-writing-001226.en: Maybe moon rivers, wide rivers, or many, many of them to cross.
good-writing-001226.zh: 也许有月亮般的河流，宽阔的河流，或者许多许多需要跨越的河流。

good-writing-001227.en: Try out a metaphor about the river of life, its ebbs, shoals, dangers, beauty.
good-writing-001227.zh: 尝试用一种比喻来描述生命的河流——它的起伏、浅滩、危险，以及它的美丽。

good-writing-001229.en: Don’t try too hard, though, or we will notice and roll our eyes.
good-writing-001229.zh: 不过，不要过于努力了，否则我们就会注意到并翻白眼了。

good-writing-001230.en: Bad metaphors stick out like—well, I would say like sore thumbs, if Neal would not cross this out and send it back for me to try again.
good-writing-001230.zh: 那些糟糕的隐喻实在让人难以忍受……如果尼尔不把这段话划掉，让我重新尝试的话，那这些隐喻就显得更加糟糕了。

good-writing-001231.en: Bad metaphors stick out of otherwise good sentences and songs.
good-writing-001231.zh: 那些糟糕的隐喻会突兀地出现在其他优秀的句子和歌曲中。

good-writing-001232.en: Let’s look at the two worst metaphors in all of musical history since those first stone flutes.
good-writing-001232.zh: 让我们来看看自那些最初的石制长笛出现以来，音乐史上最糟糕的两个比喻吧。

good-writing-001233.en: Number one is, of course, in “MacArthur Park,” and the cake that someone left out in the rain.
good-writing-001233.zh: 第一点，当然是在“麦克阿瑟公园”里，还有那个被某人留在雨中的蛋糕。

good-writing-001234.en: The writer, Jimmy Webb, whose other songs show he knows better, was describing how he felt after the catastrophic end of a passionate affair, using images he had seen in Los Angeles’s MacArthur Park.
good-writing-001234.zh: 这位作家吉米·韦伯的其他歌曲都表明他其实很有才华。他在描述一段激情恋情的悲惨结局时，使用了在洛杉矶麦克阿瑟公园看到的景象作为比喻。

good-writing-001235.en: Some of these visual images are lovely, such as the old men playing checkers by the trees.
good-writing-001235.zh: 其中一些视觉图像非常美丽，比如那些在树旁下跳棋的老人。

good-writing-001236.zh: 然后还有那个讨厌的蛋糕。

good-writing-001237.en: I do believe he saw such a thing and knew how this sodden cake felt, and it pierced him, but I ask you: Is this image not better to take to one’s therapist, rather than include in a song of heartbreak, which will go on to be mocked for nearly five decades so far, and counting?
good-writing-001237.zh: 我确信他确实看到了这样的场景，也感受到了那种痛苦的感觉。但这件事确实让他很痛苦。不过，我想问你们：这样的画面难道不应该交给心理治疗师们去处理吗？而不是被用在一首表达悲伤情绪的歌曲中。因为这样的歌曲在未来近五十年内都会被人嘲笑的，而且这种嘲笑还将持续下去。

good-writing-001238.en: The runner-up in my tiny tense opinion is “A Horse with No Name.”
good-writing-001238.zh: 在我这微小而紧张的心中，第二名则是《一个无名之马》。

good-writing-001239.en: The song, by America, is about wanting to ride through a desert away from it all, the distractions, materialism, and noisy bullshit of life in the city.
good-writing-001239.zh: 这首由America演唱的歌曲，讲述的是人们渴望远离尘嚣、物质主义以及城市生活中那些喧嚣与烦扰，去一个没有这些的沙漠中驰骋的心声。

good-writing-001240.en: The narrator claims to be on a horse with no name.
good-writing-001240.zh: 叙述者声称自己骑着一匹无名的马。

good-writing-001241.en: This is worrisome to the listener: The man can be searching without destination, just going with the flow, but there is no rideable horse without a name on earth.
good-writing-001241.zh: 这对听众来说很令人担忧：这个男人可能是在漫无目的地游荡，只是随波逐流而已。但是，如果没有名字的陪伴，根本无法享受任何“旅程”。

good-writing-001242.en: How does the cowboy get said horse’s attention, to giddyup, or trot on?
good-writing-001242.zh: 牛仔是如何吸引马的注意的？是通过吆喝马儿快跑，还是通过让马小跑呢？

good-writing-001243.en: Did he shout, “Hey, you with the big butt!” or use a clicker?
good-writing-001243.zh: 他是大喊“嘿，你那个屁股真大啊！”还是使用了某种提示工具呢？

good-writing-001244.en: Trust me, the horse had a name.
good-writing-001244.zh: 相信我，那匹马确实有名字的。

good-writing-001245.en: The metaphor comes off as contrived, and therefore meaningless.
good-writing-001245.zh: 这个比喻听起来很做作，因此毫无意义。

good-writing-001246.en: If your metaphor is forced, take it out.
good-writing-001246.zh: 如果你的比喻方式显得生硬，那就删掉它吧。

good-writing-001247.en: I have a couple of editors on almost everything I write, first Neal and then the book or magazine editor, and believe me, they seize upon forced metaphors.
good-writing-001247.zh: 我写的所有作品都会经过几位的编辑审核，首先是尼尔，然后是书籍或杂志的编辑。请相信我，他们总是会抓住那些刻意使用的隐喻来发表评论。

good-writing-001248.zh: 他们将我从自我中拯救出来。

good-writing-001249.en: Try each metaphor out carefully, and see it if feels natural.
good-writing-001249.zh: 请仔细尝试每一种比喻手法，看看它们是否使用起来自然流畅。

good-writing-001250.en: Does it add depth and meaning, or conversely, an exciting kind of mystery?
good-writing-001250.zh: 这是否增添了作品的深度与意义，还是相反地，营造出一种令人兴奋的神秘感呢？

good-writing-001251.en: Neal’s little friend Plato wrote, “Time is the moving image of eternity.”
good-writing-001251.zh: 尼奥尔的挚友柏拉图曾写道：“时间其实是永恒的动态映像。”

good-writing-001253.en: (By the way, while we’re on the subject of metaphors, my father described Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony as metaphor upon metaphor. Duh duh duh duh. Duh duh duh duh: Life is pounding on the door and then barges in with all the joy and hardship, darkness and light, life and death and new life.)
good-writing-001253.zh: （顺便说一下，既然我们在谈论隐喻这个话题，我父亲将贝多芬的第五交响曲描述得真是妙趣横生啊。生活就像是一扇门，不断地敲打着我们的心扉，然后带着所有的喜悦与苦难、光明与黑暗、生与死以及新的生命，闯入我们的生活中。）

good-writing-001254.en: Over and over, every rule of Neal’s is about creating better sentences, cleaner and richer at the same time.
good-writing-001254.zh: 一次又一次，尼尔的所有规则都围绕着如何写出更优美、更精炼的句子。

good-writing-001255.en: A successful metaphor—“love is a rose bush, beautiful and prickly and ephemeral”—enhances its environment, as does taking out a forced one.
good-writing-001255.zh: 一个成功的隐喻——“爱就像一丛玫瑰，美丽而刺人，转瞬即逝”——能够提升其表达效果，就像选用一个刻意设计的隐喻一样。

good-writing-001257.en: We already think in clichés; you owe it to your reader’s search for novelty to remove or deconstruct your hackneyed phrases.
good-writing-001257.zh: 我们本来就习惯用陈词滥调思考；既然读者在寻找新鲜感，你就有责任删去或拆解那些用滥了的表达。

good-writing-001258.en: Use clichés to your heart’s desire, but only if you twist them until they bleed.
good-writing-001258.zh: 你可以随心所欲地使用那些陈腐的套路，但前提是你要对这些套路进行改造，让它们变得新颖有趣。

good-writing-001259.en: We’re pattern seekers, us humans, and that means that our ideas—our spoken words—rest on hackneyed ideas that are recombined in new ways.
good-writing-001259.zh: 我们人类是模式探索者，这意味着我们的想法——也就是我们所说的“话语”——都是基于那些被重新组合、以新方式呈现的陈旧的想法而构成的。

good-writing-001261.en: We’re spitting out old thoughts all day long.
good-writing-001261.zh: 我们整天都在不断思考那些陈旧的想法。

good-writing-001262.zh: 作家们的思维方式与其他人并无不同。

good-writing-001263.en: We have an alphabet, and we also have a canon of idiomatic shortcuts to abstract ideas—adages and stale phrases.
good-writing-001263.zh: 我们拥有自己的字母表，同时还有一系列用于表达抽象概念的惯用短语——这些短语或称为谚语或陈词滥调。

good-writing-001264.en: (So do musicians. How many times have you heard a jazz soloist blurt out a phrase from a childhood ditty?)
good-writing-001264.zh: （音乐家们也是如此。有多少次你听到过一位爵士乐手突然唱出自己童年时期的一首民谣中的片段呢？）

good-writing-001265.en: Don’t be scared to write the first thing that comes into your head, which is often a cliché.
good-writing-001265.zh: 不要害怕写下脑海中浮现的第一句话，尽管这些句子往往都很陈腐。

good-writing-001266.en: Later you can exchange it for all-new verbiage.
good-writing-001266.zh: 之后，你可以将其兑换成全新的措辞。

good-writing-001267.en: But you might also use the cliché as a starting point and create a zinger out of it, like a comedian taking a mundane experience and throwing in an unexpected variable, getting a laugh.
good-writing-001267.zh: 不过，你也可以将这种陈词滥调作为起点，从中创造出有趣的幽默效果。就像喜剧演员一样，从平凡的场景中引入一个意想不到的元素，从而引发笑声。

good-writing-001268.en: I might first think, “She was good as gold.”
good-writing-001268.zh: 我首先想的是：“她表现得非常出色。”

good-writing-001269.en: By the time I’ve finished creating the character, the line has changed to “She was good as brass, barely.”
good-writing-001269.zh: 当我完成角色的设计之后，台词已经变成了“她的表现虽然还可以，但实在不怎么样。”

good-writing-001270.en: A year or so into my newspaper career I was assigned the storm story.
good-writing-001270.zh: 在从事新闻工作的头几年里，我负责了一篇关于风暴的报道。

good-writing-001271.en: Writing about snowstorms in upstate New York is like writing about waves in Waikiki Beach or pit crews at Talladega.
good-writing-001271.zh: 在纽约州北部描写暴风雪的情景，就如同在怀基基海滩描述海浪的波动，或者描述塔拉迪加赛道上的赛车手们一样。

good-writing-001272.en: But a good-sized blizzard, no matter how much it resembles every other good-sized blizzard, must be placed on the front page.
good-writing-001272.zh: 但是，无论这样的暴风雪与其他类似暴风雪有多么相似，它仍然必须被放在头版上。

good-writing-001273.en: Every reader expects it; the storm is what everyone is talking about, so it must be news.
good-writing-001273.zh: 每个读者都期待着这一消息；这场风暴正是大家热议的话题，因此它必定会成为新闻。

good-writing-001274.en: What can you possibly say that is fresh enough to do more than convey the same facts that appear on the weather page deep inside the paper?
good-writing-001274.zh: 你能说出什么新鲜的话呢？那些话不过是重复了报纸内页天气预报页面上已经呈现过的那些信息而已。

good-writing-001275.zh: 我仍然记得我的主题陈述：

good-writing-001276.en: “Cold, cold, cold. Freezing. It was freezing.”
good-writing-001276.zh: “冷得要命。刺骨的寒冷。简直冷得要命。”

good-writing-001277.en: Now, I knew why I wrote those words, even if my readers didn’t.
good-writing-001277.zh: 现在，我明白了自己为什么要写下那些文字，即使我的读者并不明白。

good-writing-001278.en: They were the first words of a song by the band Little Feat.
good-writing-001278.zh: 那是Little Feat乐队的一首歌中的第一段歌词。

good-writing-001279.en: (A paraphrase, really. The original repeats “Cold, cold, cold”—six “colds”—before adding “Freezing.”)
good-writing-001279.zh: （其实这是一种改写。原文在“Cold, cold, cold”——即“六个寒冷”之后，又加上了“Freezing”这个词。）

good-writing-001280.en: My editor and I both knew that the allusion would be lost on all but a handful of our readers, but so what?
good-writing-001280.zh: 我和编辑都明白，这种暗示除了少数读者之外，其他人根本不会理解。但那又怎样呢？

good-writing-001281.en: It was a weather story, and anything other than a cliché was an improvement.
good-writing-001281.zh: 这是一篇关于天气的报道，只要内容不是陈词滥调，那就算是一种进步了。

good-writing-001282.en: This event stuck in my mind—the ridiculousness of my lede, as well as its necessity—and it was on that day that I realized much of my job as a newspaper writer was to reject the clichés.
good-writing-001282.zh: 这一事件让我印象深刻——我那些冗长的导语实在太过陈腐，但它们又具有必要性。就在那一天，我意识到，作为一名新闻记者，我的工作很大程度上就是需要摒弃那些陈旧的套路。

good-writing-001283.en: I stopped being a newspaper writer more than thirty years ago.
good-writing-001283.zh: 三十多年前，我就不再从事报纸编辑工作了。

good-writing-001284.en: I still find myself deleting or twisting first-thought clichés every time I write.
good-writing-001284.zh: 每次写作时，我仍然会删改或扭曲那些最初想到的陈词滥调。

good-writing-001285.en: “So it goes” becomes “So it stops.” “You take the good with the bad” becomes “You take the mediocre with the bad.”
good-writing-001285.zh: “所以，就这样吧。”变成了“那么，就到此为止吧。” “你接受好的，也接受不好的。”变成了“你接受中等水平的东西，以及那些不好的东西。”

good-writing-001286.en: Ian Fleming turned “live and let live” into “Live and Let Die.”
good-writing-001286.zh: 伊恩·弗莱明将“Live and Let Live”改编成了“Live and Let Die”。

good-writing-001289.en: Every so often, however, you simply need to use one of the lesser-known clichés, because there are only so many words and phrases in the English language.
good-writing-001289.zh: 不过，偶尔你还是需要使用一些不太常见的陈词滥调，因为英语中的词汇和表达方式其实有限。

good-writing-001290.en: Let me give you an example: I googled a list of clichés, and under the As, there were 213 so-called clichés.
good-writing-001290.zh: 让我举个例子：我在谷歌上搜索了“陈词滥调”的相关列表，结果在“As”类别下，有213条所谓的陈词滥调。

good-writing-001291.en: Here are four side-by-side clichés that begin with the letter A:
good-writing-001291.zh: 以下是四个以字母“A”开头的常见表达方式：

good-writing-001295.en: as honest as the day is long
good-writing-001295.zh: 如此诚实，就像白天的阳光一样明亮

good-writing-001296.en: Now, obviously you cannot use “happy as a clam,” only partly because clams are not happy creatures.
good-writing-001296.zh: 显然，你不能使用“快乐如蛤蜊”这样的表达，部分原因是蛤蜊本身就不算是“快乐”的生物。

good-writing-001297.en: They are cold and have sand in some very special places, and you know exactly how miserable that can be.
good-writing-001297.zh: 它们很冷，而且在某些非常特殊的地方还有沙子。你可以想象那种痛苦的感觉有多糟糕。

good-writing-001298.en: Also, we are going to try and catch them, and kill them so we can eat them.
good-writing-001298.zh: 此外，我们还会试图抓住他们，并杀死他们，以便吃掉他们的肉。

good-writing-001299.en: So maybe you could say, “miserable as a clam.”
good-writing-001299.zh: 所以，也许你可以说：“痛苦得就像蛤蜊一样。”

good-writing-001300.en: But this brings us to “sandboy,” a young peddler of sand who sold it to barkeepers to absorb spills and spit on the floor.
good-writing-001300.zh: 但这就引出了“沙男孩”这个角色，他是一个年轻的沙贩子，将沙子卖给酒吧老板，用来吸收那些洒在地板上的饮料和唾液。

good-writing-001301.en: Sandboys were happy because they got paid for the delivery, but also they could sweep up the old sand before spreading the new and maybe find some loose change.
good-writing-001301.zh: 那些搬运沙子的人很高兴，因为他们能够因运输工作而获得报酬。此外，他们还可以清理掉那些旧的沙子，为铺设新的沙子做好准备，也许还能找到一些零钱。

good-writing-001303.en: But who among you knew that?
good-writing-001303.zh: 但是，你们当中谁知道这件事呢？

good-writing-001304.en: Probably only Neal, and his ilk.
good-writing-001304.zh: 可能只有尼尔，以及像他那样的人而已。

good-writing-001305.en: So I am going to recommend you use the phrase “happy as a sandboy” in whatever you are currently working on.
good-writing-001305.zh: 因此，我建议你在目前所从事的任何工作中都使用“快乐如沙人”这个表达。

good-writing-001309.en: Probably not, yet according to Neal, I am still instructed not to use the phrase, which I’ve never heard or read.
good-writing-001309.zh: 可能不行，不过根据尼尔的说法，我仍然被要求不要使用这个短语。我从未听说过或使用过这个短语。

good-writing-001310.en: Maybe it bears investigating just why Larry is so happy—or is he only pretending to be happy?
good-writing-001310.zh: 也许我们应该探究一下，为什么拉里如此开心——或者，他只是假装开心而已？

good-writing-001311.en: Don’t you want to know more about Larry?
good-writing-001311.zh: 你不想了解更多关于拉里的信息吗？

good-writing-001312.en: You could investigate the way you might any fictional character: What does he look like, and how do clothes hang on him, and does his voice change when he is worried?
good-writing-001312.zh: 你可以像研究任何虚构角色一样来研究这个角色：他长什么样？他的服装如何？当他感到焦虑时，他的声音会发生变化吗？

good-writing-001313.en: What does he do with his hands when he is bored or in an intimate conversation?
good-writing-001313.zh: 当他感到无聊或进行亲密交谈时，他会用双手做些什么呢？

good-writing-001314.en: I say hats off to Larry.

good-writing-001315.en: And I’m definitely not going to say he is as honest as the day is long, because it’s criminally overused.
good-writing-001315.zh: 我绝对不会说他永远那么诚实，因为“诚实”这个词已经被滥用了。

good-writing-001316.en: It has been a criminally overused cliché for centuries.
good-writing-001316.zh: 几个世纪以来，这一陈词滥调一直被过度使用，成为一种陈腐的套路。

good-writing-001317.en: But if you follow Neal’s advice to twist it, you could use “as honest as a clam,” because clams don’t have the bandwidth to lie.
good-writing-001317.zh: 但如果你按照尼尔的建议来变通使用这个表达，那么就可以用“诚实得如同蛤蜊”来形容，因为蛤蜊根本没有撒谎的能力。

good-writing-001318.en: Or you could say, “as honest as the day was long, when that used to mean something, in the old days before the insane speed of this modern life, when days race by like rabbits.”
good-writing-001318.zh: 或者你可以这样说：“在过去，当日子还长一些的时候，当速度还不那么快，当日子像兔子一样飞逝的时候，人们还是很诚实的。”

good-writing-001319.en: Or you could say he was truthful, full of truth.
good-writing-001319.zh: 或者可以说，他非常诚实，言出必行。

good-writing-001320.en: I do encourage you to use clichés in first drafts as a space holder so that you don’t bog down and lose momentum.
good-writing-001320.zh: 我鼓励你在初稿中适当使用一些陈词滥调作为过渡性的表达，这样就不会让文章显得拖沓、失去节奏感。

good-writing-001321.en: You can return to them later and see if you can come up with something more original and interesting.
good-writing-001321.zh: 你可以稍后再次尝试它们，看看是否能够想出一些更原创、更有趣的东西。

good-writing-001322.en: The most important thing I can share is to do whatever it takes to avoid coming to a standstill while your inner critic tries to convince you to give up.
good-writing-001322.zh: 我能分享的最重要的启示是：无论发生什么，都要努力避免陷入停滞状态，因为你的内心批评者可能会试图让你放弃。

good-writing-001323.zh: “永不放弃”这种说法是不是陈词滥调呢？

good-writing-001324.en: My son has it tattooed on his forearm, but whether it is or not, don’t.
good-writing-001324.zh: 我儿子在前臂上纹了这个图案，不过不管他有没有这个纹身，都不要这么做。

good-writing-001325.en: Don’t ever give up on writing.

good-writing-001327.en: For a series of terms to land, you usually need three.
good-writing-001327.zh: 要让一组列举有力地落到读者心里，通常需要三项。

good-writing-001328.en: In English, three is the magic number.
good-writing-001328.zh: 在英语中，3这个数字被认为是一种神奇的数字。

good-writing-001329.en: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly.

good-writing-001330.en: The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe.

good-writing-001332.en: Years ago, my bilingual Turkish and English writer friend Yeshim Ternar told me that when she switched into English she had to remember that two examples of anything, which are enough in Turkish, are insufficient to her American audience.
good-writing-001332.zh: 许多年前，我的两位双语作家朋友——分别使用土耳其语和英语写作的Yeshim Ternar告诉我，当她用英语写作时，必须记住：无论是什么内容，两个例子就足够了；而在土耳其语中，两个例子可能就不够了，因为她的美国读者可能无法理解这一点。

good-writing-001333.en: It’s more about the rhythm than the words, actually.
good-writing-001333.zh: 实际上，重要的是节奏，而不是具体的词汇。

good-writing-001334.en: Think of the musical pattern “duh-dah duh-dah” and how unresolved it sounds compared to “duh-dah duh-dah duh-dah.”
good-writing-001334.zh: 想象一下“duh-dah duh-dah”这种音乐节奏，与“duh-dah duh-dah duh-dah”相比，这种节奏听起来更加不完整。

good-writing-001335.en: It’s hard to sing the longer version without adding a big, resolving accent to the last “dah.”
good-writing-001335.zh: 在演唱这个较长的版本时，如果不给最后一个“dah”加上一个明显的重音符号的话，那就很难唱准了。

good-writing-001336.en: We read lists—especially lists of three—rhythmically.
good-writing-001336.zh: 我们阅读列表时，尤其是那些包含三个项目的列表时，会采用有节奏的阅读方式。

good-writing-001337.en: The rule of threes emerges naturally when you read your words aloud.
good-writing-001337.zh: 当你大声朗读这些单词时，就会自然而然地发现“三”这个数字在其中的作用。

good-writing-001338.en: When you follow the instruction to read back your work before submitting it to an editor, you’ll hear your own mistakes—and mostly we’re talking about mistakes of rhythm.
good-writing-001338.zh: 当你按照指示在将作品提交给编辑之前先阅读一遍时，你会发现自己犯了一些错误——而这些错误大多都是节奏上的问题。

good-writing-001339.en: Like poetry, prose relies on rhythm; it’s just not necessarily metrical.
good-writing-001339.zh: 就像诗歌一样，散文也需要节奏感；只不过散文并不一定要遵循严格的韵律规则而已。

good-writing-001341.en: We like our pauses, our punch lines, our crescendos, and our familiar patterns.
good-writing-001341.zh: 我们喜欢那些停顿、那些妙语、那些渐强的过程，以及那些我们熟悉的节奏模式。

good-writing-001342.en: Three examples is a familiar pattern.
good-writing-001342.zh: 三个例子是一种常见的模式。

good-writing-001343.en: Two things can be alike in many ways.
good-writing-001343.zh: 有两样事物可能在许多方面都相似。

good-writing-001344.en: Three things can be alike in few ways.
good-writing-001344.zh: 有三种事物可能在几个方面具有相似之处。

good-writing-001345.en: All that said, as Annie points out below, two examples without the third have their own rhythm, which might better fit your work in progress.
good-writing-001345.zh: 不过，正如安妮在下面所指出的，两个没有第三个元素的例子都有其独特的节奏感，这种节奏感可能更适合你正在进行的作品。

good-writing-001346.en: Rules of grammar are black-and-white and give you a simple choice of right or wrong.
good-writing-001346.zh: 语法规则是明确无误的，能够让你简单地判断什么是正确，什么是错误。

good-writing-001347.en: Rules of rhetoric or persuasion are subtle and yielding.
good-writing-001347.zh: 修辞或说服的法则都是微妙且难以捉摸的。

good-writing-001348.en: When collaborating with another, or even yourself, recognize that everybody’s voice has its quirks.
good-writing-001348.zh: 在与他人合作时，甚至是在与自己的时候，都要意识到每个人的声音都有其独特的特点。

good-writing-001349.en: Early on in our relationship, I was jarred by Annie’s use of twos rather than threes.
good-writing-001349.zh: 在我们关系的初期，我注意到安妮总是使用“二”这个数字，而不是“三”。这一点让我很惊讶。

good-writing-001350.en: But I knew better than to correct it.
good-writing-001350.zh: 但我知道不应该去纠正它。

good-writing-001352.en: Eventually, I could recognize the power of her dangling twos.
good-writing-001352.zh: 最终，我意识到她那些悬挂着的“2”数字所蕴含的力量。

good-writing-001354.en: This rule of threes is true for Neal and probably most writers.
good-writing-001354.zh: 这种“三原则”适用于尼尔，也适用于大多数作家。

good-writing-001355.en: I use two in a series as often as I do three.
good-writing-001355.zh: 我使用两个系列产品的频率，和用三个系列产品的频率一样高。

good-writing-001356.en: It’s what I’m comfortable with, and what sometimes works best for my rhythm, emphasis, or humor.
good-writing-001356.zh: 这是我能感到舒适的写作方式，有时候这种方式也能更好地体现我的节奏、重点或幽默感。

good-writing-001357.zh: 我注意到，完美的“双数”现象无处不在。

good-writing-001358.en: And here is a stunning two inside a series of four that I came upon years ago in a description of Robert Campin’s painting Portrait of a Woman.
good-writing-001358.zh: 这里有一幅令人惊叹的作品，属于四幅系列中的第二幅。我多年前在罗伯特·坎平所绘的《女子肖像》这幅画的说明中偶然发现了它。

good-writing-001359.en: “I don’t know what I love more: the eyes, the subtlety of the purple robe, the incredible headscarf (the layers! the folds!) or the pins.”
good-writing-001359.zh: “我不知道自己更喜爱什么：那双眼睛、那紫色长袍的精致设计、那条令人惊叹的头带（那些层次、那些褶皱！）还是那些别针。”

good-writing-001361.en: If you google the painting, you’ll see what I mean about this description’s greatness.
good-writing-001361.zh: 如果你在谷歌上搜索这幅画，你就会明白我所说的这种描述有多么精彩了。

good-writing-001362.en: The quote is from Campin’s star pupil, Peter Paul Rubens.
good-writing-001362.zh: 这段引文出自坎平最杰出的学生彼得·保罗·鲁本斯的作品。

good-writing-001363.en: My subject matter—family, soul, spirit, humanity, and coming through hard times—allows for a lot of open-ended thoughts without simple resolution, which threes don’t.
good-writing-001363.zh: 我的创作主题——家庭、灵魂、精神、人类以及如何在艰难时期生存——允许许多没有明确答案的开放式思考，而这些开放式思考对于三岁的孩子来说是不适用的。

good-writing-001364.en: Three in a series would leave my words wrapped up in neat, tight packages, which is the opposite of what I’m trying for.
good-writing-001364.zh: 连续发布三个作品时，我的文字会被整理成整齐、紧凑的包装形式，这与我原本追求的效果完全相反。

good-writing-001365.en: Two in a series adds suspense, as I haven’t closed off the thought process.
good-writing-001365.zh: 连续出现两个这样的情节会增添悬念，因为我还没有结束这个思考过程。

good-writing-001367.en: Don’t let Neal tell you otherwise.

good-writing-001368.en: Try things one way, move them around, take stuff out, and see if more spaciousness is what you were after.
good-writing-001368.zh: 尝试用不同的方式摆放物品，把一些东西移开，看看这样是否能让空间看起来更宽敞一些。

good-writing-001369.en: If two is too abrupt, try three, unless you don’t have a third example.
good-writing-001369.zh: 如果两个例子显得过于突兀，那么可以尝试使用三个例子，除非你实在没有第三个例子可以举例了。

good-writing-001370.en: Picasso said, “If I don’t have red, I use blue.”
good-writing-001370.zh: 毕加索曾说：“如果我没有红色，我就用蓝色来代替。”

good-writing-001373.en: Long sentences require attention to detail, conjunctions, and rhythm—and a payoff at the end.
good-writing-001373.zh: 写长句，需要留心细节、连接词和节奏，还要在句末给予读者一个有分量的落点。

good-writing-001374.en: Long sentences are acceptable, but they need to be linear, propulsive, and forward-moving, with parentheticals that don’t double back.
good-writing-001374.zh: 长句是可以接受的，但句子结构必须简洁明了、具有推动性，并且保持连贯性，其中的插入语不应导致句子结构上的重复。

good-writing-001375.en: Used judiciously, a long sentence catapults the reader through real time with urgency, immediacy, and a sense of working consciousness.
good-writing-001375.zh: 如果运用得当，长句能够以一种紧迫、即时且充满行动感的方式，引导读者快速进入故事的世界。

good-writing-001376.en: Here’s a 280-word sentence from Nikolai Gogol’s “The Overcoat”:
good-writing-001376.zh: 这是尼古拉·果戈里的小说《外套》中一个280字的句子：

good-writing-001377.en: Even at the hour when the grey St. Petersburg sky had quite dispersed, and all the official world had eaten or dined, each as he could, in accordance with the salary he received and his own fancy; when all were resting from the departmental jar of pens, running to and fro from their own and other people’s indispensable occupations, and from all the work that an uneasy man makes willingly for himself, rather than what is necessary; when officials hasten to dedicate to pleasure the time which is left to them, one bolder than the rest going to the theatre; another, into the street looking under all the bonnets; another wasting his evening in compliments to some pretty girl, the star of a small official circle; another—and this is the common case of all—visiting his comrades on the fourth or third floor, in two small rooms with an ante-room or kitchen, and some pretensions to fashion, such as a lamp or some other trifle which has cost many a sacrifice of dinner or pleasure trip; in a word, at the hour when all officials disperse among the contracted quarters of their friends, to play whist, as they sip their tea from glasses with a kopek’s worth of sugar, smoke long pipes, relate at times some bits of gossip which a Russian man can never, under any circumstances, refrain from, and, when there is nothing else to talk of, repeat eternal anecdotes about the commandant to whom they had sent word that the tails of the horses on the Falconet Monument had been cut off, when all strive to divert themselves, Akakiy Akakievitch indulged in no kind of diversion.
good-writing-001377.zh: 即便在圣彼得堡灰蒙蒙的天空已经散去、所有官员都按照自己的薪水以及个人喜好，各自在餐厅里吃完了早饭或晚餐之后，即便在所有人都在从各自和他人不可或缺的工作以及那些不安稳的官员们自愿承担的各种琐事中休息完毕之后，即便在那些总是忙于各种琐事的人都在忙着享受闲暇时光的时候——有些官员则更大胆，他们去剧院；有些则会在街上四处寻找漂亮的女孩；还有些则会在晚上向某个漂亮的女孩表达爱意，那个女孩可能是某个小圈子中的明星人物；还有些官员——这是大多数人的常见情况——会去拜访他们的同事，住在四楼或三楼的小房间里，这些房间配有前厅或厨房设施，还有些官员还喜欢追求一些时尚的东西，比如一盏灯或者别的什么东西，这些都需要花费很多钱来购买晚餐或娱乐活动。总之，在那些官员们都在朋友们的住所里闲逛、玩着惠斯特牌游戏、喝着含糖量极低的茶、抽着长长的烟斗、偶尔谈论一些俄罗斯人无论如何都不可能不谈论的八卦故事的时候，当没有什么别的事情可谈时，他们就会重复那些关于指挥官的永恒轶事——他们曾经向指挥官报告说，在Falconet纪念碑上马尾巴被切断了。而此时，所有人都在努力让自己从那些琐事中得到乐趣，但Akakiy Akakievitch却没有任何娱乐活动。

good-writing-001378.en: Whatever you think of the sentence, it’s mostly staccato, never gets hung up on metaphysics, doesn’t double back even when relying on memory, contains few Latinate multisyllabic words, slows down only to catch a breath and then resumes its urgency, and feels possible as a true stream of consciousness as well as a complete picture of the dreary lives of bureaucrats, both at the office and in their attempt to enliven themselves in the dark, ultimately rewarding the reader with a whammy of a punch line.
good-writing-001378.zh: 无论你如何看待这个句子，它都充满了断断续续的节奏感；没有陷入玄学的讨论；即使依靠记忆来书写，也不会出现重复的内容。句子中的词汇大多为单音节词，节奏缓慢，但会在适当的时候短暂暂停，然后继续以紧迫感推进。这个句子既呈现了意识流的叙述方式，也生动地描绘了官僚们在办公室里以及试图在黑暗中寻找生活希望时的悲惨生活。最后，这个句子以一个精彩的结尾来结束，给读者带来惊喜。

good-writing-001379.en: What you just read—my quick characterization of the sentence’s style—is also an acceptable long sentence.
good-writing-001379.zh: 你刚才读到的内容——我对这个句子的风格所做的简要描述——其实也可以算是一个恰当的长句。

good-writing-001380.en: Don’t fear long sentences, and don’t fear the comma as a substitute for the period.
good-writing-001380.zh: 不要害怕长句的表达方式，也无需将逗号当作句号的使用。

good-writing-001381.en: Sometimes the long sentence is not an enemy.
good-writing-001381.zh: 有时候，冗长的句子并不一定是坏事。

good-writing-001383.en: Many of our greatest writers have used long, long sentences, such as James Joyce and William Faulkner, but it has been decades since I felt like reading them.
good-writing-001383.zh: 我们的许多著名作家都喜欢使用非常长的句子结构，比如詹姆斯·乔伊斯和威廉·福克纳。不过，已经过去几十年了，我还没有再次感受到阅读这类作品的乐趣。

good-writing-001384.en: There is a nearly 4,400-word stream-of-consciousness passage in Joyce’s Ulysses, not so much a sentence as an outburst, which I think is very nice and which thrilled me in high school when I first read the book, but somewhat less so in my early twenties when I ostentatiously reread the book so that people would think I am smarter than I am.
good-writing-001384.zh: 在乔伊斯的《尤利西斯》中，有一段大约4400字的无序文字片段。这些文字更像是一种即兴的、不连贯的表达，而不是真正的句子。当我第一次阅读这本书时，这些文字让我非常着迷；但在二十出头的年纪时，当我再次阅读这本书时，虽然仍然觉得这些文字很吸引人，但那种感觉已经有所减弱了。那时，我只是为了炫耀而重新阅读这本书，想让人们认为我比实际要聪明得多。

good-writing-001385.en: My reading group chose Ulysses when I was thirty, and by this point I mostly found it impenetrable.
good-writing-001385.zh: 当我三十岁时，我的阅读小组选择了《尤利西斯》这本书。不过到那时为止，我几乎觉得这本书难以理解。

good-writing-001386.en: I had to pretend to have read the 150 pages we were supposed to consume every two weeks.
good-writing-001386.zh: 我不得不假装自己已经读完了那些我们每周应阅读150页内容的书籍。

good-writing-001387.en: Anything I contributed had been cribbed from various forewords and introductions I read at the library.
good-writing-001387.zh: 我所贡献的内容，都是从我在图书馆阅读的各种前言和介绍中摘抄而来的。

good-writing-001388.en: When I contributed my stolen bons mots, I made sure to stroke my chin like William Buckley.
good-writing-001388.zh: 当我用那些偷来的妙语发表自己的观点时，我一定会像威廉·巴克利那样，微微颔首表示认可。

good-writing-001389.en: If you are an excellent writer, go ahead and experiment with 100-word sentences.
good-writing-001389.zh: 如果你是一个写作能力很强的人，那么不妨尝试用100字的句子来写作吧。

good-writing-001390.en: Margaret Atwood, Vladimir Nabokov, and Virginia Woolf sometimes use long sentences, and I love nearly every word they have written, but most of the time I find long, long sentences difficult to track, and annoying.
good-writing-001390.zh: 玛格丽特·阿特伍德、弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫和弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫有时会使用非常长的句子。我几乎喜欢他们写的每一个字，但大多数时候，那些冗长的句子让我难以理解，甚至觉得有些烦人。

good-writing-001391.en: The rule, though, is that you can get away with anything in your writing as long as your reader wants to keep reading and not run away screaming.
good-writing-001391.zh: 不过，规则是：在写作过程中，只要读者愿意继续阅读而不想中途放弃，那么你可以随心所欲地写作。

good-writing-001392.en: Of course, Faulkner could get away with sentences that were a thousand words because of the greatness of the writing.
good-writing-001392.zh: 当然，福克纳的作品虽然字数众多，但他的作品依然可以显得简洁而有力。

good-writing-001393.en: An extremely long Faulkner sentence is stunning and brilliant, worthy of awe.
good-writing-001393.zh: 福克纳的这篇长篇小说段落极其精彩，令人惊叹不已。

good-writing-001394.en: But please raise your hand if you have been reading a lot of Faulkner since Covid.
good-writing-001394.zh: 但是，如果你在新冠疫情期间一直在阅读福克纳的作品，请举手示意。

good-writing-001396.en: While I have you, here is the most perfect 107-word sentence in the English language, from Stuart Little by E. B. White.
good-writing-001396.zh: 有你在我身边时，以下这句话就是英语中最完美的107个单词的句子了。这句话出自E.B.怀特的《斯图尔特·利特尔》一书。

good-writing-001397.en: It takes place near the end, when Stuart is searching for Margalo in Ames Crossing.
good-writing-001397.zh: 故事发生在最后的部分，当时斯图尔特正在艾姆斯交叉口寻找马加尔洛。

good-writing-001398.en: If you are going to use long sentences, try to write more like this:
good-writing-001398.zh: 如果你打算使用较长的句子，尽量这样写作：

good-writing-001399.en: In the loveliest town of all, where the houses were white and high and the elm trees were green and higher than the houses, where the front yards were wide and pleasant and the back yards were bushy and worth finding out about, where the streets sloped down to the stream and the stream flowed quietly under the bridge, where the lawns ended in orchards and the orchards ended in fields and the fields ended in pastures and the pastures climbed the hill and disappeared over the top toward the wonderful wide sky, in this loveliest of all towns Stuart stopped to get a drink of sarsaparilla.
good-writing-001399.zh: 在最美丽的城镇里，那里的房屋都是白色的，高度很高；榆树也是绿色的，而且比房屋还要高。街道很宽阔，环境也很宜人。后院则树木茂盛，非常值得一探究竟。街道的坡度很缓，水流在桥下静静地流淌。草坪的尽头是果园，果园的尽头是田野，田野的尽头则是牧场。牧场沿着山坡延伸，最终消失在广阔的天空之下。在这样一个最美丽的城镇里，斯图尔特停下来喝了一口沙萨帕里拉饮料。

good-writing-001401.en: Interrupt lyrical or otherwise long passages with an abrupt, short sentence.
good-writing-001401.zh: 在抒情的段落或其他长段落中，突然插入一个简短的句子。

good-writing-001403.en: Use intentionally short sentences to bring the reader home.
good-writing-001403.zh: 使用简短的句子来吸引读者的注意力，让他们更容易理解内容。

good-writing-001405.en: Famously, this admonition was the first of Ernest Hemingway’s four rules for writing: “Use short sentences. Use short first paragraphs. Use vigorous English. Be positive, not negative.”
good-writing-001405.zh: 众所周知，这番告诫实际上是欧内斯特·海明威提出的四条写作原则中的第一条：“使用短句。使用短小的段落。使用简洁明了的英语表达。保持积极的态度，而非消极的态度。”

good-writing-001406.en: All good rules (and all short sentences).
good-writing-001406.zh: 所有的规则都是正确的（而且所有的句子都简短）。

good-writing-001407.en: Of course, he wanted all sentences to be short.
good-writing-001407.zh: 当然，他希望所有的句子都尽量简短一些。

good-writing-001408.en: If you want to sound like Hemingway, do so.
good-writing-001408.zh: 如果你想模仿海明威的写作风格，那就这样做吧。

good-writing-001409.en: But I’m encouraging you to use short sentences occasionally, as punctuation.
good-writing-001409.zh: 不过，我鼓励你们偶尔使用简短的句子来作为标点符号的使用。

good-writing-001410.en: One of my favorite books is The Old Man and the Sea.
good-writing-001410.zh: 我最喜欢的书之一是《老人与海》。

good-writing-001411.en: But I’m equally wowed by Absalom, Absalom! and Faulkner’s notoriously long sentences.
good-writing-001411.zh: 不过，我同样被阿布萨洛姆·阿布萨洛姆以及福克纳那些众所周知的长篇句子所震撼了。

good-writing-001412.en: That book contains what once held the record for “longest legitimate published sentence in the English language,” a thought-out, fast-paced, and fully cogent spill of 1,288 words.
good-writing-001412.zh: 那本书曾经保持着“英语中发表的最长、最合理的判决”这一纪录。这是一篇结构严谨、节奏明快、逻辑严密的文章，共1,288个字。

good-writing-001413.en: Faulkner was no stream-of-consciousness writer, but he excelled at baring his characters’ thoughts.
good-writing-001413.zh: 福克纳并非那种以意识流方式进行写作的作家，但他在展现人物内心想法方面表现得非常出色。

good-writing-001414.en: By the way, here is the paragraph that precedes that longest sentence:
good-writing-001414.zh: 顺便提一下，下面这段文字是出现在那个最长的句子之前的：

good-writing-001416.en: And what sentence follows the longest sentence?
good-writing-001416.zh: 那么，最长的那个句子之后是什么句子呢？

good-writing-001418.zh: 同样简短、带有双关意义的句子。

good-writing-001419.en: Like I said, occasional short sentences.
good-writing-001419.zh: 就像我说的，偶尔用简短的句子来表达吧。

good-writing-001421.en: The punch line doesn’t have to be a short sentence; it might be a clause that manages to stand alone at the end of a sentence.
good-writing-001421.zh: 这个俏皮话不必是短句；它也可以是一个能够独立出现在句子末尾的短语。

good-writing-001422.en: Look at how this Hank Williams verse concludes:
good-writing-001422.zh: 看看这段Hank Williams的歌词是如何结尾的：

good-writing-001423.en: The silence of a falling star

good-writing-001425.en: And as I wonder where you are
good-writing-001425.zh: 而我则在思考你究竟在何处

good-writing-001426.en: I’m so lonesome, I could cry
good-writing-001426.zh: 我太孤独了，甚至想哭泣。

good-writing-001428.en: There’s nothing more final than that.
good-writing-001428.zh: 没有比这更确定的事情了。

good-writing-001429.en: Lyricists have it over book writers in expressing the obvious without irony or fancification.
good-writing-001429.zh: 抒情作家在表达显而易见的内容时，比小说作家更能够避免夸张和过度渲染。

good-writing-001431.en: The two most profound sentences I’ve ever read are both only two words.
good-writing-001431.zh: 我读过的最深刻的这两句话，都只有两个词而已。

good-writing-001432.en: One is the description of Dilsey, the black matriarch of the Compton family servants in The Sound and the Fury:
good-writing-001432.zh: 其中之一是《声音与愤怒》中康普顿家族仆人们中的黑种女族长迪尔西的描述：

good-writing-001434.en: Her family came through their hideous racist treatment and station in life, but because of Dilsey’s faith, goodness, and dignity, her love of all of God’s creation, they endured.
good-writing-001434.zh: 她的家庭经历了极其恶劣的种族主义待遇和悲惨的生活状况，但因为迪尔西的信仰、善良以及她对上帝所创造的一切的关爱，他们才得以挺过那些艰难的时刻。

good-writing-001435.en: The other is the shortest sentence in the Bible:
good-writing-001435.zh: 另一个则是《圣经》中最短的句子：

good-writing-001437.en: In the gospel of John, Jesus finally arrives in Bethany after being sent for by Mary and Martha, whose brother Lazarus—Jesus’s dear friend—is very sick.
good-writing-001437.zh: 在《约翰福音》中，耶稣在玛利亚和马大邀请下最终抵达了伯大尼。玛利亚和马大的兄弟拉撒路是耶稣的挚友，但拉撒路当时病得很重。

good-writing-001438.en: By the time Jesus arrives, perhaps a bit lackadaisically, Lazarus has been dead for four days.
good-writing-001438.zh: 当耶稣到来时，拉撒路可能已经去世四天了，也许他当时已经有些昏睡不醒了。

good-writing-001439.en: He lies in a cave, wrapped in burial clothing.
good-writing-001439.zh: 他躺在洞穴里，身上穿着葬礼用的衣服。

good-writing-001441.en: We know firsthand what those two words mean—his extreme grief at the death of his friend.
good-writing-001441.zh: 我们非常清楚那两个词的含义——他因朋友去世而陷入极度悲痛的境地。

good-writing-001442.en: But this being the Bible, we can assume he is weeping for all of humanity, the terrible pain we must all experience because our most beloved people die.
good-writing-001442.zh: 但既然这是《圣经》中的记载，我们可以认为他正在为全人类哭泣——因为我们的至亲所遭遇的惨痛痛苦，是我们所有人都必须承受的。

good-writing-001443.en: And, at the same time, in these two words, we remember that Jesus is a man, a human, born of a mother, with bodily fluids—tears!
good-writing-001443.zh: 同时，在这两个字中，我们也要记住，耶稣是一个男人，一个人类，由母亲所生，拥有血液和泪水这样的身体分泌物。

good-writing-001444.en: Needless to say, none of us can write like Faulkner or John, but I think Neal is right when he urges short sentences on you, to stop the reader, make them take in the profundity we come upon in life.
good-writing-001444.zh: 不用说，我们当中没有人能像福克纳或约翰那样进行写作。不过，我认为尼尔的观点是正确的，他建议使用简短的句子来吸引读者的注意力，让他们能够感受到生活中所蕴含的深刻意义。

good-writing-001445.en: If your efforts feel pretentious, don’t give up.
good-writing-001445.zh: 如果你的努力显得做作或不切实际，也不要放弃。

good-writing-001446.en: Here are the most important words a writer can take to heart:
good-writing-001446.zh: 以下是作家们应该铭记的最重要的词语：

good-writing-001448.en: And I can’t let this opportunity pass without reminding you of what Calvin Coolidge said to a reporter who told him a friend had bet him that he couldn’t get more than two words out of the president:
good-writing-001448.zh: 我不能让这个机会溜走，因此必须提醒你们卡尔文·柯利奇曾经对一位记者说过的话。那位记者告诉他，有个朋友打赌说，他无法从总统那里得到超过两个字的回答。

good-writing-001450.en: Rule 23: Give Your Sentence a Finale
good-writing-001450.zh: 法则23：让句子有一个精彩的收尾

good-writing-001451.en: Even if you begin your sentence with a punch, end it stronger.
good-writing-001451.zh: 即使句子的开头已经很有冲击力，也要让结尾更有力量。

good-writing-001452.en: The strongest element of a sentence usually belongs at the end.
good-writing-001452.zh: 一个句子的最重点部分通常位于句子的末尾。

good-writing-001453.zh: 那种力量通常非常有力。

good-writing-001454.en: It’s short and sweet or terse and abrupt.
good-writing-001454.zh: 它简洁而有力，或者干脆而直接。

good-writing-001455.en: “My brother got the hiccups on the way to the movies” versus “On the way to the movies, my brother got the hiccups.”
good-writing-001455.zh: “我弟弟在去电影院的路上打嗝了。” versus “在去电影院的路上，我弟弟打嗝了。”

good-writing-001456.en: The strongest element isn’t necessarily the loudest; it can be something unusual or unexpected or gripping.
good-writing-001456.zh: 最强大的元素并不一定是那些最响亮的元素；它可以是一些不寻常、出乎意料或令人着迷的元素。

good-writing-001457.en: Think of a sentence as a line of poetry.
good-writing-001457.zh: 把句子想象成一首诗的行。

good-writing-001458.en: So much rides on the last word or syllable of a line of poetry: That final word is usually followed by a pause, as a sentence is by a period.
good-writing-001458.zh: 一首诗的最后一个词或音节非常重要：这个最后的词后面通常会有停顿，就像句子后面有句号一样。

good-writing-001459.en: The last word hangs around for a little longer.
good-writing-001459.zh: 最后一个词还停留了一会儿。

good-writing-001460.en: In its luxurious pause will it echo, mirror, complement, disturb, entice, suspend?
good-writing-001460.zh: 在它那奢华的暂停时刻，它会发出回声、反映、补充、干扰、诱惑、暂停……

good-writing-001461.en: Since a verb is often the most powerful and important word in the sentence, it can work well to push the verb as close to the period as possible.
good-writing-001461.zh: 由于动词通常是句子中最有力且最重要的成分，因此将动词尽量放在句点的附近会提高句子的可读性。

good-writing-001462.en: Rather than writing “We smashed through the guardrail and sailed over the cliff in our 1997 Honda Civic with the faulty brakes,” you could try “Our 1997 Honda Civic with the faulty brakes smashed through the guardrail, and over the cliff we sailed.”
good-writing-001462.zh: 与其写“我们驾驶着1997年生产的本田思域，在刹车系统出现故障的情况下冲破了护栏，坠入了悬崖”，不如这样写：“我们那辆1997年生产的本田思域，在刹车系统出现故障的情况下冲破了护栏，坠入了悬崖。”

good-writing-001463.en: Sometimes it’s right to back into the sentence, leaving the subject and verb to the end, for effect: “With his face dark in shadow from the bunched pin oak leaves overhead, only the whites of his eyes showed.”
good-writing-001463.zh: 有时候，将主语和谓语放在句子的末尾会更合适，这样能更好地表达效果：“在头顶上茂密的橡树叶的遮掩下，他的脸庞被阴影笼罩，只有他的眼睛的白色部分露出来。”

good-writing-001464.en: If the end of the sentence can’t manage to be the strongest, then backtrack to the beginning.
good-writing-001464.zh: 如果句子的结尾无法达到最强烈的效果，那么就回到句子的开始部分重新开始。

good-writing-001465.zh: 那也是第二种选择罢了。

good-writing-001466.en: For instance: “Bullets sprayed around his head, but none found skin.”
good-writing-001466.zh: 例如：“子弹击中了他的头部，但没有击中任何皮肤。”

good-writing-001468.en: All I can add to this is that as a reader, there is almost no greater experience than when a sentence sticks the landing, and you look up and savor that literary moment in time.
good-writing-001468.zh: 我只能补充一点：作为读者，几乎没有比句子能够恰当地落在文字上、然后你抬头品味那一段文学时刻更令人愉悦的体验了。

good-writing-001469.en: One of the most famous last lines in American literature is Fitzgerald’s in The Great Gatsby: “So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.”
good-writing-001469.zh: 在美国文学中，最著名的最后一句台词当属菲茨杰拉兹在《了不起的盖茨比》中的这句话：“于是我们继续前进，小船逆着水流航行，不断地被推向过去。”

good-writing-001470.en: That’s as perfect as it gets, but you and I are probably not going to come up with that level of greatness.
good-writing-001470.zh: 这已经是最完美了，不过你我俩可能都无法达到那样的高度。

good-writing-001471.en: What we can do is create clean, honest sentences that glide to completion.
good-writing-001471.zh: 我们能做的是创造出简洁、明了的句子，让这些句子能够自然流畅地读完。

good-writing-001472.en: Let me give you an example.

good-writing-001473.en: Here is a recent rough paragraph:
good-writing-001473.zh: 这是最近的一篇简短的段落：

good-writing-001474.en: So I managed to figure out how to get free of the algae and crawl out of the chilly lake by first finding something solid on the bank that was a little mucky, then hoisting myself out by first grabbing a clump of grasses that miraculously held, and pulling myself up.
good-writing-001474.zh: 我设法找到了一种方法，可以摆脱那些藻类，从寒冷的湖中爬出来。首先，我在岸边找到了一些比较坚硬的固体物体，然后抓住那些坚韧的草茎，借助这些草茎把自己拉了出来。

good-writing-001475.en: My job is to take out all the excess.
good-writing-001475.zh: 我的工作就是去除所有多余的成分。

good-writing-001477.en: I figured out how to get free of the algae in the chilly lake and hoist myself out, by first grabbing hold of something on the bank that was solid but mucky.
good-writing-001477.zh: 我找到了一种方法，可以从冰冷的湖中摆脱那些藻类，并把自己从湖中捞出来。首先，我抓住了岸边某种既坚固又沾满污渍的东西。

good-writing-001479.en: I then grabbed a clump of grass, held tight, and pulled myself up.
good-writing-001479.zh: 然后，我抓了一把草，紧紧握住它，试图让自己站起来。

good-writing-001480.en: The most dynamic aspects of those sentences are the hoisting, and the good news that the clump of grasses held.
good-writing-001480.zh: 这些句子的最动态的部分就是“提升”操作，而且好消息是，那片草丛还是被保留了下来。

good-writing-001482.en: I kicked free of the algae in the chilly lake and grabbed something solid and mucky on the bank.
good-writing-001482.zh: 我挣脱了冰冷的湖面上的藻类，然后抓到了岸边一些又硬又脏的东西。

good-writing-001484.en: I grasped a clump of grass and pulled.
good-writing-001484.zh: 我抓住了一丛草，然后用力拉了拉。

good-writing-001486.en: And I hoisted my spent body.
good-writing-001486.zh: 然后，我把自己那已经疲惫不堪的身躯举了起来。

good-writing-001487.en: OK, it’s not Mary Oliver or Thoreau, but we can see it now and feel some energy.
good-writing-001487.zh: 好吧，虽然这并不像玛丽·奥利弗或梭罗那样深刻，但我们现在能够感受到一些这种能量的存在。

good-writing-001488.en: Move the words of your sentence like puzzle pieces.
good-writing-001488.zh: 将句子中的词语像拼图块一样排列组合。

good-writing-001489.en: Sometimes I’ll come up with a sentence at the end of a paragraph that pulls this off—flows naturally along like a stream, building strength and coming to rest on nice, clean words that create a still pool, and I’ll know that this is exactly where the piece must end.
good-writing-001489.zh: 有时候，我会在段落的末尾造出一个能够自然流畅地流淌的句子——这种句子就像一条溪流，不断向前推进，最终在简洁而优美的词语中停歇下来，形成一片宁静的“静湖”。那时我就知道，这篇文章就应该在这里结束。

good-writing-001490.zh: 法则24：让对话凝练而清晰

good-writing-001491.en: Dialogue needs to be as zippy and economical as the rest of the book.
good-writing-001491.zh: 对话也应当像书中的其他文字一样，简练、灵动、不拖沓。

good-writing-001492.en: Dialogue exposes how characters make choices, and only in passing describes their personalities.
good-writing-001492.zh: 对话展示了角色如何做出选择，但只是略带地描述了他们的性格特点。

good-writing-001493.zh: 不要让你的员工们漫无目的地闲逛。

good-writing-001495.en: Just as you don’t need to show your characters excusing themselves to the bathroom, you don’t need to fill the pages with hellos, goodbyes, and gossipy chatter.
good-writing-001495.zh: 就像你不需要在文字中反复描述角色们去洗手间的情况一样，你也无需在页面上充斥着各种问候语、告别语以及闲聊内容。

good-writing-001496.en: (Unless your character is an annoying gossip, but even then, the drivel has to be punctuated with clues to upcoming consequences.)
good-writing-001496.zh: （除非你的角色是个爱搬弄是非的人，但即便如此，那些废话也必须有能够暗示后续后果的线索来加以点缀。）

good-writing-001497.en: Pay close attention to the start of any conversation.
good-writing-001497.zh: 在开始任何对话时，要特别注意。

good-writing-001498.en: If one character is more circumspect or withdrawn, they might not ever speak first.
good-writing-001498.zh: 如果某个角色更加谨慎或内向，他们可能永远不会第一个开口说话。

good-writing-001499.en: A garrulous character opens with a joke, not a wise comment.
good-writing-001499.zh: 一个爱唠叨的人总是以笑话开始对话，而不是发表明智的评论。

good-writing-001500.en: A physical, nonthinking character might grunt approval rather than vocalize a “yes.”
good-writing-001500.zh: 一个行动力强、不善于思考的角色可能会发出微弱的认可声，而不是用明确的“是”来回应。

good-writing-001501.en: As much as in their actions, characters deserve consistency in their diction and interjections.
good-writing-001501.zh: 无论是在行为上还是在其他方面，角色们的表达方式都应该保持一致性，包括他们的措辞和感叹词的使用方式。

good-writing-001502.en: The same is true for their interior dialogue.
good-writing-001502.zh: 他们的内心对话也是如此。

good-writing-001503.en: Too little dialogue, and the reader wonders what the characters sound like, and why they’re mute.
good-writing-001503.zh: 对话太少，读者会好奇这些角色的声音是什么样的，为什么他们要选择保持沉默。

good-writing-001504.en: Stories with little overt dialogue tend to depend on an offsetting amount of interior dialogue.
good-writing-001504.zh: 那些没有明确对话的故事，往往依赖于大量内心独白来推动情节发展。

good-writing-001505.en: Too much dialogue, and your reader begs for some action or color to relieve them from all the frustrating arguments.
good-writing-001505.zh: 对话太多了，读者的希望能有一些动作或者情感上的刺激，以缓解那些令人沮丧的争论所带来的压力。

good-writing-001506.en: This holds true in nonfiction as well.
good-writing-001506.zh: 这一点在非小说类作品中同样适用。

good-writing-001507.en: The dialogue may not be literal, in quotes, but as we readers make our way through recorded experiences, we expect to see living human beings react and interact, with thoughts and emotions.
good-writing-001507.zh: 这种对话可能并不完全是字面意义上的对话，而是我们在阅读这些记录下来的经历时，期望看到真实的人类个体在其中的反应和互动，包括他们的想法和情绪。

good-writing-001508.en: We humans participate in a well-known pattern that is repeated in virtually every fictional scene and nonfictional anecdote: situation, complication, resolution.
good-writing-001508.zh: 我们人类都会经历一种在几乎所有虚构故事和非虚构故事中都反复出现的模式：情境的设定、矛盾的出现，以及最终的解决。

good-writing-001509.en: This simple arc is expressed in other ways: desire, obstacle, solution; or thesis, antithesis, synthesis; or meeting, conflict, harmony.
good-writing-001509.zh: 这种简单的结构可以用其他方式来表达：欲望、障碍、解决方案；或者论点、对立面、融合体；又或者相遇、冲突、和谐。

good-writing-001510.en: Some personalities just don’t get along; others need an outside variable to force a conflict.
good-writing-001510.zh: 有些性格的人根本合不来；而另一些人则需要某种外部因素来引发冲突。

good-writing-001511.en: But the whole point is the conflict, and that requires characters who clash.
good-writing-001511.zh: 但问题的核心就是冲突，而要实现这种冲突，就需要有相互对立的角色存在。

good-writing-001512.en: Dialogue is a quick way to watch the disagreement unfold, while revealing personalities at work.
good-writing-001512.zh: 对话是一种快速了解分歧发生过程的方式，同时也能揭示人们的内在个性。

good-writing-001513.en: In nonfiction, the anecdote might have to replace dialogue with more inferential details: physical reactions, interior dialogue reactions.
good-writing-001513.zh: 在非小说类作品中，叙述方式可能需要用更富推理性的细节来替代对话描述：比如人物的生理反应、内心独白等。

good-writing-001514.en: (“Allen shivered nervously on the couch as Lamott paused to clean her glasses before resuming her interest in his manuscript.”)
good-writing-001514.zh: “艾伦在沙发上紧张地颤抖着，而拉莫特则停下来清理了她的眼镜，之后才继续关注他的手稿。”

good-writing-001516.en: The point about dialogue is that we should know who is speaking by what they say—their words and rhythms.
good-writing-001516.zh: 对话的关键在于，我们要通过说话者的言辞和语速来判断是谁在发言。

good-writing-001517.en: Dialogue is fraught with the potential to turn off the reader with too much explanation or repartee.
good-writing-001517.zh: 对话中容易出现这种情况：过多的解释或冗长的对白反而会让读者失去兴趣。

good-writing-001518.en: (You can have either a character who speaks whimsically, or me as a reader.)
good-writing-001518.zh: 你可以选择一个以幽默方式说话的角色，或者选择我作为读者。

good-writing-001519.en: The best way to check a passage of dialogue for authenticity and ease is to read it into a recording device and play it back.
good-writing-001519.zh: 检查一段对话的真实性及流畅度的最佳方式是将它读入录音设备中，然后播放出来。

good-writing-001520.en: Every flat or stilted note will make you cringe, but now you have a chance to get it right before giving it to someone to read and dismiss you as a fraud.
good-writing-001520.zh: 任何生硬或做作的表达都会让人感到不适。现在你有一个机会，在把作品交给他人阅读并让他们认为你是个骗子之前，先确保自己把作品表达得正确无误。

good-writing-001522.en: Then read it again into the recorder.
good-writing-001522.zh: 然后再次将其读入录音机中。

good-writing-001523.en: The characters know how they would talk, what they sound like, and why they need to say what they’re saying.
good-writing-001523.zh: 这些角色知道他们应该如何说话，他们的声音听起来是什么样的，以及他们为什么需要说出他们所说的话。

good-writing-001524.en: If you make them flashy, clipped, authoritative, ironic, or whatever when they aren’t, those snippets of dialogue will ring false and we will not keep reading.
good-writing-001524.zh: 如果你让这些对话片段看起来过于华丽、刻薄、具有权威性、带有讽刺意味，或者别的什么风格，那么当这些对话实际上并不具备这些特点时，读者就会觉得这些对话虚假，自然不会继续阅读下去了。

good-writing-001525.en: Some people and characters are easier to typecast memorably.
good-writing-001525.zh: 有些人和角色更容易被记住，从而被定型为经典形象。

good-writing-001526.en: I have a friend in her late thirties who speaks like a teenager.
good-writing-001526.zh: 我有一个朋友，她已经三十多岁了，但说话的口音却像青少年一样。

good-writing-001527.en: She begins most sentences, with “Well,” but she says it lazily, one might say stupidly, as “Wool.”
good-writing-001527.zh: 她开始大多数句子时都会说“嗯”，但她说这句话的方式很懒散，甚至可以说很愚蠢，就像“羊毛”一样。

good-writing-001529.zh: “羊毛材质的话，其实相当不错。”

good-writing-001530.en: “Will you stay in the Bay Area?”

good-writing-001531.en: “Wool, I’m thinking of moving to Portland.”
good-writing-001531.zh: “伍尔，我打算搬到波特兰去住。”

good-writing-001532.en: So she would be easy to capture.
good-writing-001532.zh: 因此，她很容易被捕捉到。

good-writing-001533.en: I also have the frankly friend—“Frankly, I’m thinking of moving to Portland”—the “literally” friend, and the Harold Pinter–play friend, with his pauses and cryptic silences.
good-writing-001533.zh: 我还有那种直率的朋友——“坦率地说，我正在考虑搬到波特兰去”——还有那种“字面意义上的”朋友，以及那种喜欢用停顿和神秘沉默来营造氛围的朋友，就像哈罗德·品特表演中的那样。

good-writing-001534.en: Most conversations in my life, however, are between people who sound like me, for all intents and purposes.
good-writing-001534.zh: 然而，我生活中的大多数对话，其实都是与那些听起来和我相似的人进行的。

good-writing-001535.en: So how would I distinguish them in a patch of dialogue?
good-writing-001535.zh: 那么，在一段对话中，我该如何区分它们呢？

good-writing-001536.en: Bear down on their ages, cultures, subcultures, education, and personalities.
good-writing-001536.zh: 关注他们的年龄、文化背景、亚文化特征、教育背景以及个性特点。

good-writing-001537.en: Is the speaker earnest, sarcastic, paying attention, shy, arrogant, prone to pontificating?
good-writing-001537.zh: 说话者表现得认真吗？还是带有讽刺意味？或者只是很专注地倾听？或者显得害羞、傲慢，容易说教？

good-writing-001538.en: Hand each one a microphone and let them speak into it, and listen for what sets their speech apart.
good-writing-001538.zh: 给每个人一个麦克风，让他们对着麦克风讲话，然后注意他们说话的特点，找出他们独特的表达方式。

good-writing-001539.en: My advice is to read the masters and see how they do it.
good-writing-001539.zh: 我的建议是，请阅读那些大师的作品，看看他们是如何进行操作的。

good-writing-001540.en: J. D. Salinger, Raymond Carver, and Virginia Woolf are some of my favorites.
good-writing-001540.zh: J.D. 塞林格、雷蒙德·卡弗和弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫是我最喜欢的作家。

good-writing-001541.en: Watch great modern movies whose screenwriters are legendarily great with dialogue, like Aaron Sorkin, Diablo Cody, Billy Wilder, John Sayles, Nora Ephron, William Goldman.
good-writing-001541.zh: 观看那些由著名编剧创作的优秀现代电影，比如亚伦·索尔金、迪亚布洛·科迪、比利·王尔德、约翰·塞尔斯、诺拉·埃弗龙和威廉·戈德曼的作品。

good-writing-001542.en: Study how their conversations canter along without sounding clipped and arch.
good-writing-001542.zh: 研究一下，如何让他们的对话进行得既流畅又不会显得生硬或不自然。

good-writing-001544.en: Rule 25: In Fiction, Archetype Your Characters
good-writing-001544.zh: 法则25：在小说中塑造具有原型力量的人物

good-writing-001545.en: Below the human stereotypes are common psychological patterns that readers expect.
good-writing-001545.zh: 在人们熟悉的刻板形象之下，存在着读者期待看到的共同心理模式。

good-writing-001546.en: Distinguish your characters’ personality types so they don’t blur into one another.
good-writing-001546.zh: 区分角色的性格类型，避免它们相互混淆。

good-writing-001547.en: In one way, every character you write is an aspect of yourself that is worthy of exploring.
good-writing-001547.zh: 从某种意义上说，你笔下的每一个角色都是你自身的一个方面，值得去探索。

good-writing-001548.en: But the characters themselves have to be distinct, even memorable, and consistent with the everyday conformity of personality types.
good-writing-001548.zh: 但是，这些角色本身必须具有独特性，能够给人留下深刻印象，并且与日常所见的性格类型相符合。

good-writing-001549.en: In my first draft, a character emerges as a rough-cast amalgam.
