good-writing-001549.zh: 在我的初稿中，一个角色只是被简单地拼凑在一起，缺乏应有的立体感。

good-writing-001550.en: As I work through the drafts, impurities are removed and the surface is burnished.
good-writing-001550.zh: 在修改这些草稿的过程中，会去除其中的杂质，使表面更加光滑。

good-writing-001551.en: I’ve cleaned up the exterior to make way for the interior.
good-writing-001551.zh: 我已经清理了外部结构，为内部空间的搭建腾出了空间。

good-writing-001552.en: The comedian Duncan Trussell says that when you first meet him, you’re greeting his bodyguard.
good-writing-001552.zh: 喜剧演员邓肯·特鲁塞尔说，当你第一次见到他时，你遇到的其实是他的保镖。

good-writing-001553.en: That’s the external view of the personality, which tends to enter the world defensively, as if in imminent danger.
good-writing-001553.zh: 这就是个性的外在表现，它往往以一种防御性的方式进入这个世界，仿佛处于迫在眉睫的危险之中。

good-writing-001554.en: By the third draft, though, I’m more concerned with exposing the quirks of the character’s hidden interior, the part of him that is inevitably lovely and kind and generous, even if he looks and acts like a monster.
good-writing-001554.zh: 不过，在第三稿中，我更关注于揭示这个角色内心深处的那些微妙特质——那些即使他看起来和行为像怪物，但本质上仍然美好、善良且慷慨的特质。

good-writing-001555.en: In that second-draft characterization, the lines between show and tell blur, and with confidence I can introduce contradictions.
good-writing-001555.zh: 在第二个草案中，描述内容与叙述之间的界限变得模糊不清，我可以自信地提出各种矛盾之处。

good-writing-001556.en: If you’re having trouble getting a precise fix on a character, Jungian archetype systems (Myers-Briggs, enneagram) are a handy guide.
good-writing-001556.zh: 如果你在准确识别某个性格特征方面遇到困难，那么荣格原型理论体系（迈尔斯-布里格斯类型学、九型人格等）可以作为一个有用的参考工具。

good-writing-001557.en: The Jungian charts help you sort out the character’s hidden fears and yearnings (one type might be seeking love, another seeking admiration), their pet peeves, unhealthy behaviors, demanding beliefs, ability to get along with other specific personality types, perfectionism or sloppiness, concern for outward appearance, and on and on.
good-writing-001557.zh: 荣格类型分析图可以帮助你识别角色中隐藏的恐惧与渴望（比如，某种类型的人可能渴望爱情，另一种类型的人则渴望得到他人的赞赏）。这些图还可以揭示角色所厌恶的事物、不健康的行为习惯、刻板的信念体系、与其他特定类型人格的相处能力、完美主义倾向或粗心大意的特点，以及对外在形象的重视程度等等。

good-writing-001558.en: So if your character has a chip on her shoulder, you might notice that she generally withdraws from conflict, dislikes loud noises and people, and when healthy can share unusual psychological insights.
good-writing-001558.zh: 因此，如果你的角色身上有某种“负担感”，你可能会注意到她通常会避免冲突，不喜欢嘈杂的声音和人群。此外，当她状态良好时，她还会展现出一些不同寻常的心理洞察力。

good-writing-001559.en: But a boastful character thrives in conflict, listens to heavy metal, and when healthy enjoys a hearty laugh over a silly subject.
good-writing-001559.zh: 但一个爱炫耀的人总是喜欢在冲突中表现自己，喜欢听重金属音乐，而且只要心情好，就会因为一些有趣的事情而开心地大笑。

good-writing-001560.en: Your reader is unconsciously aware of these behavioral attributes and will be annoyed if your characters don’t play out their archetypal roles.
good-writing-001560.zh: 你的读者会无意识地注意到这些行为特征，如果角色们无法扮演他们典型的角色，他们就会感到不满。

good-writing-001561.en: Some authors present us with archetypal characters who adorn fabulous settings and plots.
good-writing-001561.zh: 一些作者塑造了具有典型特征的人物形象，这些人物生活在奇妙的背景和情节中。

good-writing-001562.en: Genre fiction—historical, sci-fi, horror, whatever—focuses mostly on how the characters deal with the outside world of things and other people, and their characters don’t necessarily grow or change; they’re just tortured over and over again.
good-writing-001562.zh: 类型小说——无论是历史题材、科幻题材还是恐怖题材——主要关注的是角色如何与外部世界中的事物和其他人相处。这些角色往往不会真正成长或发生变化；他们只是不断地经历着痛苦的折磨而已。

good-writing-001563.en: I can name some excellent authors who write this way, but they might feel insulted.
good-writing-001563.zh: 我可以列举一些以这种方式写作的优秀作家，不过他们可能会觉得受到了冒犯。

good-writing-001564.en: That’s because we’re told that characters are supposed to develop.
good-writing-001564.zh: 这是因为我们被告知，角色应该是具有成长发展的。

good-writing-001565.en: Writers whose characters change over time stay within the archetype model but move the character from a healthy place to an unhealthy place or vice versa.
good-writing-001565.zh: 那些角色随着故事的发展而发生变化的小说家，仍然遵循原型模型，只不过是将角色从“健康状态”转变为“不健康状态”，或者相反地改变他们的状态。

good-writing-001566.en: These writers often include interior dialogue, so we can have what the movies call reaction shots—a bit of a riff on how the character is thinking about the events around her.
good-writing-001566.zh: 这些剧本通常包含内部对白，因此我们可以采用电影中所谓的“反应镜头”——即用来表现角色对周围事件思考过程的镜头。

good-writing-001567.en: It gets quite complicated when you notice that each archetype has its own way of getting better and worse, and your reader knows intuitively when you’ve got that wrong.
good-writing-001567.zh: 当你发现每个原型都有其独特的优劣之分时，情况就会变得相当复杂了。而读者能够直观地察觉到你是否处理错了这个问题。

good-writing-001568.en: It may take only a sentence or two to distinguish a character’s external specialness—their unique set of physical attributes.
good-writing-001568.zh: 要区分一个角色的独特外在特征，只需用一两句话就能说明——即他们独特的身体属性。

good-writing-001569.en: Their internal specialness must be attended to through every scene they inhabit.
good-writing-001569.zh: 他们内在的特殊性必须体现在他们所处的每一个场景中。

good-writing-001570.en: When an actor asks “What’s the motivation?” for their role’s action or statement, they’re tying together a coherent personality.
good-writing-001570.zh: 当演员在表演某个动作或表达某个观点时，他们会提出“这种行为的动机是什么？”这个问题。实际上，这个问题正是将演员的个性特征与他们的行为联系起来的关键。

good-writing-001571.en: Your characters deserve believable, complex, contradictory, and surprising personalities, like your own.
good-writing-001571.zh: 你的角色应该拥有可信、复杂、矛盾且令人惊讶的性格特点，就像你自己的性格一样。

good-writing-001573.en: Each of our characters is probably some aspect of our own multilayered nature—the helper, the martyr, the know-it-all, the diplomat, etc.
good-writing-001573.zh: 我们的每一个角色，都代表着我们自身多层面的本质的某个方面——比如：乐于助人的人、爱逞强的人、自以为是的人、善于交际的人等等。

good-writing-001574.en: So it’s possible to do the deep dive with each of these inner characters, who make up you, and get to know them at the level of personal inquiry.
good-writing-001574.zh: 因此，我们可以深入探究构成你自身的这些内在特质，并从个人探索的角度来了解它们。

good-writing-001575.en: Why do you need to be right?
good-writing-001575.zh: 你为什么需要一直正确呢？

good-writing-001576.en: Where does that victimized self-righteousness spring from?
good-writing-001576.zh: 那种受害后的自以为是感，究竟从何而来呢？

good-writing-001577.en: Why do you try to be diplomatic with a jerk?
good-writing-001577.zh: 你为什么要对一个混蛋还采取 diplomat 的态度呢？

good-writing-001578.en: When I wrote my second novel, Rosie, the little girl who had lost her father was me, although I was twenty years older.
good-writing-001578.zh: 当我写第二本小说《罗西》时，那个失去父亲的女孩形象就是我自己的写照，只不过我的年龄要大二十岁而已。

good-writing-001579.en: But boy, did I know the grief and emptiness and disbelief Rosie felt.
good-writing-001579.zh: 但是，我完全能够体会到罗西所感受到的悲伤、空虚以及难以置信的情绪。

good-writing-001580.en: Her mother, Elizabeth, was an elegant alcoholic, and while I was not elegant, I could write the hell out of her alcoholism.
good-writing-001580.zh: 她的母亲伊丽莎白是个优雅的酒鬼。虽然我并不优雅，但我可以非常生动地描述她酗酒的习性。

good-writing-001581.en: Elizabeth’s best friend, a zaftig codependent with a huge heart and capacity to express love?
good-writing-001581.zh: 伊丽莎白最好的朋友，一个充满爱心的、依赖性强的女孩，她有着巨大的爱心，并且能够表达出对爱的真挚之情。

good-writing-001583.en: And James, Elizabeth’s future husband, was a funny writer who (like most writers) had equal proportions of grandiosity and shaky self-esteem.
good-writing-001583.zh: 而詹姆斯，伊丽莎白的未来丈夫，则是一个幽默的作家。像大多数作家一样，他同样具有强烈的野心感，但自尊心却并不坚定。

good-writing-001584.en: The marvelous travel and spiritual writer Pico Iyer wrote, “Writing is, in the end, that oddest of anomalies: an intimate letter to a stranger.”
good-writing-001584.zh: 那位杰出的旅行与灵性作家皮科·艾耶写道：“写作，归根结底，是一种最奇特的异态现象——一种向陌生人发送的亲密信件。”

good-writing-001585.en: This does not mean you need to tell us your weight or the name of the person you hate most in the world and will never forgive.
good-writing-001585.zh: 这并不意味着你需要告诉我们你的体重，或者那个你最讨厌、永远都不会原谅的人的名字。

good-writing-001586.en: This means you write from who and where you are, not from who and where you think we want you to be.
good-writing-001586.zh: 这意味着，你应该以自己真实的身份和所处的环境来写作，而不是以我们认为你应该遵循的身份和环境来写作。

good-writing-001587.en: As the saying goes, you be you.
good-writing-001587.zh: 正如那句谚语所说，做你自己吧。

good-writing-001588.en: Gaddis got to be Gaddis, Kerouac got to be Kerouac, but I have not felt moved to read either in forty years.
good-writing-001588.zh: 加迪斯终究还是加迪斯，克鲁亚克终究还是克鲁亚克，但四十年来，我从未真正被这两种风格所吸引，想要去阅读它们。

good-writing-001589.en: You, on the other hand, may very well catch my attention and lure me into reading what you make of it all.
good-writing-001589.zh: 而您，很可能会吸引我的注意力，并促使我阅读您所写的内容。

good-writing-001591.en: Start with the concrete—what happened—and after, when appropriate, riff on your thoughts about consequences.
good-writing-001591.zh: 从具体的事情——发生了什么——写起；随后，在适当的时候，再展开你对其后果的思考。

good-writing-001592.en: Disastrously, you probably learned this directive as “show, don’t tell,” which is often flat-out wrong and has led to a lot of strangely thin short stories populating literary journals.
good-writing-001592.zh: 糟糕的是，你可能把这条规则理解为“用展示而不是讲述的方式表达”，但实际上这种理解是完全错误的。这种错误导致了很多故事显得空洞无物，这些故事充斥在文学期刊中。

good-writing-001593.en: The central idea behind “show, don’t tell” is that setting, character, voice, and plot should go a long way in satisfying the reader’s curiosity.
good-writing-001593.zh: “展示而非讲述”这一理念的核心思想是：环境、角色、语气以及情节都应该起到激发读者好奇心的作用。

good-writing-001594.en: It’s a helpful old rule so far as it goes: Showing things physically and through the subtlety of diction and psychological tropes is the starting point of any scene.
good-writing-001594.zh: 从效果来看，这确实是一条有用的规则：通过具体的表现方式，以及精妙的措辞和心理描写来呈现事物，是任何场景的出发点。

good-writing-001595.en: These touchstones are necessary for the seamless world that we cherish finding.
good-writing-001595.zh: 这些标准是我们所追求的无缝连接的世界的必要条件。

good-writing-001596.en: I think of The Great Gatsby as the preeminent “show, don’t tell” novel, and it works sublimely.
good-writing-001596.zh: 我认为《了不起的盖茨比》是一部典型的“通过场景描写而非直接叙述”来呈现故事的小说，这种写作方式非常出色。

good-writing-001597.en: Using an inconsequential, disinterested character as his narrator, Fitzgerald adopts a nonjudgmental tone throughout.
good-writing-001597.zh: 菲茨杰拉德以一位无关紧要、冷漠无情的角色作为自己的叙述者，在整部作品中都保持了一种非评判性的语气。

good-writing-001598.en: Until the very end of the book, that is, when out of the blue comes this sentence:
good-writing-001598.zh: 直到书的最后部分，也就是在某一刻突然出现了这句话：

good-writing-001599.en: They were careless people, Tom and Daisy—they smashed up things and creatures and then retreated back into their money or their vast carelessness or whatever it was that kept them together, and let other people clean up the mess they had made.
good-writing-001599.zh: 他们是一群粗心大意的人，汤姆和黛西就是这样——他们总是破坏各种东西和生物，然后又回到他们的金钱中，或者继续他们的那种无拘无束的生活状态中。他们让其他人来收拾他们造成的混乱局面吧。

good-writing-001600.en: It’s a remarkable and memorable sentence for other reasons, but mainly it just plain sticks out.
good-writing-001600.zh: 这句话之所以引人注目且令人难忘，还有其他原因，但最主要的原因还是因为它本身就很独特、很突出。

good-writing-001602.en: Running into it as I finish up Gatsby, I might mumble, “I kind of thought that about Tom and Daisy, but nobody told me to before. Now I know.”
good-writing-001602.zh: 当我读完《 Gatsby》这本书时，我可能会嘟囔着说：“我原本以为关于汤姆和黛西的事情应该由别人来告诉我，但没有人之前提醒过我。现在我知道了。”

good-writing-001603.en: All of a sudden the book is a moral tale, a tragedy, and the character Gatsby is even more sympathetic.
good-writing-001603.zh: 突然间，这本书变成了一个道德故事，一个悲剧，而角色盖茨比则变得更加令人同情了。

good-writing-001604.en: By suddenly telling, Fitzgerald rounds out the reader’s thoughts just as the tale comes to a conclusion.
good-writing-001604.zh: 通过突然的揭示，菲茨杰拉德在故事结束时为读者勾勒出了完整的画面。

good-writing-001605.en: Fitzgerald couldn’t help himself, and needed it understood that his view wasn’t solipsistic, amoral, or tolerant.
good-writing-001605.zh: 菲茨杰拉德无法控制自己的情绪，他希望人们明白，他的观点并非唯我论、无道德主义或宽容主义的。

good-writing-001606.en: He wasn’t modern, in other words.
good-writing-001606.zh: 换句话说，他并不具有现代性。

good-writing-001607.en: And he made that clear by showing and then, briefly, telling.
good-writing-001607.zh: 他通过展示并简要地说明来明确表达了这一点。

good-writing-001608.en: Strangely, a couple of generations later, his progeny—the brat novelists of the eighties and nineties, for instance—pursued random landscapes of characters who are solipsistic, amoral, and tolerant.
good-writing-001608.zh: 奇怪的是，几代之后，他的后代——比如八十年代和九十年代的那些小说家们——所塑造的角色往往都是那种自我中心、无道德感且宽容大度的形象。

good-writing-001610.en: They took showing without telling to an absurd meaninglessness.
good-writing-001610.zh: 他们把“不告而进”这一行为演绎成了毫无意义的行为。

good-writing-001611.en: Of course most authors don’t wait until the end to pass judgment or comment on their characters.
good-writing-001611.zh: 当然，大多数作者并不会等到最后才对角色做出评价或评论。

good-writing-001612.zh: 他们先展示，然后才进行叙述。

good-writing-001613.en: You get a little scenery and dialogue, then a little commentary.
good-writing-001613.zh: 首先会有一段简短的风景描写和对话，然后是一个简短的评论。

good-writing-001614.en: I think of it as showing, then riffing.
good-writing-001614.zh: 我将其视为一种展示和即兴发挥的过程。

good-writing-001616.en: Faulkner has Quentin say “Yes,” and then for three pages we have a stream-of-consciousness riff that doesn’t advance the story one instant, but tells us a lot about how Quentin sees the world.
good-writing-001616.zh: 福克纳让昆廷说“是”，然后接下来的三页里，我们看到了一段无意识的叙述，这段叙述并没有推动故事的发展，但却让我们很好地了解了昆廷如何看待世界。

good-writing-001617.zh: 这里有一个更直接的例子。

good-writing-001618.en: I literally pulled the first novel I saw from my shelves, Conjugating Hindi by Ishmael Reed.
good-writing-001618.zh: 我真的从书架上下载了第一本我看到的书籍，即伊什梅尔·里德所写的《Conjugating Hindi》。

good-writing-001619.en: He sat down at the table.

good-writing-001620.en: He tried to get back to his online Hindi lessons.
good-writing-001620.zh: 他试图继续学习他在线提供的印地语课程。

good-writing-001621.en: It was hard to get his head wrapped around the use of prepositions in Hindi.
good-writing-001621.zh: 要理解印地语中介词的使用方式非常困难。

good-writing-001622.zh: 实际上，它们属于后置词。

good-writing-001623.en: He was getting more out of Hindu history and literature than from the Hindi language, which for him was like a UFC fighter that had brought him to the mat and held him in a guillotine hold.
good-writing-001623.zh: 他从印度教的历史和文学作品中获得的收获，比从印地语中获得的要多。对他来说，印地语就像一名UFC拳击手，将他按在绞刑架上，使他无法动弹。

good-writing-001624.en: Puttbutt said that he quit Japanese lessons when it was required that he study Kanji, which is to English what “Jaws” was to swimmers.
good-writing-001624.zh: 帕特巴特说，当他被要求学习汉字时，他便放弃了日语课程。对游泳运动员来说，“Jaws”这个术语就像汉字对英语一样重要。

good-writing-001625.en: Boa lived in the country where most of the Black intellectual fire power was taken up with convincing millions of Whites that Blacks weren’t chimps, monkeys, gorillas, and apes, which was how the ancestors of these Whites were treated in Europe where they weren’t considered White.
good-writing-001625.zh: 博阿生活在这样一个地方：那里，大多数黑人知识分子的力量被用来说服数百万白人，让他们明白黑人并非黑猩猩、猴子或大猩猩，这些动物在欧洲并不被视为“白人”。而白人的祖先在欧洲则被当作“白人”来对待。

good-writing-001626.en: The response to these literary sermons was denial and ridicule.
good-writing-001626.zh: 对于这些文学讲道，人们的反应是否认和嘲笑。

good-writing-001627.en: The back and forth had become a big marketing enterprise.
good-writing-001627.zh: 这种争论已经发展成了一个巨大的营销活动。

good-writing-001628.en: Moreover, men who would never be profiled racially dominated the discussion of race and when it became the version of someone who knew the experience from the inside and someone who peeped from behind the curtains, their version prevailed.
good-writing-001628.zh: 此外，那些从不涉及种族问题的男性主导了关于种族问题的讨论。而当这种讨论变成那些了解内部情况的人以及从幕后观察的人所讲述的版本时，他们的观点便占据了主导地位。

good-writing-001630.en: No matter how difficult it was to train your brain to accept a new word order, the experience was worthwhile.
good-writing-001630.zh: 无论训练大脑接受新的语序有多么困难，这种经历都是值得的。

good-writing-001631.en: And it goes on, this riff.
good-writing-001631.zh: 然后，这个节奏继续下去了。

good-writing-001632.en: The action is at the beginning: sitting down, working out Hindi prepositions.
good-writing-001632.zh: 动作发生在开始时：坐下，练习印地语中的介词用法。

good-writing-001633.en: That takes almost no time to read.
good-writing-001633.zh: 阅读起来几乎不需要时间。

good-writing-001634.en: But through “telling, not showing,” we’re taken through some thoughts about history and language and by association to racism in American literary criticism, then police profiling and the white-dominated media, and suddenly back full circle to translating Hindi, but now with a racially oriented viewpoint.
good-writing-001634.zh: 但是，通过“讲述而非展示”的方式，我们得以思考历史与语言的问题。这些思考又涉及到美国文学批评中的种族主义现象，以及警察定性分析和以白人为主的媒体机制。最终，我们又回到了翻译印地语的任务上——不过这次，我们的视角带有种族主义色彩。

good-writing-001635.en: This passage isn’t stream-of-consciousness meandering, but an accurate depiction of how our minds riff, collecting new variables and information on the way, culminating in newfound thoughts.
good-writing-001635.zh: 这段文字并非那种无意识的、漫无边际的描写，而是对我们的思维过程进行了准确的描述——我们的思维在过程中不断收集新的变量和信息，最终形成新的想法。

good-writing-001636.en: Without riffing on abstractions, the plot would be pointless in a way.
good-writing-001636.zh: 如果不对抽象概念进行讨论的话，这个情节就会显得毫无意义。

good-writing-001637.en: Conjugating Hindi is a book about culture and racism and history and critical theory, and also a little about someone learning a new language.
good-writing-001637.zh: 《印地语的学习》是一本关于文化、种族主义、历史以及批判理论的书籍，同时也涉及了某人学习新语言的过程。

good-writing-001638.en: No question, a lot of the time, “show, don’t tell” works.
good-writing-001638.zh: 毫无疑问，很多时候“展示而非讲述”的方法确实很有效。

good-writing-001639.en: Annie Dillard instructs us not to describe emotions, implying that readers can’t be compelled to feel anything just by being told how the writer or a character feels.
good-writing-001639.zh: 安妮·迪拉德教导我们不要描述情感，暗示读者不会因为作者或角色的情感描述而被迫产生某种感受。

good-writing-001640.en: Most feelings can be portrayed through observable behaviors.
good-writing-001640.zh: 大多数情感都可以通过可观察的行为来体现。

good-writing-001641.en: Apologies to Annie Dillard, but I’ll make up an example:
good-writing-001641.zh: 向安妮·迪拉德表示歉意，不过我姑且举一个例子吧：

good-writing-001642.en: You would have thought them early birds, these few spectators sprinkled around the aluminum bleachers as if in their customary seats for a high school football game, this pair hunched under a blanket hiding their faces, that couple nearly back to back, the man’s vision fixed on the metal foot plank where his feet splayed, the woman’s red eyes facing forward, still trying to make sense of the twisted metal scaffold where the booster rocket failed, while a soldier in green fatigues on the viewing stand’s top step marched head high back and forth, back and forth, an hour now since the disaster.
good-writing-001642.zh: 那些早早到达现场的观众们，他们像往常一样坐在铝制看台上，观看高中橄榄球比赛。有一对情侣躲在毯子下面，遮住自己的脸；还有一对情侣几乎挨在一起，男人的目光固定在金属踏板上，他的双脚则平放在那里；而女人的眼睛则直直地盯着前方，试图理解那座扭曲的金属支架的构造，那里就是助推火箭坠落的地方。与此同时，一个穿着绿色军装的士兵站在观察台上，来回踱步，灾难发生已经有一个小时了。

good-writing-001643.en: Nowhere does it say, “They were shocked.”
good-writing-001643.zh: nowhere提到“他们感到震惊”这一表述。

good-writing-001645.en: I am completely fine with an author telling me useful information about the characters and their predicaments if it helps the story.
good-writing-001645.zh: 如果这种描述能够有助于故事的呈现，我完全不介意作者向我提供关于角色及其困境的有用信息。

good-writing-001646.en: Chekhov famously said, “Don’t tell me the moon is shining; show me the glint of light on broken glass,” and of course that is lovely, but not necessary.
good-writing-001646.zh: 契诃夫曾经说过：“不要告诉我月亮在发光；而是让我看到碎玻璃上反射出的光芒。”当然，这听起来很美，但并非必要之事。

good-writing-001647.en: I’m glad to know whatever you want to tell me about the moon, whether it was full or new, yellow or white, bright or behind clouds, or that today, an unmanned American spacecraft landed on it—you don’t need to show me a close-up of the American flag.
good-writing-001647.zh: 我很高兴能听到你想告诉我的关于月亮的一切，无论是月亮是满月还是新月形，是黄色还是白色，是明亮的还是被云层遮住的。或者，今天有一艘美国的无人航天器在月亮上着陆了——你不需要向我展示美国国旗的特写照片了。

good-writing-001649.en: Tell me when you can save me a lot of time before getting to an important moment in the paragraph or plot.
good-writing-001649.zh: 在段落或情节的重要时刻到来之前，告诉我你什么时候能够为我节省大量时间。

good-writing-001650.en: Tell me to spare me from tedium.
good-writing-001650.zh: 请告诉我如何避免这种乏味的感觉。

good-writing-001651.en: Tell me to skip having to repeat yourself.
good-writing-001651.zh: 告诉我，不要让我重复自己的话了。

good-writing-001652.en: “This was Ed Shap’s first girlfriend and he was drenched in flop sweat.”
good-writing-001652.zh: “这是埃德·沙普的第一任女友，他当时浑身湿透，汗流浃背。”

good-writing-001653.zh: 我们看到了逐渐扩散的湿意。

good-writing-001654.en: “Ed had thrown up his lunch an hour before but had brushed his teeth since.”
good-writing-001654.zh: 埃德在一小时前就已经吐了午餐，不过之后还是刷了牙。

good-writing-001656.en: Good information and we didn’t have to watch.
good-writing-001656.zh: 信息很准确，我们甚至不需要观看视频就能了解情况。

good-writing-001657.en: “Now his breath smelled faintly of minty soup.”
good-writing-001657.zh: “现在，他的呼吸中隐约有薄荷汤的味道。”

good-writing-001658.en: We know a lot in three sentences—how vulnerable he is, how much he cares that all goes well.
good-writing-001658.zh: 我们用三个句子就能了解很多事情——他有多么脆弱，以及他多么关心一切是否顺利进行。

good-writing-001659.en: I for one feel that he is going to get through this date without losing his first girlfriend on a technicality.
good-writing-001659.zh: 我个人觉得，他能够度过这个日子，而且不会因此失去他的第一任女友。

good-writing-001660.en: As always, the rule is that you can do anything in your writing that works, that you can get away with, that is satisfying to the reader.
good-writing-001660.zh: 一如既往，规则是：在写作中，只要方法可行、能够得逞，并且能让读者满意的话，就可以采用任何方法。

good-writing-001661.en: Rule 27: Give Them a Hero’s Welcome
good-writing-001661.zh: 法则27：让人物像英雄一样登场

good-writing-001662.en: Start off by telling the reader who to root for.
good-writing-001662.zh: 开篇就告诉读者，应该为谁加油、站在谁的一边。

good-writing-001663.en: If you’re writing fiction, within a page or so of your protagonist appearing, prove through the eyes of another character that they are lovable and lovely.
good-writing-001663.zh: 如果你正在创作小说，那么在主角出现的这一页左右的位置，通过另一个角色的视角来展现这个主角是如何可爱和迷人的。

good-writing-001664.en: Entering into a novel, the reader knows so little that they’re uncomfortable, even squirmy or jittery.
good-writing-001664.zh: 进入这个新颖的叙事环境后，读者会感到非常不安，甚至有些紧张或焦躁。

good-writing-001665.en: We’re generous, us readers, and will give an author as many as fifty pages of suspicion before feeling secure in the major characters, settings, and themes.
good-writing-001665.zh: 作为读者，我们往往比较宽容。在对主要角色、背景设定和主题产生信任之前，我们会先给作者多达五十页的描写空间，以便对它们进行初步的评估。

good-writing-001666.en: But one thing we will not put off is deciding who to root for.
good-writing-001666.zh: 但有一件事我们不会拖延，那就是决定支持谁。

good-writing-001667.en: I didn’t know this was a rule until a teacher asked us to read the first page of ten novels at random.
good-writing-001667.zh: 直到一位老师要求我们随机阅读十本小说中的第一页时，我才意识到这是一条规则。

good-writing-001668.en: All the ones I read had a first-page scene in which the protagonist was complimented by another character.
good-writing-001668.zh: 我读过的所有作品都在第一页设置了一个场景，在这个场景中，主角会收到另一个角色的赞美。

good-writing-001669.en: Maybe it was a random error, and this isn’t a real rule, but I just tried it with Conjugating Hindi by Ishmael Reed, and sure enough, tucked into the bottom of the first page describing the central character I found the phrase “He was popular among his students....”
good-writing-001669.zh: 也许那只是一个随机的错误，实际上这并不是什么真正的规则。不过，我试着用伊什梅尔·里德所著的《Conjugating Hindi》这本书来实践这个做法，结果确实在首页的页脚发现了这样的短语：“他在学生中很受欢迎……”

good-writing-001670.en: That’s definitely a character to cheer for.
good-writing-001670.zh: 那绝对是一个值得支持的角色。

good-writing-001672.en: You, as a writer, are asking us to come sit by the campfire and listen to your story, and very few of us want to spend all that time with you if your character annoys us or puts us off.
good-writing-001672.zh: 你，作为一个作家，要求我们围坐在篝火旁，聆听你的故事。但如果你的角色让我们感到厌烦或惹恼了我们，那么我们当中很少有人愿意花那么多时间听你的故事。

good-writing-001673.en: Remember: You need to get us to turn the page, and I am not going to keep reading if I don’t like the main figure.
good-writing-001673.zh: 记住：你需要让我们翻过这一页。如果我不喜欢这个主角，我是不会继续读下去的。

good-writing-001674.en: The wonderful novelist Ethan Canin, who taught for years at the Iowa Writers’ Workshop, told me thirty-five years ago that the most important aspect of a novel was a likable narrator.
good-writing-001674.zh: 那位杰出的小说家伊桑·卡宁曾在爱荷华作家工作坊任教多年。35年前，他告诉我，一部小说最重要的元素就是一位令人喜爱的叙述者。

good-writing-001675.en: Think of being led on a tour through a distant country: If the tour guide is learned but not likable, you’re going to have a lousy time.
good-writing-001675.zh: 想象一下，被带去参观一个遥远国家的情景：如果导游虽然知识渊博，但让人感觉不愉快，那么你的参观体验就会非常糟糕。

good-writing-001676.en: You want someone at the helm who’s worth spending time with.
good-writing-001676.zh: 你希望领导者是一个值得与之共事的人。

good-writing-001677.en: You like their vibe, their observations, and what they make of people and life; you like who they are and how they treat people.
good-writing-001677.zh: 你喜欢他们那种独特的氛围、他们的观察视角，以及他们对人和生活的看法；你喜欢他们作为一个人所展现出的特质，以及他们对待他人的方式。

good-writing-001678.en: So it is with main characters: They can do terrible things and make awful mistakes, because otherwise there is probably no plot.
good-writing-001678.zh: 对于主角来说也是如此：他们可能会做出可怕的事情，也会犯严重的错误。因为否则的话，很可能就不存在什么情节可言了。

good-writing-001679.en: But still, we have to want to spend time with them.
good-writing-001679.zh: 不过，我们仍然需要花时间陪伴他们。

good-writing-001680.en: Ignatius J. Reilly is a train wreck of a central character in John Kennedy Toole’s A Confederacy of Dunces, but a lovable train wreck.
good-writing-001680.zh: 伊格纳提乌斯·J·雷利是约翰·肯尼迪·托尔所著《一群糊涂虫》一书中一个混乱不堪的主角，不过他还是个挺可爱的“混乱角色”。

good-writing-001681.en: (Now, by the same token, Ethan told me that same day that you should never write out of spite or revenge, while I have told oceans of students they need no other reason.)
good-writing-001681.zh: 同样地，伊桑也在那天告诉我，写作行为绝不应出于恶意或报复之心；而我也曾告诉过许多学生，写作无需其他任何理由。

good-writing-001683.en: Keep your first description of a character or place distinctive enough that you aren’t tempted to add to it later.
good-writing-001683.zh: 第一次描写人物或地点时，就要写得足够鲜明，这样以后才不会总想再补上几笔。

good-writing-001684.en: Soon after any character enters, describe them physically, in one concise paragraph.
good-writing-001684.zh: 任何角色进入游戏后，都用一段简洁的文字描述他们的外貌特征。

good-writing-001685.en: You won’t need to ever again.

good-writing-001686.en: Add an additional descriptor, or repeat one, only when it might help the reader, not to reinforce something you’ve already expressed.
good-writing-001686.zh: 只有在可能帮助读者的前提下，才添加或重复描述某些要素；而不要为了强化你已经表达过的内容而重复描述相同的内容。

good-writing-001687.en: If he’s a pirate with a hook for a hand, the hook will need to play a role in a pivotal action scene.
good-writing-001687.zh: 如果他真是个手持钩子的海盗，那么这个钩子就必须在某个关键场景中发挥作用。

good-writing-001688.en: But if she wears an eye patch, you might never mention it again.
good-writing-001688.zh: 但如果你让她戴着眼罩，那么你可能就再也不会提起这件事了。

good-writing-001689.en: This rule has an unfortunate corollary: You better spend a lot of time on that introductory paragraph.
good-writing-001689.zh: 这条规则有一个不幸的附带结果：你必须在那个介绍性段落上投入大量的时间。

good-writing-001690.en: Each sentence in that paragraph will probably need to be revised and refined, changed and sorted, multiple times.
good-writing-001690.zh: 那段文字中的每一句话都可能需要多次的修改和完善工作，包括内容的调整与整理。

good-writing-001691.en: The character’s first entry needs to be memorable, both in psychological foreshadowing, and in their physical attributes.
good-writing-001691.zh: 这个角色首次出现的形象必须令人难忘，无论是在心理层面的伏笔设置上，还是在其外在特征上都是如此。

good-writing-001692.en: They can be short or tall, of course, or even medium height, but they also have to display either defects (a lopsided smile, or a slight crossing of the eyes, akimbo elbows), or striking affects (a lustrous gleam, imperceptible drool, charging walk), or admirable qualities (a swimmer’s shoulders, honest hairline, confident jaw).
good-writing-001692.zh: 当然，他们可以是矮个子，也可以是高个子，甚至可以是中等身高。但他们必须具备一些特征：比如不对称的笑容、轻微的撇眉动作、正确的手臂摆放方式；或者具有一些令人印象深刻的特质：比如像游泳运动员那样的肩膀曲线、清晰的发际线、自信的面部轮廓。

good-writing-001693.en: Here is the great short story writer Gina Berriault using one telling detail to fix a new character in our mind forever.
good-writing-001693.zh: 这是著名的短篇故事作家吉娜·贝里亚尔运用一个细节来为我们塑造了一个永恒的新角色的故事。

good-writing-001694.en: It’s all we know about this central character’s looks: “His profile with that heavy chin that he liked to remind everybody was Hapsburg hung openmouthed against the blowing fog and the cold jet-black ocean of night.”
good-writing-001694.zh: 关于这个主角的外貌，我们所知道的一切就是这些：“他的轮廓鲜明，那颗突出的下巴让人联想到哈布斯家族的贵族形象；他张着大嘴，面对着浓雾和漆黑的夜空。”

good-writing-001695.en: And here’s an example of a character’s first description wandering through multiple aspects of his life and personality, from the second paragraph of Andrew Sean Greer’s novel Less: “His slim shadow is, in fact, still that of his younger self, but at nearly fifty he is like those bronze statues in public parks that, despite one lucky knee rubbed raw by schoolchildren, discolor beautifully until they match the trees. So has Arthur Less, once pink and gold with youth, faded like the sofa he sits on, tapping one finger on his knee and staring at the grandfather clock. The long patrician nose perennially burned by the sun (even in cloudy New York October). The washed-out blond hair too long on the top, too short on the sides—portrait of his grandfather. Those same watery blue eyes.”
good-writing-001695.zh: 以下是安德鲁·肖恩·格里尔的小说《LESS》中第二段落对亚瑟·莱斯的描述示例： “他的身影其实还是年轻时的模样，不过已经五十多岁了。就像那些矗立在公共公园里的青铜雕像一样，尽管被学童们反复摩擦，它们依然保持着美丽的光泽，直到与周围的树木融为一体。亚瑟·莱斯的容貌也是如此——曾经充满青春活力的粉红色和金色，如今已经褪去，就像他坐着的沙发一样。他那长长的贵族式鼻子长期暴露在阳光下（即使在纽约的十月天阴云密布时也是如此）。头顶的金色头发过长，两侧则太短——这正是他祖父的样貌。还有那双淡蓝色的眼睛……”

good-writing-001696.en: This might possibly not be someone to admire.
good-writing-001696.zh: 这个人可能并不值得欣赏。

good-writing-001697.en: Keeping the telling detail in line with the personality reminds me of Anton Chekhov’s weaponry rule: If a gun is mentioned, it has to be fired.
good-writing-001697.zh: 将描述细节与角色的性格特征相结合，让我想起了安东·契诃夫的“武器规则”：如果提到了枪，那么这支枪就必须被使用。

good-writing-001698.en: Likewise, if my character has a faded look, at some point they have to fail.
good-writing-001698.zh: 同样地，如果我的角色看起来很暗淡无光，那么他们最终也必然会失败。

good-writing-001699.en: Consider every prop, setting, expression, and character in your story as a clue.
good-writing-001699.zh: 将故事中的每一个道具、场景、表情以及角色都视为线索。

good-writing-001700.en: All novels are detective stories to the reader puzzling out the meanings.
good-writing-001700.zh: 所有的小说对读者来说都是侦探故事，需要读者自己去解开其中的含义。

good-writing-001701.en: You can insert all the red herrings you want, but the more unusual the object or description, the more the reader expects it to fill an empty space in the compact puzzle that will be completed a little before the final page.
good-writing-001701.zh: 你可以插入任何你想要的“误导性的线索”，但越是奇怪的物品或描述，读者就越会期待它能填补那个需要被填满的“空白空间”——这个“空白空间”最终会出现在最后一页之前。

good-writing-001703.en: I used to agree with Neal on this, and then I got old.
good-writing-001703.zh: 我以前总是同意尼尔的观点，但后来年纪渐长，想法也发生了变化。

good-writing-001704.en: Now I am glad if a careful, respectful writer mentions important physical or historical details about a character more than once.
good-writing-001704.zh: 现在，如果一位细心且尊重的作家多次提及某个角色的重要外貌或历史细节，我会感到很高兴。

good-writing-001705.en: In the first third of a novel, we have been introduced to a number of characters and are just coming to know them, and things can get muddled for me.
good-writing-001705.zh: 在小说的第一部分，我们刚刚认识了一些角色，对这些角色的了解还有限，因此可能会觉得有些混乱。

good-writing-001706.en: I’ll probably remember big deals about each person but maybe not some piece of connective or relational information between the people that factors significantly as the plot unfolds.
good-writing-001706.zh: 我可能会记住每个人之间的重大交易细节，但那些在情节发展中起到重要作用、涉及各人之间联系或关系的信息，可能就不会被记在心里了。

good-writing-001707.en: This is why you need a writing group or partner who will let you know that you already told them that, and it bugs them.
good-writing-001707.zh: 这就是为什么你需要一个写作小组或合作伙伴，他们能够确认你已经向他们传达过这些信息了，而这一点让他们感到困扰。

good-writing-001708.en: Or they might say they would have liked to have been reminded that Julie’s first of three marriages ended with the ex in jail, where she met her second husband in the visitor’s holding pen, who was also visiting her ex, with whom he had dealt Quaaludes in college.
good-writing-001708.zh: 或者，他们可能会说，他们希望有人能提醒他们，朱莉的第一次婚姻以她的前任入狱而告终。而她第二次结婚时的丈夫，则是在监狱的探视室里与她的前任相识的。这位前任在大学时期就经常服用喹阿鲁德类药物。

good-writing-001709.en: Remind us in subtle, thoughtful ways, and then see what your writing friends have to say.
good-writing-001709.zh: 以微妙而富有洞察力的方式提醒我们，然后看看你的写作伙伴们会有什么说法。

good-writing-001710.zh: 法则29：闻一闻玫瑰的芬芳

good-writing-001711.en: Sight is only one of five senses; let your readers enjoy touch, hearing, smell, and taste.
good-writing-001711.zh: 视觉只是五种感官之一；也让读者体验触觉、听觉、嗅觉和味觉。

good-writing-001712.en: Go back and add the sensory information you left out: smells, flavors, feelings, noises.
good-writing-001712.zh: 回去添加那些你遗漏的感官信息：气味、味道、感觉、声音。

good-writing-001713.en: You’re probably already perfectly good at providing the visuals.
good-writing-001713.zh: 你可能已经非常擅长提供这些视觉效果了。

good-writing-001714.en: Most of us have memories that lean heavily on an internal movie screen.
good-writing-001714.zh: 我们大多数人都有那种依赖于内心想象来回忆记忆的能力。

good-writing-001715.en: But living in the present isn’t like that: We’re taking cues from sounds, smells, and our tingling skin all the time, and then there’s the taste of lamb korma!
good-writing-001715.zh: 但是，活在当下并不是那样：我们时刻都在捕捉着声音、气味以及皮肤上的触感。此外，还有羊肉咖喱那独特的味道！

good-writing-001716.zh: 你想要一个无缝衔接的世界吗？

good-writing-001717.en: Evoke the rumbling train, the distant whistle, the neighbors arguing next door, the sweet fragrance of masa tortillas on any crumbled street in rural Mexico.
good-writing-001717.zh: 回忆起那隆隆的火车声、远处的汽笛声、隔壁邻居的争吵声，以及墨西哥乡村街道上那些碎裂的玉米饼散发出的甜美香气。

good-writing-001718.en: Humans rely more on visual cues than most other animals.
good-writing-001718.zh: 人类比其他大多数动物更依赖视觉线索来感知世界。

good-writing-001719.en: Our sight is remarkable and can pick up extremely fine detail.
good-writing-001719.zh: 我们的视力非常敏锐，能够捕捉到极其细微的细节。

good-writing-001720.en: On a dark night, our eyes can make out a lit match a couple miles away.
good-writing-001720.zh: 在漆黑的夜晚，我们的眼睛能够分辨出几英里外点燃的火柴的光亮。

good-writing-001721.en: This assists our hunting, our socializing through recognition of cultural and individual details, and our ability to travel long distances into new environments.
good-writing-001721.zh: 这有助于我们的狩猎活动，通过识别文化和个体特征来建立社交联系，以及让我们能够跨越长距离前往新的环境。

good-writing-001722.en: A human eye can take in a million impressions at once.
good-writing-001722.zh: 人类眼睛能够同时捕捉到一百万个视觉印象。

good-writing-001724.en: We also hear well, through a broader spectrum of tonality than most creatures.
good-writing-001724.zh: 我们还能够听到更宽广的音色范围，这比大多数生物要优越得多。

good-writing-001725.en: But that reliance on sight backed up by sound means that our other senses—taste, touch, and smell—offer writers an opportunity to fulfill the reader’s desire for novelty.
good-writing-001725.zh: 但这种对视觉的依赖，再加上听觉的辅助作用，意味着我们的其他感官——味觉、触觉和嗅觉——能够为作者提供机会，满足读者对新鲜感的需求。

good-writing-001726.en: If I’m not thinking about smell much in my daily life, the most familiar of odors can seem worth noting, even remarkable.
good-writing-001726.zh: 如果在日常生活中我不太关注气味，那么最熟悉的那些气味似乎也值得被注意到，甚至可以说是相当引人注目。

good-writing-001727.en: A hit of gasoline at the pump.

good-writing-001728.en: A sweet trace of bay leaf in the woods.
good-writing-001728.zh: 森林中弥漫着一丝芳香的月桂叶味。

good-writing-001729.zh: 一只臭鼬在我院子里游荡？

good-writing-001730.en: No, it’s just my neighbor lighting up another skunkweed joint.
good-writing-001730.zh: 不，只是我的邻居又在点燃另一处大麻烟头而已。

good-writing-001731.en: Viewing the kitchen counter is mundane no matter how well written; smelling a strawberry-rhubarb pie pulls the reverse lever on the time travel machine.
good-writing-001731.zh: 无论描述多么生动，观察厨房的台面都显得很乏味；而闻到草莓大黄派的香气时，就会拉动时间旅行机器上的反向把手。

good-writing-001732.en: Proust didn’t begin Remembrance of Things Past with a view of his room as a child, but with the taste of a madeleine.
good-writing-001732.zh: 普鲁斯特创作《往事与记忆》时，并非以他童年时的房间为灵感，而是以马德兰蛋糕的口感为出发点。

good-writing-001733.zh: 以下是那段著名的文字：

good-writing-001734.en: No sooner had the warm liquid mixed with the crumbs touched my palate than a shudder ran through me and I stopped, intent upon the extraordinary thing that was happening to me.
good-writing-001734.zh: 那温热的液体与碎屑混合在一起后，立刻触碰到我的舌尖。一种难以言表的愉悦感涌遍全身，我停止了咀嚼，全神贯注地观察着正在发生在我身上的这一奇妙的景象。

good-writing-001735.en: An exquisite pleasure had invaded my senses, something isolated, detached, with no suggestion of its origin.
good-writing-001735.zh: 一种精妙愉悦感侵入了我的感官，这种感觉是孤立的、独立的，完全无法推测其起源。

good-writing-001736.en: And at once the vicissitudes of life had become indifferent to me, its disasters innocuous, its brevity illusory—this new sensation having had on me the effect which love has of filling me with a precious essence; or rather this essence was not in me it was me....
good-writing-001736.zh: 顿时，人生的种种变迁对我来说变得无足轻重了——那些灾难、那些短暂而虚幻的生命，都变得微不足道。这种新的感觉，就像爱情一样，让我感受到一种珍贵的情感；或者更确切地说，这种“珍贵感”并不存在于我身上，而是存在于我自己身上……

good-writing-001739.en: How could I seize and apprehend it?
good-writing-001739.zh: 我如何能够抓住并逮捕它呢？

good-writing-001740.zh: ……突然间，那些记忆便清晰地浮现在了面前。

good-writing-001741.en: The taste was that of the little piece of madeleine which on Sunday mornings at Combray (because on those mornings I did not go out before mass), when I went to say good morning to her in her bedroom, my aunt Léonie used to give me, dipping it first in her own cup of tea or tisane.
good-writing-001741.zh: 那味道就像是一小块马德琳蛋糕的滋味。在康布雷，那些星期天的早晨（因为那些早晨我会在弥撒之前出门），当我会去她的卧室向她道别时，我的姑妈莱奥妮总会先在自己的茶或饮料中蘸一点这种味道，然后让我品尝。

good-writing-001742.en: The sight of the little madeleine had recalled nothing to my mind before I tasted it.
good-writing-001742.zh: 看到那个小蛋糕时，我脑海中没有任何相关的记忆。直到我尝到了它，才想起了以前的事情。

good-writing-001743.en: And all from my cup of tea.
good-writing-001743.zh: 而这一切，都来自我的茶壶里。

good-writing-001744.en: The sight of the little madeleine had recalled nothing to my mind before I tasted it.
good-writing-001744.zh: 看到那个小蛋糕时，我脑海中没有任何相关的记忆。直到我尝到了它，才想起了以前的事情。

good-writing-001745.en: I make a separate pass through my fiction to add other senses in action, because I know I’m overly attached to visuals in my early drafts.
good-writing-001745.zh: 在创作过程中，我会特意留出一部分时间来构思那些具有视觉冲击力的场景，因为我知道在初稿阶段，我过于依赖视觉上的表现力了。

good-writing-001746.en: Senses can be found inside, too, in subtle touch and bouts of ordinary synesthesia.
good-writing-001746.zh: 感官也存在于内部，通过微妙的触感以及普通的联觉现象来体现。

good-writing-001747.en: I don’t just judge truth, I land in it, with a slight feeling of fullness in my lower belly or guppies rushing up my spine.
good-writing-001747.zh: 我不会仅仅判断事物的真实性，我会全身心地体验它，会感受到下腹部有一种轻微的充实感，或者会有小鱼在脊柱上快速游动的感觉。

good-writing-001748.en: A noisy cocktail party in a high-ceilinged room is metallic to my ears, while the seaside is scented with salted cod and boardwalk taffy.
good-writing-001748.zh: 在天花板很高的房间里，喧闹的鸡尾酒派对声对我来说就像是一种噪音；而在海边，则弥漫着咸鳕鱼和甜甜圈带来的香气。

good-writing-001750.en: I love this rule and I love books and poems rich in sounds and tastes and touch.
good-writing-001750.zh: 我喜欢这条规则，也喜欢那些充满声音、味道和触感的书籍和诗歌。

good-writing-001751.en: Smells are such profound links to memories.
good-writing-001751.zh: 气味与记忆之间存在着如此紧密的联系。

good-writing-001752.en: A lighted candle, your grandma’s biscuits, honeysuckle, gunpowder, the night, the dawn.
good-writing-001752.zh: 一支点着的蜡烛，你祖母做的饼干，金银花，火药，夜晚，黎明。

good-writing-001753.en: Once my very young son was riding on someone’s shoulders late at night.
good-writing-001753.zh: 有一次，我年幼的儿子在深夜时骑在别人的肩膀上。

good-writing-001754.en: He looked up at the sky and said, swooning, “It smells like moon.”
good-writing-001754.zh: 他抬头望向天空，恍惚地说：“闻起来像月亮的味道。”

good-writing-001755.en: So light a candle or get outside before the sun rises, and inhale deeply.
good-writing-001755.zh: 那么，在太阳升起之前，点燃一支蜡烛，或者到户外去，深呼吸几次吧。

good-writing-001756.en: Scribble down copious notes about the experience, although you will use only one sentence in your writing.
good-writing-001756.zh: 请尽可能详细地记录下你的经历，不过在写作时只需要用一句话来描述即可。

good-writing-001757.en: And touch, wow: the lawn and orange peel and the skin of the oldest and youngest people you know.
good-writing-001757.zh: 还有那种触感……哇塞：草坪的触感，以及你认识的最年长者和最年轻者的皮肤触感。

good-writing-001758.en: Go get your silk blouse out of the closet, close your eyes, and feel its slinky smoothness.
good-writing-001758.zh: 把你的丝绸衬衫从衣柜里取出来，闭上眼睛，感受它那细腻的触感。

good-writing-001759.en: Find a burlap sack and a rose petal and a rock and your own hand: Close your eyes and let the descriptors come.
good-writing-001759.zh: 找到一条麻袋、一片玫瑰花瓣以及一块石头；然后，闭上你的眼睛，让这些元素自然呈现出来。

good-writing-001760.en: Read the masters and see how they do it, Hemingway and Fitzgerald and Mary Oliver and Terry Tempest Williams and Shakespeare.
good-writing-001760.zh: 阅读那些大师的作品，看看他们是如何做到这一点的——海明威、菲茨杰拉德、玛丽·奥利弗、特里·坦佩斯特·威廉姆斯，还有莎士比亚。

good-writing-001761.en: Our senses ground us to this earth and to each other, and paradoxically, they are how our imaginations take flight.
good-writing-001761.zh: 我们的感官将我们与彼此紧密地联系在一起；而矛盾的是，正是这些感官也激发了我们的想象力。

good-writing-001762.en: I am so grateful when a writer includes a lot of carefully chosen details about the world outside us, above us and below us and all around us, because then I see, hear, touch, taste, and smell those moments as if for the first time.
good-writing-001762.zh: 当一位作家能够详细而精心地描述我们周围的世界时，我会感到非常感激。因为我就能像第一次那样，去感知那些细节——看到它们、听到它们、触摸它们、品尝它们、闻到它们的气味。

good-writing-001763.zh: 他们用喷雾剂把我弄醒了。

good-writing-001764.zh: 法则30：别隔着一层感知来写

good-writing-001765.en: Don’t point out that someone is thinking, opining, or experiencing what is already happening on the page.
good-writing-001765.zh: 对于已经直接呈现在文字中的事情，不必再特意交代某个人正在思考、发表看法或亲身感受它。

good-writing-001766.en: The less self-conscious the character, the more gripping.
good-writing-001766.zh: 角色的自我意识越低，其表现就越具有吸引力。

good-writing-001767.en: Don’t start a sentence with “He thought” or “She wondered” or “They felt,” or anything that filters the scene through a character’s brain.
good-writing-001767.zh: 不要用“他思考着”、“她疑惑着”或者“他们感觉到”这样的开头方式来开始一个句子，因为这些表达方式都是通过角色的视角来描述的。

good-writing-001768.en: Staying on top of this rule takes more work than you might think.
good-writing-001768.zh: 遵守这一规则需要付出比想象中更多的努力。

good-writing-001769.en: Our everyday conversation is littered with “I was wondering,” “I feel like,” “I hate it when,” “I’m worried that,” “I think that,” and on and on.
good-writing-001769.zh: 我们的日常对话中常常会出现“我想知道”、“我觉得”、“我讨厌这种情况”、“我担心”、“我认为”等等这样的表达。

good-writing-001770.en: Dialogue in real life and on the page improves when we engage the thought as an activity.
good-writing-001770.zh: 在现实生活中以及文字交流中，当我们把思考作为一种活动来参与时，交流的效果会更好。

good-writing-001771.en: Often the way out is by the character asking a question: “What would happen if?”
good-writing-001771.zh: 通常，解决问题的办法就是让角色提出一个问题：“如果……会怎么样？”

good-writing-001772.en: Sometimes the thought is just shortened: “That’s right” instead of “I feel like you’re right about that.”
good-writing-001772.zh: 有时候，这个想法会被简略表达出来：用“没错”来代替“我觉得你在这个问题上的判断是正确的”。

good-writing-001773.en: “Bruce, you’re such a jerk,” Mabel said.
good-writing-001773.zh: “布鲁斯，你真是个混蛋，”梅布尔说道。

good-writing-001774.en: What follows are three possible responses by Bruce, in pairs.
good-writing-001774.zh: 以下是布鲁斯可能给出的三种回应，成对出现。

good-writing-001775.en: In each pair, the first one filters his response.
good-writing-001775.zh: 在每一对关系中，第一对会过滤掉其响应信息。

good-writing-001776.en: Notice how much more the second version, without a filter, grabs you.
good-writing-001776.zh: 请注意，第二版版本在没有滤镜的情况下，能够吸引你的注意力，而且效果要好得多。

good-writing-001781.en: “I think you are right,” he said.

good-writing-001783.en: As an author, your superpower of self-reflection can emerge as a pernicious obstacle.
good-writing-001783.zh: 作为一位作家，你的自我反思能力可能会成为一个严重的障碍。

good-writing-001786.en: Thinking is the opposite of action.

good-writing-001787.en: If you’re writing nonfiction, action may not be the motion of a story, but of an argument.
good-writing-001787.zh: 如果你在撰写非虚构作品，那么故事的驱动力可能并非动作，而应该是论点。

good-writing-001788.en: Self-reflection in the midst of a logical argument stalls out the same as in a car chase.
good-writing-001788.zh: 在逻辑论证过程中进行自我反思，其效果就像在追逐游戏中一样，会陷入停滞状态。

good-writing-001790.en: I think Socrates is a man.
good-writing-001790.zh: 我认为苏格拉底是一个真实存在的人。

good-writing-001791.en: Therefore, I believe that Socrates is mortal.
good-writing-001791.zh: 因此，我认为苏格拉底是死去的。

good-writing-001793.en: Because it is understood that thoughts and beliefs drive statements, presenting them in a sentence will be assumed to signal doubt.
good-writing-001793.zh: 因为人们认为，思想和信念是驱动言论的驱动力。因此，如果将这些思想或信念以句子的形式表达出来，就会被视为一种质疑的迹象。

good-writing-001794.en: If that’s what you want, fine, but otherwise try to scrap verbs of consciousness.
good-writing-001794.zh: 如果你真的想要这样，那好吧。但除此之外，尽量避免使用那些与意识相关的动词。

good-writing-001795.en: This is not a hard-and-fast rule.
good-writing-001795.zh: 这并不是一条绝对不可违反的规则。

good-writing-001796.en: Sometimes it is perfectly appropriate to indicate that the character is musing.
good-writing-001796.zh: 有时候，明确指出该角色正在沉思是完全合适的。

good-writing-001797.en: There’s even a corner of literary writing called metafiction or ur-fiction, which is intentionally self-conscious, to the point of elevating authorship to the surface.
good-writing-001797.zh: 在文学创作中，甚至还存在一种被称为“元小说”或“本我小说”的文学形式。这种形式具有极强的自我意识，甚至将作者的身份提升到了一个更为突出的位置。

good-writing-001798.en: By layering in the author as a character, usually biased and therefore unreliable as a narrator, meaning is disrupted, which is a riddle of its own surrounding the more typical puzzles found in any novel.
good-writing-001798.zh: 通过将作者塑造成一个角色来呈现故事，通常这种呈现方式会带有偏见，因此作为叙述者时其可靠性也会受到质疑。这样一来，故事的意义就被打破了，而这一矛盾本身，又构成了与任何小说中常见的谜题相呼应的又一个谜题。

good-writing-001799.en: Masters at this such as Italo Calvino or Umberto Eco embrace the postmodern philosophers of the late twentieth century, and their works can be genius in elaborating the kinks and possibilities in meaning.
good-writing-001799.zh: 像伊塔洛·卡尔维诺或翁贝托·埃科这样的大师们，都借鉴了二十世纪末的后现代哲学思想，他们的作品在细腻地描绘意义的复杂性和可能性方面展现了卓越的才华。

good-writing-001800.en: But before trying it yourself, recognize how much they have demanded of themselves, and the reader, in order to retain seamlessness both of the traditional story elements and of the lurking presence of a philosopher masquerading as a narrator.
good-writing-001800.zh: 但在尝试之前，请先认识到他们为了保持传统故事元素之间的连贯性，以及那个伪装成叙述者的哲学家的存在，而付出的巨大努力。

good-writing-001801.en: They have entered a hall of mirrors that requires a rich understanding to navigate.
good-writing-001801.zh: 他们进入了一个“镜子大厅”，要在这个迷宫中穿行，需要深刻的理解力。

good-writing-001802.en: I love to read them; I wouldn’t dare imitate them.
good-writing-001802.zh: 我喜欢阅读它们；我可不敢模仿它们。

good-writing-001803.en: Memoir and other forms of subjective nonfiction may also find verbs of opinion to be appropriate, especially in separating out facts from reflections.
good-writing-001803.zh: 回忆录及其他形式的主观性非小说作品同样可以使用“意见性动词”，尤其是在区分事实与个人反思时。

good-writing-001804.en: But even there, it might be wise to point out the subjectivity sparingly.
good-writing-001804.zh: 但即便如此，也还是应该谨慎地指出其中的主观性。

good-writing-001807.en: If you are blessed someday to be copyedited by a fierce, anorexic Croatian, as I was once, you will stop filtering your narration so often, or risk his contempt each time he catches you at it.
good-writing-001807.zh: 如果你有幸有一天能由一位脾气暴躁、患有厌食症的克罗地亚人来编辑你的故事，就像我曾经那样，你就不会再频繁地过滤自己的叙述了——否则每次他发现你这样做时，都会对你感到厌恶。

good-writing-001808.en: If you can’t break the habit, then go over your (theoretically) final draft and be on the lookout for verbs of opinion—“believed,” “felt,” “thought.”
good-writing-001808.zh: 如果你无法改掉这个习惯，那么请重新检查你的（理论上最终的）稿子，注意那些表示主观意见的动词，比如“认为”、“感觉”、“思考”等。

good-writing-001809.en: You’ll discover that you can take out a lot of them.
good-writing-001809.zh: 你会发现，你可以选择取消很多这些选项。

good-writing-001810.en: As Neal grudgingly acknowledges, you’ll settle sometimes on a sentence where a character does wonder, feel, or believe this or that.
good-writing-001810.zh: 正如尼尔不得不承认的那样，有时候你会把故事设定在角色会思考、感受或相信某些事情的场景上。

good-writing-001811.en: Of his examples above, I would have had Bruce the jerk say, “I think you’re right.”
good-writing-001811.zh: 在上面的例子中，如果让那个讨厌的布鲁斯来说话的话，他可能会说：“我觉得你说得对。”

good-writing-001812.en: This sounds more natural to me.
good-writing-001812.zh: 这对我来说听起来更自然一些。

good-writing-001813.en: These rules were never meant to dress you as an exterminator, fixated on eradicating every adverb, every filtering word, every “very” and “it.”
good-writing-001813.zh: 这些规则从来就没有旨在让你看起来像那种一心要消除所有副词、所有过滤词，以及所有“非常”和“它”的词语的人。

good-writing-001814.en: Few of you work for Terminix.
good-writing-001814.zh: 你们当中很少有人在Terminix公司工作。

good-writing-001816.en: The rules are simply suggestions for writing better sentences, clearer and more inviting.
good-writing-001816.zh: 这些规则只是关于如何写出更优美、更清晰、更吸引人的句子的建议而已。

good-writing-001817.en: With my fading memory, I recall a fashion icon suggesting that after getting ready for an evening out, you take off one thing—the brooch or the barrette, for instance, or the paisley pocket handkerchief.
good-writing-001817.zh: 在我的记忆逐渐模糊的印象中，我记得有一位时尚界的大师曾说过，在准备参加晚间活动时，应该脱掉某样东西——比如胸针或发夹，或者那些带有花边图案的口袋手帕。

good-writing-001818.en: Obviously, certain events dictate that you wear a Last Supper cummerbund, and far be it from me, etc.
good-writing-001818.zh: 显然，某些场合要求你必须穿着“最后的晚餐”风格的束腰外衣。我可绝对不会违背这一习俗啊。

good-writing-001819.en: Like most protocols, they apply to most of us, most of the time, in most circumstances.
good-writing-001819.zh: 像大多数协议一样，它们适用于我们中的大多数人，在大多数情况下都能得到应用。

good-writing-001820.en: Neal suggests in Rule 9 that you question transitions, and here the suggestion is that you question each filtering word.
good-writing-001820.zh: 在规则9中，尼尔建议对过渡词进行质疑，这里的建议是，你需要对每个过滤词都进行质疑。

good-writing-001821.en: Leave in the ones that you like.

good-writing-001822.en: Some tense, angry copy editor may some day attempt to change your mind, but don’t forget whose work it is, and that you work for you.
good-writing-001822.zh: 有些紧张、愤怒的编辑人员或许有一天会试图改变你的想法，但请记住，这是他们的工作，而你只是为自己工作而已。

good-writing-001824.en: Your reader will fill in the gaps; you only need to be complete enough.
good-writing-001824.zh: 读者会自行补上空白；你只需提供足够完整的线索。

good-writing-001825.en: It’s weird, but your reader of fiction, memoir, or biography probably knows much more about your characters than you do.
good-writing-001825.zh: 这很奇怪，但你的小说、回忆录或传记的读者，很可能比你自己更了解你的角色。

good-writing-001826.en: You’ve created what’s actual and plausibly true to your character in the scenes of the book.
good-writing-001826.zh: 你在书中的各个场景中，成功地塑造了符合你角色特点的真实且可信的人物形象。

good-writing-001827.en: Your reader fills in a lot of gaps.
good-writing-001827.zh: 你的读者能够填补许多空白。

good-writing-001828.en: How many characters’ ears have you described?
good-writing-001828.zh: 你描述过多少个角色的耳朵？

good-writing-001829.en: If any, just the funny ones, I suspect.
good-writing-001829.zh: 如果有的话，大概只是那些有趣的部分吧。我这么认为。

good-writing-001830.en: Your reader has sketched in the normal ears without prompting.
good-writing-001830.zh: 你的读者在无需提示的情况下，直接输入了正常听音。

good-writing-001831.en: Likewise, the reader constructs backstory and emotional characteristics that you haven’t bothered about.
good-writing-001831.zh: 同样，读者也会构建出一些你未曾注意到的背景故事和情感特征。

good-writing-001832.en: Just like you in real life.
good-writing-001832.zh: 就像你在实际生活中的样子一样。

good-writing-001833.en: If a stranger addresses you with a world-weary sarcastic demeanor, you might project on her a tough childhood or a past or present addiction.
good-writing-001833.zh: 如果一个陌生人用一种厌倦世界的、讽刺的语气与你交谈，那么你可能是在向她传达一种艰难的童年经历，或者某种过去的或现在的成瘾问题。

good-writing-001834.en: We all take tiny clues and blow them up into big stories.
good-writing-001834.zh: 我们都会从一些微小的线索出发，然后将这些线索发展成宏大的故事。

good-writing-001835.en: We’re quite often wrong, but who cares?
good-writing-001835.zh: 我们经常会犯错，但那又有什么关系呢？

good-writing-001836.en: All Hamlet has to say is “To be or not to be...” and we’re off and running.
good-writing-001836.zh: 哈姆雷特所要说的只有一句：“存在还是不存在……”，然后我们便开始行动了。

good-writing-001837.en: He’s overly cautious, so he probably didn’t get a lot of direction from his father.
good-writing-001837.zh: 他过于谨慎，因此可能很少从父亲那里得到指导。

good-writing-001838.en: Most likely he’s not quite completely formed, and we can expect some juvenile behavior to come.
good-writing-001838.zh: 很可能他还没有完全成熟，因此我们可能会看到一些幼稚的行为。

good-writing-001839.en: Our interpretations are bound to be modern, informed by the post-Freud world, and psychologically grounded in the trauma theory of childhood.
good-writing-001839.zh: 我们的解读方式必然具有现代性，其理论基础是后弗洛伊德主义的思想体系，并且在心理层面上以儿童时期的创伤理论为基础。

good-writing-001840.en: Harsh people come from dysfunctional families.
good-writing-001840.zh: 性格暴躁的人通常来自功能失调的家庭。

good-writing-001841.en: Child abusers were abused as children.
good-writing-001841.zh: 虐待儿童的行为，其实也是儿童时期就习得的不良行为。

good-writing-001842.zh: 好的父母会培养出聪明的孩子。

good-writing-001843.zh: 反社会人格者通常来自暴力背景。

good-writing-001844.en: These are tropes that the culture maintains, and even though they are unreliable (some sex workers have high self-esteem), the tropes are inserted by the reader when the backstory is left out.
good-writing-001844.zh: 这些都是文化所保留下来的刻板印象。尽管这些刻板印象并不真实（有些性工作者其实自尊心很强），但在省略了背景故事的情况下，这些刻板印象仍然被保留了下来。

good-writing-001845.en: Letting the reader fill in the gaps can be a lifesaver in the right hands—a novelist who can provide context and layering in other ways than backstory—or it can simply be laziness in the wrong hands, reducing characters to paper cutouts.
good-writing-001845.zh: 让读者自行填补空白，在合适的人手中可以成为解决问题的关键——比如，对于小说家来说，可以通过其他方式来提供背景信息和层次感，而不是仅仅依赖背景故事。但在不合适的人手中，这种做法可能会变成一种懒惰的行为，导致角色被简化为无生命的模型。

good-writing-001846.en: Just because the reader is filling in the blanks doesn’t let you off the hook.
good-writing-001846.zh: 即使读者在填写空白处，也并不能让你免于承担责任。

good-writing-001847.en: Nothing wrong with being direct with the backstory.
good-writing-001847.zh: 直接说明事情的来龙去脉并没有什么错。

good-writing-001848.en: Here’s most of the second paragraph of Dickens’s Great Expectations:
good-writing-001848.zh: 以下是狄更斯《远大期望》第二段的大部分内容：

good-writing-001849.en: As I never saw my father or my mother, and never saw any likeness of either of them (for their days were long before the days of photographs), my first fancies regarding what they were like, were unreasonably derived from their tombstones.
good-writing-001849.zh: 因为我从未见过我的父亲或母亲，也从未见过他们任何一张照片（因为在那个时代，还没有照片这种东西），所以我最初对他们的印象，都是从他们的墓碑上得来的，这些印象其实毫无根据。

good-writing-001850.en: The shape of the letters on my father’s, gave me an odd idea that he was a square, stout, dark man, with curly black hair.
good-writing-001850.zh: 我父亲名字中的字母形状让我联想到一个身材魁梧、皮肤黝黑、留着卷曲黑色头发的男人。

good-writing-001851.en: From the character and turn of the inscription, “Also Georgiana Wife of the Above,” I drew a childish conclusion that my mother was freckled and sickly.
good-writing-001851.zh: 从碑文的内容和措辞来看，“还有乔治亚娜，上述人物的妻子”，我得出了一个幼稚的结论：我的母亲一定是个有雀斑且身体虚弱的人。

good-writing-001852.en: To five little stone lozenges, each about a foot and a half long, which were arranged in a neat row beside their grave, and were sacred to the memory of five little brothers of mine—who gave up trying to get a living, exceedingly early in that universal struggle—I am indebted for a belief I religiously entertained that they had all been born on their backs with their hands in their trousers-pockets, and had never taken them out in this state of existence.
good-writing-001852.zh: 在他们的坟墓旁边，排列着五个小石制的小雕像，每个大约一英尺半长。这些雕像是为了纪念我的五个弟弟而立的——他们在那场普遍的奋斗中，非常早便放弃了追求生活的努力。我感激自己始终坚信，他们的父母在生命中的大部分时间都是仰面躺着，双手插在裤兜里，从未以这样的姿态生活过。

good-writing-001854.en: Remember sixty years ago how Mad magazine had its own illustrated clichés?
good-writing-001854.zh: 还记得六十年前《Mad》杂志曾经拥有自己的插图式经典形象吗？

good-writing-001855.en: “Nursing a pet peeve” showed a middle-aged man in an easy chair with a strange creature in his lap sucking on a bottle.
good-writing-001855.zh: 《照顾一只让人生气的小动物》这一画面中，一个中年男子坐在椅子上，膝上抱着一只奇怪的生物，同时正在吮吸着一个瓶子。

good-writing-001856.en: My own absolute pet peeve in literature is when crime novelists kill off the parents of the lead character in a car wreck.
good-writing-001856.zh: 在文学作品中，我最无法忍受的一点是，犯罪小说家们总是让主角在车祸中丧生的父母角色也死在车祸中。

good-writing-001857.en: At least once a month, I make my husband stop whatever he is doing to listen to me read aloud: “Jill [or James or Philip or Grace] lost her [or his or their] parents in a car accident when she [or he or they] was [were] fifteen.”
good-writing-001857.zh: 至少每个月一次，我会让丈夫停止手头的工作，让我来朗读这段文字：“吉尔[或詹姆斯或菲利普或格蕾丝]在十五岁时，因车祸失去了父母。”

good-writing-001858.en: This often comes up in dialogue when people have just met and are getting to know each other:
good-writing-001858.zh: 这种对话内容经常出现在人们初次见面、相互了解的阶段。

good-writing-001860.en: “They died in a car crash when I was little.”
good-writing-001860.zh: “我小时候，他们在一场车祸中去世了。”

good-writing-001862.en: “I was raised by my grandparents. They were wonderful and did the best they could...”
good-writing-001862.zh: 我是由祖父母抚养长大的。他们非常善良，尽了自己最大的努力来照顾我……

good-writing-001863.en: “Were? Have they passed, too? Oh, no! Don’t tell me...”
good-writing-001863.zh: “我们呢？他们也通过了吗？哦，不！请不要告诉我……”

good-writing-001864.en: “Yes, strange as it sounds, they too were killed in a car crash.”
good-writing-001864.zh: “是的，尽管听起来很奇怪，他们也是在一场车祸中丧生的。”

good-writing-001865.en: “Jeez, so incredibly sad. Do you have siblings?”
good-writing-001865.zh: “天啊，真是令人难以置信的悲伤。你有兄弟姐妹吗？”

good-writing-001866.en: “Don’t ask. I’ll fill you in on the way to the restaurant. Let me drive.”
good-writing-001866.zh: “不要问了。我会在去餐厅的路上告诉你路线。让我来开车吧。”

good-writing-001868.en: Dead, absent parents are the novelist’s way of saying, “Reader, fill in the blanks. I don’t have the time or interest to introduce you to the parents. I already have enough characters on my hands.”
good-writing-001868.zh: 逝去的、不在世的父母，是这位小说家表达的方式：“读者啊，请自行填补这些空白吧。我既没有时间，也没有兴趣去介绍那些父母们的信息。我手头已经有足够多的角色了。”

good-writing-001869.zh: 法则32：让句子承载多重意义

good-writing-001870.en: Sentences convey more than information; their other purposes must be tended.
good-writing-001870.zh: 句子传递的不只是信息；你也必须照顾到它的其他作用。

good-writing-001871.en: If you’re writing strictly for meaning, the paragraph can be your basic unit.
good-writing-001871.zh: 如果你只是从意义的角度来写作，那么段落就可以作为你的基本写作单位。

good-writing-001872.en: But if your interest is good writing, then the unit is the sentence.
good-writing-001872.zh: 但如果你对写作感兴趣的话，那么写作的基本单位就是句子。

good-writing-001873.en: No sentence can be bypassed as simply transitional.
good-writing-001873.zh: 没有任何句子可以仅仅因为过渡性的原因而被忽略。

good-writing-001874.en: Each sentence must serve multiple purposes, including two or more of meaning, plotting, character, diction, rhythm, harmony, color, and seamlessness.
good-writing-001874.zh: 每个句子都必须具备多种功能，包括意义、情节、人物塑造、语言运用、节奏、韵律、和谐性以及流畅性等方面的特点。

good-writing-001875.en: For Annie and me as writers, our eyes are on constructing a sentence that does more than convey a simple meaning.
good-writing-001875.zh: 对于我和安妮这样的作家来说，我们的目标就是创造出那些不仅仅能传达简单意义的句子。

good-writing-001877.en: Read a little Chaucer and you’ll get what I mean.
good-writing-001877.zh: 读一点乔叟的作品，你就会明白我的意思了。

good-writing-001878.en: By writing in meter, Chaucer has taken care of rhythm; his words have to fit into the scheme and also have to sound right, or seamless, without what’s known as a false note.
good-writing-001878.zh: 通过采用格律诗的形式，乔叟成功地实现了诗歌的节奏感；他的文字必须遵循一定的韵律结构，并且发音要清晰流畅，避免出现所谓的“错误音位”。

good-writing-001879.en: While bouncing to the beat, he draws highly distinctive portraits of lovely, flawed people who almost, but not quite, exaggerate our everyday weaknesses.
good-writing-001879.zh: 在节奏的推动下，他创作出了一系列非常独特的肖像画，这些画中的人物虽然有些缺点，但却真实地展现了他们的真实面貌。这些肖像画几乎完美地再现了我们的日常弱点，不过也有些夸张了。

good-writing-001880.en: We’re meeting them in rooms and on trails that are carefully described in few words, adding color.
good-writing-001880.zh: 我们在那些被简洁描述过的房间里、在那些被精心规划的步道上与他们相遇，为这些场景增添色彩。

good-writing-001881.en: And as a storyteller who plots well, Chaucer can’t be beat.
good-writing-001881.zh: 而作为一个善于构思故事的人，乔叟的才华真是无与伦比。

good-writing-001882.en: Seldom are we far from meaning, plotting, character, diction, rhythm, harmony, color, and seamlessness.
good-writing-001882.zh: 我们很少会忽略对意义、情节、人物塑造、语言运用、节奏、和谐性、色彩以及整体流畅性的处理。

good-writing-001883.en: She has risen, and dressed at first light,
good-writing-001883.zh: 她已经起床了，在黎明时分便穿好衣服准备出发。

good-writing-001884.en: For May will have no slothfulness a-night,
good-writing-001884.zh: 五月的夜晚将不会显得慵懒。

good-writing-001885.en: The season pricks at every gentle heart,
good-writing-001885.zh: 这个季节总是会刺痛每一个温柔的心。

good-writing-001886.en: And makes it from its sleep begin to start,
good-writing-001886.zh: 然后，它从沉睡的状态中醒来，开始活动起来。

good-writing-001887.zh: 并说道：“起来吧，履行你们的宗教义务吧！”

good-writing-001888.en: And this made Emily rouse her remembrance
good-writing-001888.zh: 这让艾米丽想起了往事。

good-writing-001889.en: Of the honour due to May, and so to rise.
good-writing-001889.zh: 对于五月所应得的荣誉，便如此升起。

good-writing-001890.en: She was clothed fresh to watching eyes;
good-writing-001890.zh: 她穿着整洁，看起来非常干净；

good-writing-001891.en: Her yellow hair was braided in a tress
good-writing-001891.zh: 她的黄色头发被编成了辫子。

good-writing-001892.en: Behind her back, a yard long, I guess.
good-writing-001892.zh: 在她的背后，大概有那么一码远吧。

good-writing-001893.en: And in the garden, as the sun up-rose,
good-writing-001893.zh: 而在花园里，当太阳升起时，

good-writing-001894.en: She walked up and down, and as she chose
good-writing-001894.zh: 她走来走去，然后做出了选择。

good-writing-001895.en: Gathered flowers, mingled, white and red,
good-writing-001895.zh: 收集来的花朵，相互交融，白色与红色交织在一起

good-writing-001896.en: To make a woven garland for her head,
good-writing-001896.zh: 为她制作一个头饰的编织花环，

good-writing-001897.en: And sang like an angel, as she went along.
good-writing-001897.zh: 她一边走，一边用天使般的声音歌唱着。

good-writing-001898.en: This sentence-first approach is the primary distinction between ordinary writing and literary writing.
good-writing-001898.zh: 这种先入为主的观念，正是普通写作与文学写作之间的主要区别所在。

good-writing-001899.en: Ordinary writing is explanatory or plot-driven or character-driven or style-driven, and its sentences hang on consistency of the book’s singular purpose.
good-writing-001899.zh: 普通写作可以是解释性的、以情节为驱动的、以人物为驱动的，或者以风格为驱动的。这些句子的结构都遵循了书籍整体主旨的一致性。

good-writing-001900.en: You’re not supposed to reread a sentence in a page-turner.
good-writing-001900.zh: 在那些引人入胜的书籍中，不应该重读某个句子。

good-writing-001901.en: Literary works—fiction or nonfiction—deserve time to be pondered over.
good-writing-001901.zh: 文学作品——无论是小说还是非小说类作品——都值得花时间去品味和思考。

good-writing-001902.en: What’s going on in the sentence?
good-writing-001902.zh: 这个句子中到底在讲什么？

good-writing-001903.en: Is it as simple as it seemed on my first reading?
good-writing-001903.zh: 就像我第一次阅读时想象的那样简单吗？

good-writing-001904.en: If the feeling is “How did the author do that?” or “How did the author think that way?” then you’re reading a layered sentence.
good-writing-001904.zh: 如果你的感受是“作者是怎么做到这一点的？”或者“作者是这么思考的？”那么说明你正在阅读一个具有多重层次的句子。

good-writing-001905.en: Sure, a good metaphor is a dramatic element.
good-writing-001905.zh: 当然，一个恰当的隐喻确实是一种戏剧性的表现手法。

good-writing-001906.en: But it needs to be encased in a believable character’s diction and serve a purpose of pushing along not just any old meaning, but one that is important to the plot.
good-writing-001906.zh: 但是，这种表达需要用一种可信的、符合角色特色的语言来呈现，并且必须能够传达出对剧情至关重要的信息。

good-writing-001907.en: As in an earlier rule, bringing in new sensory information can often fatten up a sentence in a good way, connecting the sentence’s usefulness for plot or character to a satisfying recognition by the reader of the novel’s other charms—for instance, its seamlessness and color.
good-writing-001907.zh: 就像之前的规则所提到的那样，引入新的感官信息通常能够提升句子的可读性。通过将句子对情节或角色的重要性与读者对小说其他魅力的感知结合起来，比如小说的流畅性和色彩感，就能达到更好的效果。

good-writing-001908.en: Layering your sentences means going back and looking at each one, asking, “Could it be more rhythmic, more psychologically astute, more sensory, more abrupt, more engaged in the plot, more characteristic of the player, more melodic? Is it doing two or more of those? Can I add one more?”
good-writing-001908.zh: 分层处理句子意味着需要仔细审视每一个部分，思考：“是否可以让这些部分更具节奏感、更具心理深度、更具感官冲击力？是否可以让这些部分更加突兀，更能吸引玩家的注意力？或者，是否可以让这些部分更具旋律性？如果可以的话，我还能添加更多这样的元素吗？”

good-writing-001909.en: Of course the distinction between ordinary and literary writing is artificial.
good-writing-001909.zh: 当然，普通写作与文学性写作之间的区别其实是一种人为的区分。

good-writing-001910.en: The tools of the high artist are available to the Sunday painter.
good-writing-001910.zh: 这位高艺师的工具现在也可以被那些业余画家所使用。

good-writing-001911.en: No matter what I’m writing—a book or a business plan—my sentences can be better layered.
good-writing-001911.zh: 无论我写的是什么——无论是书籍还是商业计划书——我的句子都可以更加层次分明、结构更清晰。

good-writing-001913.en: I make sentences for a living.
good-writing-001913.zh: 我通过创作句子来谋生。

good-writing-001914.en: After I create one decent sentence, I create another.
good-writing-001914.zh: 在我造出一句通顺的句子之后，我会继续造出更多类似的句子。

good-writing-001915.en: Sentences are the beads with which I assemble the necklace of each paragraph and passage.
good-writing-001915.zh: 句子就像是我用来编织每一段和每一篇文章的“项链”的珠子。

good-writing-001916.en: For example, I wrote a sentence in my late twenties with only six words, but what a story they foretold: “Against all odds, the cat lived.”
good-writing-001916.zh: 例如，在二十五六岁的年纪时，我写了一个只有六个单词的句子，但那个句子所蕴含的故事真是令人惊叹：“尽管面临种种困难，那只猫还是活了下来。”

good-writing-001917.en: Anyone in their right mind will think, “Oh, thank God,” except for cat-hating spouses at their wits’ end with the stench of the lion’s den that seeps from the cat box.
good-writing-001917.zh: 任何头脑清醒的人都会想：“哦，谢天谢地。”不过，那些对猫深恶痛绝的配偶们，在无法忍受猫屎散发出的恶臭时，才会这样想。

good-writing-001918.en: It’s apparently a miracle, in six words.
good-writing-001918.zh: 用六个字来形容的话，这显然是个奇迹。

good-writing-001920.en: The star of the sentence, said cat, was a tabby who shared my houseboat on San Francisco Bay, and at that point, toward the end of my drinking career, existed in part as my main source of happiness.
good-writing-001920.zh: 这句话的“主角”是一只斑猫，它和我住在旧金山湾的那艘小船上。在我的饮酒生涯即将结束的时候，它在一定程度上成了我主要的快乐来源。

good-writing-001921.en: One day I came home from a walk to find her hunched over in a corner, her back to me, and upon closer inspection, discovered a gaping hole in her chest.
good-writing-001921.zh: 有一天，我散步回家后，发现她蜷缩在角落里，背部朝向我。仔细查看后，我发现她的胸部有一个巨大的伤口。

good-writing-001922.en: She was frozen, unblinking, barely holding on.
good-writing-001922.zh: 她僵硬地站着，眼睛无法眨动，勉强维持着身体的平衡。

good-writing-001923.en: I raced her to a pet emergency room, where the vet and I noticed after he soaked up the blood that we could see her lungs.
good-writing-001923.zh: 我迅速将她送往宠物急诊室。在那里，兽医和我注意到，由于她身上沾满了血液，我们能够看到她的肺部情况。

good-writing-001924.en: (For the record, cat lungs are triangular, about the size of scones.)
good-writing-001924.zh: 需要注意的是，猫的肺是三角形的，大小大约与松饼相当。

good-writing-001925.en: The vet did not think either had been punctured by whatever had pierced her chest, which was good news.
good-writing-001925.zh: 兽医认为，无论是哪种物体刺穿她的胸部，都没有造成任何严重的损伤，这真是个好消息。

good-writing-001928.en: It was suggested at this point that I go wait at home, as all the blood had drained from my face, in solidarity with the cat.
good-writing-001928.zh: 当时有人建议我待在家里等待，因为我的脸上已经没有血迹了，这是为了与那只猫保持同等的待遇。

good-writing-001929.en: Against all odds, the cat lived.
good-writing-001929.zh: 尽管面临种种困难，那只猫还是活了下来。

good-writing-001930.en: The vet surmised that she had leapt onto one of the pilings next to my houseboat, and that there must have been a sharp stick poking out of it.
good-writing-001930.zh: 兽医推测，她应该是跳到了我船屋旁边的那些桩子上，而且那个桩子上一定插着一根尖锐的棍子。

good-writing-001931.en: Somehow—and this was proof for me that there is a God in heaven—the stick had gone right between her lungs, missing both of them.
good-writing-001931.zh: 不知怎么的——这对我来说证明了天界确实存在上帝——那根棍子正好打在了她的肺部中间，打断了她的两条肺。

good-writing-001932.en: Also against all odds, I brought her home the next day.
good-writing-001932.zh: 即便面临种种困难，我还是在第二天把她带回了家。

good-writing-001933.en: She was stitched and bandaged and pretty nonchalant about the whole thing—like, whatev.
good-writing-001933.zh: 她接受了缝合和包扎处理，对这一切表现得相当淡然，好像根本不在乎一样。

good-writing-001934.en: I would have milked this injury for months.
good-writing-001934.zh: 我本可以利用这次受伤的机会获得数月的好处。

good-writing-001935.en: She lived another ten years, long enough to help get me sober.
good-writing-001935.zh: 她又活了十年，这十年时间足够让我戒除酗酒的习惯。

good-writing-001936.en: And I told you that story by creating one decent sentence after another, putting a period at the end of each one, pausing, looking it over to see if I could make it better, clearer, more visual, thereby advancing the plot and raising the stakes.
good-writing-001936.zh: 我通过不断地创作一个又一个简洁的句子来讲述这个故事。在每个句子的末尾加上句号，然后暂停一下，仔细思考如何使句子更加清晰、生动，从而推动故事的进展并增加故事的紧张感。

good-writing-001937.zh: 法则33：勇于写那些难写的事

good-writing-001938.en: Don’t shy away from the big mysteries of life.
good-writing-001938.zh: 不要回避人生那些重大的谜题。

good-writing-001939.zh: 没有什么是无法表达的。

good-writing-001940.en: Make the effort: Write the material whose articulation first stumps you, the stuff that makes people tick until the last tock.
good-writing-001940.zh: 付出努力吧：写出那些能够首先吸引你注意力的材料，那些能够让人们一直关注到最后一刻的材料。

good-writing-001941.en: Part of “show, then tell” is to stretch your imagination, whether it’s heading into the physical world or abstract judgments of that world or painful emotions.
good-writing-001941.zh: “先展示，再讲述”这一理念的一部分，就是激发你的想象力，无论是面对现实世界的种种现象，还是对现实世界的抽象判断，甚至是那些令人痛苦的情绪，都需要用想象力来呈现。

good-writing-001942.en: If you stop at “She was beautiful in a vague way,” you are giving up.
good-writing-001942.zh: 如果你只停留在“她看起来很美丽”这种描述上，那你就放弃得太早了。

good-writing-001943.en: It sounds kind of literary and meaningful, but lands to the reader as a cheat.
good-writing-001943.zh: 这听起来似乎有些文学性且富有意义，但实际上对读者来说只是一种欺骗。

good-writing-001944.en: If you stop at “He believed in God but wasn’t sure which one,” you’re not allowing yourself to riff on the divine.
good-writing-001944.zh: 如果你只停留在“他相信上帝，但不确定具体是哪位上帝”这一点的描述上，那么你就没有充分表达出对神圣事物的崇敬之情。

good-writing-001945.en: If you stop at “The car was one of those cheap Indian things,” you haven’t completed your research on domestic car production in India.
good-writing-001945.zh: 如果你只停留在“那辆车是印度那种便宜的国产车型”这一层次，那你的关于印度国内汽车生产的研究就不够深入。

good-writing-001946.en: An odd corollary is to force a little more simplicity on yourself.
good-writing-001946.zh: 一个有趣的启示是：给自己设定更简单的目标吧。

good-writing-001947.en: Yes, expressing the obvious is deadly.
good-writing-001947.zh: 是的，表达显而易见的事情其实是一种风险行为。

good-writing-001948.en: But so is ignoring the fundamentals that drive human behavior and emotion.
good-writing-001948.zh: 但忽视那些驱动人类行为和情感的基本因素，同样也是不对的。

good-writing-001949.en: Here’s the twentieth-century philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein: “The aspects of things that are most important for us are hidden because of their simplicity and familiarity.”
good-writing-001949.zh: 这是20世纪的哲学家路德维希·维特根斯坦的观点：“对我们来说最重要的事物特征，往往因为它们的简单性和普遍性而隐藏起来。”

good-writing-001950.en: Your characters have simple beliefs: Nothing is as important as protecting my kids.
good-writing-001950.zh: 你的角色们有着简单的信念：没有什么比保护自己的孩子更重要了。

good-writing-001952.zh: 玫瑰的气味就像奶奶的味道。

good-writing-001953.en: A wide panorama always reminds me of possibility.
good-writing-001953.zh: 广阔的全景总是让我联想到无限的可能性。

good-writing-001954.en: Don’t be afraid to punctuate a scene by expressing the obvious.
good-writing-001954.zh: 不要害怕在某个场景中通过表达显而易见的内容来突出重点。

good-writing-001955.en: Finding a way to evoke the ineffable is related to Donald Murray’s idea that “syntactic failure is a sign you’re trying to say something important.”
good-writing-001955.zh: 寻找一种方式来表达那些难以言表的东西，这与唐纳德·穆雷的观点有关：他认为“句法上的失败意味着你正在尝试表达一些重要的内容”。

good-writing-001956.en: In other words, if it’s hard to write, it’s probably worth writing.
good-writing-001956.zh: 换句话说，如果写作很困难的话，那么写下来或许还是值得的。

good-writing-001957.en: Isn’t the whole point of writing to figure out something you don’t already know?
good-writing-001957.zh: 写作的初衷不就是为了了解那些你并不知晓的事情吗？

good-writing-001958.en: Most fiction and biography writers discover aspects of their characters along the way.
good-writing-001958.zh: 大多数小说和传记作家在创作过程中都会发现他们笔下人物的某些特质。

good-writing-001959.en: In general nonfiction, the author seeks motivations and causes of events.
good-writing-001959.zh: 在一般性的非小说作品中，作者会试图揭示事件的动机和原因。

good-writing-001960.en: The act of writing refines the author’s notions and often opens new possibilities.
good-writing-001960.zh: 写作的过程能够锤炼作者的思想，并常常开辟新的可能性。

good-writing-001961.en: I once heard the novelist Siri Hustvedt complain that her protagonists keep getting killed off at the end of the story.
good-writing-001961.zh: 我曾经听到小说家Siri Hustvedt抱怨说，她的故事中的主角总是在故事结束时被杀死。

good-writing-001962.en: She wants to protect her characters from themselves but can’t.
good-writing-001962.zh: 她想要保护自己的角色不受自身的影响，但实际上做不到这一点。

good-writing-001963.en: In many traditions, God is expected to be so ineffable that it’s hubris, even sin, to try to explain the concept.
good-writing-001963.zh: 在许多传统中，人们认为上帝是如此难以捉摸，以至于试图解释上帝的概念本身就是一种傲慢，甚至是一种罪恶的行为。

good-writing-001964.en: But those same traditions fill libraries with stacks of theology—the study of God.
good-writing-001964.zh: 但这些传统却让图书馆里堆满了关于神学的书籍——即对上帝的研究。

good-writing-001965.en: Don’t pretend that anything is off-limits to your consideration and articulation.
good-writing-001965.zh: 不要假装有任何事情是你无法思考和表达的。

good-writing-001966.en: You go where your characters go, inside and out, in their metaphysical meanderings and hikes through the woods.
good-writing-001966.zh: 你跟随你的角色们去往他们所去的地方——无论是室内还是室外，在那些形而上的旅程中，以及穿过森林的途中。

good-writing-001967.en: Often nonfiction writers believe that they must wrap things up neatly and maintain an objective stance that might wobble if contaminated by subjectivity or the Great Irrational.
good-writing-001967.zh: 通常，非虚构作品的作者认为，他们必须把事情处理得井井有条，并保持客观立场，以免被主观性或那些难以预测的因素所干扰。

good-writing-001968.en: Wittgenstein said, “The limits of language are the limits of my world.”
good-writing-001968.zh: 维特根斯坦说：“语言的界限，就是我的世界的界限。”

good-writing-001969.en: Well...my words include “mystery” and “supernatural” and my syntax includes questions and paradoxical statements.
good-writing-001969.zh: 嗯……我的文字中包含了“神秘”和“超自然”这样的概念，而我的语法结构则充满了疑问句和具有矛盾性的陈述句。

good-writing-001970.en: When I worked in daily newspapers, I could only ask a question that could be answered in the next paragraph.
good-writing-001970.zh: 在我从事报纸工作的时候，我只能提出那些可以在下一段中得到回答的问题。

good-writing-001971.en: Magazine, blog, and book writers often restrain themselves the same way, but that’s a shame.
good-writing-001971.zh: 杂志、博客和书籍的撰稿人通常也会如此约束自己，但这种情况确实很遗憾。

good-writing-001972.en: They have room and therefore license to raise the stakes, even if it makes some of their readers uncomfortable.
good-writing-001972.zh: 他们有空间，因此有权利提高赌注，即使这会让一些读者感到不适。

good-writing-001973.en: Here is novelist José Saramago on what’s important about the hard stuff: “Inside us there is something that has no name, that something is what we are.”
good-writing-001973.zh: 小说家何塞·萨拉马戈对生活中重要事物的看法如下：“在我们内心深处，存在着某种无法命名的东西，而那东西正是我们自身的本质。”

good-writing-001974.en: While Saramago is claiming its unnameability, he is also tipping off his interest in the subject as an author.
good-writing-001974.zh: 虽然萨拉马戈强调自己无法为作品命名，但他同时也表明了自己对这个问题的浓厚兴趣，这反映出他作为一位作家的创作倾向。

good-writing-001975.en: What does he care to write about?

good-writing-001977.en: And here’s how you do just that, if you’re Cormac McCarthy: “They were watching, out there past men’s knowing, where stars are drowning and whales ferry their vast souls through the black and seamless sea.”
good-writing-001977.zh: 而要做到这一点，如果你是科马克·麦卡锡的风格，那么可以这样表达：“他们在一旁观察着，那些男人之外的世界，那里星星密布，鲸鱼则把它们庞大的身躯载渡在漆黑而无缝的海洋中。”

good-writing-001979.en: Please please please write the hard stuff—write about life, and death, and loss, and hope, and how on earth you survived that childhood or injury or marriage.
good-writing-001979.zh: 请务必写下那些沉重而真实的故事吧——写下关于生活、死亡、失去、希望的故事，还有你是如何在那个童年、受伤或婚姻的艰难时期中挺过来的。

good-writing-001980.en: Find a way to write about people’s underlying fears, maybe psychological but also mystical—fear of death, of legacy, of emptiness and lovableness.
good-writing-001980.zh: 找到一种方式来描写人们内心深处的恐惧，无论是心理层面的恐惧，还是与神秘相关的恐惧——对死亡的恐惧、对遗产的恐惧、对空虚与无爱的恐惧。

good-writing-001981.en: Write about who you think you are down deep, past the persona and curation and the stories you believe about yourself, because you are probably similar to me, and I love it when someone holds up a mirror.
good-writing-001981.zh: 写下你内心深处真正的自我，超越那些表面上的形象和包装，也超越那些你自认为关于自己的各种故事。因为你很可能与我相似，而我喜欢有人能成为我的镜子，让我看到真实的自己。

good-writing-001983.en: We’re a species that craves stories about itself.
good-writing-001983.zh: 我们是一个喜欢讲述自己故事的物种。

good-writing-001984.en: Tell us our story, through your lens, whether in fiction or nonfiction.
good-writing-001984.zh: 请通过你的视角，无论是虚构作品还是非虚构作品，告诉我们你的故事。

good-writing-001985.en: It is really all you have to offer us.
good-writing-001985.zh: 这真的就是你们能给我们的一切了。

good-writing-001986.en: We are all going to die.

good-writing-001988.en: How do we live fully, boldly in the face of that?
good-writing-001988.zh: 我们如何能够在面对这些挑战时，依然能够充满勇气地、充分地生活下去呢？

good-writing-001989.en: This is hard to think and write about, but we want you to.
good-writing-001989.zh: 这是很难去思考和书写的，但我们希望你能做到这一点。

good-writing-001990.en: It is essential that you try.
good-writing-001990.zh: 你必须尝试一下，这是非常重要的。

good-writing-001991.en: We’re here on the incarnational side of things to discover the truth of who we are.
good-writing-001991.zh: 我们在这里，是为了探索关于我们自身本质的真相。

good-writing-001992.zh: 我们是动物、人类，也是神圣的存在。

good-writing-001993.en: That is hard stuff to capture but that is what I most long to read: truth.
good-writing-001993.zh: 那是一种难以捕捉的题材，但正是这种题材是我最渴望去阅读的内容：真相。

good-writing-001996.en: This will not go well, but don’t give up.
good-writing-001996.zh: 这不会顺利进行，但请不要放弃。

good-writing-001997.en: Write an incredibly shitty first draft that will be way too long and overwrought and sophomoric.
good-writing-001997.zh: 写出一份极其糟糕的初稿，内容冗长、过于夸张，而且充满幼稚的感伤。

good-writing-001998.en: Then take out all the boring parts and see what is left.
good-writing-001998.zh: 然后去掉所有那些无聊的部分，看看还剩下什么。

good-writing-001999.en: Then try again and see if you can make it better.
good-writing-001999.zh: 然后再试一次，看看是否能够改进得更好。

good-writing-002001.en: Talk to people about what you are working on and see if their input throws some lights on for you, or even provides phrases that will help you capture what you are after in your next draft.
good-writing-002001.zh: 与人们讨论你正在从事的工作，看看他们的意见能否为你提供启示，或者能否提供一些表达方式来帮助你捕捉下一份草案中需要表达的内容。

good-writing-002002.en: (P.S. I’ve always said that if you want to be a writer, you should get the smartest, funniest friends, but it is best if they are not writers, too, because then they won’t let you steal all their great lines about these profound matters.)
good-writing-002002.zh: （附言：我一直认为，如果你想成为作家，就应该结交一些最聪明、最有趣的朋友。不过，最好这些朋友本身也不是作家，因为那样他们就不会让你偷走他们那些关于这些深刻主题的伟大台词了。）

good-writing-002004.en: A rule may be of universal use, but need not be universally used.
good-writing-002004.zh: 一条规则也许普遍有用，却不必在所有地方都使用。

good-writing-002005.en: As I’ve said, these are tips, not rules, until the time that you decide to adopt them.
good-writing-002005.zh: 正如我所说，这些只是建议而已，而不是必须遵守的规则。直到你决定采纳它们之前，都只能把它们当作建议来对待。

good-writing-002006.en: But even then, they’re not black-and-white like grammar.
good-writing-002006.zh: 但即便如此，它们也不像语法那样是绝对的对与错。

good-writing-002007.en: And at some point, you probably will need to break a rule—leave in a “very,” keep a weak verb, stick with a Latinate noun.
good-writing-002007.zh: 在某个时刻，你可能需要打破一些规则——比如使用“very”来修饰形容词，使用弱动词，或者使用拉丁语来源的名词。

good-writing-002008.en: My advice is to consciously practice each rule over and over at first.
good-writing-002008.zh: 我的建议是，在最初阶段，应该有意识地反复练习每条规则。

good-writing-002009.en: Know the rule backward and forward—trust its protective coating—before you test it and then break it.
good-writing-002009.zh: 在测试并损坏它之前，要彻底了解这一规则，并充分信任其保护性能。

good-writing-002010.en: Relearn the rule after breaking it.
good-writing-002010.zh: 在打破这个规则之后，重新学习这个规则。

good-writing-002011.en: For the sake of argument, let’s distinguish four ways we use words: to convey information, to narrate our own lives back to ourselves, to come to agreement, and to entertain.
good-writing-002011.zh: 为了便于讨论，让我们区分一下我们使用词语的四种方式：传递信息、向自己叙述自己的生活经历、达成共识，以及娱乐目的。

good-writing-002012.en: Most communication is quite practical—giving directions, offering or receiving help or instructions, checking in, assessing health, those sorts of things.
good-writing-002012.zh: 大多数沟通都是非常实用的——比如给出指示、提供帮助或解释，进行状态检查，评估健康状况等等。

good-writing-002013.en: It’s in that realm that the rules of grammar presumably developed.
good-writing-002013.zh: 语法规则可能就是在这样的领域中逐渐发展出来的。

good-writing-002014.en: The more practical the communication, the more narrow, repeatable, colorless, and recognizable it is.
good-writing-002014.zh: 沟通越实用，它就越具有针对性、可重复性、无色性以及易识别性。

good-writing-002015.en: The rules of grammar you learned in class are the tightest set of rules of all.
