good-writing-002015.zh: 你在课堂上学习的语法规则，是所有规则中最为严谨的一套。

good-writing-002016.en: They are aimed at practical knowledge expressed through expository writing.
good-writing-002016.zh: 这些目标是通过说明性写作来呈现实用知识。

good-writing-002017.en: The rules help make instructions clear and airtight.
good-writing-002017.zh: 这些规则有助于使说明更加明确且不容置疑。

good-writing-002018.en: Good grammar narrows possibilities into a single, shareable meaning.
good-writing-002018.zh: 良好的语法能够将复杂的含义简化为一个易于理解、可供分享的单一含义。

good-writing-002019.en: But most of the words going through my head aren’t communicated to anyone else.
good-writing-002019.zh: 但是，我脑海中闪过的那些想法，并没有被传达给其他人。

good-writing-002020.en: They aren’t purely instructive; they’re often simply descriptive.
good-writing-002020.zh: 这些内容并不完全是教育性的；它们往往只是对事物的描述而已。

good-writing-002021.en: I’m reminding myself of ongoing interests, worries, observations, and conclusions.
good-writing-002021.zh: 我在提醒自己关注那些持续存在的兴趣、担忧、观察和结论。

good-writing-002022.en: Most of my thoughts are fragments that scarcely require grammar.
good-writing-002022.zh: 我的大部分想法都是些简短的片段，几乎不需要使用语法来表达。

good-writing-002023.en: I narrate my life with abandon.
good-writing-002023.zh: 我毫无保留地讲述着我的生活。

good-writing-002024.en: Notice that one set of rules, highly constrained, establishes boundaries for writing that engages in exposition and the classic thesis-support paradigm, while a different set of rules, less constrained, allows in the fickle, free-verse meanderings of our internal narrative.
good-writing-002024.zh: 需要注意的是，有一套规则非常严格，它规定了写作中需要遵循的界限，包括那些需要详细阐述的段落以及传统的论点支撑结构。而另一套规则则相对宽松，它允许我们在写作中自由地运用各种表达方式，随心所欲地表达我们的内心想法。

good-writing-002025.en: Somewhere in between these two models floats creative nonfiction like memoir, or essays, or political speeches, or documentaries, or lyrics, which may have elements of practical knowledge and even wisdom, but also have distinct first-personalness that doesn’t mind a little ambiguity or subjectivity.
good-writing-002025.zh: 在这两个模型之间的某个范围内，存在着一种创意性的非虚构作品——比如回忆录、散文、政治演讲、纪录片或歌词。这类作品可能包含一些实用性的知识或智慧元素，但同时又具有鲜明的个人色彩，不介意一些模糊性或主观性。

good-writing-002026.en: Whether writing in the first or third person, the first person is always implied in fiction.
good-writing-002026.zh: 无论是在第一人称还是第三人称的书写方式下，小说中总是隐含着第一人称的视角。

good-writing-002027.en: The author is not operating a mechanical conveyor of information.
good-writing-002027.zh: 作者并没有使用任何机械装置来传递信息。

good-writing-002028.en: The author is replicating human consciousness, because we humans constantly think about things and sum up as we’re experiencing things.
good-writing-002028.zh: 作者是在复制人类意识的过程，因为我们人类总是在思考各种事物，并在体验这些事物的过程中对它们进行总结。

good-writing-002029.en: Part of the realism of a fictional work is the reader’s belief that the author is replicating the feeling of consciousness accurately.
good-writing-002029.zh: 一部虚构作品的真实感，部分在于读者对作者能够准确再现意识状态的信任。

good-writing-002030.en: And consciousness does not speak to us in tidy, complete sentences.
good-writing-002030.zh: 而意识并不会用整齐、完整的句子来与我们交流。

good-writing-002031.en: Consciousness is more than an instruction manual; it also loves the scalloped, spiky edges of an aloe plant.
good-writing-002031.zh: 意识不仅仅是一份操作指南；它还会喜欢芦荟植物那些尖锐、有棱角的边缘。

good-writing-002032.en: And it abets our desire for companionship, agreement, intimacy.
good-writing-002032.zh: 这激发了我们对于伴侣关系、共识以及亲密关系的渴望。

good-writing-002033.en: So fragments are allowed in fiction.
good-writing-002033.zh: 因此，在小说中允许使用碎片化的表达方式。

good-writing-002036.en: This book is nonfiction, isn’t it?
good-writing-002036.zh: 这本书属于非虚构类作品，对吧？

good-writing-002037.en: How can I rationalize the incomplete “Like this”?
good-writing-002037.zh: 我该如何解释这种“不完整”的“喜欢”行为呢？

good-writing-002039.en: I’m writing in a particularly conversational nonfiction style.
good-writing-002039.zh: 我采用一种非常口语化的非虚构写作风格来撰写这篇文章。

good-writing-002040.en: It replicates a more typical style of fiction.
good-writing-002040.zh: 它采用了一种更为典型的叙事风格。

good-writing-002041.en: I’m not actually breaking a rule.
good-writing-002041.zh: 实际上，我并没有违反任何规则。

good-writing-002042.en: I’m turning on a different rule set, the rules of fiction.
good-writing-002042.zh: 我现在正在启用一套不同的规则，即虚构世界的规则。

good-writing-002044.en: When we break the rules, often we’re simply changing frameworks, maybe recognizing the entertainment value of drama.
good-writing-002044.zh: 当我们打破规则时，往往只是改变了原有的框架而已，或者是在尝试发现戏剧性元素所带来的娱乐价值。

good-writing-002045.en: My first professional writing was journalism.
good-writing-002045.zh: 我的第一份职业写作工作是新闻工作。

good-writing-002046.en: As a newspaperman, I learned how to write without reference to myself, in a straightforward way that mainly linked a lot of subject-verb-object sentences together.
good-writing-002046.zh: 作为一名记者，我学会了如何在不涉及个人背景的情况下进行写作，采用一种直接明了的文体，将许多主语-谓语-宾语的句子结构有机地结合在一起。

good-writing-002047.en: A few months after leaving newspapers for a corporate career, I found myself writing a speech for the president of my company.
good-writing-002047.zh: 在离开报社后，开始从事企业管理工作后不久，我不得不为公司的总裁撰写一份演讲稿。

good-writing-002053.en: The rules were out the door!

good-writing-002054.en: But in the words of every frowning eighth-grade teacher, with freedom came responsibilities.
good-writing-002054.zh: 但正如每个皱着眉头的八年级老师都会说的那样，自由伴随着责任。

good-writing-002055.en: How to carry emotion without manipulating the truth?
good-writing-002055.zh: 如何在不歪曲事实的情况下表达情感呢？

good-writing-002056.en: How to persuade rather than explain?
good-writing-002056.zh: 如何以说服而非解释的方式来进行沟通呢？

good-writing-002057.en: In fact, I had to learn a new set of rules, and they were more subtle and more difficult.
good-writing-002057.zh: 实际上，我不得不学习一套新的规则，而这些规则更为复杂且难以掌握。

good-writing-002058.en: Notice who your audience is and what the purpose of your writing is, and learn the rules that accompany those conditions.
good-writing-002058.zh: 注意你的读者是谁，以及你写作的目的是什么，并了解与这些条件相关的规则。

good-writing-002059.en: You may never need to break a rule again.
good-writing-002059.zh: 也许你以后再也不会需要违反任何规则了。

good-writing-002061.en: The first rule of Fight Club, I mean Writing Club, is you don’t talk to yourself about the rules of writing.
good-writing-002061.zh: 《写作俱乐部》的第一条规则是：你不可独自讨论写作的规则。

good-writing-002062.en: Just write and write and write.
good-writing-002062.zh: 只要不停地写作下去吧。

good-writing-002063.en: At some point, God willing, an editor and then a hidebound copy editor will step in and want you to stick to their rules, which maybe you will or maybe you won’t.
good-writing-002063.zh: 在某个时刻，如果一切顺利的话，就会有一个编辑，然后是一个固执的校对员出现，他们会要求你遵守他们的规则。也许你会遵守这些规则，也许就不会了。

good-writing-002065.en: Until then, just write the best you can, the way the words come through you.
good-writing-002065.zh: 在此之前，就尽力以最自然、最真实的方式表达你的想法吧。

good-writing-002066.en: You can break any rules that you can get away with.
good-writing-002066.zh: 你可以打破任何你能轻易做到的规则。

good-writing-002067.en: We’ve already discussed the rule against semicolons, and how often I use them (so they must be OK).
good-writing-002067.zh: 我们已经讨论过禁止使用分号的规定，以及我使用分号的频率（因此使用分号应该是没有问题的）。

good-writing-002068.en: We’ve gone over “show, then tell,” and so forth.
good-writing-002068.zh: 我们已经讨论过“先展示，再讲述”等概念了。

good-writing-002069.en: Don’t write in the second person?
good-writing-002069.zh: 不要使用第二人称来写作吧？

good-writing-002070.en: Tell that to Italo Calvino in If on a Winter’s Night a Traveler—or to Lorrie Moore, who frequently uses second person in those wonderful early short stories.
good-writing-002070.zh: 请向伊塔洛·卡尔维诺在《一个冬夜的旅行者》中的作品里，或者向洛莉·摩尔说吧——后者在那些出色的短篇故事中经常使用第二人称的视角。

good-writing-002071.en: Readers find patois and dialect annoying?
good-writing-002071.zh: 读者们觉得地方口音和方言很烦人吗？

good-writing-002073.en: What about the great Far Tortuga by Peter Matthiessen, or Trainspotting by Irvine Welsh, or Their Eyes Were Watching God by Zora Neale Hurston?
good-writing-002073.zh: 那么，彼得·马蒂森的《伟大的法拉托图加》、欧文·韦尔希思的《火车迷》以及佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿的《他们的眼睛在注视上帝》这些作品又如何呢？

good-writing-002074.en: The most important thing in fiction is a likable narrator?
good-writing-002074.zh: 在小说中，最重要的是一个令人喜爱的叙述者吧？

good-writing-002075.en: What about Humbert Humbert in Nabokov’s Lolita, and Merricat Blackwood in Shirley Jackson’s We Have Always Lived in the Castle?
good-writing-002075.zh: 那么，纳博科夫的《洛丽塔》中的洪伯特·洪伯特，以及雪莉·杰克逊的《我们一直生活在城堡里》中的梅里卡特·布莱克伍德，他们又有什么特别之处呢？

good-writing-002076.en: And speaking of Jackson, let’s point out again that she said, “A confused reader is an antagonistic reader,” and this in fact is the one rule I swear by as if written by the Psalmist.
good-writing-002076.zh: 说到杰克逊，我们再强调一下她说过的话：“一个混乱的读者，就是一个充满敌意的读者。”这实际上是我坚信的一条规则，就像诗篇作者所写的那样。

good-writing-002077.en: If I can’t follow what you are up to in your first chapter, that is absolutely as far as I am going to read.
good-writing-002077.zh: 如果我无法理解你在第一章中所描述的内容，那我就不打算继续阅读下去了。

good-writing-002078.en: Maybe I would have stuck it out for another few chapters in my younger days, when I was able to dive into a postmodern Japanese novel with some excitement, or William S. Burroughs, or Gertrude Stein.
good-writing-002078.zh: 也许在年轻的时候，我会继续读下去，直到读完几章之后才会停下来。那时，我还能怀着些许兴奋的心情去阅读后现代风格的日本小说，或者威廉·S·伯罗斯的作品，还有格特鲁德·斯坦的作品。

good-writing-002079.en: Nowadays, the princess does not do Dada.
good-writing-002079.zh: 如今，那位公主已经不再做那些无意义的事情了。

good-writing-002080.en: The princess wants you to tell me a rich, layered, and touching story.
good-writing-002080.zh: 公主希望你能讲述一个丰富、富有层次感且令人感动的故事。

good-writing-002082.en: Your job is to complete the project.
good-writing-002082.zh: 你的任务是把这个写作项目完成。

good-writing-002083.en: The final quality and consequences are not yet your business.
good-writing-002083.zh: 最终质量如何、会产生什么后果，眼下还不是你需要操心的事。

good-writing-002084.en: Fear of failure drives procrastination, writer’s block, and other forms of not-writing.
good-writing-002084.zh: 对失败的恐惧会导致拖延、写作障碍以及其他形式的无法写作的情况。

good-writing-002085.en: A writing job requires a commitment, but that’s not as big a deal as it sounds.
good-writing-002085.zh: 写作工作需要投入时间和精力，但其实并没有听起来那么困难。

good-writing-002086.en: The agreement to write the piece was made at the beginning.
good-writing-002086.zh: 撰写这篇文章的协议在最初阶段就已经达成。

good-writing-002087.en: When I made that choice, I had factored in my time, my talent, my interest, and my ability to concentrate.
good-writing-002087.zh: 当我做出那个选择时，我已经考虑了自己的时间、才能、兴趣以及集中注意力的能力等因素。

good-writing-002088.en: None of those was in question.

good-writing-002089.en: Only after jumping in do I start to doubt my time, my talent, my interest, or my ability to concentrate.
good-writing-002089.zh: 只有一跃加入之后，我才开始怀疑自己的时间、才华、兴趣，以及集中注意力的能力。

good-writing-002090.en: But wait, I never choose a project that’s over my head.
good-writing-002090.zh: 但是等等，我从来不会选择超出自己能力范围的项目。

good-writing-002092.en: Even when it’s chosen for me by a boss, it’s typically within my capacities.
good-writing-002092.zh: 即使是由一位首领为我选择的角色，那也通常还是在我的能力范围之内。

good-writing-002093.en: So if it’s not over my head, then surely I can finish it.
good-writing-002093.zh: 所以，如果这不是我无法克服的困难，那我肯定能够完成它。

good-writing-002094.en: The base level of work called completion is already in the bag.
good-writing-002094.zh: 基本的工作任务已经完成，即所谓的“完成度”已经达到了要求。

good-writing-002095.en: Here’s the only problem: My fearmongering inner critic has chosen to ignore that.
good-writing-002095.zh: 唯一的问题就是：我那爱散布恐慌的内心批评声音选择忽略了这一点。

good-writing-002096.en: The difficulty isn’t my writing; it’s the gremlin in my head.
good-writing-002096.zh: 问题的根源并不在我的写作能力上，而是我头脑中的那些“小麻烦”因素在作祟。

good-writing-002097.en: As my buzzkill wife is known to say about the writer’s life, “It’s going to go badly.”
good-writing-002097.zh: 正如我那位爱挑剔的妻子常说的那样，关于这位作家的生活状况，她会说：“情况肯定会很糟糕。”

good-writing-002099.en: I’m going to stumble into dead ends, difficult passages, unnecessary digressions, crummy sentences, lapses in logic, and every other kind of mind-twister.
good-writing-002099.zh: 我可能会遇到一些死胡同、难以理解的段落、不必要的冗长描述、糟糕的句子结构、逻辑上的混乱，以及所有其他令人困惑的内容。

good-writing-002100.en: But I knew when I committed to the project that it would present obstacles.
good-writing-002100.zh: 但我知道，当我开始这个项目时，会遇到各种障碍。

good-writing-002102.en: So one way to address not-writing is to remember that it was never intended to be smooth; the logjams in the middle were always going to show up to be sorted out.
good-writing-002102.zh: 因此，解决“不写作”问题的一种方法是记住，这种写作方式本来就不应该是流畅的；中间那些“障碍”终究会被解决掉。

good-writing-002103.en: A peskier issue is removing concerns about quality and consequences.
good-writing-002103.zh: 一个有趣的问题是，需要消除关于质量及后果方面的担忧。

good-writing-002104.en: Here’s a thought: My job is to write the book.
good-writing-002104.zh: 有个想法：我的任务就是撰写这本书。

good-writing-002105.en: My editor’s job is to worry about its consistency.
good-writing-002105.zh: 我的编辑工作就是确保内容的连贯性。

good-writing-002106.en: My publisher’s job is to worry about its sales.
good-writing-002106.zh: 我的出版商的主要职责是关注出版物的销售情况。

good-writing-002107.en: I can be interested in its consistency and sales, but they are not my responsibility, at least not yet.
good-writing-002107.zh: 我可能会对它的稳定性和销量感兴趣，但这些并不属于我的责任范围，至少目前还不属于我的责任。

good-writing-002108.en: First, quality: The funny thing about the sophistication of my ideas, language, and presentation is that those are a given before I start.
good-writing-002108.zh: 首先，是质量问题：我的想法、语言以及表达方式的精致性，其实是一种先天具备的特点，这种特点在我开始工作之前就已经存在了。

good-writing-002109.en: I’m so used to the world telling me to improve myself that I don’t notice that as an adult in the third third of life, I’ve already improved about as much as I can.
good-writing-002109.zh: 我已经习惯了这个世界要求我不断自我提升的氛围，以至于我没有意识到，作为人生中第三分之一阶段的成年人，我已经尽可能地提高了自己的水平了。

good-writing-002110.en: At least 80 percent of the project’s quality is already baked in before I start, because I have my acquired knowledge, my helpful and harmful biases, and my limits, none of which is going to change much over the course of completing the project.
good-writing-002110.zh: 在我开始这个项目之前，至少80%的项目质量就已经基本确定了。因为我拥有的是我积累的知识、那些对我有帮助或有害的偏见，以及我的局限性。在项目的完成过程中，这些因素都不会发生太大的变化。

good-writing-002111.en: What if I didn’t worry about quality while writing?
good-writing-002111.zh: 如果我在写作时不去关心质量的话，会怎么样呢？

good-writing-002113.en: And when I’ve completed a first crummy draft and a second more polished draft, then maybe I can trust that it’s ready for an editor.
good-writing-002113.zh: 当我完成了一个初稿和一个更完善的修订稿之后，那么我就可以相信这份稿子已经准备好被编辑处理了。

good-writing-002114.en: In the meantime I don’t have to do the editor’s job for her.
good-writing-002114.zh: 与此同时，我不必替她完成编辑工作。

good-writing-002115.en: Second, sales: The publisher bought the book from me with an eye toward the maximum number of copies likely to be sold.
good-writing-002115.zh: 其次，关于销售方面：出版商从我这里购买了这本书，其目标是尽可能多地销售这本书的副本。

good-writing-002116.en: After the editor has decided the book is ready for market, the publisher might assign me some promotional duties—social media posts, appearances, podcasts, workshops, networking—but none of that is of any importance during the period that I’m writing the book.
good-writing-002116.zh: 在编辑确认这本书已经准备好上市之后，出版社可能会安排一些推广工作给我——比如发布社交媒体帖子、参加各种活动、主持播客、举办研讨会、建立人际关系等。但在我撰写这本书的这段时间里，这些活动都并不重要。

good-writing-002118.zh: 之后再担心晋升的问题吧。

good-writing-002119.zh: 这对自出版者来说也是真的。

good-writing-002120.en: Your job is to complete the current draft.
good-writing-002120.zh: 你的任务就是完成当前的草案工作。

good-writing-002122.en: Speaking of completion, how do you know you’ve ended the book in the right place?
good-writing-002122.zh: 说到完成度，如何判断自己是否将书在正确的位置完成了呢？

good-writing-002123.en: Have you written a tragedy or comedy or something in between?
good-writing-002123.zh: 你写过悲剧、喜剧还是其他类型的作品呢？

good-writing-002125.en: Even if Orson Welles is right, and the relative happiness of a movie or book’s ending depends on where you end it, make sure the final pages are gratifying to the reader.
good-writing-002125.zh: 即使奥森·威尔斯的观点是正确的，即一部电影或书籍的结局是否令人满意取决于我们如何结束故事，但至少最终部分应该能让读者感到满意。

good-writing-002126.en: That means all escape routes seem closed; the denouement seems inevitable.
good-writing-002126.zh: 这意味着所有的逃生路线似乎都已被切断；事情的结局似乎不可避免。

good-writing-002127.en: C. S. Lewis said, “I sometimes think that writing is like driving sheep down a road. If there is any gate open to the left or the right, the readers will most certainly go into it.”
good-writing-002127.zh: C.S. 路易斯曾说：“我有时觉得写作就像驱赶羊群穿过一条道路。如果左边或右边有任何门是开着的，读者们肯定会走进去。”

good-writing-002128.en: You’ve tied up loose ends without bringing in extra string.
good-writing-002128.zh: 你虽然解决了一些遗留问题，但并没有增加额外的线材。

good-writing-002129.en: Whatever you do, don’t introduce a deus ex machina, a convenient and magical solver of all problems, ten pages before the ending, in desperation to resolve things, quit writing, and get on with your life.
good-writing-002129.zh: 无论你做什么，都不要引入所谓的“救世主”——那种能够轻松解决所有问题的神奇解决方案。在故事即将结束的前十页出现这种解决方案，其实只是出于无奈才采用的手段罢了。请停止这种做法，继续你的生活吧。

good-writing-002130.en: There is no worse ending for a crime novel than to discover after a dozen red herrings have been tossed aside that the culprit didn’t mean to kill the victim; it was a head wound from an everyday bar fight.
good-writing-002130.zh: 对于一本犯罪小说来说，没有比这更糟糕的结局了：在抛掉了无数无用的线索之后，才发现真正的凶手并非有意杀害受害者；原来只是因为一场普通的酒吧斗殴而造成了头部受伤。

good-writing-002131.en: For some reason, TV scriptwriters seem to believe that this is OK once in a while.
good-writing-002131.zh: 出于某种原因，电视剧本作家似乎认为这种情况偶尔发生一下是可以接受的。

good-writing-002133.en: Many fiction authors write without a preliminary outline.
good-writing-002133.zh: 许多小说作者都是在没有事先制定大纲的情况下进行创作的。

good-writing-002134.en: They let the story tell itself as it goes, and don’t know where it will end until it does.
good-writing-002134.zh: 他们让故事自然发展，直到它结束之前，他们根本不知道它会以何种方式结束。

good-writing-002135.en: Nonfiction writers have a similar experience when the book they proposed changes course as their research takes them down new channels into new revelations.
good-writing-002135.zh: 非虚构类作家的创作过程也类似，当他们所提议的书籍在研究中发现新的线索时，书的走向就会随之改变，带来新的发现。

good-writing-002136.en: Getting ahead of the story flattens the experience; let go of some of the outline and let it blossom.
good-writing-002136.zh: 提前构思故事内容会破坏创作的体验感；不妨放开一些固定的框架，让故事自然发展。

good-writing-002137.en: Whether you’re writing a novel or a biography or a news article or a personal essay or a screenplay, the temptation is often to rush the ending.
good-writing-002137.zh: 无论你是写小说、传记、新闻文章、个人随笔还是剧本，人们往往倾向于急于完成故事的结尾部分。

good-writing-002138.en: The finish line promises a sense of accomplishment and rest.
good-writing-002138.zh: 终点线代表着一种成就感和休息的时刻。

good-writing-002139.en: Lots of books close with little more than a succession of plot points, the author having decided that their riffing on ideas is useless once the consequences are set in stone.
good-writing-002139.zh: 许多书籍的结尾都只是简单地罗列了一系列的情节要点而已。作者认为，一旦后果已经确定下来，那么对这些情节的详细叙述就变得毫无意义了。

good-writing-002140.en: But since we grow up with a belief that tales conclude with moral statements, the ending is the perfect time to equivocate, and let the happy or tragic ending be resolved while continuing the discussion of life’s ambiguities.
good-writing-002140.zh: 但因为我们从小就被灌输这样的观念：故事总是以道德性的结论来结束，所以这种模糊的结局正是绝佳的机会，可以用来探讨生命中那些模糊不清的问题，让快乐或悲剧性的结局得以升华。

good-writing-002141.en: What author has more complete resolutions than Jane Austen with her happy marriages?
good-writing-002141.zh: 哪位作家能比简·奥斯汀更完美地描绘出那些幸福的婚姻呢？

good-writing-002142.en: But look at the very last paragraph of Emma:
good-writing-002142.zh: 但是，看看艾玛文章的最后一段：

good-writing-002143.en: The wedding was very much like other weddings, where the parties have no taste for finery or parade; and Mrs. Elton, from the particulars detailed by her husband, thought it all extremely shabby, and very inferior to her own.
good-writing-002143.zh: 这场婚礼和其他婚礼没什么两样，参加婚礼的人们并不喜欢那些繁琐的仪式或华丽的装饰；根据丈夫所描述的情况，埃尔顿夫人认为这一切都相当寒酸，远不如她自己的婚礼那么精致。

good-writing-002144.en: —“Very little white satin, very few lace veils; a most pitiful business!—Selina would stare when she heard of it.”—But, in spite of these deficiencies, the wishes, the hopes, the confidence, the predictions of the small band of true friends who witnessed the ceremony, were fully answered in the perfect happiness of the union.
good-writing-002144.zh: “很少使用白色缎子，也很少使用蕾丝面纱；真是可怜的装饰啊！——当塞琳娜听到这件事时，一定会感到非常失望。”——不过，尽管存在这些不足，那些见证这一仪式的小团体所怀有的愿望、希望、信心以及预测，最终都得到了实现，使得这对恋人能够沉浸在完美的幸福之中。

good-writing-002145.en: The manners in this novel of manners are being questioned to the end!
good-writing-002145.zh: 这部小说中的各种礼仪规范最终都受到了质疑！

good-writing-002146.en: One thing I love about Austen is that her characters grow more and more verbose as each of her novels proceeds.
good-writing-002146.zh: 我喜欢奥森作品的一点就是，在她的每一部小说中，角色们的表达都越来越丰富多样。

good-writing-002147.en: The author holds close to “show, don’t tell” at the beginning, then loosens the straps as the book races to a conclusion, which slows things down and builds tension.
good-writing-002147.zh: 作者在开头就坚持“用表演来呈现，而非直接叙述”的写作方式，随后随着故事的推进，这种手法逐渐变得柔和，从而营造出更为紧张的氛围。最后，故事的节奏被放缓，使得整个情节更加引人入胜。

good-writing-002148.en: Often characters who spoke curtly in the first third of an Austen novel become blowhard speechifiers toward the end.
good-writing-002148.zh: 在奥斯汀小说的前三分之一部分，那些说话简洁的角色，往往会在小说的后半部分变得说话方式夸张、口无遮拦。

good-writing-002149.en: But we’re so engaged we don’t notice that Austen is in full riff mode toward the finale.
good-writing-002149.zh: 但我们如此投入于其中，以至于没有注意到在剧情接近高潮时，奥斯汀的表演风格已经完全进入到了狂热状态。

good-writing-002150.en: Yes, you know the ending about fifty pages in, but by extending the torture, especially toward the end, you don’t care.
good-writing-002150.zh: 是的，你知道故事在第五十页处就结束了。不过，如果继续延长这个折磨的过程，尤其是在故事接近尾声时，那也没关系。

good-writing-002151.en: You just want to hear Austen’s voice—her ideas, and her twists—ringing through the characters’ dialogue and orations, consistency of diction be damned.
good-writing-002151.zh: 你只是想听到奥斯汀的声音——她的想法、她的戏剧性转折——在角色的对话和言论中回荡，不必讲究语言的连贯性。

good-writing-002153.en: The best reason to finish whatever you are writing is that everything inside you says not to.
good-writing-002153.zh: 完成你正在写的任何事情的最佳理由是：你内心的声音都在告诫你不要这样做。

good-writing-002154.en: The worst inner voice, that of perfectionism, insists that your work is not going anywhere in its current form, and you should toss it out and begin something new, something that it will tell you in a few weeks is also not worth finishing.
good-writing-002154.zh: 最糟糕的内心声音，也就是完美主义者的声音，会不断强调：以目前的形式，你的作品根本无法取得任何成就。因此，你应该放弃现有的作品，开始一些新的创作。不过，几周后，那些新作品也会被证明根本不值得完成。

good-writing-002155.en: Finishing your project is a subversive act.
good-writing-002155.zh: 完成你的项目是一种具有颠覆性的行为。

good-writing-002156.en: Maybe it turns out worse than you had hoped, too weak to submit to an agent or a quarterly, but finishing gave you a couple of advantages.
good-writing-002156.zh: 也许结果会比你预期的还要糟糕，因为力量太弱，无法与那些需要定期提交报告的事务竞争。不过，能够完成这项任务还是有一些好处的。

good-writing-002157.en: The first is that you have weakened and worn down the bad voice.
good-writing-002157.zh: 首先，你们已经削弱并削弱了那个糟糕的声音。

good-writing-002158.en: You are the one who calls the shots now.
good-writing-002158.zh: 现在，由你来决定一切了。

good-writing-002159.en: The second is that with a finished and possibly shitty first draft, you may now know what you were shooting for all along.
good-writing-002159.zh: 其次，有了已经完成且可能还不太完善的第一稿后，你现在应该已经清楚自己原本的目标是什么了。

good-writing-002160.en: OK, it wasn’t what you have printed out and are reading with a sinking heart and chocolate cravings.
good-writing-002160.zh: 好吧，这并非你打印出来、怀着沉重的心情和渴望巧克力之心所阅读的那份内容。

good-writing-002161.en: But knowing what your writing isn’t is part of how you find out what it is.
good-writing-002161.zh: 但了解你的写作特点，正是你发现其本质的方式之一。

good-writing-002162.en: In Bird by Bird, I wrote about a painter setting out to capture his vision on a canvas, beginning with the upper-right quadrant.
good-writing-002162.zh: 在《一鸟一鸟》一书中，我讲述了一位画家如何尝试将他的构想描绘在画布上，从画布的右上方开始绘制。

good-writing-002163.en: When he is done, he sees that it is not at all what he had envisioned, so he conceals it with white paint, and tries again, now knowing one thing that it isn’t.
good-writing-002163.zh: 当他完成之后，他发现结果完全不符合他的预期。于是他用白色颜料将结果遮盖起来，然后再次尝试，不过这次他明白了一个事实：结果并不如他所愿。

good-writing-002164.en: The second time, he comes closer, but his concept and vision still evade him.
good-writing-002164.zh: 第二次时，他靠近了一些，但他的理念和视野仍然没有改变。

good-writing-002165.en: With his third attempt, his canvas finally approaches not what he had first imagined, but something maybe better.
good-writing-002165.zh: 在第三次尝试之后，他的作品终于达到了他最初设想的目标，不过还是比最初想象的要好一些。

good-writing-002166.en: I don’t mean that you don’t put aside work when you have tried everything unsuccessfully to make it salable.
good-writing-002166.zh: 我的意思并不是说，在你已经尝试了所有方法但都无法让作品具有吸引力之后，就不应该再继续从事这项工作了。

good-writing-002167.en: I have given up on a number of essays and manuscripts over the years, after having finished them.
good-writing-002167.zh: 这些年来，我放弃了许多论文和手稿，因为它们在完成之后我就不再继续关注它们了。

good-writing-002168.en: Writing and writing again is how we writers practice scales, how we get better over time.
good-writing-002168.zh: 写作，不断地写作，这就是我们作家们提升自己技巧的方式，也是我们在时间推移中不断进步的方法。

good-writing-002169.en: When we commit to finishing our work, this forces us to stay at the keyboard, pushing on through to the end.
good-writing-002169.zh: 当我们决定完成这项工作时，就会被迫持续工作，直到最后一步。

good-writing-002170.en: Think of finishing as a little like being in labor, where you realize ten hours in that you don’t even actually like children.
good-writing-002170.zh: 完成这项任务的过程，有点像分娩时的感觉——在分娩的第十个小时时，你就会意识到自己其实并不喜欢孩子。

good-writing-002173.en: Samuel Beckett said, “Ever tried. Ever failed. No matter. Try again. Fail again. Fail better.”
good-writing-002173.zh: 塞缪尔·贝克特说过：“曾经尝试过，也曾经失败过。但没关系，继续尝试吧。再次失败，但这次要失败得更好。”

good-writing-002174.en: This is the way of most artists and writers.
good-writing-002174.zh: 这是大多数艺术家和作家的行事方式。

good-writing-002175.en: Not giving up or giving in, getting each day’s work done, is the payoff, loosening us up, cortisone for the soul.
good-writing-002175.zh: 不放弃、不妥协，每天完成手头的工作，这就是回报。这让我们放松下来，就像给灵魂带来了一剂镇静剂。

good-writing-002176.en: Now as to endings, what I’m about to say is extremely personal to me, and I’m sure if Neal and I were to discuss this, it would end in an ugly fight.
good-writing-002176.zh: 至于结局的问题，我要说的内容对我来说非常私人化。我敢肯定，如果我和尼尔讨论这个问题，最终的结果肯定会是激烈的争吵。

good-writing-002177.en: I hate sad or ambiguous endings.
good-writing-002177.zh: 我讨厌悲伤或模糊的结局。

good-writing-002178.en: Please, for the love of God, don’t end your work with a miserable outcome for the main characters, except for the villain.
good-writing-002178.zh: 请，看在上帝的份上，不要让你的作品以主角的悲惨结局来结束，除了反派角色之外。

good-writing-002179.en: I don’t see the point in keeping us at the campfire for 300 pages, caring for your characters, pulling for them to come through the drama of humankind, only to conclude with bad or sad news.
good-writing-002179.zh: 我觉得没有必要让我们在火堆旁等待300页的篇幅，去关心那些角色的故事，期待他们能够挺过人间的种种苦难，最后却只能得到糟糕或悲伤的消息。

good-writing-002180.en: You might say that a sad ending is like real life half the time, to which I would counter, “Oh, really? I hadn’t noticed.”
good-writing-002180.zh: 你可能会说，悲伤的结局在现实生活中经常会出现，对此我回应说：“真的吗？我之前没注意到呢。”

good-writing-002181.en: I read to get lost in a riveting story and good writing.
good-writing-002181.zh: 我阅读是为了沉浸在一个引人入胜的故事和精彩的文字中。

good-writing-002182.en: I love plots most of all that involve people coming through difficult and deeply human circumstances, with, as Salinger’s Esme put it, all their f-a-c-u-l-t-i-e-s intact, their hearts and spirits and senses of humor restored even if they (like the rest of us) face challenging futures.
good-writing-002182.zh: 我最喜欢那些描绘人物在艰难且充满人性挑战的情境下成长的故事。正如塞利格曼笔下的埃斯梅所写的那样，这些角色尽管面临着种种困难，但他们的情感、心灵以及幽默感依然完好无损。至少，他们和我们其他人一样，也面临着充满挑战的未来。

good-writing-002183.en: I don’t want a story where God or Life or The Good have saved our characters from drowning, only to beat them to death on the beach.
good-writing-002183.zh: 我不想要这样的故事：上帝、生命或者“善”从溺水危机中拯救了我们的角色，却最终在沙滩上将他们击毙。

good-writing-002184.en: Also, two-thirds of the way through any excellent book, I’m so grateful for the ride—the attention and clarity and beauty and tension that the author has provided—that I’m pretty easy at that point.
good-writing-002184.zh: 此外，在读完任何一本优秀的书籍的半程之后，我会为作者所创造出的那种专注、清晰、美妙且充满张力的阅读体验而感到无比感激。在那种状态下，我几乎不会感到疲倦。

good-writing-002185.en: Neal is right for once that you just want to stay in Jane Austen’s company toward the end of Emma or any of her books.
good-writing-002185.zh: 尼尔说得对，在《艾玛》或她的任何一本书的结尾部分，我们确实应该继续沉浸在简·奥斯汀的世界里。

good-writing-002186.en: Of course, none of us can write like her, but we can all strive to be trustworthy and friendly narrators of the stories we seek to tell.
good-writing-002186.zh: 当然，我们没有人能够像她那样写作，但我们可以努力成为那些值得信赖且友善的故事讲述者，能够讲述我们渴望分享的故事。

good-writing-002187.zh: 法则36：敬重有才华的编辑

good-writing-002188.en: Writing is collaborative, and editors save your skin.
good-writing-002188.zh: 写作需要合作，而编辑往往能救你一把。

good-writing-002189.en: Editors don’t improve me; they fill in my blind spots.
good-writing-002189.zh: 编辑们并不能让我变得更好；他们只是弥补了我的不足之处而已。

good-writing-002190.en: I can’t improve much on the many years that have brought me here during the relatively short time I spend writing the book.
good-writing-002190.zh: 在撰写这本书的这段相对较短的时间里，我无法对过去多年的经验做出太多改进。

good-writing-002191.en: I’ll probably always sport the same blind spots.
good-writing-002191.zh: 我可能永远都会保留那些“盲点”。

good-writing-002192.en: I forget to move beyond visuals.
good-writing-002192.zh: 我忘记去关注那些视觉上的东西了。

good-writing-002193.en: My characters aren’t paranoid enough, or are cardboard.
good-writing-002193.zh: 我的角色不够多疑，或者他们的形象过于刻板。

good-writing-002194.zh: 我的语言变得更加优美了。

good-writing-002195.en: I can only get a sentence so far along and then I run out of good ideas for refining it.
good-writing-002195.zh: 我目前只能写出这么一小段内容，之后就再也没有好的想法可以用来完善它了。

good-writing-002196.en: But a good editor chimes in with further suggestions for some of my sentences, passages, and scenes.
good-writing-002196.zh: 不过，一位优秀的编辑还提出了一些关于我的句子、段落和场景的修改建议。

good-writing-002197.en: If I listen openly, I can have fun making changes.
good-writing-002197.zh: 如果我能敞开心扉去倾听，那么做出改变就会变得有趣。

good-writing-002198.zh: 我的第一个读者是安妮。

good-writing-002199.en: She gently points out phrases I might want to rework, and I dispute every one of them.
good-writing-002199.zh: 她会温和地指出那些我可能需要修改的语句，而我会逐一对这些建议提出反对意见。

good-writing-002200.en: “Oh, I thought of that, but no.” “The flow would be lost.” “I think I need that for later.”
good-writing-002200.zh: “哦，我考虑过这个问题了，但是不行。”“那种节奏就会乱了。”“我觉得我需要留着这个，以后再用。”

good-writing-002201.en: Within twenty-four hours I come to my senses and make every one of her corrections.
good-writing-002201.zh: 在二十四小时内，我会恢复理智，并立即实施她提出的每一个改进措施。

good-writing-002202.en: Annie, who is more grown-up than I am, swallows whole most of my suggested changes for her work, having decided that she completed her part already—the first draft—and trusting that my role is different.
good-writing-002202.zh: 安妮比我成熟得多，她几乎完全接受了我建议的所有修改建议。她认为自己已经完成了初稿，因此不再需要我的帮助了——我相信我的角色与她不同。

good-writing-002203.en: She then applies herself to what she calls the dental draft.
good-writing-002203.zh: 然后，她开始着手处理她所谓的“牙科设计”工作。

good-writing-002204.en: When we show each other the improved sentence, the response is always the same: “Yeah, that works.”
good-writing-002204.zh: 当我们向对方展示改进后的句子时，他们的反应总是一样的：“嗯，这样很好用。”

good-writing-002205.zh: 句子要么有效，要么无效。

good-writing-002206.en: When they’re missing something, they don’t work.
good-writing-002206.zh: 当他们缺少某些东西时，他们就无法正常工作。

good-writing-002207.en: When they’re all put together, they work.
good-writing-002207.zh: 把它们全部放在一起后，就能发挥作用了。

good-writing-002208.en: The scariest moment in our relationship descended in our third week dating, when Annie asked to read something of mine.
good-writing-002208.zh: 我们恋情中最可怕的时刻发生在相识的第三周，当时安妮请求让我给她读一些东西。

good-writing-002209.en: While I could claim to be a writer because I had made a living from it, calling oneself a writer isn’t the same as being a good writer.
good-writing-002209.zh: 虽然我可以自称为作家，因为我靠写作为生，但自称作家并不等同于真正成为一个优秀的作家。

good-writing-002210.en: As Annie silently read my short story on the couch we shared, my insides scrambled.
good-writing-002210.zh: 在沙发上，安妮静静地阅读着我写的短篇小说，那一刻，我的内心充满了激动与感动。

good-writing-002211.en: When she set it down and expressed satisfaction with my prose, I was relieved.
good-writing-002211.zh: 当她放下手中的东西，并对我的散文表示满意时，我松了一口气。

good-writing-002212.en: But I remained skeptical until a few days later when she offered me a first pass at editing an essay of hers.
good-writing-002212.zh: 但我仍然持怀疑态度，直到几天后她提出让我尝试编辑她的一篇论文。

good-writing-002213.en: No professional writer would offer an unskilled writer a piece to edit.
good-writing-002213.zh: 没有哪个专业的作家会向没有写作能力的写手提供需要编辑的作品。

good-writing-002214.en: A daily newspaper forces real-time collaborations.
good-writing-002214.zh: 一份日报促进了实时协作。

good-writing-002215.en: Reporters and editors labor under deadlines that allow only one working draft that is manipulated in bursts as the clock ticks.
good-writing-002215.zh: 记者和编辑们必须在紧迫的截止时间内完成工作，因此他们只能先完成一个初稿，之后在最后阶段对初稿进行最后的修改。

good-writing-002216.en: Mistakes are removed (mostly) and, in the rush, also added.
good-writing-002216.zh: 错误大多已经被纠正了，而在匆忙之中，一些内容也被添加了进来。

good-writing-002217.en: Injecting errors of fact is inexcusable, but arrogant editors often find other, acceptable ways to butcher copy, dragging down syntax, usage, and rhythm.
good-writing-002217.zh: 故意捏造虚假事实是不可原谅的行为，但有些傲慢的编辑们却总能找到其他、更可接受的方式来歪曲文本，从而破坏文本的语法结构、使用规范以及节奏感。

good-writing-002218.en: I could respect an editor who made two improvements for every added defect, and if the ratio reached closer to 3:1, they had something to teach me.
good-writing-002218.zh: 我能够尊重那些在每处缺陷上都会进行两次改进的编辑。如果这种比例能够接近3:1，那么他们就有东西可以教我了。

good-writing-002219.en: When I moved to the editing desk, I held a weekly writing session with my group of talented reporters.
good-writing-002219.zh: 当我开始从事编辑工作后，我每周都会与我的那些有才华的记者们一起举行写作会议。

good-writing-002220.en: We six would each clip an article that another of us had published the prior week.
good-writing-002220.zh: 我们六个人各自摘抄了上周其他成员发表的文章。

good-writing-002221.en: The rule was to highlight one sentence or paragraph that we might all admire.
good-writing-002221.zh: 规则是选出一句或一段我们都会欣赏的句子或段落。

good-writing-002222.en: The choice passage would be read aloud, and then the writer questioned on how they arrived at that clever wording.
good-writing-002222.zh: 这段选文的朗读部分会被大声读出来，然后作者会询问他们是如何想出如此巧妙的措辞的。

good-writing-002223.en: Together, we learned new rules by examining good writing, without ever criticizing or correcting.
good-writing-002223.zh: 我们一起通过研究优秀的写作案例来学习新的写作规则，而在这个过程中，我们从未进行过任何批评或修正。

good-writing-002225.en: When peers meet, though, they can search for mutual respect.
good-writing-002225.zh: 不过，当同龄人相遇的时候，他们可以寻求彼此之间的相互尊重。

good-writing-002226.en: An untalented editor is worse than no editor at all.
good-writing-002226.zh: 一个没有才华的编辑，还不如没有编辑好。

good-writing-002227.en: You won’t feel protected from your blind spots, and you can’t trust the suggested changes.
good-writing-002227.zh: 你无法真正避免自己的盲点所带来的风险，而且也无法信任那些被建议的修改方案。

good-writing-002228.en: If you don’t happen to be married to a great editor, take the time to find one.
good-writing-002228.zh: 如果你没有嫁给一位出色的编辑，那就花时间找一位吧。

good-writing-002229.en: A serious editor will always let you have your way with your natural voice, ideas, and the book’s gestalt.
good-writing-002229.zh: 一位严谨的编辑会允许你自由地表达你的个人观点、想法以及整本书的整体风格。

good-writing-002230.en: An editor isn’t there to alter your voice or change the impression that the work will leave or improve on the quality you brought to the work.
good-writing-002230.zh: 编辑的角色并不是去改变你的表达方式，或者改变作品给人的印象，或是提升你为作品所付出的努力所带来的质量。

good-writing-002231.en: What they can do is get that quality to appear consistently.
good-writing-002231.zh: 他们能够做到的是让这种品质始终保持一致。

good-writing-002232.en: They’re there for blind spots, of which I have many, and they’re angels as they swoop in on gossamer wings and delicately lift my dragging sentences into the air.
good-writing-002232.zh: 他们存在于那些我容易忽视的“盲点”之中。他们就像天使一样，以轻盈的翅膀飞入我的生活中，然后轻轻地将我那些冗长的句子提入空中。

good-writing-002234.en: It is no exaggeration to say that good editors are 30 percent of the reason you love the work of the writers you do.
good-writing-002234.zh: 毫不夸张地说，优秀的编辑能力是您能够欣赏到作家作品的重要原因之一，这个比例高达30%。

good-writing-002235.en: They would never take this much credit, but it has been Neal’s and my experience.
good-writing-002235.zh: 他们绝不会把这么多的功劳据为己有，但这确实是尼尔和我的经历所得。

good-writing-002236.en: You work your butt off trying to get your story just right, and then give it to a writing partner or friend, and they fashion the first edit.
good-writing-002236.zh: 你拼命地工作，试图把你的故事写得很完美，然后把它交给一位写作伙伴或朋友进行初稿修改。

good-writing-002237.en: You’re told that your lede is weak and that the first page reads like you are just clearing your throat, and that you should end the whole thing two pages or chapters before you do, but the structure is fine—or it isn’t, but they have a suggestion—and of course there are way too many adverbs, and you have repeated yourself here, and here and here, and this sentence doesn’t work...
good-writing-002237.zh: 他们指出，你的段落结构不够完善，第一页的内容看起来就像是在空口唾沫，建议你在正文的前两页或几个章节处结束这部分内容。不过，整体结构其实还是可以的——或者也可以说不是这样。不过他们给出了一些改进建议。当然，这里的副词使用太多了，而且你还反复使用了相同的句子结构，还有这句话的语法也不正确……

good-writing-002238.en: Then you do (some of) what they’ve suggested because you trust that they are both tough and respectful and know what they are talking about.
good-writing-002238.zh: 那么，你就会按照他们建议的方式去做吧，因为你相信他们都是非常坚定且尊重他人的人，而且他们很清楚自己在说什么。

good-writing-002239.en: You absolutely cannot see your own blind spots and pontificating and showing off.
good-writing-002239.zh: 你绝对无法察觉自己的盲点，更无法做到不发表意见或炫耀自己。

good-writing-002240.en: After a while with a manuscript, you can’t even see your typos.
good-writing-002240.zh: 过一段时间之后，当你处理一份手稿时，甚至都看不出自己写错的字了。

good-writing-002241.en: When you edit yourself, your eyes glance off the page because you’ve gone over it too many times.
good-writing-002241.zh: 当你自己编辑文本时，你的目光会不自觉地扫过页面上的内容，因为你已经反复阅读过很多次了。

good-writing-002242.en: Then maybe a publisher buys it!
good-writing-002242.zh: 那么，也许会有出版商购买它吧！

good-writing-002243.en: And you will be assigned to an editor.
good-writing-002243.zh: 然后，你将被分配到一个编辑手中。

good-writing-002244.en: This is fantastic, kind of a miracle, but confusing, because you’d thought you were “finished.”
good-writing-002244.zh: 这真是太棒了，简直就像一种奇迹。不过，这也会让人感到困惑，因为你可能会以为自己已经“完成了”所有工作。

good-writing-002246.en: Now your real, honest-to-God professional editor reads it slowly and marks it up, and thinks evil thoughts about what would be a better way to introduce this or that, and how—no offense—you can definitely lose twenty-five pages in the middle.
good-writing-002246.zh: 现在，你那位真正认真、专业的编辑正在慢慢地阅读这篇文章，并对其进行修改。他们还在思考：用哪种方式来介绍这个或那个部分会更合适一些……不过，无意冒犯——你肯定可以删掉文章中间的25页内容。

good-writing-002247.en: If it’s a book, they write a long editorial letter with ten main points, all the things they found wrong, the things that could be better, a few solutions, and two or three things they especially like.
good-writing-002247.zh: 如果是书籍的话，他们会撰写一份长达数页的评论文章，其中包含十个主要观点：他们发现的问题、可以改进的地方、一些解决方案，以及他们特别喜欢的几点。

good-writing-002248.en: This moment, when you receive the editorial letter, is a real test of your mettle.
good-writing-002248.zh: 此刻，当你收到这封编辑通知时，其实是对你能力的真正考验。

good-writing-002249.en: Can you get past the lifelong resistance to authority, the hurt feelings, the but but but everyone told me it was good?
good-writing-002249.zh: 你能克服对权威的终生抵触情绪、那些痛苦的感受吗？虽然大家都说这东西很好，但我还是觉得有些不妥。

good-writing-002250.en: Can you retain a little self-respect in the presence of someone correcting your many mistakes?
good-writing-002250.zh: 当有人正在指出你的许多错误时，你还能保持一点自尊吗？

good-writing-002252.en: And then you start to feel the kind of relief that is called a blessing.
good-writing-002252.zh: 然后，你就会开始感受到那种被称为“幸运”的缓解感。

good-writing-002253.en: Because now you have a map and a little light to see by.
good-writing-002253.zh: 因为现在你有一张地图，还有一盏可以照亮的小灯作为指引。

good-writing-002254.en: Someone invested in you has given you their best expertise and writing advice on how to vastly improve an already good piece of work, how to make it cleaner and richer, how to bring forth depth and charm, how to keep your voice as clear and true as possible, and, of course, how to save you from embarrassment.
good-writing-002254.zh: 那些关心你的人，已经倾尽全力地提供了他们最宝贵的写作建议。他们告诉你如何改进一篇已经很不错的作品，如何使其更加简洁且富有吸引力，如何增添作品的深度与魅力，如何确保你的声音尽可能清晰、真实。当然，他们还教会了你如何避免尴尬的局面。

good-writing-002258.en: When I was twenty-seven, my friend and boss Tom Geyer, who was president of a national newspaper chain, said offhandedly, “I think I would have liked a career as a hack writer.”
good-writing-002258.zh: 在我27岁的时候，我的朋友兼上司汤姆·盖耶，他是一家全国性报纸连锁企业的负责人，突然说道：“我觉得自己会喜欢做记者这种职业。”

good-writing-002259.en: He had just promoted me into the business side of newspapers.
good-writing-002259.zh: 他刚刚将我提拔到报纸的商务部门工作。

good-writing-002260.en: Two years later, he offered me a huge new job, which would make me wealthy in a very short time.
good-writing-002260.zh: 两年后，他为我提供了一个非常优厚的新工作，这个机会让我在很短的时间内就能变得非常富有。

good-writing-002261.en: Instead I resigned to resume my poorly paid reporting career.
good-writing-002261.zh: 相反，我选择辞职，继续从事那份报酬微薄的报道工作。

good-writing-002262.en: Little did he know that he had sabotaged his own plans for me with a single unmemorable—to him—comment.
good-writing-002262.zh: 他根本不知道，他只是用一句对他来说并不起眼的评论，就破坏了自己为我制定的计划。

good-writing-002263.en: Since then, I’ve defined myself as a hack writer.
good-writing-002263.zh: 从那时起，我就一直认为自己是位兼职作家。

good-writing-002264.en: I can write anything for anybody, for pay.
good-writing-002264.zh: 我可以为了任何目的，以任何报酬来写作。

good-writing-002265.en: When she was twenty-seven, my wife was already recognized in a quite different writing category.
good-writing-002265.zh: 当她二十七岁时，我的妻子已经以一种截然不同的写作风格而受到认可。

good-writing-002266.en: No hack—she was several years into the life of a literary writer.
good-writing-002266.zh: 她已经从事文学创作多年了，没有那种临时抱佛脚的做法。

good-writing-002267.en: Despite living for decades in our different roles in the world—one of us a hack, the other a literary author—when we finally met in 2016 and gingerly passed each other the draft pages emerging from our current work, and then received them back littered with scratches and comments, we knew exactly what the other meant by their coded suggestions—“tighten this,” “weak verb,” “passive phrase,” “add sensory material,” “cut this.”
good-writing-002267.zh: 尽管我们分别在不同的领域工作——其中一个是个职业作家，另一个则是个业余写手——但在2016年我们终于相遇的时候，当我们小心翼翼地互相传递着各自作品中的草稿时，那些草稿上满是批注和意见。我们立刻明白对方通过那些隐晦的提示想要表达什么：“加强这个部分”，“动词使用不当”，“被动语态使用不当”，“添加一些感官描述”，“删掉这部分内容”。

good-writing-002268.en: These rules may not be as necessary as grammatical conventions, but they seem to be universal.
good-writing-002268.zh: 这些规则可能并不像语法规则那样必不可少，但它们似乎具有普遍性。

good-writing-002269.en: Agreement on what is true is more difficult than ever, and our words are suffering.
good-writing-002269.zh: 确认什么是真实的这件事比以往任何时候都更加困难，而我们的言辞则因此受到了影响。

good-writing-002270.en: The acceptability of a sentence now runs a gauntlet of fads, prejudices, and know-nothingism as emotions and arguments over beliefs terrorize us all.
good-writing-002270.zh: 现在，一个句子的可接受性面临着各种潮流、偏见以及无知态度的挑战。各种情绪和关于信念的争论正在恐吓着我们所有人。

good-writing-002271.en: Still, the rules in this book continue to aid my hack writing even as the audience for any piece of writing gets more judgmental and skeptical.
good-writing-002271.zh: 不过，这本书中的规则仍然有助于我进行写作。尽管任何作品的受众都越来越具有评判性和怀疑的态度，但这些规则仍然能帮我更好地完成写作。

good-writing-002272.en: These tips aid my wife’s literary writing in exactly the same way, because they ring with the universal human experience.
good-writing-002272.zh: 这些建议对我妻子的文学创作同样有所帮助，因为它们能够反映人类共有的体验。

good-writing-002273.en: They may betray some old, seemingly outdated cultural accoutrements, but most of them have a counterpart in any language.
good-writing-002273.zh: 它们可能会抛弃一些看似过时的传统文化习俗，但其中大部分习俗在任何语言中都有对应的表达方式。

good-writing-002274.en: These rules economize, favor the plainspoken and the specific, keep the reader’s attention sharp, and in other ways show respect for the audience’s time and desire for novelty.
good-writing-002274.zh: 这些规则注重简洁明了的表达方式，能够吸引读者的注意力，同时也在其他方面体现了对读者时间和对新奇事物的需求的尊重。

good-writing-002275.en: They’re not just for professional writers.
good-writing-002275.zh: 它们并不只是为专业作家们准备的。

good-writing-002276.en: A politician or lawyer can turn to these same rules of rhetoric, as can a lyricist, a teacher, or a family storyteller.
good-writing-002276.zh: 无论是政治家还是律师，都可以运用这些修辞规则；同样，诗人、教师或家庭故事讲述者也可以如此行事。

good-writing-002277.en: The ancient Greeks recorded the orations of Pericles and the dialogues of Socrates with the reverence and sense of immortal remembrance that caused the Egyptians to build pyramids.
good-writing-002277.zh: 古希腊人怀着对伯利克里演讲的敬重以及对于苏格拉底对话录的铭记之情，将其记录下来。这种对历史人物的敬重与对智慧的传承之情，就如同古埃及人建造金字塔那样，具有永恒的意义。

good-writing-002278.en: Americans connect our ideals to the persuasively written Declaration of Independence, preamble to the Constitution, and Gettysburg Address, the last one read aloud at least once by nearly every schoolchild in my day.
good-writing-002278.zh: 美国人将我们的理想与《独立宣言》、宪法的序言，以及葛底斯堡演说联系在一起。在我那个时代，几乎每个孩子都至少读过一次葛底斯堡演说。

good-writing-002279.en: Likewise, Britons quote Churchill and Shakespeare, Chinese Confucius and Mao, South Africans Mandela and Tutu, Iranians Mohammed and Rumi.
good-writing-002279.zh: 同样，英国人也会引用丘吉尔和莎士比亚的观点；中国人则会引用孔子和毛泽东的思想；南非人则会引用曼德拉和图图的思想；伊朗人则会引用穆罕默德和鲁米的思想。

good-writing-002280.en: Our collective interest in elegant writing shines through the irony we all recognize in Lincoln’s famous words: “The world will little note, nor long remember what we say here.”
good-writing-002280.zh: 我们对于优雅写作的共同兴趣，体现在我们都熟悉的林肯那句著名的话中：“世人不会注意我们在这里所说的话，更不会长久记住这些话。”

good-writing-002282.en: For one thing, the Gettysburg Address is literally carved in stone at the Lincoln Memorial.
good-writing-002282.zh: 首先，葛底斯堡演说的内容被刻在林肯纪念园的石柱上，是真实存在的。

good-writing-002283.en: In the twentieth century, the word “rhetoric” lost its luster, tarnished by the modern malevolence of propaganda and Madison Avenue.
good-writing-002283.zh: 在二十世纪，“修辞学”这个词已经失去了其光彩，因为它被现代宣传手段以及马迪森广告公司所取代而变得黯淡无光。

good-writing-002284.zh: 但那样做并没有抓住重点。

good-writing-002285.en: Writing in a way that persuades your reader to continue reading is not the devil’s work.
good-writing-002285.zh: 以能够说服读者继续阅读的方式写作，并不是什么难事。

good-writing-002286.en: Persuasion, including the rhetorical devices, is separate and distinct from dogma, control, competitiveness, and emotion.
good-writing-002286.zh: 说服技巧，包括各种修辞手段，与教条、控制欲、竞争心理以及情绪等因素是分开且有所区别的。

good-writing-002287.en: It is true that these rules can be employed for thought control and advertising, but they work just as well in works of touching love and happy agreement.
good-writing-002287.zh: 的确，这些规则可以用于思维控制和广告效果，但它们在表达爱意和表达愉悦情感的作品中同样有效。

good-writing-002288.en: It is exactly that impartiality that gives them their universality, and when things are truly common among humans, we can trust them.
good-writing-002288.zh: 正是这种公正性使得它们具有普遍性。当某些事物真正适用于所有人类时，我们就能信任它们。

good-writing-002289.en: Now writing is being altered even more.
good-writing-002289.zh: 现在，写作方式已经被进一步改变了。

good-writing-002290.en: I’m not convinced that books will survive the next few generations.
good-writing-002290.zh: 我并不认为书籍能够存活到下一代。

good-writing-002291.en: Communication of knowledge and ideas has been transformed by technology and the common library called the Internet.
good-writing-002291.zh: 知识和思想的传播因技术以及被称为“互联网”的公共图书馆而发生了变革。

good-writing-002292.en: Clicking through websites has largely replaced ferreting out bits of information hidden in the pages of books.
good-writing-002292.zh: 通过点击网页来获取信息，已经很大程度上取代了从书籍中查找信息的做法。

good-writing-002293.en: The new way takes seconds; the older one took hours.
good-writing-002293.zh: 新方法只需要几秒钟就能完成；而旧方法则需要几个小时的时间。

good-writing-002294.en: Maybe books of fiction will survive, but surely not practical nonfiction.
good-writing-002294.zh: 也许小说的作品能够留存下来，但实用的非虚构作品肯定无法存活下去。

good-writing-002295.en: Ah, but these rules of good writing don’t exist only on the written page.
good-writing-002295.zh: 啊，但这些关于良好写作的规则并不只存在于书面文字中。

good-writing-002296.en: They inform all types of communication, including everyday speech.
good-writing-002296.zh: 它们能够处理各种形式的通信，包括日常对话。

good-writing-002297.en: We enjoy being entertained and persuaded in conversation, on film, through headphones, in private, and out in crowds.
good-writing-002297.zh: 我们喜欢在交谈中、在电影中、通过耳机聆听、在私密场合以及在大人群中都能得到娱乐和启发。

good-writing-002298.en: Instead of reading, people are listening—to books, yes, but also to experts on podcasts.
good-writing-002298.zh: 人们不再只是阅读，而是开始倾听——无论是阅读书籍，还是通过播客听取专家的意见。

good-writing-002299.en: As those experts script or improvise their words, they’re following many of the rules of rhetoric and persuasion that lifted Pericles two millennia ago and later, Shakespeare.
good-writing-002299.zh: 这些专家在撰写或即兴表达自己的观点时，遵循了许多修辞和说服的法则。这些法则早在两千年前就由伯利克里所采用，后来又被莎士比亚所发扬光大。

good-writing-002300.en: Strong verbs keep the listener’s attention exactly the same way they keep the reader’s.
good-writing-002300.zh: 强有力的动词能够像吸引读者的注意力一样，同样吸引听众的注意力。

good-writing-002301.en: I can’t prove it, but I tend to believe that the rules of persuasion and sentence-making will survive any changes in media, and may always assist us in refining the words we use to understand the human experience.
good-writing-002301.zh: 我无法证明这一点，但我倾向于认为，无论是媒体的形式如何变化，还是那些关于说服和判断的规则，都会一直存在，并且它们始终会帮助我们更好地选择那些能够准确表达人类经验的词语。

good-writing-002303.en: The modern era is swamped with so much murk and bullshit that when a writer finds the words and figures of speech to convey truth, and entice me into their story, I enter gratefully.
good-writing-002303.zh: 现代社会充满了如此多的混乱与无意义的废话，只有当作家找到能够传达真相的词语和修辞手法，并吸引我进入他们的故事时，我才会欣然投入其中。

good-writing-002304.en: When a writer chooses a verb that is so precise that it makes me look up from the page with admiration, I’m going to keep on reading.
good-writing-002304.zh: 当一位作家选择的动词如此精确，以至于让我在欣赏中抬起头来看时，我会继续阅读下去的。

good-writing-002305.en: When a writer presents me with a tightly edited piece of work where they have clearly taken out all the boring and show-offy parts, this is work that I may very well foist on others.
good-writing-002305.zh: 当一位作家向我提交一篇经过精心编辑的作品时，那些繁琐且浮夸的部分显然已经被删除了。这样的作品，我很乐意分享给其他人。

good-writing-002306.en: My poor husband suffers from being gravely overeducated, and so I suggest that you gloss over the above references to Socrates and Pericles and focus instead on the seminal idea of his book: “These rules economize, favor the plainspoken and the specific, keep the reader’s attention sharp, and in other ways show respect for the audience’s time and desire for novelty.”
good-writing-002306.zh: 我可怜的丈夫因为过度教育而深受困扰。因此，我建议你们可以略过上述对苏格拉底和伯利克里的描述，而是重点讨论他书中提出的核心思想：“这些规则能够节约时间，强调清晰明了的表达方式，保持读者的注意力集中，同时还能体现出对读者时间和对新奇事物的需求的尊重。”

good-writing-002307.en: Neal shared these thirty-six rules with me on our fourth or fifth date, and while their simplicity and brilliance were not the main reason I agreed to marry him a couple of years later, they didn’t hurt.
good-writing-002307.zh: 在我们的第四或第五次约会时，尼尔把这些36条规则告诉了我。虽然这些规则的简单性和巧妙性并不是我两年后同意嫁给他的主要原因，但它们确实起到了作用。

good-writing-002308.en: His rules helped me become a better writer, and if you follow them, your writing will get better, too.
good-writing-002308.zh: 他的规则帮助我成为了一名更优秀的作家。如果你遵循这些规则，你的写作水平也会得到提升。

good-writing-002309.en: Your work will get more economical, sharper, and more riveting.
good-writing-002309.zh: 你的作品会变得更加经济高效、更具吸引力，同时也更引人注目。

good-writing-002310.en: It is possible that it will become both more fun for us to read and more fun for you to write.
good-writing-002310.zh: 有可能，这样对我们来说阅读会变得更加有趣，对您来说写作也会更加愉快。

good-writing-002311.en: Our hope is that you will be able to edit your work in a more focused and efficient way.
good-writing-002311.zh: 我们希望您能够以更加集中且高效的方式来编辑您的作品。

good-writing-002312.en: Long, boring descriptions, out; generic verbs, out; endlessly inserted adjectives and adverbs, out out out.
good-writing-002312.zh: 冗长、乏味的描述，不用了；那些陈旧的、缺乏表现力的动词，也无需使用；那些无休止地出现的形容词和副词，也该删除了。

good-writing-002315.en: I think in terms of three drafts.
good-writing-002315.zh: 我认为可以分成三个阶段来进行。

good-writing-002316.en: I start with a shitty first draft, then a much tighter second draft, and finally the dental draft.
good-writing-002316.zh: 我是从一个很粗糙的初稿开始创作的，然后进行了更精细的修改，最后才完成最终的定稿。

good-writing-002317.en: I have these rules in the back of my mind with the shitty first draft but do not bog down in perfectionism.
good-writing-002317.zh: 我在脑海中已经把这些规则记在心里了，尽管初稿还不尽如人意，但我不会过于执着于完美主义的要求。

good-writing-002318.en: I bring them forward somewhat for the second draft, being stricter about adverbs, adjectives, and excessive details.
good-writing-002318.zh: 为了进行第二次的修改，我会稍微调整一下这些内容，对副词、形容词以及不必要的细节进行更严格的规范处理。

good-writing-002319.en: But the third draft is when I bear down on the work, tooth by tooth, sentence by sentence, poking and jiggling, and these rules are the tools for the cleaning, the drilling, the filling, the polishing.
good-writing-002319.zh: 但是，在第三个阶段，我才会真正开始这项工作——逐字逐句地修改，反复调整，这些规则就是用来进行清理、细化、补充和修饰的工具。

good-writing-002320.en: Neal’s bossy rules about what constitutes good writing can get you to hold yourself accountable, and this is good for any writer.
good-writing-002320.zh: 尼尔关于什么是优秀写作的严格标准会要求作者对自己负责，这对任何作家来说都是好事。

good-writing-002321.en: Commit to spending the time it takes to find the exact right words, phrases, and descriptions that best express your creative intention, and, paradoxically your work will become freer, looser, and truer.
good-writing-002321.zh: 请投入所需的时间，去找到最能表达你创意意图的恰当词语、短语和描述。如此一来，你的作品就会变得更加自由、更自然、更真实。

good-writing-002322.en: Discipline, in my experience, is what leads to freedom.
good-writing-002322.zh: 以我的经验来看，自律正是通往自由的道路。

good-writing-002323.en: I hope these rules and meditations serve as a guide and structure on which to base or improve your writing, as they have for me.
good-writing-002323.zh: 我希望这些规则与思考的指引能够成为你写作的指南和框架，帮助你改进自己的写作能力，就像它们曾经帮助过我一样。

good-writing-002324.en: Writing is hard for people like me.
good-writing-002324.zh: 对于像我这样的人来说，写作是一件很困难的事情。

good-writing-002325.en: Neal, who began as a journalist, sits down to write what is on his mind—novels, nonfiction, short essays—and just does it, as if he is still on deadline and the editor in chief is breathing down his neck.
good-writing-002325.zh: 尼尔最初是一名记者，后来开始创作自己感兴趣的作品——小说、非虚构作品、短篇随笔等。他只是简单地投入其中，仿佛自己仍处于截止日期的紧张状态中，而主编则时刻关注着他的创作进度。

good-writing-002326.en: I feel more like Cindy Lou Who, tiny and vulnerable and brave.
good-writing-002326.zh: 我觉得自己更像小叮当——娇小、脆弱却又勇敢。

good-writing-002327.en: Everything I write takes several drafts, and the first one is always unreadable, even as its completion is a small miracle of determination beating back self-doubt.
good-writing-002327.zh: 我写的每篇文章都需要经过多次修改才能臻于完善。而第一篇作品，即便在完成后，也往往还不尽如人意，因为那需要坚定的决心来克服内心的犹豫与不安，这本身就是一种奇迹。

good-writing-002328.en: This is where these rules make a difference: Every first draft of mine is way too long, as in, for example, the year-long series of pieces I wrote for The Washington Post on being older.
good-writing-002328.zh: 这些规则在这里确实起到了作用：我的每篇初稿都过于冗长了。比如，我为《华盛顿邮报》撰写的那篇关于年龄增长的长篇系列文章，就因为篇幅过长而不得不被删掉。

good-writing-002330.en: I would write 1,800, including many long elegant literary descriptions.
good-writing-002330.zh: 我会写出1800字的内容，其中包含了许多优美而冗长的文学性描述。

good-writing-002331.en: Rule 7 reminds me that if it sounds literary, it isn’t, so I would take (most of) them out, begrudgingly.
good-writing-002331.zh: 规则7提醒我，如果某些内容听起来像文学性的描述，那实际上并不是如此。因此，我会不情愿地将这些内容删掉，或者大部分内容都删掉。

good-writing-002332.en: Now the piece might be 1,600 or so words.
good-writing-002332.zh: 现在，这段文字大概有1,600个字左右。

good-writing-002333.en: Rule 14 encourages me to take out the boring parts, so there go another 300, mostly descriptions of nature or my own disappointing state of mind.
good-writing-002333.zh: 规则14鼓励我剔除那些乏味的部分，于是又多了300字的内容，这些内容大多是关于自然的描述，或者是我自己心情不佳时的内心写照。

good-writing-002334.en: Next to go are many adjectives, adverbs, filtering words, and clichés.
good-writing-002334.zh: 接下来需要淘汰的，还有许多形容词、副词、过滤词以及陈词滥调。

good-writing-002335.en: Then I remember an admonition of the legendary movie producer in early Hollywood Samuel Goldwyn, “If you have a message, send a telegram,” so I take out (many of) the messages.
good-writing-002335.zh: 然后我记起了那位传奇电影制片人在早期好莱坞时留下的告诫：“如果你有要传达的信息，那就发一份电报吧。”于是，我拿出了那些信息中的大部分内容。

good-writing-002336.en: Finally, with disappointment over how much of my deathless prose has been lost, I hand it over to Neal, which brings us to Rule 36: Worship (Talented) Editors.
good-writing-002336.zh: 最后，对于自己那些不朽的散文作品中有多少已经流失，我感到非常遗憾。我将这些作品交给了尼尔。这也就意味着，我们即将进入第36条规则：对才华横溢的编辑们的崇拜。

good-writing-002337.en: Believe me, at this point, with maybe 1,175 words left, there is nothing else that can possibly go.
good-writing-002337.zh: 相信我，在还剩大约1,175个字的情况下，已经没有更多的内容可以补充了。

good-writing-002340.en: Neal comes back in half an hour with the marked-up pages.
good-writing-002340.zh: 半小时后，尼尔带着那些已做标记的页面回来了。

good-writing-002341.en: He says something along the lines of how he is going to love it with a little bit of cutting and jiggling, which means it is terrible as is.
good-writing-002341.zh: 他说自己会喜欢这种带有轻微切割和扭曲效果的作品，不过这样的作品其实已经很糟糕了。

good-writing-002342.en: We sit down together and look at his illegible markings.
good-writing-002342.zh: 我们坐在一起，仔细查看他那些难以辨认的标记。

good-writing-002343.en: He thinks the entire first paragraph can go, a paragraph I worked on for an hour.
good-writing-002343.zh: 他认为整个第一段可以删掉，这一段是我花了一个小时才写出来的。

good-writing-002344.en: “Hmmm,” I respond, with indifference and contempt.
good-writing-002344.zh: “嗯，”我漠不关心且轻蔑地回应道。

good-writing-002346.en: And soon we’re off and running, collaborating pretty excitedly, with him pointing out weak verbs and the need for better transitions from one point to the next, and ideas he has for additions (which may in fact be good, although they necessitate cutting out more of my words, which he has thoughtfully done).
good-writing-002346.zh: 很快，我们就开始合作了。他非常热情地提出了一些改进建议，指出了动词使用上的不足，以及需要在不同段落之间实现更好的过渡。他还提出了一些补充建议（这些建议可能确实很有用，不过它们需要删减我的一些文字，不过他已经仔细地处理好了这个问题）。

good-writing-002347.en: This is what it takes for me to hand in my best possible work to my official editors, who then burnish it even further.
good-writing-002347.zh: 这就是我需要做的事情：向我的正式编辑们提交我最优秀的作品，而他们还会进一步提升作品的品质。

good-writing-002348.en: I wish I were more like Muriel Spark, the prolific British writer who was said to feel so plugged in to God that she sat down to write feeling like she was taking dictation.
good-writing-002348.zh: 我希望自己能更像穆里尔·斯帕克，这位多产的英国作家。据说她与上帝有着深刻的联系，以至于她在写作时仿佛是在接受上帝的启示一般。

good-writing-002349.en: I have never once in forty-five years had this experience, nor, for that matter, would I ever be close to a person who would announce this, no matter if it was true.
good-writing-002349.zh: 在四十五年的时间里，我从未有过这样的经历。同样，我也永远不会接近那些会公开这种事情的人，无论这种事情是否真实。

good-writing-002350.en: The rest of us flail and slog and write terrible first drafts, and then we make them better.
good-writing-002350.zh: 我们其他人则只能辛苦地撰写那些糟糕的初稿，然后努力让它们变得更好一些。

good-writing-002351.en: We do this because we’re writers.
good-writing-002351.zh: 我们这样做是因为我们是作家。

good-writing-002352.en: It helps to accept that writing is 80 percent stalling, 10 percent laundry, and 10 percent struggling to capture ideas, experiences, and imagination in words.
good-writing-002352.zh: 重要的是要认识到，写作过程中，有80%的时间是在拖延，10%的时间是在处理一些琐事，还有10%的时间则是在努力将想法、经历和想象用文字表达出来。

good-writing-002353.en: Sometimes when I want to give up, I remember being in labor.
good-writing-002353.zh: 有时候，当我想要放弃的时候，我会想起自己分娩时的情景。

good-writing-002354.en: Everything painful feels good when it’s over.
good-writing-002354.zh: 所有痛苦的经历在结束时都会带来愉悦的感觉。

good-writing-002355.en: Plus no one cares if we write or not, so we damn well better.
good-writing-002355.zh: 而且，没人会在乎我们是否去写这些作品，所以我们还是得这么做吧。

good-writing-002356.en: I do care that people write well, because of my starvation for truth, and for the joy of reading.
good-writing-002356.zh: 我确实很在意人们能否写出优秀的作品，因为我对真相的渴望，以及我对阅读乐趣的追求。

good-writing-002357.en: Good writing has been my rock and salvation since my parents first read to me.
good-writing-002357.zh: 自从父母第一次给我读书以来，优秀的写作能力就一直是我坚持下去的依靠和救星。

good-writing-002358.en: Tonight when I crawl into bed, a good book is waiting for me, in which I will get lost and found.
good-writing-002358.zh: 今晚，当我爬入床铺时，一本好书正在等着我。在书中，我可能会迷失，但最终又能找到方向。

good-writing-002359.en: Neal will be there, too, also lost in a book, and we will be in peace.
good-writing-002359.zh: 尼尔也会在那里，同样沉浸在阅读中。我们将能安心地待着。

good-writing-002360.en: Suddenly, one of us will exclaim—I mean “say” (Rule 4)—“Listen to this,” and then we’ll read a sentence or description to each other, and shake our heads at how fine it is.
good-writing-002360.zh: 突然，我们中的一个人会大声说道——我的意思是“说”（规则4）——“听这个吧”，然后我们会互相朗读一个句子或一段描述，并摇头表示这真是美妙极了。

good-writing-002361.en: You are fully capable of creating good sentences, too, with practice, guidance, an editor or writing partner, and dedication to the craft.
good-writing-002361.zh: 通过练习、指导、编辑或写作伙伴的帮助，以及对写作艺术的执着追求，你完全能够写出优秀的文章。

good-writing-002362.en: Trust me on this, but better yet, trust yourself: You’ve got this.
good-writing-002362.zh: 相信我吧，更重要的是，要相信自己：你能够做到这一点。

good-writing-002365.en: Use Strong Verbs: Replace weak verbs, which are imprecise (“walked,” “stood”), with vivid verbs, which are specific (“trudged,” “malingered”).
good-writing-002365.zh: 使用明确的动词：用更具体的动词替换那些不够准确的动词，比如“walked”和“stood”，而用“trudged”和“malingered”这样的动词来替代它们。

good-writing-002366.en: Question “Being” and “Having”: The verbs “to be” and “to have” are the weakest of all; by nature static, they slow a narrative.
good-writing-002366.zh: 问题：“存在”与“拥有”：动词“是”和“有”是最弱的动词；它们本质上是静态的，会减缓叙事的节奏。

good-writing-002367.en: Keep It Active: Pay attention to words that end in -ed or -en and are preceded by a form of “to be,” and watch out for -ing endings; try flipping the sentence to get it more active.
good-writing-002367.zh: 保持活跃状态：注意那些以“-ed”或“-en”结尾的单词，并且这些单词前面通常带有“to be”的形式。同时，要警惕以“-ing”结尾的单词；试着将句子结构调整一下，使其更加具有活力。

good-writing-002368.en: Stick with “Said”: When attributing a quote, “said” is the default verb; the reader’s attention is on who said it, not how it was said.
good-writing-002368.zh: 在引用他人言论时，默认使用“说”作为动词；读者的注意力集中在说这句话的人身上，而不是说的方式。

good-writing-002369.en: Don’t Show Off: Let others be erudite; your job is to befriend your reader.
good-writing-002369.zh: 不要自夸：让他人显得博学多才吧；你的任务则是与读者建立友谊。

good-writing-002370.en: Prefer Anglo-Saxon Words: Favor shorter, punchier Anglo-Saxon words over fancy, abstract Latinate words.
good-writing-002370.zh: 偏好使用盎格鲁-撒克逊语词汇：比起那些花哨、抽象拉丁语词汇，更倾向于使用更简洁、更直接的盎格鲁-撒克逊语词汇。

good-writing-002371.en: Sound Natural: Unless you’re writing a technical manual, keep your language conversational and use modern speech patterns.
good-writing-002371.zh: 语言要自然流畅：除非你正在编写技术手册，否则请使用口语化的语言，并采用现代的语言表达方式。

good-writing-002372.en: Trust Your Voice: Your natural voice has its own tempo, pitch, ease, and overall sound.
good-writing-002372.zh: 相信你的声音：你的自然嗓音具有独特的节奏、音高、流畅度以及整体音质特点。

good-writing-002374.en: Question Transitions: Transitional phrases (“then,” “next,” “when,” “meanwhile,” “however”) are not needed unless a gap in time or logic has opened.
good-writing-002374.zh: 问题过渡：除非在时间或逻辑上存在间隔，否则不需要使用诸如“然后”、“接下来”、“当……时”、“与此同时”、“然而”等过渡性短语。

good-writing-002375.en: Link Ideas with Semicolons: If two sentences are tightly linked and one progresses from the other, consider separating them with a semicolon.
good-writing-002375.zh: 用分号连接句子：如果两个句子之间有紧密的联系，且一个句子的内容是在推进另一个句子的内容，那么可以使用分号将它们分开。

good-writing-002376.en: Drop “Very” and Other Crutch Words: The word “very” seldom improves a sentence.
good-writing-002376.zh: 去掉“非常”这类修饰性词汇：在句子中，“非常”这个词其实很少能提升句子的表达效果。

good-writing-002377.en: Jettison [All Those] Tiny Words: Remove the clutter of short words (pronouns, prepositions, connectors).
good-writing-002377.zh: 删除那些琐碎的词汇：去掉所有不必要的短词（如代词、介词、连接词等）。

good-writing-002378.en: Dress Up “This”: Pronouns are hard for readers to follow, especially “this” and “it.”
good-writing-002378.zh: “这个”的代词用法很棘手，读者很难理解“这个”和“它”这两个词的具体含义。

good-writing-002379.en: Remove the Boring Stuff: Spend less time defending what you’ve written, and more time revealing the truth.
good-writing-002379.zh: 消除那些无用的内容：减少花时间去维护自己写的内容，而更多地花时间去揭示真相。

good-writing-002380.en: Refresh Your Words: Don’t repeat a distinctive word unless you must.
good-writing-002380.zh: 精炼你的措辞：除非必要，否则不要重复一个具有独特意义的词。

good-writing-002381.en: Know Your Words Inside and Out: Examining the etymology of words makes them more concrete and useful.
good-writing-002381.zh: 深入了解词语的构成：研究词语的词源可以使这些词语更加具体且易于理解。

good-writing-002382.en: Stay in Tune: The better word is both precise and unnoticed.
good-writing-002382.zh: 保持专注：更恰当的词汇应该是既精确又不易被察觉的。

good-writing-002383.en: A thesaurus is your book of magic spells.
good-writing-002383.zh: 同义词词典，就是你的魔法咒语书。

good-writing-002384.en: Find the Hidden Metaphor: Metaphors mirror humdrum experiences through elegant comparison.
good-writing-002384.zh: 找到隐藏的比喻手法：比喻通过优雅的对比来反映平凡的生活体验。

good-writing-002385.en: In the hands of an expert, they both illuminate and offer depth of field.
good-writing-002385.zh: 在高手笔下，比喻既能使事物豁然清晰，又能赋予它们层次和纵深。

good-writing-002386.en: Twist Clichés: We already think in clichés; you owe it to your reader’s search for novelty to remove or deconstruct your hackneyed phrases.
good-writing-002386.zh: 颠覆陈词滥调：我们总是习惯于使用那些陈腐的表达方式；为了给读者带来新鲜感，你有必要去除或拆解那些陈旧的表达方式。

good-writing-002387.en: Knock Three Times: For a series of terms to land, you usually need three.
good-writing-002387.zh: 需要三次敲击才能触发某些效果：通常，需要三次这样的操作才能让某些条件得到满足。

good-writing-002388.en: Stretch Out: Long sentences require attention to detail, conjunctions, and rhythm—and a payoff at the end.
good-writing-002388.zh: 冗长的句子需要注重细节、正确使用连接词，并保持良好的节奏感——最终能带来令人满意的效果。

good-writing-002389.en: Short Sells: Interrupt lyrical or otherwise long passages with an abrupt, short sentence.
good-writing-002389.zh: 短暂停顿：用一句简短的句子突然打断那些冗长的抒情或长句。

good-writing-002390.en: Give Your Sentence a Finale: Even if you begin your sentence with a punch, end it stronger.
good-writing-002390.zh: 为你的句子加上一个完美的结尾：即使你以一个重击开始你的句子，也要以更强大的方式结束它。

good-writing-002391.en: Crystallize Your Dialogue: Dialogue needs to be as zippy and economical as the rest of the book.
good-writing-002391.zh: 使对话更加生动有趣：对话部分应该像书的其余部分一样，简洁而富有表现力。

good-writing-002392.en: In Fiction, Archetype Your Characters: Below the human stereotypes are common psychological patterns that readers expect.
good-writing-002392.zh: 在小说中，塑造典型的人物形象：在人类的刻板印象之下，存在着一些读者普遍预期会出现的心理模式。

good-writing-002393.en: Show, Then Tell: Start with the concrete—what happened—and after, when appropriate, riff on your thoughts about consequences.
good-writing-002393.zh: 先展示事实：从具体事件开始描述发生了什么；在适当的时候，再谈谈你对这些后果的看法。

good-writing-002394.en: Give Them a Hero’s Welcome: Start off by telling the reader who to root for.
good-writing-002394.zh: 给予他们英雄般的欢迎：首先告诉读者，应该支持谁。

good-writing-002395.en: Once Is Enough: Keep your first description of a character or place distinctive enough that you aren’t tempted to add to it later.
good-writing-002395.zh: 一次就足够了：让角色或地点的首次描述具有足够的独特性，这样就不会有后来想要对其进行更多修改的冲动了。

good-writing-002396.en: Smell the Roses: Sight is only one of five senses; let your readers enjoy touch, hearing, smell, and taste.
good-writing-002396.zh: 感受玫瑰的香气：视觉只是五种感官之一；让读者的体验还包括触觉、听觉、嗅觉和味觉。

good-writing-002397.en: Don’t Filter: Don’t point out that someone is thinking, opining, or experiencing what is already happening on the page.
good-writing-002397.zh: 不要进行过滤：不要指出某人在思考、发表意见或体验页面上正在发生的事件。

good-writing-002398.en: Trust Your Reader: Your reader will fill in the gaps; you only need to be complete enough.
good-writing-002398.zh: 信任你的读者：读者会填补那些空白；你只需要做到足够完整即可。

good-writing-002399.en: Layer Your Sentences: Sentences convey more than information; their other purposes must be tended.
good-writing-002399.zh: 分层表达句子：句子不仅仅用于传递信息；它们还有其他用途，这些用途也需要被重视。

good-writing-002400.en: Write the Hard Stuff: Don’t shy away from the big mysteries of life.
good-writing-002400.zh: 不要回避生活中那些复杂而重要的难题。

good-writing-002401.en: Break the Rules: A rule may be of universal use, but need not be universally used.
good-writing-002401.zh: 打破规则：某些规则虽然具有普遍适用性，但并不一定需要被普遍遵循。

good-writing-002402.en: Finish the Damn Thing: Your job is to complete the project.
good-writing-002402.zh: 完成这项该死的任务：你的任务就是完成这个项目。

good-writing-002403.en: The final quality and consequences are not yet your business.
good-writing-002403.zh: 最终质量如何、会产生什么后果，眼下还不是你需要操心的事。

good-writing-002404.en: Worship (Talented) Editors: Writing is collaborative, and editors save your skin.
good-writing-002404.zh: 编辑提示：写作是一个合作的过程，编辑们会尽力保护你的权益。

good-writing-002406.en: Neal: My bedroom shared the basement with my dad’s small but sublime fiction library, a wide bookcase that loomed over the pool table.
good-writing-002406.zh: 尼尔：我的卧室与父亲那本虽小但非常珍贵的文学藏书共享一个地下室。那是一个宽大的书架，高耸在台球桌的上方。

good-writing-002407.en: These few hundred dark clothbound books, dust jackets torn or discarded, opened their leaves to me as a beginning, as my guidance, my standards, and my expectations for my formative reading.
good-writing-002407.zh: 这几百本装帧粗糙的书籍，其封面已破损或被丢弃。这些书籍对我来说，是一种开始，是我的指导，是我的标准，也是我对自己阅读体验的期望。

good-writing-002408.en: It was a random rainy day in 1962 when I pulled down Irving Stone’s The Agony and the Ecstasy to see what was going on in these fat, small-type, mysterious adult books.
good-writing-002408.zh: 1962年那个下雨的随机日子里，我翻开了欧文·斯通所著的《痛苦与狂喜》这本书，想看看这些厚实而小巧的、充满神秘色彩的成人读物里到底有什么内容。

good-writing-002409.en: Without ever being told to, I let my dad’s library take over as curator, my tastes over the next ten years refined by his literary heavyweights—Shakespeare, Joyce (Dad had read everything, even Finnegans Wake and Stephen Hero), Faulkner, Hemingway, Twain, Austen, Henry Miller, Sinclair Lewis, Salinger, Katherine Anne Porter—and, osmotically, my own writing improved.
good-writing-002409.zh: 在没有任何人的要求下，我让父亲的藏书室成为了我的阅读场所。在接下来的十年里，我的阅读品味逐渐受到他那些经典文学作品的影响——莎士比亚、乔伊斯（父亲几乎读遍了所有作品，包括《芬尼根之眠》和《斯蒂芬·希罗》）、福克纳、海明威、马克·吐温、奥斯汀、亨利·米勒、辛克莱·刘易斯、塞林格、凯瑟琳·安妮·波特……通过这些作品，我的写作水平也得到了提升。

good-writing-002411.en: Read well and you’ll write well.
good-writing-002411.zh: 阅读得好的话，写作也会变得出色。

good-writing-002412.en: Pore through literary fiction and the possibilities of sentences open up.
good-writing-002412.zh: 穿透文学小说的外壳，句子所蕴含的无限可能性便显现出来。

good-writing-002413.en: Thanks, Dad, and also for you and Mom, both trained copy editors, correcting our grammar at the dinner table.
good-writing-002413.zh: 谢谢爸爸，也谢谢妈妈——她们都是受过专业训练的文字编辑，会在餐桌上帮助我们纠正语法错误。

good-writing-002414.en: Rules are easier to retrieve when they’re stored young.
good-writing-002414.zh: 当规则被存储得较为简单时，检索起来就更加容易了。

good-writing-002415.en: Most of the guidance in the book was delivered to me in cursory and curmudgeonly form at deadline by editors and fellow reporters in my newspapering days.
good-writing-002415.zh: 在那些日子里，当我还在报社工作、负责撰写报道时，这本书中的大部分指导内容都是编辑和同事以粗略且敷衍的态度在截止日期前交给我处理的。

good-writing-002416.en: These ad hoc word coaches included Rob Borsellino, Sam Daleo, Jim McGarvey, Meg Lundstrom, Dean Chang, Manny Mendoza, Lucy Lu, Craig Gilbert, Mikhail Horowitz, Kent Allen, and of course many I’ve forgotten.
good-writing-002416.zh: 这些临时组成的词汇教练包括罗布·博尔塞利诺、萨姆·达莱奥、吉姆·麦加维、梅格·伦德斯特罗姆、迪恩·张、曼尼·门多萨、露西·卢、克雷格·吉尔伯特、米哈伊尔·霍罗维茨、肯特·艾伦，当然还有许多我忘记的名字。

good-writing-002417.en: Finally, forty years ago, Marilynne Robinson encouraged me on long sentences, on describing the supposedly ineffable, and on trusting my voice.
good-writing-002417.zh: 终于，四十年前，玛丽莲·罗宾逊鼓励我使用长句来表达自己的思想，去描述那些看似难以用语言表达的情感，并相信自己能够用文字表达出自己的心声。

good-writing-002418.en: Writing professor Alexandra Youmans was instrumental in this book finding its way.
good-writing-002418.zh: 这本书的出版与写作教授亚历山德拉·尤曼斯有着密切的关联。她在这一过程中发挥了关键作用，帮助这本书得以问世。

good-writing-002419.en: Working with an early draft, she provided several of the examples sprinkled in, and introduced me to the “Unadorned This” demon that became Rule 13.
good-writing-002419.zh: 在初步的草稿基础上，她补充了其中几个例子，并向我介绍了被称为“无装饰性 This”的规则，这一规则后来成为了第13条规则。

good-writing-002420.en: Anne: My father, Ken Lamott, was a great writer.
good-writing-002420.zh: 安妮：我的父亲，肯·拉莫特，是一位非常出色的作家。

good-writing-002421.en: He taught me how to write, how to put into words what I saw, thought, and imagined, starting at an early age.
good-writing-002421.zh: 他从很小的时候就开始教我如何写作，如何把我的所见、所思、所想象的事物用文字表达出来。

good-writing-002422.en: He taught me the habits of writing, of sitting down at the desk at the same time every day, no matter what, and to keep working on my material until I got it right, got it to be the best I could muster, and then to do one more draft.
good-writing-002422.zh: 他教会了我写作的技巧，比如每天固定时间坐在书桌前进行写作，无论发生什么情况都不会改变。他还教导我要不断练习，直到能够完美地完成作品，达到自己所能达到的最佳水平。之后，再进行一次修改。

good-writing-002423.en: He helped me learn to read and love poetry, to read great books to see how it was done, to immerse myself in the beautifully written word.
good-writing-002423.zh: 他帮助我学会了阅读和欣赏诗歌，让我能够阅读那些优秀的书籍，了解文字的奥秘，让我能够沉浸在这美妙而富有感染力的文字之中。

good-writing-002424.en: He taught me that getting to write was a privilege.
good-writing-002424.zh: 他教会我，能够写作是一种特权。

good-writing-002425.en: He is the reason I got to be a writer, too.
good-writing-002425.zh: 他也是让我能够成为作家的原因。

good-writing-002426.en: Both of Us: We adore and admire our agent, Sarah Chalfant of the Wylie Agency, who found us the perfect editor and publisher, Tracy Behar of Penguin/Avery.
good-writing-002426.zh: 我们俩都非常钦佩我们的经纪人——来自Wylie代理公司的Sarah Chalfant。她为我们找到了理想的编辑和出版人——来自Penguin/Avery公司的Tracy Behar。

good-writing-002427.en: As a collaborative entity, we each thank the other for their love, humility, and expertise.
good-writing-002427.zh: 作为一个协作团队，我们每个人都感谢对方的爱、谦逊以及专业知识。

good-writing-002428.en: It never fails to surprise us the luck of finding an expert, friendly editor in-house.
good-writing-002428.zh: 能够找到一位专业且友善的内部编辑，真是件令人惊喜的事情。

good-writing-002741.en: Neal Allen is a writer, spiritual coach, and speaker.
good-writing-002741.zh: 尼尔·艾伦是一位作家、精神导师和演讲者。

good-writing-002742.en: He is the author of Shapes of Truth and Better Days.
good-writing-002742.zh: 他是《真理的形貌》和《更美好的日子》这两本书的作者。

good-writing-002743.en: A former journalist and corporate executive, he holds master’s degrees in Political Science and Eastern Classics.
good-writing-002743.zh: 他曾经是一名记者和企业高管，同时拥有政治学及东方古典学领域的硕士学位。

good-writing-002744.en: Anne Lamott is the author of twenty books, including the New York Times bestsellers Somehow; Help, Thanks, Wow; Dusk, Night, Dawn; Traveling Mercies; and Bird by Bird, as well as seven novels.
good-writing-002744.zh: 安妮·拉莫特是二十本书籍的作者，其中包括《纽约时报》畅销书《不知怎么地》、《帮助吧，谢谢，哇》；《黄昏、夜晚、黎明》；《流浪的痛苦》以及《鸟与鸟》等作品。此外，她还创作了七部小说。

good-writing-002745.en: She is a recipient of a Guggenheim Fellowship and an inductee to the California Hall of Fame.
good-writing-002745.zh: 她是古根海姆奖学金的获得者，同时也被列入了加利福尼亚名人堂的名单中。

good-writing-002746.en: Neal and Anne live in Northern California.
good-writing-002746.zh: 尼尔和安妮住在北加州。

chapters.title: Read This First
chapters.html:
Read This First

I first wrote professionally for a newspaper in New York’s Hudson Valley. As a cub reporter at the Kingston Daily Freeman in the late seventies, I cut my teeth on town meetings, county court, the police blotter, and obituaries. I learned to obey the front page’s tight style restraints: omniscient third person, complete sentences, no exclamations or questions, sixth-grade vocabulary, scarce adjectives or adverbs, pretense of objectivity, inverted pyramid, few parentheticals, no slang, no alliteration or rhyming, no long quotes, stricture after stricture straitjacketing my weirder impulses. The result? Efficient, economical, and colorless language. I had a lot to learn about writing, and in retrospect the overly mannered style of hard news was a godsend to a mind that had spent its youth immersed in literary and experimental fiction, where rules are to be broken and anarchy is always knocking.

One morning, my editor Sam Daleo looked me in the eye: “Neal, the trick is to write with your verbs.” He explained the difference between a vivid verb and a weak one. Thumb forward in this book of rules, and you’ll see that as Rule 1, with an explanation for how and why it works. In my mind, it’s the Daleo Rule. And for a long time, it protected and encouraged me.

I was happy with my one rule of rhetoric and persuasion, and my career progressed at a steady pace. I became a better and better newsman in terms of fact-gathering and reporting. My writing didn’t look so different from what I scanned on the front pages of The New York Times or The Washington Post, at least to me. And then one day I woke up to the Times’s front-page story on the marriage of Prince Charles and Lady Di.

Here is how New York Times political writer R. W. Apple Jr. revealed the spectacle in his second paragraph: “The 2,500 guests inside Christopher Wren’s Baroque masterpiece, St. Paul’s Cathedral, the hundreds of thousands who watched the wedding party ride in magnificent horse-drawn carriages from Buckingham Palace to the cathedral and back, and the 700 million television viewers around the world witnessed a fairy tale come to life: the handsome Prince Charles in naval uniform marrying the lovely 20-year-old Diana Spencer, daughter of an earl, amid the sort of splendor the modern world has all but forgotten.”

This syntax didn’t emulate Tom Wolfe or Hunter Thompson in a magazine displaying the New Journalism that was all the rage. It wasn’t a feature story masquerading as an eventful occurrence. Here stood a hard news reporter packing information into one elegant phrase after another, and I trembled in shame. Where did the legendary Johnny Apple learn to do that? He was thinking differently from me about newspaper writing. For both of us it might be a craft, not an art, but he showed without telling that daily journalism could be graceful and as beckoning as literary fiction.

By a couple of years later I had accumulated three or four rules of rhetoric, enough to survive in the medium-sized newspaper where I now worked. The Bergen Record in Hackensack, New Jersey, had a circulation of 150,000, but because it catered to some of the richest people in the state, it landed on the doorstep with a thud, fat and thick with advertising and a wide-open news hole overflowing with local and wire reporting. The newsroom employed 260 editors, reporters, feature writers, illustrators, opinion writers, cartoonists, photographers, clerks, and librarians, a number more typical of papers three times its size. Among the sixty or so writers a few stood out as stylists. I dissected their stories and occasionally asked for advice. By the time I left five years later, I had corralled another five or six rules.

Think about that. A meager six or eight rules of rhetoric could maintain a career, and ten were enough to be admired by peers.

That’s the germination of this book. From my time at the Record through a corporate career in publicity and marketing, and into a third life as a spiritual coach and author, writing has stood fast as my default expertise. I’ve made a living from magazine writing, business writing and editing, speechwriting, copywriting, short story writing, ghostwriting, memoir editing, scriptwriting, presentation writing, and book writing...and all along my hack writing career, I have quietly expanded my kit bag of rules for good writing. The bag contains thirty-six now, which doesn’t mean I’m three times the writer I was in the eighties. I still can’t conceive of arriving at Johnny Apple’s second paragraph all by myself. But thirty-six rules are more than enough for me to amuse myself with complex sentence puzzles every time I sit at my keyboard. These rules don’t restrict me so much as they encourage me to stretch into more and more possibilities, leaps of imagination, and lovely explorations.

Thomas Mann defined a writer as someone for whom writing is more difficult than it is for other people. Most books are not composed by people whose primary concern, expertise, and profession is words and rhetoric. Most books are written by academics, other experts, or pundits. Many fiction writers, some of them quite successful, are less concerned with their sentences than with moving the plot along. For many authors, the main interest is the overall theme they are elaborating or the argument they are proving. But for some professional writers, the central interest always remains the sentence. Next comes the consistency or flow of the material. The topic or plot of the book, the content of the speech or lyrics, takes third place—just the material with which to exercise persuasive prowess.
